Until an admin role exists the principal sets each person's weekly hours (in minutes; 40 hours when unset, shown as a default) and skills, and schedules leave (whole weekdays at a fifth of the weekly hours each), client meetings and internal commitments (minutes on each weekday from one date to another, a meeting optionally linked to its job); only weekdays Monday to Friday count. Available = weekly hours less leave and commitments in the week, never below zero. Demand is estimated remaining work: the estimates of open, applicable tasks a person owns (WORK-009 owner resolution) whose due date (the task's, else the job's) falls in the week, plus the review estimate of each job they review that is not signed off and falls due in the week. Actual time is the person's recorded time in the week, and per job their total time on it, shown beside the estimates and never subtracted from them. A person is overloaded when demand exceeds available. Open tasks or reviews due in the week without an estimate are unscheduled; open tasks due before the week are listed as past due; neither counts toward demand. A deadline conflict is a job due in the week that is not signed off, with one explanation for each of its people who is overloaded or on leave between the week's start and its due date, and for each unscheduled item on it. The view filters by skill (people who have it) and service (the job's work type, WORK-007) and drills down to each job; reviewers and the principal see the whole firm, a preparer sees only themselves. The job's people (or a reviewer or the principal) adjust an open task's estimate or the job's review estimate; every change is audited. CAPACITY-002 and CAPACITY-003 build on this model.

- **CAPACITY-002 — Reassignment and dependency aware scheduling.** Reassign and reschedule work when staff are absent or overloaded, proposing eligible coverage with client authority, skills, remaining capacity, dependency order and independent reviewer constraints. Preview notifications and affected deadlines; a manager approves the plan and owns unresolved conflicts. **Acceptance evidence:** Remove an assigned preparer for leave, preview alternate staffing and move a dependent job chain. Approve the feasible changes, refuse an ineligible/self-review assignment and inspect new owners, notifications and unresolved deadline conflicts. **Semantics (CAPACITY-002):** a manager is a reviewer or the principal (the people who reschedule under WORK-004); they plan cover for a person on leave or over capacity between two dates (at most 92 days apart). The plan takes the open jobs that person prepares, and the jobs not yet completed that they review, falling due from the first date through 14 days after the last, ordered so each job comes after the planned jobs it waits for (WORK-003) and otherwise by due date. For each role the person holds it proposes an eligible colleague (preparer: an active preparer, reviewer or the principal; reviewer: an active reviewer or the principal) who is not the person, never reviews their own work, is not the job's partner as preparer, is not on CAPACITY-001 leave on the due date and still has the job's estimated minutes free that week (available less demand less the plan's earlier moves); the colleague covering a job's prerequisite comes first, then one with the job's work type among their skills, then the most free minutes, then email order. A manager may name the preparer or reviewer, move a due date (with where it comes from) or leave a job out; a named person who is ineligible, would review their own work or lacks the capacity, or a prerequisite that would fall due after the job waiting for it, refuses the plan until changed. The preview lists every line, the notifications and the unresolved conflicts (no eligible colleague free); approval needs the preview's fingerprint, applies every feasible line in one batch (role tasks follow, WORK-009), sends each notice in-app and by email with its delivery recorded, and records each conflict owned by the approving manager in the plan and among the client's unresolved items (CRM-003), where it can be handed on and is closed with a resolution note by its owner or the principal. **Client authority (ACCESS-002, inherited before it ships):** until client grants exist every active member may work any client; when ACCESS-002 adds client and team grants, a proposed or named colleague must hold the client's grant. CAPACITY-002 is done for every capability that exists today.

- **CAPACITY-003 — Capacity forecasts and hiring plans.** Forecast future workload from approved recurring engagements, historical completion/time, pipeline and seasonality, with visible assumptions and confidence ranges. Compare staffing, hiring or service-change scenarios without altering actual assignments or promised deadlines. **Acceptance evidence:** Project the next tax season from recurring work and prior actuals, add a hypothetical hire and lost client, and compare demand/capacity by skill. Inspect each week's forecast as a range with its stated confidence level, and confirm a client with no prior actuals widens the range and is named as the reason. Trace estimates to sources and save a scenario without changing live work. **Semantics (CAPACITY-003):** a manager (a reviewer or the principal, as in CAPACITY-002; a preparer sees only their own capacity under CAPACITY-001) forecasts 1 to 53 Monday-to-Sunday weeks (UTC dates) from a Monday. Demand is the periods of active, approved recurring rules (WORK-002) whose due date (the period's last day plus the rule's days) falls in a week, counted in that week; paused rules, skipped periods and periods whose job is already signed off are left out, and one-off jobs are not forecast. A period's time traces to its source: the client's prior actuals for that template, which are the recorded time (TIME-001) on its signed-off jobs of earlier periods (a signed-off job with no recorded time is not one), using only periods starting in the same calendar month when there are any (seasonality); the estimate is their mean rounded to the minute, and the range runs from 90% of the smallest (rounded down) to 110% of the largest (rounded up). Without prior actuals the period uses the rule's time budget, else the work type's budget, else the sum of the template's task estimates, with a range from 50% to 150% of it (rounded to the minute), and the reason names the client; with none of these its estimate is zero and the reason says so. Each week states its confidence: high when every period due in it rests on at least three prior actuals, medium when each rests on at least one, low when any rests on none (each such reason listed). Capacity is each active person's weekly hours less leave and commitments on the week's weekdays (CAPACITY-001); by skill, a person counts in full under each of their skills, and demand counts under the skill named like its work type (lower case); a skill is short by its demand's high end less its capacity. A scenario adds hypothetical hires (weekly minutes and skills from a start date), changes a person's weekly hours from a date (zero for a departure), drops lost clients' periods (listed as left out) and scales a work type's time to a percentage (0 drops the service); it is compared week by week and by skill with the baseline. Forecasting computes from live records and stores nothing; saving a scenario stores only its name, window and changes (audited) and changes no job, rule, assignment, estimate, due date or capacity row; reopening it recomputes from current records. **Pipeline (CRM-005):** each open prospect’s requested service contributes its own visible unweighted assumption that the prospect wins, with current stage, source, owner and whole-prospect annual fee in its stored currency. An exact case-insensitive service/work-type name match is the default; the manager may choose another work type or leave the service unestimated. Its first assumed work target defaults to the forecast start or is selected per service; demand repeats at the selected template’s monthly/quarterly/annual cadence through the window, or occurs once without a template. Each engagement uses the same no-actuals estimate chain as recurring work (work-type budget, else template task estimates), with a 50%–150% range rounded to the minute. Missing matches or budgets contribute zero explicitly labeled unestimated, with a named low-confidence reason. Pipeline demand counts in weekly and skill totals in baseline and scenarios; service percentage changes scale it too. Fees never become hours. Won and lost prospects are excluded. These assumptions create no assignments, signed scope or promised deadlines. Saved scenarios retain the selected work type and first target and recompute from current records. CAPACITY-003 is done for every capability that exists today.

### Time billing payments and reporting

- **TIME-001 — Time budgets and activity suggestions.** Record time against client/job/task with manual entry and timers, billable status and snapshotted rate; compare actual hours/cost with approved budgets. Suggest missing entries from consented work/email/calendar activity with source links, never silently creating billable time. Corrections retain authorship and respect locks. **Acceptance evidence:** Record time, change the rate and inspect unchanged prior amounts and budget variance. Stop/restart a timer, reject one activity suggestion and approve another; verify only approved minutes enter WIP and unauthorized edits are refused. **Timers and budgets (implemented subset):** a person runs at most one timer, kept by the server so it continues across restarts and devices; stopping it records one time entry through the manual-entry path (rate in force snapshotted, closed periods refused) for the elapsed time rounded up to the next whole minute (at least 1, at most 1440), dated the UTC day the timer started, and a discarded timer records nothing. A job's budget is the minutes approved by the reviewer or principal who starts it, or by its recurrence rule (WORK-002); actual is every recorded entry in any review state plus adjustments, at their snapshotted amounts, and variance is actual minus budget. **Billable status (implemented subset):** each time entry is billable or not, chosen by the person when they record it by hand or start a timer (billable unless they choose otherwise), and a TIME-002 correction keeps the returned entry's status unless the person changes it. A non-billable entry keeps its snapshotted rate and amount and counts in the job's actual time, cost and variance, but neither it nor any adjustment to it is ever ready to bill: it stays out of WIP, is refused in a billing export and stays out of the job's margin (TIME-004). **Semantics (TIME-001):** a time entry or timer names its job, and so its client, and optionally one of that job's checklist tasks; a correction keeps the task unless the person changes it. **Activity suggestions:** consent is per person, off by default, given and withdrawn only by that person on their Jobs screen. While it is on, that person's own audited work actions on jobs they can record time on (completing a checklist task, accepting or returning a document, opening, replying to or requesting a correction in a discussion, any tax-notice timeline action, discarding a timer) taken at or after the moment of consent suggest one entry per job and UTC day on which they recorded no time of their own on that job; each suggestion lists and links its source actions. Only that person sees, approves or rejects their suggestions: approval needs the minutes and an explicit billable choice and records the entry through the manual-entry path (rate in force on that day snapshotted, closed periods refused); rejection records nothing; each decision is kept once with its source action ids. Approved suggestions are ordinary time, so they reach WIP only once approved on a timesheet (TIME-002) and only if billable. Withdrawing consent removes every pending suggestion, and consenting again never uses earlier actions. Email and calendar activity are not sources until MAIL-001 and INTEGRATE-005 ship, each with its own per-source consent (written into those clauses).

- **TIME-002 — Timesheet approval and period locks.** Staff submit timesheets to managers, who approve or return entries with reasons. Closing a billing period locks approved time; corrections use an authorized adjustment that preserves the original. Invoice/export reservations prevent the same work being billed twice. **Acceptance evidence:** Submit a weekly timesheet, return and correct one entry, approve it and close the period. Attempt direct edits and duplicate billing, then post an authorized adjustment and inspect its history.

- **TIME-003 — Billing rates and rate cards.** Billing rates are set by staff member, role and service or work type, with client-specific overrides and effective dates. The precedence is client and service, then client, then service, then staff member, then role. Role is the person's practice role (principal, reviewer or preparer). Service rates may target a WORK-007 work type or the engagement template the job was started from. Within either service scope (service or client and service), a matching work-type card takes precedence over template cards, then the latest effective date and creation order resolve cards for that target. Template cards continue to apply to jobs started from that template when no work-type card in that scope is in force; work types without a default template may have their own rates. Each time entry snapshots the rate it resolved and where that rate came from. A rate change takes effect from its date and never rewrites past entries. **Acceptance evidence:** Set rates for a practice role, a staff member, a 1040 service, a client and that client plus service. Record time with only the role matching, then with staff, service, client and client-plus-service rates also matching in turn; inspect each entry's resolved rate and source to prove every precedence level: client and service, client, service, staff member, role. Verify role means principal, reviewer or preparer. Start two jobs with distinct work types sharing a template and inspect their distinct service rates; a type without a default template also accepts its own rate. Verify client overrides, work-type versus template specificity, effective dates and recorded snapshots through archive restore. Change the staff rate effective next month and confirm past entries are unchanged.

- **TIME-004 — Expenses and disbursements.** Record billable and non-billable expenses (filing fees, postage, mileage at the firm-set rate, software pass-throughs) against a client and work item. Each expense can carry a receipt, a markup and an approval, and approved billable expenses become BILL-002 invoice lines. Staff reimbursements are kept separate from client charges, and expenses count in WIP and profitability (BILL-003). Amounts are integer cents: a markup is a whole percent from 0 to 100 of cost, a billable expense charges its cost plus the markup rounded half up to the cent, and a non-billable expense charges nothing; mileage is miles to one decimal place at the firm's cents-per-mile rate in force on the expense date, rounded half up. A reviewer or the principal approves or rejects an expense, nobody but the principal approves their own, and an expense dated in a closed billing period (TIME-002) cannot be recorded. Staff-paid expenses are owed back to that person at cost, and the principal records each reimbursement. Until BILL-002 issues invoice documents, an expense's invoice line is its line in the reviewed billing export, reserved once; BILL-002 inherits approved billable expenses as invoice lines before it ships. Until BILL-003 ships, WIP is the value of everything ready to bill, and a job's profitability is its margin before staff cost: fixed fee, approved billable time (TIME-001) and its adjustments and approved billable expense charges, less the cost of every approved expense, billable or not; BILL-003 keeps expenses in its WIP and profitability. **Acceptance evidence:** Record a state filing fee with a receipt and a 10% markup, approve it, invoice it and inspect the invoice line and WIP. A non-billable expense stays off the invoice and appears in profitability. An unapproved expense cannot be invoiced.

- **BILL-001 — Reviewed immutable billing exports.** Reviewers prepare time/fixed-fee CSV drafts with snapshotted sources. The principal approves once with a note; the approved bytes and digest remain unchanged and each source belongs to one live export. Draft voiding releases reservations; CSV cells neutralize spreadsheet formulas and preserve source currency. **Acceptance evidence:** Prepare a mixed time/fixed-fee export, reject source reuse and non-owner approval, approve as principal and download twice. Verify identical CSV bytes, source locks, formula-safe cells and a voided draft's released sources. **Receiving ERASURE-002 (ct 22 Oct 2026):** Approved exports stay immutable; only ERASURE-002's confirmed expiry removes their bytes, keeping number, totals, revision and SHA-256.

- **BILL-002 — Invoices retainers and recurring fees.** Create numbered USD invoices from approved time, fixed scope, milestones or recurring retainers; separate fee entitlement from job completion. Preview invoice lines, terms, authorized sales-tax treatment, credits and client recipients, then approve and deliver PDF/portal invoices. Retainer deposits, credits, price changes, cancellation and prorations remain traceable. Select exactly one invoice authority: Blotter, QuickBooks Online or Xero; schedule generation is idempotent. **Acceptance evidence:** Bill a fixed engagement and hourly extra, start a monthly retainer, apply a deposit and preview a fee amendment. Approve/deliver invoices, repeat the schedule event and inspect one invoice per entitlement with USD totals and retained source links. **Engagement history (CRM-003, inherited before this ships):** issued, sent and voided invoices appear in the client's history with author, time and source link, visible only to those who may read the job, and any unresolved item they create names an owner, next action and due condition. **Acceptance evidence (CRM-003):** an issued invoice appears in the client history linked to its source time and fees. **Inherited BASE-001:** satisfy its authority, audit, erasure and portability activation gate with named public-door evidence before this new path ships. **Receiving ERASURE-002 (ct 22 Oct 2026):** Before shipping, BILL-002 adds its records and provider copies to ERASURE-002's classes, clocks, holds, preview, erasure, receipt and restore fence (ct 22 Oct 2026). **Native semantics (sx-blotter-c36/c37, 22 Oct; approved with change by ct, batch 11 H):** The principal selects the sole invoice authority; the principal or an ACCESS-002 financial-authority holder (for the clients the holder holds) authorizes independent fixed/milestone/explicit-proration entitlements, records supplied deposit/credit evidence and tax treatment, approves numbered USD PDF snapshots and delivers them to an authorized billing contact. Approved time, adjustments and expenses share source reservations with reviewed exports; a numbered document never releases its source links. No taxability, bank settlement, charge or automatic proration is inferred. Monthly rules approved by the principal or a financial-authority holder create one draft per rule/month; issue and send are separate person actions unless a holder's recorded automatic-issue consent covers the rule revision (below); price changes and cancellation apply from the reviewed future month while existing entitlement prices remain. An explicit recorded credit allocation changes the current balance, never the issued PDF. Invoice links are contact/revision-bound, expire after 30 days, expose only their invoice and recheck live billing/portal/email authority. Unresolved sends are held for provider-evidence reconciliation without replay. Restored rules are paused and old invoice links revoked. Issued/sent/voided history links to its source job; open balances name an owner, next action and due date. Native invoice search and merge/undo preserve immutable document bytes and sources. Existing performance reports project the selected job cohort’s native invoices, retainers, supplied credits and open USD receivables from live sources, with job/document/source links, generation time and the same values in CSV/PDF; they never label supplied credit evidence as provider settlement. Each report download records its client scope and named downloader for erasure receipts. Invoices, credits, rules and deliveries join ERASURE-002 billing/link classes, holds, counts, receipt and journal fence; open invoice balances and unapplied deposits/credits refuse whole-client erasure and billing expiry. Erased-client invoice identities are absent from normal billing lists and use opaque expiry labels; explicit retained detail/PDF reads require the principal and are audited. Retention clocks use issue and later void/credit/allocation dates in the firm timezone; expiry requires principal confirmation and preserves amounts, number, attribution and SHA-256. INTEGRATE-001 inherits QBO/Xero authority selection and reconciliation before those connectors ship; unavailable external authorities refuse. PAY-001 inherits actual settlement evidence and balances before collections ship. AUTOMATE-001 inherits invoice creation as an additional action before it is exposed; current invoice schedules create approved-rule drafts and, within a recorded consent, issue and send them.

  **Ruled (ct 22 Oct):** the principal or an ACCESS-002 financial-authority holder prepares, issues, sends and voids. Selecting the invoice authority and confirming retention expiry stay principal-only. A holder may enable automatic issue and send for one rule revision. The consent records a per-invoice USD cap, the recipient and a reason, and it is audited. Each run rechecks the consenter's live authority, the rule's terms and the recipient's billing role and email or portal consent. A run issues and sends only within the cap and with no exception. Otherwise it leaves a draft with a named exception. The invoice states 'auto-issued under rule revision N'. Delivery may be by email PDF to a billing contact without portal access. A restore brings rules back paused and without consent. **Semantic implemented (sx-blotter-c37):** the consent is one record on the rule: the rule revision the holder reviewed (any amendment, pause or reactivation is a new revision and ends it), the cap, one recipient contact and a reason; recording it is audited and needs step-up, and it never travels in an archive. Each hourly run rechecks that the revision is unchanged, that the consenter is still the principal or a financial-authority holder holding the client, that the invoice recipient is the consented contact with a billing role and email consent (portal access is not needed), and that the invoice total is within the cap. With no exception it issues the numbered PDF under the consenter's authority (the PDF reads 'This invoice was auto-issued under rule revision N') and sends it once; otherwise the invoice stays a draft carrying the named exception and nothing is sent, and a held send or exception is never retried by a later run. A contact without portal access receives the PDF by email alone: no invoice link is mailed and the stored link is born revoked. AUTOMATE-001 inherits automatic issue only through this consent.

- **PAY-001 — Card ACH and authorized collections.** Collect invoices by card and US ACH through Stripe, with saved-method mandates and explicit authorization for recurring or due-date automatic collection. Show fees in USD, payment terms and ACH pending/settled/returned states; distinguish provider acceptance from settlement. Verify webhook signatures, deduplicate events, reconcile partial payments, refunds, disputes and returns, and own failed-payment follow-up. Provider onboarding, US bank access and saved-method/auto-pay migration from Karbon Payments, TaxDome Payments, Canopy Payments and Financial Cents (MIGRATE-007) are engineering obligations; a method or authorization that cannot move becomes a tracked client reauthorization, and no client is charged automatically without a valid mandate. **Acceptance evidence:** Pay a real authorized low-value invoice by card and ACH, authorize a recurring mandate and inspect provider receipts and ledger reconciliation. At the provider test edge exercise duplicate/out-of-order events, ACH return, partial payment, refund and failed collection; revoke the mandate and verify no later debit. **Engagement history (CRM-003, inherited before this ships):** payments, failures and refunds appear in the client's history with author, time and source link, visible only to those who may read the job, and any unresolved item they create (a failed payment) names an owner, next action and due condition. **Acceptance evidence (CRM-003):** trace a request from email through upload and review to its payment in the client history. **Inherited BASE-001:** satisfy its authority, audit, erasure and portability activation gate with named public-door evidence before this new path ships. **Receiving ERASURE-002 (ct 22 Oct 2026):** Before shipping, PAY-001 adds its records and provider copies to ERASURE-002's classes, clocks, holds, preview, erasure, receipt and restore fence (ct 22 Oct 2026).

  **Implemented PAY-001 subset (26 October 2026):** See `STRIPE.md` for the exact adopted invoice-bounded consent, provider reconciliation, retained records and inactive restore semantics. Recurring collection and incumbent migration remain unbuilt and no automatic retry is authorized. PAY-002, BILL-005, MIGRATE-007, NOTIFY-001 and ERASURE-002 retain their named obligations.

- **PAY-002 — Payment plans and client payment self service.** In the portal, clients see open invoices, statements and payment history. They can pay several invoices in one payment, save or remove payment methods, set up auto-pay, and accept a firm-offered installment plan with an amount, a schedule and a mandate. Scheduled charges run only under explicit authorization, with a reminder before each debit. A missed or returned installment creates owned follow-up instead of an unauthorized retry. **Acceptance evidence:** A client pays two invoices in one card payment, and the payment is allocated correctly. The client accepts a three-installment ACH plan; the second installment is returned, which creates owned follow-up with no retry outside the authorized policy. After the client removes a saved card, a later auto-pay is refused. **Inherited BASE-001:** satisfy its authority, audit, erasure and portability activation gate with named public-door evidence before this new path ships. **Receiving ERASURE-002 (ct 22 Oct 2026):** Before shipping, PAY-002 adds its records and provider copies to ERASURE-002's classes, clocks, holds, preview, erasure, receipt and restore fence (ct 22 Oct 2026).

- **BILL-003 — WIP receivables realization and profitability.** Report unbilled WIP, earned/deferred retainers, aged receivables, collection follow-up (reminders and statements under BILL-004), credits, write-ups/downs, billed-versus-recorded realization, utilization and client/job/service profitability using approved time, cost and invoice/payment sources. Drill into calculation inputs, exclude duplicate exports and keep uncollected, settled and written-off amounts distinct. Partners approve credits, write-offs and collection messages. **Acceptance evidence:** Run WIP, aging and profitability for a client with hourly work, fixed fees, a retainer, partial payment and credit. Reconcile totals to approved sources and provider state, approve a write-off and inspect the changed period report without rewriting historical invoices. **Inherited BASE-001:** new capabilities, record kinds and doors retain native authority, revocation, audit and portability/erasure integrity; supply the named public-door activation evidence in BASE-001 before shipping. **Implemented native slice (BILL-003):** the performance report groups its selected jobs by client and service/work type, separately for each stored currency. The inclusive period-start cohort and existing client/service/assignee filters apply before grouping. Totals sum approved billable time and adjustments, earned fixed fees, approved expense charges and costs, margin before staff cost, unreserved ready-to-bill WIP and approved export snapshots. Draft reservations remove WIP but never count as approved exports; voiding restores that WIP. Each group links to its source jobs and their calculation inputs. **Implemented native completion (sx-blotter-c40, 22 Oct):** ready-to-bill WIP excludes every source a billing export or an invoice (draft or issued) has reserved; voiding a draft restores it. An issued non-void invoice's open balance is its gross less applied credits and approved write-offs; reminders, statements, the portal and erasure blockers read that one balance. The report adds, for the same period-start cohort and filters, receivables aged by whole days past the due date at the report's firm-local date (current, 1-30, 31-60, 61-90, over 90); retainer invoices earned (billing month already begun) or deferred (billed for a later month); and per client, service and job: recorded value (approved time, fee and expense lines on issued invoices), write-ups and write-downs (the adjustment lines), billed, billed-against-recorded realization, collected (recorded deposits applied), credits applied, written off, uncollected, invoiced expense cost, staff cost and profit, with each client's unbilled WIP beside them; collected, credited, written-off and uncollected are never merged. Under Blotter as the invoice authority the provider state of money is the practitioner-recorded deposit receipt references and credits; PAY-001 and any QuickBooks or Xero authority inherit the obligation to add their provider payment, refund, return and dispute states to the same figures when they ship. A write-off is approved by the principal or a financial-authority holder in a native person session (as for credits, ct 22 Oct), for a stated USD amount of an issued invoice's open balance with a reason; it is audited, immutable, refused above the balance, and never rewrites the issued invoice, its PDF or its totals: only the balance, the reports and statements dated after it change. Staff cost is the principal-recorded hourly cost rate in force on the entry date times the minutes of invoiced time and adjustments (minutes with no rate are counted, never guessed) and is shown only to the principal and financial-authority holders; profit is billed less write-offs, invoiced expense cost and staff cost. Utilization stays on the report's capacity lines. Write-off and staff-cost records join ERASURE-002's billing and staff classes, retained rows, expiry redaction of reasons, invoice clocks and restore fence. **Receiving ERASURE-002 (ct 22 Oct 2026):** Before shipping, BILL-003 adds its records and provider copies to ERASURE-002's classes, clocks, holds, preview, erasure, receipt and restore fence (ct 22 Oct 2026).

- **BILL-004 — Invoice reminders statements and bulk resend.** Overdue-invoice reminders run on a firm schedule (for example 3 days before the due date, on it, and 7, 14 and 30 days after) using MSG-001 templates. They stop when an invoice is paid, disputed or on a payment plan, and can be overridden per client. Staff can bulk resend selected invoices and generate monthly client statements of open invoices, credits and payments. Quick collect charges a saved method only within its PAY-001 authorization. Every reminder is recorded in the client's history. **Acceptance evidence:** Issue three invoices with different due dates, let the reminders run and pay one between steps; only the unpaid invoices are reminded, on schedule. Bulk resend two invoices. Generate a statement and reconcile it to open balances. Quick collect one invoice with an authorized saved card; a quick collect without authorization is refused. **Inherited BASE-001:** satisfy its authority, audit, erasure and portability activation gate with named public-door evidence before this new path ships. **Inherited MSG-002 marketing consent (ct 20 Oct 21:21Z):** Invoice reminders send engagement class only, with MSG-002's send-time recheck. **Receiving ERASURE-002 (ct 22 Oct 2026):** Before shipping, BILL-004 adds its records and provider copies to ERASURE-002's classes, clocks, holds, preview, erasure, receipt and restore fence (ct 22 Oct 2026). **Implemented native slice (sx-blotter-c37, 22 Oct; reminder-consent default approved by ct 22 Oct 23:45Z):** reminders are automatic outbound mail, so the firm schedule runs only under a recorded consent of the principal or a financial-authority holder without client scopes: the steps in days from the due date (negative before it), one firm engagement-class MSG-001 template version and a reason, audited and step-up confirmed; pausing ends it. Each hourly run rechecks the consenter's live authority and the template version (otherwise the schedule pauses with a named reason), and for each issued invoice with an open balance, no dispute or payment-plan hold and a client not opted out, sends the latest passed step once (earlier passed steps are recorded as skipped, never sent late) to the invoice's billing contact with the numbered PDF, after MSG-002's engagement send-time recheck (active, authorized billing contact with email consent and no hard bounce); a refused recheck or placeholder holds that step, named, and is never replayed. A client follows the firm schedule, opts out or has its own steps; every reminder, hold and override is in the client's history. Paid means the invoice balance is zero after recorded receipts, deposits, credits or approved write-offs (BILL-003) and observed net settled provider payments. Bulk resend sends one reviewed preview of up to 50 issued invoices (their billing recipients, documents and one reason) through BILL-002's delivery. A client statement as of a date lists open issued invoices with aging, recorded credits and their applications, observed provider payment states and net amounts, and totals equal to the open balances; its CSV is an export. Quick collect requires PAY-001’s current invoice-bounded saved-method authorization and fresh-confirmed financial authority; its provider receipts update the same open balance. Any edit to reminder steps or the consented template version pauses the schedule and ends its consent. Reminder tables join the link and firm classes, erasure steps, expiry effects and observed provider/recipient copies; a restore returns the schedule paused and without consent, and claimed reminders held.

- **BILL-005 — Payment gated delivery and credit hold.** A firm can require payment before releasing selected work product in the portal, such as a final return copy. The client sees the file as locked until paid. A card payment unlocks it on provider confirmation. For ACH the firm chooses whether a pending payment unlocks it or settlement is required. Records the client supplied are never withheld, consistent with Circular 230 §10.28; only the firm's own work product can be gated. Clients past a firm balance threshold go on credit hold: staff see the hold, and creating new work warns. - **VAULT-001 — Client credential vault.** Clients and staff store client-provided logins, such as bank, payroll, state tax and sales-tax portal credentials, encrypted under per-firm keys. Each credential is visible only to staff permitted on that client. Every reveal requires the staff member's MFA step-up (ACCESS-004) and is logged. Clients add and update credentials through the portal. Credentials never appear in AI context, emails, search or plain exports; archives either encrypt or exclude them, at the owner's choice. Rotation reminders are optional. **Current semantics:** credentials are AES-GCM ciphertext under the firm's vault key, derived from the installation's own VAULT_KEY secret (never the session secret) and the firm's random salt; one installation is one firm, and without VAULT_KEY the vault refuses to store or reveal. Staff permitted on a client are the principal, reviewers and a preparer holding a job on that client (ACCESS-001 job scope; ACCESS-002 inherits configurable client grants before it ships); others get not found, and lists show names, portal addresses, authors, times and rotation dates only; usernames, passwords and notes stay sealed. A reveal needs a step-up from that session in the last 5 minutes: a fresh TOTP, passkey or recovery-code answer, even when the session already passed its sign-in check; agent keys never reveal. Every reveal and every refused reveal by permitted staff is logged with person, credential, time and outcome, and shows in the client's history. Clients add and replace credentials through their contact-scoped link (CRM-001 authority) and never read one back. Rotation dates show as due on the staff list; no reminder is sent. Archives carry the ciphertext (default), readable only where the same VAULT_KEY is configured, or leave it out; either way a restored credential that cannot be opened says so. ### Agent surface (Base-delivered)
#### BASE-AGENT-001 — One MCP door per seed

*Tier:* Agent surface

**Requirement.** Every seed, hosted or self-hosted, serves one remote MCP endpoint at `/mcp` over Streamable HTTP. It speaks the current revision (2026-07-28) and accepts 2025-11-25 clients through the twelve-month deprecation window. It implements `server / discover`, tools, resources and prompts. Lists are deterministic and carry `ttlMs` and `cacheScope: "private"`. Roots, Sampling and Logging are not served.

**Acceptance.**
1. `server / discover` returns the supported versions, capabilities, `serverInfo` and instructions.
2. A 2026-07-28 request works with no handshake, and a 2025-11-25 client completes `initialize` and lists the same tools.
3. An unsupported version returns `UnsupportedProtocolVersion`.
4. Two `tools / list` calls return the same order, with cache fields.
5. A foreign Origin returns 403, and a header and body method mismatch returns `HeaderMismatch`.
6. An oversized body returns 413 with no effect.

#### BASE-AGENT-002 — The seed's jobs are tools, through the UI's own actions

*Tier:* Agent surface

**Requirement.** Each Core job a person does in the product is a tool. Where one is not, the Agent surface says why: it runs on a device, it is a person's interactive screen, it belongs to a connector or the import door, or it is an installation fact. Risk is never the reason: a risky job is a tool with its class (BASE-AGENT-006). Tools are named `<seed>.<area>.<verb>` and declare input and output schemas and truthful annotations. Each calls the same server action as the UI, so validation and authorization are written once, and the seed's embedded agents use the same registry. A business refusal returns `isError` with the seed's stable error code.

**Acceptance.**
1. The Core clause ids in each tool's `_meta`, with the not-a-tool reasons that `server / discover` serves, cover every Core clause in the contract, and no reason is risk; the harness and `rer check` fail on a gap.
2. Each tool's fixture result validates against its `outputSchema`.
3. Read tools declare `readOnlyHint`; tools that can carry destructive declare `destructiveHint`, and tools that can carry external declare `openWorldHint`.
4. A refusal returns the same error code the UI gets for the same action.
5. The UI action and its tool, on the same fixture, give the same record state and the same audit event type.
6. The seed's embedded agents appear in the audit as calls to the same tools.

#### BASE-AGENT-003 — Records are resources

*Tier:* Agent surface

**Requirement.** Each primary record type has a URI template, and tools return `resource_link`s to the records they touch. A read returns exactly the fields the caller's role sees in the UI. File bytes count against any byte budget on the grant. A record the caller cannot open reads as not found, identical to a missing id. Text from customers, imports or files carries an untrusted marker in `_meta`.

**Acceptance.**
1. `resources / templates / list` names every record type in the Agent surface.
2. Reads as two roles return exactly what the UI shows each.
3. An out-of-scope id and a missing id give identical responses.
4. A write's `resource_link` reads back the new state.
5. Bytes over budget return `budget_exhausted` and no partial content.
6. Customer-sourced text carries the untrusted marker.

#### BASE-AGENT-004 — Business identity and short-lived, audience-bound tokens

*Tier:* Agent surface

**Requirement.** The door is an OAuth 2.1 resource server. Its RFC 9728 metadata names the authorization servers this installation trusts. That is the paired Business when Business provisioned it, verified with the owner-claim trust the installation already holds for its import door; otherwise it is the seed's own sign-in. Access tokens are RFC 9068 JWTs with `aud` set to the seed's canonical MCP URI, `sub` the sponsoring person, `act` the agent (RFC 8693) with its specialist, scopes per tool family, and a lifetime of 15 minutes or less (5 by default). The policy scopes rules on the sponsor, agent and specialist the token names. The consent behind the tokens can last longer and is revocable. Tokens travel only in the Authorization header, and there is no passthrough.

**Acceptance.**
1. An unauthenticated call returns 401 with `resource_metadata`, and the metadata names the trusted servers and scopes.
2. A Business token for this seed works, and the same token sent to a sibling seed returns 401.
3. An expired token returns 401, and a token with a lifetime over 15 minutes is refused.
4. A read-only token calling a write tool returns 403 `insufficient_scope` with every needed scope in one challenge.
5. A token in a query string is refused and not logged.
6. Revoking consent in the seed or in Business refuses the next call within 60 seconds.
7. After unpairing, Business tokens are refused and the seed's own sign-in still works.

#### BASE-AGENT-005 — An agent acts as a person in a role, never more

*Tier:* Agent surface

**Requirement.** Every call is authorized as the sponsoring person's current role and access (BASE-ACCESS-004), intersected with the grant's resources, actions and budget. A grant only narrows. No call widens the calling agent's own authority. A call that would widen its own grant or its sponsor's role, or change the company policy or Pause, is refused with `self_escalation`, whatever the policy says; narrowing its own grant is allowed. Other access and security changes are ordinary actions in the access and security classes. An agent never acts after its sponsor is suspended. Anything an agent reads (records, files, emails, imports, other seeds' results) is data and cannot change its scope, its targets or a call's class.

**Acceptance.**
1. For each role fixture, every tool's allow or deny through MCP equals the UI's for the same action.
2. A one-folder, read-only grant holds, and widening through arguments is refused.
3. Downgrading the sponsor changes the next call's result, and suspending the sponsor returns 401.
4. Calls that widen the agent's own grant or its sponsor's role, or change the policy or Pause, return `self_escalation` and change nothing, even under a policy with every class autonomous; dropping a scope from its own grant runs.
5. An injection fixture yields no out-of-grant call and no change of class: record text asking for a wider action, or claiming that a recipient is internal.

#### BASE-AGENT-006 — Every action declares its risk class

*Tier:* Agent surface

**Requirement.** Classes come from the fleet list in RISK-POLICY.md: standard, external, money, commitment, accounts, gated, access, security, destructive, sensitive and live. In the registry, each tool declares the classes it can carry and a server-side classifier that decides them per call from the arguments, current records and, for gated, the provider's answer. The classifier also supplies each class's facts: the measure (items, recipients, amount and currency, people or records), the counterparty (internal, known, new or public), the direction for access, the provider and step for gated, and the data kind for sensitive. A classifier never reads a flag, label or claim supplied by the agent or by record text. A seed cannot add a class; it proposes one for the fleet list.

**Acceptance.**
1. Every tool in `tools / list` carries its possible classes in `_meta`, equal to the Agent surface table.
2. For each tool, fixture calls cover every class it can carry, and the computed classes and facts equal the fixture's expected values.
3. An argument or record text asserting a class or a confirmation (`internal: true`, `confirmExternal: true`) leaves the computed classes unchanged.
4. Money calls carry amount and currency, external calls their counterparty and recipient count, access calls their direction, and destructive calls their item count.
5. No tool in `tools / list` declares a class outside the fleet list, and `rer check` fails on one.
6. A refused call's audit row still records its computed classes.

#### BASE-AGENT-007 — The company's policy decides, at one chokepoint

*Tier:* Agent surface

**Requirement.** Every agent door calls one decision function: MCP, the integration API with agent tokens, and the seed's embedded agents. It evaluates the call's classes against the company's policy, as above. The seed ships no dispositions and fills no gap with one: agent access opens only under a complete policy that setup has asked for (RISK-POLICY.md), and before then every agent call returns `policy_unset` with the setup link and changes nothing. *Autonomous* runs the call. *Review* runs it and adds it to the review feed. *Approval* saves a pending action with server-computed facts and returns `input_required`, with a URL-mode elicitation to the seed's approval page and a pending handle. Each person the rule names approves the exact saved revision in a signed-in browser, and changed inputs need a new approval. The retried call returns the result and a receipt. A rejection returns `approval_rejected`, and a lapse past the wait the rule sets returns `approval_expired`. *Blocked* returns `policy_blocked`, naming the class, rule and revision.

**Acceptance.**
1. The Base harness runs each tool under each disposition for every class it can carry, and sees it run, run and enter the review feed, wait with no effect, or be refused.
2. Before setup is complete, the setup page lists every class the seed's tools carry with examples and no answer pre-selected, an agent call returns `policy_unset` with the setup link and changes nothing, and an incomplete revision cannot be confirmed; a `*` rule completes it, and a tool an upgrade adds with an unanswered class appears in `tools / list` once that class is answered, while the other tools keep running.
3. Under "money autonomous up to $500, approval up to $10,000, blocked above", calls of $400, $600 and $20,000 run, wait and are refused; a per-day cap sends the call that crosses it to the next rule.
4. A call carrying two classes takes the stricter disposition.
5. An approval shows server-computed facts and an expiry, returns the URL elicitation and a handle, and completes once after the named approver approves; a changed input needs a new approval, and a rejection or lapse leaves no effect.
6. The same call through MCP, the integration API and an embedded agent gets the same decision.
7. A policy change applies to the next call within 60 seconds, and the audit cites the new revision.
8. A policy document with a bad signature or another Business's id is rejected, and the door keeps the last valid revision.

#### BASE-AGENT-008 — Truthful attribution

*Tier:* Agent surface

**Requirement.** Every agent act is recorded and shown as `"<agent> for <person>"`, and mail and messages an agent sends outside name it that way as their sender. An approval, a review mark, a confirmation (a warning dialog, a typed-field confirmation, a delivery confirmation), a decision or a signature attributed to a person comes only from that person's signed-in session. When an agent does the equivalent act, the record names the agent, and the act carries its own class; a binding decision or a signature is commitment. Agent doors ignore arguments that stand for a person's confirmation. No tool solves a bot check, or enters a person's own password or 2FA code at an outside service. A provider step that demands a person goes to a person, whatever the policy says; the gated class marks such steps before they run.

**Acceptance.**
1. An agent call carrying a person-confirmation flag is classified and decided exactly as without it.
2. Approving, marking reviewed or answering a policy question with an agent or device token returns 403 and changes nothing.
3. A form-mode elicitation "accept" never completes an approval.
4. Where an agent's decision, signature or field confirmation runs without a person, it reads `"<agent> for <person>"` in the record, the activity view, exports and any certificate, never as the person's own act.
5. After a person approves an agent's prepared action, the record shows the person as approver and the agent as preparer.
6. Activity and exports at 1440 and 390 show `"<agent> for <person>"` for every agent act.
7. Mail an agent sends to an outside address names `"<agent> for <person>"` as its sender.

#### BASE-AGENT-009 — Every agent action is audited with its class and decision

*Tier:* Agent surface

**Requirement.** Extending BASE-OPS-005, each call that reads private data or changes anything records the agent client, name and specialist, and the run or task id (`traceparent` when sent); the sponsoring person, the grant, the tool and the targets; the classes and their facts, and the policy revision and rule; the decision (autonomous, review, approval, blocked, unset or self_escalation) and the outcome (done, refused, pending or failed); the approval or review id and person, and the idempotency key. For a period, the seed's Agents page shows actions by class and decision with the notable ones, the review feed (Mark reviewed, Flag, and Undo where reversible), pending approvals, steps waiting for a person and setup questions. Business shows the same across seeds.

**Acceptance.**
1. One write leaves a complete audit row.
2. Refused, pending, unset and self-escalation calls are audited.
3. The Agents page's counts by class and decision equal the audit rows on a fixture week.
4. The review feed lists exactly the calls decided as review; Mark reviewed records the person, and Undo restores a reversible one.
5. Filtering by agent or class lists only those rows, and export includes every field.
6. Removing the agent keeps its rows and its name.
7. The Agents page works at 1440 and 390 with no serious or critical axe findings.

#### BASE-AGENT-010 — Agents can follow changes

*Tier:* Agent surface

**Requirement.** The seed emits a typed event for every record change and for every approval, review and policy decision. Each event carries a stable id, a type, the record URI, the actor (a person, or an agent acting for a person) and a time. Events never carry secrets or more than the subscriber may read. Agents can read events three ways: `subscriptions / listen`, an `events.list` tool with a cursor, and signed webhooks from Base `integrations` using the same ids. Every channel delivers at least once and filters by access at delivery.

**Acceptance.**
1. A subscribed record changed in the UI produces a notification within 10 seconds.
2. `events.list` returns the same event id the webhook carries.
3. Replaying from a cursor returns the same ids in order.
4. After access is revoked, no channel delivers events about that record.
5. A failed webhook is visible and replays without duplicate effects.
6. `approval.pending`, `approval.decided`, `review.flagged` and `policy.adopted` carry the class and decision and nothing the subscriber may not read.

#### BASE-AGENT-011 — Limits are policy, and Pause stops everything

*Tier:* Agent surface

**Requirement.** Business limits are rules in the company's policy: per-call and per-day thresholds on any class's measure, such as money moved, outside recipients or items destroyed; spend caps on provider cost (models, SMS, email) per seed, specialist or agent, which setup asks with the classes; "no cap" is an answer. Tools with provider cost declare an estimate before they run, and an exhausted cap returns `budget_exhausted` before any partial effect. The seed's capacity limits (request rate, body and byte sizes) protect the installation: they bound rate and size, never daily business volume, are documented and are not policy. A grant carries budgets only when the person granting it sets them. A **Pause agents** control in the seed, and Pause all agents in Business when paired, refuses every agent token within 60 seconds until a person resumes; browser sessions and devices keep working.

**Acceptance.**
1. A rate overrun returns 429 with `Retry-After`.
2. A per-day cap of three outside recipients sends the fourth to the rule that applies past the cap.
3. An exhausted spend cap returns `budget_exhausted` with no partial effect and shows the spend.
4. Under the answer "no cap", a spending call runs and its spend shows in usage; a call that spends nothing is unaffected by any cap.
5. The usage view shows calls, decisions by class, money moved and provider spend per agent.
6. Pause and Pause all agents each stop the next call within 60 seconds, and resume restores access.
7. An agent token cannot resume.

#### BASE-AGENT-012 — Writes are idempotent and conflict-safe

*Tier:* Agent surface

**Requirement.** Every mutating tool requires an idempotency key and takes an optional expected revision. The same key with the same arguments returns the first outcome for at least 24 hours; the same key with different arguments returns `idempotency_conflict`; a stale revision returns `revision_conflict` with the current revision. Long work returns a job handle and a status tool, with no dependence on the Tasks extension.

**Acceptance.**
1. Two calls with one key give one effect and equal results.
2. A retry with a new JSON-RPC id and the same key, after a dropped stream, returns the recorded outcome.
3. The same key with different arguments returns a conflict and no effect.
4. A stale revision returns a conflict naming the current revision.
5. A job handle used by another person's token reads as not found.

#### BASE-AGENT-013 — Manifest, docs and the conformance journey

*Tier:* Agent surface

**Requirement.** `server / discover` instructions and an on-site `/docs/agents` page are generated from the action registry. The page lists tools by job, with each tool's classes, the test that adds each computed class, its scopes, resource templates, event types, capacity limits and error codes, and the specialist role. `prompts / list` carries the specialist's jobs. Base ships the conformance journey, a harness that `rer verify` runs against `rer dev` and seeds run in CI. It is an MCP client; a signed-in test person takes a person's steps (setup answers, approvals, review marks, resume) through the URLs the door returns, and the same browser leg runs the UI-parity actions and the page checks at 1440 and 390. It runs every acceptance point of BASE-AGENT-001 to 012 and of the seed's SURFACE clauses under two company policies: *all autonomous* (`*`), and *held* (standard review, every other class the seed declares approval, which the test person grants), plus the single-class variants a point names. A point that names no disposition passes under both.

**Acceptance.**
1. The docs list exactly the names in `tools / list` and `resources / templates / list`.
2. Each tool's classes, and the test behind each computed one, are documented.
3. The harness fails on any of: a tool without a schema; an effect under approval or blocked, or before setup is complete; a computed class that differs from its fixture; a flag that changes a class or completes a person's step; a role-parity mismatch; a wrong-audience token being accepted; a duplicate effect on retry.
4. Every acceptance point runs under both policies, every decision matches the policy in force, and under all autonomous no call waits for a person or is refused by policy.
5. A stranger agent given only the seed URL completes the specialist journey through MCP.

before1.text: # Blotter Blotter is practice management for a small bookkeeping and accounting firm: recurring client jobs with their due dates, document requests that clients answer through a private upload link, reviewer sign-off, staff capacity, and time exported for your own billing. It runs in your own Cloudflare account. 100% free and open source, MIT licensed. Blotter's contract is the practice manager a US firm moves to from Karbon, TaxDome or Canopy: US firm setup in USD, calculated federal and state deadlines, IRS e-file signatures, invoices and payments. [CONTRACT.md](CONTRACT.md) and the run site's [/contract](https://run-blotter.com/contract) page show what the code does today and what is next. Today's release records new amounts in US dollars (records from the first release keep their Australian dollars), takes due dates entered by people with their source, and does not file returns, calculate tax, keep client books or give advice. ## Run Blotter You need macOS, Linux or Windows with WSL2, and Git. These are the two steps on [run-blotter.com/run](https://run-blotter.com/run). Install rer (it brings its own Node if you have none; if the installer ends with a line to run, run it): ```sh curl -fsSL https://runeditrun.com/install.sh | sh ``` Then start Blotter: ```sh rer dev just-every/run-blotter ``` Already have Node 22 or later? `npx -y @runeditrun/rer dev just-every/run-blotter` does both steps in one line. To start it again later, run `cd run-blotter && rer dev`. `rer dev` installs the locked dependencies, selects pinned Node 22.20.0 and pnpm 10.12.4, prepares a local D1 database and starts the app on a free port. The first launch takes several minutes; if it is interrupted, run it again. It prints `RER_READY` with the address and `RER_OPEN` with a sign-in link. Open the `RER_OPEN` link on this computer: you are signed in as the principal. Confirm **Finish setup**, then open the workspace at `/app`. The link is a local credential; keep it private. If `rer dev` says the server limit is reached, stop a server you no longer need with the command it prints, or start with `RER_SERVER_LIMIT=8 rer dev`. Stop Blotter with `rer dev --stop`. ### Try the other roles locally Local mail is suppressed, so team members sign in as local personas instead of by email. In **Team & safety**, save `reviewer@dev.localhost` as a reviewer and `preparer@dev.localhost` as a preparer. Then stop the app and restart as one of them: ```sh rer dev --stop rer dev --as reviewer # or: rer dev --as preparer ``` Open the new `RER_OPEN` link. `rer dev` with no `--as` returns to the principal. The run site is live at [https://run-blotter.com](https://run-blotter.com), and its run page is [https://run-blotter.com/run](https://run-blotter.com/run). The local run entrypoint is `/run` in the static site built by `rer build --site`. The [documentation](docs/README.md) is maintained as repository Markdown and ships as `/docs` and its guide pages in that same static build. ## Do the first jobs 1. **Team & safety:** set your own hourly rate (in cents, before tax; `15000` is $150.00), add a reviewer and a preparer, and set their rates. On a deployed installation, **Send an invitation** emails them a sign-in link. 2. **Clients & templates:** add a client with a contact email, and save the prefilled **Quarterly sales-tax return** template (checklist, document requests, fixed fee). Under **Start a job**, choose the client, template, period start (for example `2026-07-01`), the due date you have checked, where it comes from, the preparer and the reviewer. 3. **Jobs → open the job → Client documents:** **Send a reminder with an upload link.** Blotter mails the client the link (on a deployed installation) and shows it to you once. Open the link in a private window: that is the client's view. Upload a file for each request, then back in the job **Accept** each one or **Ask again**. For larger packets, staff use **Document packets → Add a packet or corrected version**: up to 20 MiB and 2,000 declared pages, with confirmed-byte progress, pause/resume for seven days, immutable prior versions, internal page notes and review. Select the exact original to resume. Client details also expose searchable document folders by client/period. New packets start internal; corrections retain preceding contact grants and create no share links. 4. **Checklist:** tick every step and **Submit for review**. As the assigned reviewer (or the principal, for someone else's work), choose **Sign off** with a note. Signing off closes the upload link. 5. **Roll forward:** on the signed-off job, record the next period's due date under **Roll forward to the next period**. Blotter creates the next period's job with the same client, template and people. It refuses a second copy. 6. **Time & billing:** record time on a job (**Time** section; it uses your current rate). In **Time & billing**, choose items, **Prepare export**, then as the principal **Approve** it with a note and **Download CSV**. An approved export cannot change; each time entry or fixed fee can be exported once. 7. **Preparations:** create an agent key in **Team & safety** and give it to your agent with [API.md](API.md). Its roll-forwards, reminders and exports wait here until you **Approve** or **Decline**; decisions are recorded. 8. **Move in:** load [the documented fixture](fixtures/client-list.csv) or your own list, map source columns, **Preview (dry run)**, review any duplicate choices and preview again, then **Import these clients**. **View journal** shows the original file and progress; **Undo import** removes the untouched imported clients/contacts while keeping native work and edited records. Native matches add source provenance without changing permissions. See [IMPORTING.md](IMPORTING.md) for the CSV shape. 9. **Team & safety:** **Download practice archive**, and **Erase a client file** by typing its name and a reason. The exact first-release scope is in [ACCEPTANCE.md](ACCEPTANCE.md). ## Backup and restore The archive holds clients, templates, jobs, document requests and files, time, exports, imports and the audit log. Sign-in accounts, sessions, agent keys and client upload links are not included: create new keys and send new reminders after a move. Restore only into an empty installation, from **Team & safety** or the command line: ```sh rer export --output exports/practice.rer # In a new, empty checkout: copy the archive into its exports/ folder first; # --input must be a path inside the checkout. rer import --input exports/practice.rer --yes rer dev ``` The restored checkout gets a new local owner; your practice data, exports and history come back unchanged. After erasing a file, make a new archive and retire older ones. An older archive is refused unless you also supply the newer archive that carries the erasure journal (`--journal exports/newer.rer`, or the second file field in **Restore**). `rer reset --yes` deletes local data; export first. ## Deploy your installation You need a Cloudflare account with Workers and D1, a sending address verified with Resend, and a Resend API key for email sign-in and reminders. Never put credentials in Git, commands, screenshots or chat. 1. Stop local serving (`rer dev --stop`) and commit your changes. In `deploy.json`, set `MAIL_FROM` to your verified sending address. Keep the project, package, Worker and D1 names unchanged, and keep `AUTH_LOCAL` `false`. 2. In your shell's private environment, supply `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` and `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`, and `OWNER_EMAIL`, `SESSION_SECRET`, `SETUP_TOKEN` and `MAIL_API_KEY`, plus `VAULT_KEY` to use the client credential vault. Generate the session, setup and vault values as independent random strings of at least 32 characters, with your secret manager; keep `VAULT_KEY` with your backups, since archived credentials open only under the same key. 3. Run `rer deploy --dry-run` to build and check the plan without provider calls (it already needs the variables from step 2), then `rer deploy`. It creates or reuses the D1 database, applies the migrations, deploys the Worker and its assets, checks health and prints the URL. 4. Open the printed address's `/signin`, request a link for the owner email and follow it. Confirm **Finish setup**, then open `/app`. [RUN-LOCALLY.md](RUN-LOCALLY.md) and [SEED-COMMAND-CONTRACT.md](SEED-COMMAND-CONTRACT.md) describe every `rer` command. [OPERATIONS.md](OPERATIONS.md) covers running it. ## Develop `rer verify` builds the Worker, typechecks, runs the integration flows in `tests/` against the built Worker (only the mail provider is faked) and checks the hosted output. [SOURCES.md](SOURCES.md) records where the code came from.

# Blotter product contract

Target edition: 17 October 2026. Blotter is the practice manager a US bookkeeping or accounting firm uses to complete client engagements from signed scope through recurring work, communications, document collection, review and payment. It replaces Karbon, TaxDome or Canopy and offers the connected close and small-firm automation depth buyers seek from Financial Cents and Double. USD and US practice norms are the default. Difficulty building provider applications, bank/payment connections, desktop bridges or native apps is work to deliver, not a smaller product boundary.

This is the product destination. Status below describes current code, not a reduction of that destination. The previous first-release ACCEPTANCE.md described an Australian BAS-style workflow with manual deadlines, link uploads, independent review and billing CSVs; there was no root CONTRACT.md or existing product clause ID to rename. Its useful guarantees are retained here. The Status table classifies each clause as published, target or push-further, including implemented foundations. Existing UI, homepage and runtime behavior are unchanged by this document.

## Product target

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Category | Accounting practice management software |
| Incumbents a buyer switches from | Karbon, TaxDome, Canopy, Financial Cents, Double |
| First buyer | A US principal or operations manager of a bookkeeping or accounting firm with 1–15 staff, running recurring client engagements and tax-season work |

## How acceptance is judged

Every named clause gives buyer behavior and an acceptance journey through the app, authenticated HTTP API, CLI or authorized provider door. ACCEPTANCE.md lists the same journeys and statuses. A cited local file/test proves only its stated implemented subset; it does not prove real-provider acceptance, tax authority access, native distribution, production capacity or accessibility. Real-provider journeys use authorized accounts; automated tests fake only paid/network edges. Source freshness, provider acknowledgment, settlement and human judgment are distinct facts.

Current statuses describe this candidate tree. The exact commit and its verification runs are reported in the branch handoff; a status claim is counted only after the guarded landing and CT judgment. Due dates are recorded by people, set by WORK-002 rules or calculated from approved deadline rules (DUE-001, DUE-003).

## Target clauses

### US practice and client engagements

- **US-001 — US firm setup and currency.** A US principal configures a firm in USD with US addresses, EIN/entity classifications, fiscal years, service lines, time zones and notification hours. Money uses integer cents and explicit currency; US 1099/W-2, federal/state tax and sales-tax engagements have appropriate terminology. Historical AUD records retain their currency and are never relabeled USD. **Acceptance evidence:** Set up a US bookkeeping and tax practice, add an LLC and individual client, select USD and America/New_York, and create payroll, sales-tax and annual-tax work. Inspect currency and dates across a daylight-saving change; imported AUD history remains AUD. **Implemented currency and identifiers (US-001):** New templates, rates and native prospects default to USD; each stored fee, time entry and expense carries its currency. Existing money rows and historical export snapshots remain AUD, with no conversion or relabeling. Jobs inherit their template currency, time requires a rate in that currency, mixed-currency exports are refused, and WIP, reimbursement and pipeline fee totals are grouped by currency. New client EINs accept nine digits; eleven-digit ABNs remain legacy ABNs. Native and CSV inputs retain that distinction, and search keeps SEARCH-001 role restrictions and last-four masking. The demo uses US filings and America/New_York office instants, using each date’s daylight-saving offset. **Firm settings (US-001):** the principal records the firm name, US street/city/state/ZIP address, nine-digit EIN, entity classification, fiscal year-end month/day, service lines, default USD or AUD currency, IANA time zone and staff email notification hours. New templates, hourly rates and native prospects use the firm default unless explicitly overridden; historical money and exports never change. Workspace activity instants and today use the firm zone with its date-specific daylight-saving offset; date-only deadlines keep their recorded day. A recorded filing calendar holds a name, jurisdiction, date and required source or firm-defined label: these are human-entered dates, not automatic agency calculations (DUE-001/003). Notification start is inclusive and end exclusive in the firm zone; an earlier end spans midnight and equal times allow all day. In-app alerts appear immediately; staff emails outside the window remain durably deferred until the hourly trigger runs inside it. Completed attempts are not resent, and inactive recipients are not mailed. Client sends and sign-in mail keep their current behavior. Settings and calendars survive practice archive restore. Future notification channels (NOTIFY-001), connected-mail schedules (MAIL-003), automation (AUTOMATE-001), and deadline calculations (DUE-001/003) inherit the firm zone and applicable notification hours before shipping; CRM-001 carries client entity/contact structure and phone/SSN-digit matching for CRM-004 and SEARCH-001. **Inherited MSG-002 marketing consent (ct 20 Oct 21:21Z):** The firm's US postal address appears on every marketing email, and a marketing send without it is refused.

- **CRM-001 — Client entities and contacts.** Manage individuals, businesses and trusts with multiple contacts, authorized signers, portal users, responsible partner, assigned team, service scope, lifecycle and consent preferences. Contacts carry roles (primary, billing, tax, bookkeeping) that route invoices, requests and signatures. A contact may represent several entities without sharing their private records; duplicates are merged under CRM-004. Search, edit, archive and reactivate clients without losing engagement history. **Acceptance evidence:** Create a business with two contacts and an individual linked to its owner; assign different staff and portal permissions, change a contact, archive/reactivate the business and inspect retained jobs. A contact without entity authority cannot read its records. **Inherited CRM-005:** CRM-005 prospect contacts, including every additional authorized contact, move to the one converted client before this ships. **Implemented semantics (ct 19 Oct 12:58Z):** an entity is an individual, business or trust; its responsible partner is an active reviewer or principal, its assigned team lists active staff, and services and a related owner/household client are recorded without granting job access. Each contact relationship belongs to one entity; the same normalized email may represent several entities without pooling authority. Staff explicitly record primary/billing/tax/bookkeeping roles, signer authority, portal permission and request/email consent, with a note. Existing single contacts retain only their existing entity's collection authority.
