### Work deadlines and team delivery

- **WORK-001 — Reusable engagement templates.** A principal or reviewer creates reusable monthly, quarterly or annual templates containing a checklist, document request list and fixed fee. Starting an engagement copies the template into its own period work so staff have concrete tasks and requests. Work types and statuses are WORK-007; task-level owners and dates are WORK-009; the maintained US starter library is WORK-008. **Acceptance evidence:** Through the app or authenticated HTTP doors, create a recurring template, start a client job and inspect copied checklist, requests, recurrence, fee, preparer and reviewer. A preparer cannot create templates.

- **WORK-002 — Automatic recurring work and roll forward.** Approved recurrence rules create the next period automatically with assigned staff, fresh requests, dependencies, budget and calculated due dates. Support monthly closes, quarterly payroll/sales tax, annual returns and custom schedules, including fiscal-year ends. Each rule has a creation lead time (how far ahead of a period's start its work is created, set by the firm, for example three months as in Karbon) and an end date. A rule may already hold future periods, whether it generated them or a migration imported and claimed them (MIGRATE-006); a period the rule already holds is never generated again, and the next generated period follows the last held one without a gap. Preview the schedule, pause/skip a period and catch up after downtime without duplicate client-period engagements; historical sign-offs remain immutable. **Acceptance evidence:** Enable monthly and fiscal-year recurrence with a three-month lead time, let scheduled work become due and inspect exactly the periods inside the lead time, each once, with fresh requests. Attach two existing future jobs to a monthly rule and advance the horizon; the rule creates only the following period. Restart the scheduler, pause a client, skip a period and override a due date; no duplicate or silently altered prior job appears. **Semantics (WORK-002):** a principal or reviewer approves one rule per client and template; approving it is the approval. Periods start on the first period's day in the chosen months, which are the template's own monthly, quarterly or annual cadence or a subset of it (custom schedules); a fiscal year is an annual first period in its first month. The end date is the last period's start, inclusive. The lead time is whole months: a period's job is created once the run's UTC calendar date reaches its start less the lead time. Its due date is the period's last day plus the rule's calendar days (a firm rule), or, when the rule names a client obligation, that obligation's calculated working due date for the period (DUE-001, DUE-003), shown in the rule's preview and stored with each job it creates. Budget is the rule's time budget in minutes, copied to each job; staff, fresh document requests and the template's task dependencies (WORK-003) come with each job. The scheduler is an hourly Cron Trigger (minute 17, UTC; `rer dev` runs it; deploys register it) plus Run now; each run creates, in order, every period through the horizon not yet held (generated, claimed or skipped), so restarts repeat nothing and runs after downtime or a pause catch up. A job that already exists for the client, template and period is claimed instead of duplicated; staff may also claim one, and imported future items (MIGRATE-006) must be claimed the same way before that clause ships. Skipping needs a reason. A rule whose people can no longer do the work is held and named in the run log, never reassigned. Created jobs are never changed by a rule: a person overrides a due date on the job, and sign-offs stay immutable.

- **WORK-003 — Dependencies and conditional workflow.** Templates define task dependencies, conditional branches, required evidence and preparer/reviewer gates across jobs. Completion events advance only eligible steps, with visible reasons for blocked work; a dependency cycle is rejected and an authorized exception requires a recorded reason. **Acceptance evidence:** Create a close feeding a tax engagement, branch on an organizer answer and complete prerequisite tasks. Inspect automatic advancement and blocked successors; reject a cycle and record an authorized exception without fabricating evidence. **Semantics (WORK-003):** a template task may wait for other tasks of its job, for accepted client documents (its required evidence) and for the same client's prerequisite job from a named template, submitted for review (preparer gate) or signed off (reviewer gate); that prerequisite is the job whose period contains this job's last period day. A task may apply only when a job question has one of the chosen answers: unanswered, it waits; answered otherwise, it does not apply, is not needed for review, and counts as satisfied for tasks waiting on it. Job staff can record workflow questions directly; confirmed PORTAL-004 submissions write their validated bound choices to those same questions, with contact attribution. Drafts and unconfirmed carried values never choose a workflow branch; future answer sources inherit those rules before shipping. Completion events (task done or reopened, document accepted, answer, job submitted, returned or signed off, exception) stamp each gated task that became ready and alert its owner, and clear the stamp when it is blocked again. A cycle among a template's tasks is refused when it is saved; templates are saved as new versions that may wait only on templates that already exist, so cross-job waits cannot form a cycle. The job's reviewer, its manager or the principal may record an exception with a required reason: the task can then be worked, but nothing it waited for is completed, its own required attachment is still required, review still needs every applicable task done and every document accepted, and an unanswered branch question is never waived.

- **WORK-004 — Bulk work scheduling and assignment.** Preview and create or reschedule work for a selected client segment in bulk, resolving preparer/reviewer roles, staff eligibility and client-specific exceptions. Changes show impacted jobs and conflicts before approval and preserve existing work and independent review. Until CRM-002 client groups exist, the bulk segment is the clients selected in the batch, with include/exclude per client; once CRM-002 lands, choosing a group pre-selects its clients. Bulk start refuses any self-review assignment, including a principal as both preparer and reviewer. A solo principal starts such a job one at a time, where REVIEW-001’s acknowledged self-review applies. **Acceptance evidence:** Preview quarterly jobs for the clients selected in a batch using per-client include/exclude; once CRM-002 client groups exist, verify choosing a group pre-selects its clients. Override two assignees, exclude one client and commit. Re-submit the same batch and inspect no duplicates, then bulk reassign work while refusing inactive or self-review assignments. Verify bulk start refuses every self-review assignment, including a principal assigned as both preparer and reviewer; verify a solo principal can instead start such a job one at a time with REVIEW-001’s acknowledged self-review.

- **WORK-005 — Firm work queues.** Staff see a due-date-ordered work queue with client, period, preparer, reviewer, status and outstanding checklist/document counts. Preparers see their assigned jobs; principals and reviewers see firm work and can open its detail. **Acceptance evidence:** Create two jobs for different preparers, open the work queue as each role and inspect dates, assignees, status and outstanding counts. Directly requesting another preparer's hidden job is refused.

- **WORK-006 — Personal plans boards and calendars.** Provide a weekly personal action plan of the person's jobs and tasks (WORK-009), Kanban boards and firm/client calendars filtered by work type, primary status, sub-status, assignee, due date, blocked status and priority. Board columns are the firm's primary statuses, or the selected work type's sub-statuses (WORK-007). Moving a card sets that status on the underlying job, respects workflow and review gates and fires status automations; calendar changes show deadline and capacity consequences. **Acceptance evidence:** Plan a preparer's week from the overdue queue, group a 1040 board by sub-status, move an eligible card and inspect the same job's new status in queue, calendar and client views. A blocked review transition is refused and filters persist after refresh. **Status model (WORK-007, inherited before this ships):** moving a card or planning a job uses WORK-007's moves, sub-status limits and review gates and is recorded in its status history. **Acceptance evidence (WORK-007):** the moved card's change appears in the job's status history. **Semantics (WORK-006):** a person's plan is a Monday-to-Sunday week: the jobs (where they are preparer, reviewer, manager or partner) and their own open tasks they place on its days, each job shown with its status, flags and WORK-007 move control, plus WORK-009's open tasks due in or before the week (or undated) and open jobs due in or before it to plan from; placing work never changes its status. Each person plans their own week; until an admin role exists the principal opens and plans anyone's (pattern 2). Boards, calendars and the queue share filters over the jobs a person may read: work type, stage, sub-status, client, assignee (the job's preparer, reviewer, manager or partner), due dates as an inclusive range, overdue (due before today in UTC and not completed), blocked (open with remaining tasks of which none is ready, each waiting on a WORK-003 dependency or answer, with those reasons shown) and priority (Low, Normal or High, Normal by default, set by the job's people until it is completed). A board has a column per stage, or for one chosen work type a column per stage and each sub-status that type may use (plus In review – partner sign-off when a job is in it); a card move is WORK-007's move, so In review and Completed are reached only by submission and sign-off. The firm calendar shows jobs and their open tasks on their due dates over at most 62 days; the client filter makes it one client's calendar. Moving a job's due date on the calendar is WORK-004's reschedule (principal or reviewer): its preview lists the task dates that follow it, anything that would fall due before today, and each person's estimated demand against available hours (CAPACITY-001) in every week the job's estimated work leaves or enters, and it commits only with that preview's fingerprint. Each person's last board filters (with the column grouping) and calendar filters are kept for them, so a refresh opens the same view. **Automations (AUTOMATE-001, inherited before it ships):** a board card or plan move is a WORK-007 status change recorded in the job's history, so AUTOMATE-001's status triggers fire on it as on any other move; WORK-006 is done for every capability that exists today.

- **WORK-007 — Firm work types and status model.** The firm defines work types such as Monthly Bookkeeping, 1040, 1120-S, Payroll Quarterly, Sales Tax, Advisory and internal firm work. Each type has a default template, job roles (for example Manager, Preparer, Reviewer and Partner sign-off), default budget hours, a color and its permitted statuses. Every work item carries exactly one work type and one status. The status is one of six fixed primary stages (Planned, Ready to start, In progress, Waiting, In review, Completed) plus optional firm-defined sub-statuses under each stage, for example "Waiting – on client documents" or "In progress – ready to file". The firm limits each sub-status to selected work types. Statuses drive Kanban columns and personal plans (WORK-006), queue filters and saved views, automation triggers and actions (AUTOMATE-001), client-facing progress labels (PORTAL-003) and status reports (REPORT-001), including counts and time in each status. Entering In review or Completed still requires the REVIEW-001 gates, and no sub-status can bypass them. Every status change records who made it, when, and the old and new status. Renaming a sub-status keeps history. Deleting a sub-status that jobs still use is refused until a previewed bulk reassignment moves those jobs to another permitted status. **Acceptance evidence:** Create a 1040 work type and two sub-statuses under Waiting: "on client documents" and "on 8879 signature". Limit the second to 1040 and confirm it is not offered on a Monthly Bookkeeping job. Move a 1040 job through both sub-statuses on the board. An automation fires once on entering "on 8879 signature". Filter the queue and a saved view by that sub-status, and read a time-in-status report. Moving a job to Completed without review is refused. Deleting a sub-status in use is refused until a previewed bulk reassignment moves its jobs; status history is retained. Import a Karbon work item under MIGRATE-001 and confirm it keeps its work type and status. **Capacity (CAPACITY-001, inherited before this ships):** the capacity view's service filter selects jobs by work type. **Acceptance evidence (CAPACITY-001):** filter the capacity week by the 1040 work type and see only 1040 demand. **Semantics (WORK-007):** until an admin role exists the principal defines work types (name unique ignoring case, optional default template, default budget in minutes applied when a job is started without one, #rrggbb color) and sub-statuses (one stage each, unique by name within it, limited to selected work types or open to every type). Saving a template also creates a work type of the template's name with it as default template; a job carries the work type chosen when it is started, otherwise its template's, and a rolled-forward job keeps its predecessor's. A new job starts Planned; jobs that existed before the status model start In progress, with history beginning at their current stage as of their submission, sign-off or creation. Planned, Ready to start, In progress and Waiting (and their sub-statuses) are set by the job's people while it is open; In review is reached only by submission (or a client's approval that submits, recorded as that approval) and Completed only by sign-off; a return goes to In progress; entering In review or Completed clears the sub-status, and the database refuses any sub-status outside the job's current stage. Each history entry records the old and new stage and sub-status, who and when (UTC); a rename shows the new name throughout history; a deleted sub-status keeps its name in history. Deleting a sub-status that jobs use requires a preview naming the jobs and their target stage (open stages only for an open-stage sub-status, the same stage otherwise) and commits only with that preview's fingerprint, moving the jobs and recording each move. The queue filters by work type, stage and sub-status over the jobs a person may read; time in status runs from each entry to the next (or now), in whole minutes rounded down, with entries, jobs now in it, total and average. Each person keeps private saved views of the queue (work type, stage, sub-status by name). A sub-status may carry a client label: the client link shows it while the job is in that sub-status, otherwise the stage's name (PORTAL-003). **Job roles (WORK-007):** a work type may also need a Manager and a Partner; a job of that type names them when it starts (jobs from recurring rules and bulk scheduling use the template's own type, which needs neither). The partner is an active reviewer or the principal and never the preparer (enforced on every reassignment, offboarding and handover); the reviewer's sign-off records the review and leaves the job In review – partner sign-off, and only the named partner or the principal completes or returns it; a return clears the recorded review. **Inherited before they ship:** AUTOMATE-001 status triggers and set-status actions, WORK-006 plans and boards, REPORT-001 status reports and the MIGRATE-001 Karbon import carry WORK-007's status model in their own text and acceptance; WORK-007 is done for every capability that exists today.

- **WORK-008 — Starter US template library.** Blotter maintains a versioned starter library of US templates that a firm can adopt and edit: monthly bookkeeping close, quarterly payroll (941, state withholding and unemployment), sales-tax filing, the 1040, 1120-S, 1065, 1120, 1041 and 990 returns, year-end 1099 and W-2, tax notice response, new-client onboarding and client offboarding. Each template carries a work type and statuses (WORK-007), tasks with relative dates and role assignments (WORK-009), request lists, an organizer (PORTAL-004), budget hours and message templates (MSG-001). Adopting a template copies that version into the firm. Library updates arrive as a previewed diff the firm accepts or ignores change by change, and they never overwrite firm edits or existing jobs. **Acceptance evidence:** In a new US firm, browse the library and adopt the 1040 and monthly close templates. Edit one task and start a job from each, then inspect the copied tasks, requests, relative dates, statuses and messages. Publish a library update, preview its diff, accept one change and reject another. The firm's edited task survives and existing jobs are unchanged. **Semantics (WORK-008):** the maintained native library contains monthly close; quarterly 941, state withholding and unemployment; sales-tax filing; 1040, 1120-S, 1065, 1120, 1041 and 990 returns; year-end 1099 and W-2; notice response; onboarding and offboarding. Each adoption makes a firm template, its own WORK-007 work type with all six stages, WORK-009 role tasks and relative dates, requests, an integer-minute default budget and MSG-001 message copies. Hours are minutes divided by 60, rounded to two decimals for display; planning offsets are whole days from the recorded period start or due date, not statutory calculations. The principal adopts a chosen version, edits tasks, requests and budget, and edits messages through MSG-001. A new job copies the then-current tasks, requests, budget and message text/version; later library changes never mutate those jobs. Authored releases are bundled with the app; a principal can import a reviewed newer release package with its source/change note and author recorded. Imported releases are immutable, never claim agency verification and never change adoptions automatically. An update preview compares the prior adopted release, current firm copy (including MSG-001 edits/deletions) and new release, one task, request, message, budget or description at a time. Each change is accepted or ignored; a conflicting firm edit must be retained, and stale previews are refused. Ignored changes remain firm choices and the reviewed release becomes the next comparison baseline. **PORTAL-004 integration:** every authored library workflow now carries a versioned organizer with conditions and supporting-request bindings; firm question edits and individual release choices follow the same three-way conflict rules, and existing job snapshots stay unchanged. Published packages can bind confirmed organizer choices to WORK-003 workflow questions; those bindings are validated before publication/adoption.

- **WORK-009 — Task assignees due dates and instructions.** Each task in a work item can have its own assignee (a named person or a job role), a start and due date relative to the work's start or due date, a time estimate, instructions with an SOP link, a required attachment and a client-facing flag (PORTAL-003). Completing a task records who completed it and when. Changing the person in a job role re-routes that role's open tasks, while completed tasks keep their completer. Personal plans (WORK-006) list the person's tasks as well as their jobs. Until WORK-007 adds firm job roles, a job's roles are Preparer, Reviewer and Manager, and the Manager is the job's reviewer unless someone is named when the job starts. The work's start date is its period start. Task start and due dates are whole days before or after the work's start or due date and are computed when read, so open tasks follow every change to the job's due date or people; completing a task records its completer and time and keeps the owner and dates it had then. A task may be assigned by name to any active practice member or the principal; that person can then read the job and act on their own tasks (ACCESS-001). A task that needs an attachment completes only with one. A client-facing task shows only its name, due date and done state on the client's link; PORTAL-003 inherits client-facing tasks before it ships. Until WORK-006 ships, a person's weekly plan for a Monday-to-Sunday week lists their open tasks due in or before that week or with no due date, and their open jobs as preparer, reviewer or manager due in or before it; WORK-006 inherits tasks before it ships. **Acceptance evidence:** Create a template with three tasks due 10, 5 and 2 days before the work's due date, assigned to Preparer, Manager and a named person. Start a job and inspect the computed task dates and owners. Move the work's due date and see the open task dates follow. Change the job's Preparer and confirm the open tasks move to the new person, while a completed task keeps its original completer and time. Open a task's SOP link, and see the tasks in the new owner's weekly plan.

- **DUE-001 — Sourced US obligations and extensions.** Provide maintained federal and firm-selected state deadline templates for 1040, 1120-S, 1065, 941 and sales tax, with entity/period/fiscal-year applicability, weekend/holiday rules, state/local frequency and jurisdiction-specific extensions or disaster relief. Import IRS and state revenue calendar updates with source URL, effective date and rule version. A firm approves applicable rules and material changes, sees recalculated due dates and can override with reason; original, extended and internal dates remain distinct. Extension work stays open until the tax authority supplies filing evidence. **Acceptance evidence:** Configure all five obligation types for clients in two states and different fiscal years. Calculate a weekend/holiday case, import a source revision and preview affected jobs before approval. Record an extension and override; verify separate original/extended/internal dates, preserved provenance and no claim of filing from a checklist. **Inherited BASE-001:** new capabilities, record kinds and doors retain native authority, revocation, audit and portability/erasure integrity; supply the named public-door activation evidence in BASE-001 before shipping. **Semantics (DUE-001):** Blotter ships a maintained catalog (release 2026.1, effective 1 January 2026) of sourced rules, each with its agency source URL, version and effective date: federal 1040 (15th day of the 4th month after the tax year; Form 4868 extension to the 15th day of the 10th), 1120-S and 1065 (15th day of the 3rd month; Form 7004 to the 15th day of the 9th), 941 (last day of the month after each calendar quarter) and state sales tax (California CDTFA quarterly: last day of the month after the quarter; Texas Comptroller monthly: the 20th of the month after). Blotter does not fetch agency sites: a person imports each IRS or state revision. Until an admin role exists the principal approves each catalog rule for the firm (approving a state's rule selects that state; pattern 2), and a principal or reviewer configures a client obligation: one approved rule with the client's two-letter state, fiscal-year-end month (calendar-year rules always December) and internal lead days (0–90); a rule applies only to its entity types (individual, business, trust) and a state rule only to its own state. A job started from an obligation, rolled forward from such a job, or created by a WORK-002 rule that names one takes its period from its template's cadence (starting on the first of a month; an annual period ends in the fiscal-year-end month, quarterly periods are the tax year's quarters) and keeps these dates apart: the statutory date; the original due date, which is the statutory date moved to the next business day past Saturdays, Sundays and federal legal holidays (5 U.S.C. 6103; a Saturday holiday is observed the Friday before, a Sunday one the Monday after) and, for federal rules, DC Emancipation Day (16 April, observed; 26 U.S.C. 7503), with the reason recorded; the extended due date (shifted the same way), which applies once a person on the job records the extension request, or at once for an automatic extension; a relief date from an approved disaster postponement whose jurisdiction, states, rules and inclusive window cover the original or extended date; the internal target (that external date less the obligation's lead days, moved earlier to a business day); and any override. The job's working due date is the override, else the relief, extended or original date; an override needs a principal or reviewer and a reason and never changes a calculated date. A source revision is a JSON document with version, effective date, https source and changed rules (keeping each rule's key and jurisdiction) or relief windows; only the principal previews and approves it. The preview lists every job not yet signed off whose dates or rule version change, and approval commits only with that preview's fingerprint, approving the revision's rules and recalculating those jobs; a job whose working date was set by hand (an override, or a WORK-004/WORK-006 move) keeps it while its calculated dates update. Filing is never inferred from a checklist, review, sign-off or status: only a recorded agency acknowledgment (submission ID, accepted date and an acknowledgment file on the job, labeled practitioner-recorded until INTEGRATE-008 supplies stack status) marks a return filed, and a job whose extension was recorded cannot be signed off until it exists (pattern 3). Agent keys cannot approve rules or revisions. Rules, revisions, relief, obligations and job dates are carried by native archives and move with a merged client (CRM-004); the acknowledgment file follows file erasure and stale-archive fencing.

- **DUE-002 — Tax notices and resolution work.** Capture a federal/state notice with its source file, agency, tax period, response date, assigned practitioner, authorization and resolution plan. Track research, client questions, agency contact, response submission and follow-up until an acknowledged resolution or documented exception; link transcripts and filing receipts without treating them as tax advice. A notice opens from a document already filed on a job, such as a client upload, and its response date is the one printed on the notice, recorded and then verified by a person; Blotter never computes it. Until AUTHZ-001 tracks Forms 2848 and 8821, the authorization is the reference staff record on the notice; until INTEGRATE-006 retrieves transcripts, a transcript is a file staff attach, and AUTHZ-001 and INTEGRATE-006 inherit these links before they ship. The timeline is append-only. A notice closes only as resolved, backed by an evidence file on an agency contact, transcript, receipt or accepted response and with no failed response after the last accepted one, or as a documented exception with its reason; the assigned practitioner, a reviewer or the principal closes it. **Acceptance evidence:** Open a notice from a client upload, verify the response deadline, assign a practitioner, link an authorized transcript and response receipt, and schedule follow-up. A failed response stays open; closing requires evidence and a recorded outcome.

- **DUE-003 — Wider US obligation catalog and firm defined deadlines.** Beyond DUE-001's five obligation types, Blotter maintains sourced deadline templates for Forms 1120, 1041, the 990 series, 940, W-2/W-3, 1099-NEC/1099-MISC, 1040-ES and 1120-W estimated payments, state withholding and unemployment returns, state annual reports and franchise taxes, and FinCEN 114 (FBAR) with its automatic extension. A firm can also define its own obligations: a fixed date, N days after period end, or the nth weekday of a month, each with a recorded source or a firm-defined label. The same approval, override, weekend/holiday and provenance rules as DUE-001 apply. **Acceptance evidence:** Configure 1040-ES quarterly estimates including a weekend shift, the January 31 W-2 and 1099-NEC deadlines, an FBAR with its automatic October extension, and a firm rule of 15 days after month end. Inspect the calculated dates and their sources. Import a source revision and preview the affected jobs before approving it. The firm rule shows as firm-defined rather than as an agency deadline. **Inherited BASE-001:** new capabilities, record kinds and doors retain native authority, revocation, audit and portability/erasure integrity; supply the named public-door activation evidence in BASE-001 before shipping. **Semantics (DUE-003):** the 2026.1 catalog adds 1120 (15th day of the 4th month; Form 7004 to the 15th day of the 10th; a fiscal year ending 30 June that starts before 1 January 2026 uses the 15th day of the 3rd month, extended to the 15th day of the 10th), 1041 (15th day of the 4th; Form 7004 to the last day of the 9th), the 990 series (15th day of the 5th; Form 8868 to the 15th day of the 11th), 940, W-2/W-3 and 1099-NEC (31 January after the calendar year), 1099-MISC filed electronically (31 March), 1040-ES (15 April, 15 June, 15 September and 15 January: the 15th day of the tax year's 4th, 6th, 9th and 13th months, one per quarter period) and 1120-W (15th day of the 4th, 6th, 9th and 12th months), FinCEN 114 (15 April with the automatic extension to 15 October, labeled automatic), state withholding and unemployment returns (California EDD DE 9 and Texas TWC C-3: last day of the month after the quarter), and state franchise taxes and annual reports (Texas franchise report 15 May, extension to 15 August on request; Delaware corporation annual report and franchise tax 1 March). Only the principal defines a firm rule (defining it approves it; pattern 2): a fixed month and day (the first such date after the period ends), a number of calendar days after the period ends, or the nth (1–5, or last) weekday of the month a chosen number of months after the period-end month. It carries an optional source or label (default "Firm-defined") and shows as a firm-defined deadline, never as an agency deadline, with no source URL; DUE-001's holiday shift (federal legal holidays, without DC Emancipation Day), obligation, override, revision and provenance rules apply to it unchanged.

- **RESOLVE-001 — Transcript analysis and resolution cases.** From authorized IRS account and wage-and-income transcripts (INTEGRATE-006), Blotter builds a per-year view for each client. It shows the assessed balance and the accrued penalties and interest as of the transcript date, each transaction code with a plain explanation, unfiled years, the collection statute expiration date (CSED) for each assessment, refund statute dates, and hold, lien or levy indicators. Each figure links to its transcript line. When a new pull changes a year, the change is flagged and routed to the assigned practitioner as notice or resolution work (DUE-002). Financial information for Forms 433-A and 433-F is collected through a PORTAL-004 organizer. Derived figures are labeled with their transcript date and are never presented as advice; the practitioner chooses the resolution path. **Acceptance evidence:** Load authorized account transcripts for four years, including one unfiled year. Inspect each year's balance, codes, CSED and unfiled flag against the source lines. Pull again with a new transaction code and see a change alert routed to the practitioner. Collect 433-A data through an organizer and inspect it on the case. No resolution recommendation is made without the practitioner's decision. **Inherited BASE-001:** new capabilities, record kinds and doors retain native authority, revocation, audit and portability/erasure integrity; supply the named public-door activation evidence in BASE-001 before shipping. **Inherited PORTAL-004:** before its 433-A/F case organizers ship, they retain versioned conditional/required questions, authorized per-question contact responsibility, supporting uploads, save/resume, explicitly confirmed prior-period carry, immutable submitted corrections and staff completeness/review; only submitted current confirmations drive case/workflow choices. **Implemented native boundary:** a principal or reviewer explicitly reviews the frozen version of a firm-authored tax organizer designated for 433-A collection and creates a native case on its authorized open job. The case links to the existing organizer, submissions, corrections, staff review and supporting originals without duplicating their payloads. Only submitted current confirmations appear as case facts. Transcript context is unavailable; no recommendation or agency action is produced. Case links and practitioner attribution are portable structural records; existing organizer and file holds, signed-work retention, erasure and stale-restore fencing apply.

### Client communication portal and documents

- **MAIL-001 — Gmail and Microsoft 365 shared inbox.** Connect Gmail/Google Workspace and Microsoft 365/Exchange mailboxes with scoped OAuth, shared/delegated mailbox access and visible sync health. Triage threads into clients and engagements, assign email as work, comment internally, send/reply with the authorized identity using firm or personal templates (MSG-001) and file attachments against the correct job. Colleague visibility follows MAIL-002; snooze, scheduled send and no-reply follow-up are MAIL-003. Preserve message/thread identity, timestamps and authors, prevent duplicate sends/imports, and quarantine ambiguous client matches. Revocation stops access and surfaces unsynced work. **Acceptance evidence:** Connect a real authorized Google mailbox and Microsoft shared mailbox, receive and reply to client threads, delegate one as a job and file an attachment. Send the same event twice, introduce an ambiguous sender and revoke access; inspect one copy, explicit triage and actionable sync failure. **Time suggestions (TIME-001, inherited before this ships):** a person's connected-mailbox activity becomes a TIME-001 activity-suggestion source only with that person's separate consent for mail, given and withdrawn by them; each suggestion links the message it came from, and nothing is recorded until they approve it. **Acceptance evidence (TIME-001):** with mail consent, a sent client reply suggests time on its job linking that message; without it, or after withdrawal, mail suggests nothing. **Offboarding (ACCESS-006, inherited before this ships):** a departing staff member's connected mailbox, triaged threads and mailbox grants appear in the offboarding preview; the batch moves triaged threads to the work successor and deactivation revokes the mailbox grants. **Acceptance evidence (ACCESS-006):** offboard a preparer with a connected mailbox; their grant is revoked, triaged threads follow the successor and sent mail keeps its author. **Message templates (MSG-001, inherited before this ships):** an inbox reply composes from a firm or personal template, previews it for the exact recipient, is refused while a placeholder is unresolved, sends the version's attachments and stores its rendered text. **Acceptance evidence (MSG-001):** reply to a client thread with the "Month-end close request" template and inspect the rendered reply, its attachment and the stored text. **Engagement history (CRM-003, inherited before this ships):** sent and received client emails appear in the client's history with author, time and source link, visible only to those who may read the job, and any unresolved item it creates (an unanswered client email) names an owner, next action and due condition. **Acceptance evidence (CRM-003):** trace a request from the client's email through upload and review in the client history. **Inherited BASE-001:** satisfy its authority, audit, erasure and portability activation gate with named public-door evidence before this new path ships. **Receiving ERASURE-002 (ct 22 Oct 2026):** Before shipping, MAIL-001 adds its records and provider copies to ERASURE-002's classes, clocks, holds, preview, erasure, receipt and restore fence (ct 22 Oct 2026).

- **MAIL-002 — Mailbox privacy and sharing.** When staff connect their own mailboxes, colleagues see only threads with matched client contacts and threads the mailbox owner explicitly shares. Personal, vendor and other non-client mail stays visible only to the mailbox owner. A user can mark any thread, sender or domain private, so it is never shared, triaged or summarized. A shared team mailbox such as info@ is visible to its assigned members. Firm administrators cannot read private threads through the app or API, and AI features (AI-001) and search (SEARCH-001) exclude them. Marking a client thread private later removes colleagues' access. Attachments already filed to a job stay filed, with the filing recorded. **Acceptance evidence:** Connect a preparer's mailbox containing a client thread, a personal thread and a vendor thread. A colleague and the owner see only the client thread. Mark the client thread private: colleagues lose access, while its filed attachment stays on the job with its filing record. Add a private-domain rule and confirm a new email from that domain is not shared. The API, search and AI summaries cannot read private threads. **Inherited BASE-001:** satisfy its authority, audit, erasure and portability activation gate with named public-door evidence before this new path ships. **Receiving ERASURE-002 (ct 22 Oct 2026):** Before shipping, MAIL-002 adds its records and provider copies to ERASURE-002's classes, clocks, holds, preview, erasure, receipt and restore fence (ct 22 Oct 2026).

- **MAIL-003 — Triage controls snooze and scheduled send.** Each user and each shared mailbox has a triage list. From it a thread can be marked done, snoozed until a date and time (when it returns to triage), assigned to a colleague with a note, converted into a work item or task, or linked to existing work. Replies can be scheduled for a future time and canceled until sent. A no-reply follow-up reminder fires if the client has not answered by a date. Each client and work item has an email-in forwarding address. Triage counts by person show who has a backlog. **Acceptance evidence:** Snooze a thread until tomorrow at 9:00 and see it return. Assign another thread to a colleague with a note. Convert one thread into a 1040 work item and link another to existing work. Schedule a reply for Monday at 8:00, cancel and reschedule it, and confirm exactly one send. Without prior actuals the period uses the rule's time budget, else the work type's budget, else the sum of the template's task estimates, with a range from 50% to 150% of it (rounded to the minute), and the reason names the client; with none of these its estimate is zero and the reason says so. Each week states its confidence: high when every period due in it rests on at least three prior actuals, medium when each rests on at least one, low when any rests on none (each such reason listed). Capacity is each active person's weekly hours less leave and commitments on the week's weekdays (CAPACITY-001); by skill, a person counts in full under each of their skills, and demand counts under the skill named like its work type (lower case); a skill is short by its demand's high end less its capacity. A scenario adds hypothetical hires (weekly minutes and skills from a start date), changes a person's weekly hours from a date (zero for a departure), drops lost clients' periods (listed as left out) and scales a work type's time to a percentage (0 drops the service); it is compared week by week and by skill with the baseline. Forecasting computes from live records and stores nothing; saving a scenario stores only its name, window and changes (audited) and changes no job, rule, assignment, estimate, due date or capacity row; reopening it recomputes from current records. **Pipeline (CRM-005):** each open prospect’s requested service contributes its own visible unweighted assumption that the prospect wins, with current stage, source, owner and whole-prospect annual fee in its stored currency. An exact case-insensitive service/work-type name match is the default; the manager may choose another work type or leave the service unestimated. Its first assumed work target defaults to the forecast start or is selected per service; demand repeats at the selected template’s monthly/quarterly/annual cadence through the window, or occurs once without a template. Each engagement uses the same no-actuals estimate chain as recurring work (work-type budget, else template task estimates), with a 50%–150% range rounded to the minute. Missing matches or budgets contribute zero explicitly labeled unestimated, with a named low-confidence reason. Pipeline demand counts in weekly and skill totals in baseline and scenarios; service percentage changes scale it too. Fees never become hours. Won and lost prospects are excluded. These assumptions create no assignments, signed scope or promised deadlines. Saved scenarios retain the selected work type and first target and recompute from current records. CAPACITY-003 is done for every capability that exists today.

### Time billing payments and reporting

- **TIME-001 — Time budgets and activity suggestions.** Record time against client/job/task with manual entry and timers, billable status and snapshotted rate; compare actual hours/cost with approved budgets. Suggest missing entries from consented work/email/calendar activity with source links, never silently creating billable time. Corrections retain authorship and respect locks. **Acceptance evidence:** Record time, change the rate and inspect unchanged prior amounts and budget variance. Stop/restart a timer, reject one activity suggestion and approve another; verify only approved minutes enter WIP and unauthorized edits are refused. **Timers and budgets (implemented subset):** a person runs at most one timer, kept by the server so it continues across restarts and devices; stopping it records one time entry through the manual-entry path (rate in force snapshotted, closed periods refused) for the elapsed time rounded up to the next whole minute (at least 1, at most 1440), dated the UTC day the timer started, and a discarded timer records nothing. A job's budget is the minutes approved by the reviewer or principal who starts it, or by its recurrence rule (WORK-002); actual is every recorded entry in any review state plus adjustments, at their snapshotted amounts, and variance is actual minus budget. **Billable status (implemented subset):** each time entry is billable or not, chosen by the person when they record it by hand or start a timer (billable unless they choose otherwise), and a TIME-002 correction keeps the returned entry's status unless the person changes it. A non-billable entry keeps its snapshotted rate and amount and counts in the job's actual time, cost and variance, but neither it nor any adjustment to it is ever ready to bill: it stays out of WIP, is refused in a billing export and stays out of the job's margin (TIME-004). **Semantics (TIME-001):** a time entry or timer names its job, and so its client, and optionally one of that job's checklist tasks; a correction keeps the task unless the person changes it. **Activity suggestions:** consent is per person, off by default, given and withdrawn only by that person on their Jobs screen. While it is on, that person's own audited work actions on jobs they can record time on (completing a checklist task, accepting or returning a document, opening, replying to or requesting a correction in a discussion, any tax-notice timeline action, discarding a timer) taken at or after the moment of consent suggest one entry per job and UTC day on which they recorded no time of their own on that job; each suggestion lists and links its source actions. Only that person sees, approves or rejects their suggestions: approval needs the minutes and an explicit billable choice and records the entry through the manual-entry path (rate in force on that day snapshotted, closed periods refused); rejection records nothing; each decision is kept once with its source action ids. Approved suggestions are ordinary time, so they reach WIP only once approved on a timesheet (TIME-002) and only if billable. Withdrawing consent removes every pending suggestion, and consenting again never uses earlier actions. Email and calendar activity are not sources until MAIL-001 and INTEGRATE-005 ship, each with its own per-source consent (written into those clauses).

- **TIME-002 — Timesheet approval and period locks.** Staff submit timesheets to managers, who approve or return entries with reasons. Closing a billing period locks approved time; corrections use an authorized adjustment that preserves the original. Invoice/export reservations prevent the same work being billed twice. **Acceptance evidence:** Submit a weekly timesheet, return and correct one entry, approve it and close the period. Attempt direct edits and duplicate billing, then post an authorized adjustment and inspect its history.

- **TIME-003 — Billing rates and rate cards.** Billing rates are set by staff member, role and service or work type, with client-specific overrides and effective dates. The precedence is client and service, then client, then service, then staff member, then role. Role is the person's practice role (principal, reviewer or preparer). Service rates may target a WORK-007 work type or the engagement template the job was started from. Within either service scope (service or client and service), a matching work-type card takes precedence over template cards, then the latest effective date and creation order resolve cards for that target. Template cards continue to apply to jobs started from that template when no work-type card in that scope is in force; work types without a default template may have their own rates. Each time entry snapshots the rate it resolved and where that rate came from. A rate change takes effect from its date and never rewrites past entries. **Acceptance evidence:** Set rates for a practice role, a staff member, a 1040 service, a client and that client plus service. Record time with only the role matching, then with staff, service, client and client-plus-service rates also matching in turn; inspect each entry's resolved rate and source to prove every precedence level: client and service, client, service, staff member, role. Verify role means principal, reviewer or preparer. Start two jobs with distinct work types sharing a template and inspect their distinct service rates; a type without a default template also accepts its own rate. Verify client overrides, work-type versus template specificity, effective dates and recorded snapshots through archive restore. Change the staff rate effective next month and confirm past entries are unchanged.

- **TIME-004 — Expenses and disbursements.** Record billable and non-billable expenses (filing fees, postage, mileage at the firm-set rate, software pass-throughs) against a client and work item. Each expense can carry a receipt, a markup and an approval, and approved billable expenses become BILL-002 invoice lines. A reviewer or the principal approves or rejects an expense, nobody but the principal approves their own, and an expense dated in a closed billing period (TIME-002) cannot be recorded. Staff-paid expenses are owed back to that person at cost, and the principal records each reimbursement. Until BILL-002 issues invoice documents, an expense's invoice line is its line in the reviewed billing export, reserved once; BILL-002 inherits approved billable expenses as invoice lines before it ships. Until BILL-003 ships, WIP is the value of everything ready to bill, and a job's profitability is its margin before staff cost: fixed fee, approved billable time (TIME-001) and its adjustments and approved billable expense charges, less the cost of every approved expense, billable or not; BILL-003 keeps expenses in its WIP and profitability. **Acceptance evidence:** Record a state filing fee with a receipt and a 10% markup, approve it, invoice it and inspect the invoice line and WIP. A non-billable expense stays off the invoice and appears in profitability. An unapproved expense cannot be invoiced.

### Connections and extensibility

## Honest boundaries

- Blotter owns practice CRM, engagement scope, workflow, inbox, portal, document/request custody, review, capacity, time/WIP, invoices, collections and follow-up. It remains its own product. General firm file storage connects to [Chest](https://github.com/just-every/run-chest), Google Drive, OneDrive/SharePoint or Dropbox under INTEGRATE-003; client workpapers and request evidence stay part of Blotter. It does not absorb an unowned neighboring category.
- Tax-return calculation, tax advice and federal/state e-filing stay with the qualified practitioner and Lacerte, ProSeries, Drake, UltraTax CS or CCH Axcess. DUE-001 owns calculated obligation deadlines and extension workflow, INTEGRATE-002 owns the packet/status bridge, and INTEGRATE-006 owns authorized IRS transcripts. Completed work is never evidence of a filed or accepted return.
- QuickBooks Online and Xero remain authoritative books. LEDGER-001/002 bring client close context into practice work; INTEGRATE-001 separately connects firm revenue accounting. Gusto remains the payroll calculation, payroll payment and remittance authority; Blotter owns the related practice work and status evidence, not a second payroll engine. Payroll: [Envelope](https://github.com/just-every/run-envelope).
- Stripe supplies card/ACH processing, regulated onboarding and bank settlement. Blotter owns invoices, mandates, payment-state reconciliation and exceptions under PAY-001. Karbon Payments, TaxDome Payments, Canopy Payments and Financial Cents payment history is migrated, and saved methods move to valid mandates or become tracked client reauthorizations under MIGRATE-007. Signature/KBA providers supply specialist identity verification; Blotter owns the engagement-letter journey and signed evidence. Required commercial/provider agreements and US sender registration are implementation clauses, never exclusions.
- Google and Microsoft supply email/calendar transport; Twilio supplies US SMS transport; booking providers supply appointment booking. Blotter retains consent, authority, delivery distinctions and owned failure follow-up. AI reads only authorized practice data under visible provider terms, can be paused, and never replaces professional judgment or creates source evidence. USD fees and US buyers come first; additional jurisdictions require explicit sourced templates and acceptance.

### Agent surface (Base-delivered)
#### BASE-AGENT-001 — One MCP door per seed

*Tier:* Agent surface

**Requirement.** Every seed, hosted or self-hosted, serves one remote MCP endpoint at `/mcp` over Streamable HTTP. It speaks the current revision (2026-07-28) and accepts 2025-11-25 clients through the twelve-month deprecation window. It implements `server / discover`, tools, resources and prompts. Lists are deterministic and carry `ttlMs` and `cacheScope: "private"`. Roots, Sampling and Logging are not served.

**Acceptance.**
1. `server / discover` returns the supported versions, capabilities, `serverInfo` and instructions.
2. A 2026-07-28 request works with no handshake, and a 2025-11-25 client completes `initialize` and lists the same tools.
3. An unsupported version returns `UnsupportedProtocolVersion`.
4. Two `tools / list` calls return the same order, with cache fields.
5. A foreign Origin returns 403, and a header and body method mismatch returns `HeaderMismatch`.
6. An oversized body returns 413 with no effect.

#### BASE-AGENT-002 — The seed's jobs are tools, through the UI's own actions

*Tier:* Agent surface

**Requirement.** Each Core job a person does in the product is a tool. Where one is not, the Agent surface says why: it runs on a device, it is a person's interactive screen, it belongs to a connector or the import door, or it is an installation fact. Risk is never the reason: a risky job is a tool with its class (BASE-AGENT-006). Tools are named `<seed>.<area>.<verb>` and declare input and output schemas and truthful annotations. Each calls the same server action as the UI, so validation and authorization are written once, and the seed's embedded agents use the same registry. A business refusal returns `isError` with the seed's stable error code.

**Acceptance.**
1. The Core clause ids in each tool's `_meta`, with the not-a-tool reasons that `server / discover` serves, cover every Core clause in the contract, and no reason is risk; the harness and `rer check` fail on a gap.
2. Each tool's fixture result validates against its `outputSchema`.
3. Read tools declare `readOnlyHint`; tools that can carry destructive declare `destructiveHint`, and tools that can carry external declare `openWorldHint`.
4. A refusal returns the same error code the UI gets for the same action.
5. The UI action and its tool, on the same fixture, give the same record state and the same audit event type.
6. The seed's embedded agents appear in the audit as calls to the same tools.

#### BASE-AGENT-003 — Records are resources

*Tier:* Agent surface

**Requirement.** Each primary record type has a URI template, and tools return `resource_link`s to the records they touch. A read returns exactly the fields the caller's role sees in the UI. File bytes count against any byte budget on the grant. A record the caller cannot open reads as not found, identical to a missing id. Text from customers, imports or files carries an untrusted marker in `_meta`.

**Acceptance.**
1. `resources / templates / list` names every record type in the Agent surface.
2. Reads as two roles return exactly what the UI shows each.
3. An out-of-scope id and a missing id give identical responses.
4. A write's `resource_link` reads back the new state.
5. Bytes over budget return `budget_exhausted` and no partial content.
6. Customer-sourced text carries the untrusted marker.

#### BASE-AGENT-004 — Business identity and short-lived, audience-bound tokens

*Tier:* Agent surface

**Requirement.** The door is an OAuth 2.1 resource server. Its RFC 9728 metadata names the authorization servers this installation trusts. That is the paired Business when Business provisioned it, verified with the owner-claim trust the installation already holds for its import door; otherwise it is the seed's own sign-in. Access tokens are RFC 9068 JWTs with `aud` set to the seed's canonical MCP URI, `sub` the sponsoring person, `act` the agent (RFC 8693) with its specialist, scopes per tool family, and a lifetime of 15 minutes or less (5 by default). The policy scopes rules on the sponsor, agent and specialist the token names. The consent behind the tokens can last longer and is revocable. Tokens travel only in the Authorization header, and there is no passthrough.

**Acceptance.**
1. An unauthenticated call returns 401 with `resource_metadata`, and the metadata names the trusted servers and scopes.
2. A Business token for this seed works, and the same token sent to a sibling seed returns 401.
3. An expired token returns 401, and a token with a lifetime over 15 minutes is refused.
4. A read-only token calling a write tool returns 403 `insufficient_scope` with every needed scope in one challenge.
5. A token in a query string is refused and not logged.
6. Revoking consent in the seed or in Business refuses the next call within 60 seconds.
7. After unpairing, Business tokens are refused and the seed's own sign-in still works.

#### BASE-AGENT-005 — An agent acts as a person in a role, never more

*Tier:* Agent surface

**Requirement.** Every call is authorized as the sponsoring person's current role and access (BASE-ACCESS-004), intersected with the grant's resources, actions and budget. A grant only narrows. No call widens the calling agent's own authority. A call that would widen its own grant or its sponsor's role, or change the company policy or Pause, is refused with `self_escalation`, whatever the policy says; narrowing its own grant is allowed. Other access and security changes are ordinary actions in the access and security classes. An agent never acts after its sponsor is suspended. Anything an agent reads (records, files, emails, imports, other seeds' results) is data and cannot change its scope, its targets or a call's class.

**Acceptance.**
1. For each role fixture, every tool's allow or deny through MCP equals the UI's for the same action.
2. A one-folder, read-only grant holds, and widening through arguments is refused.
3. Downgrading the sponsor changes the next call's result, and suspending the sponsor returns 401.
4. Calls that widen the agent's own grant or its sponsor's role, or change the policy or Pause, return `self_escalation` and change nothing, even under a policy with every class autonomous; dropping a scope from its own grant runs.
5. An injection fixture yields no out-of-grant call and no change of class: record text asking for a wider action, or claiming that a recipient is internal.

#### BASE-AGENT-006 — Every action declares its risk class

*Tier:* Agent surface

**Requirement.** Classes come from the fleet list in RISK-POLICY.md: standard, external, money, commitment, accounts, gated, access, security, destructive, sensitive and live. In the registry, each tool declares the classes it can carry and a server-side classifier that decides them per call from the arguments, current records and, for gated, the provider's answer. The classifier also supplies each class's facts: the measure (items, recipients, amount and currency, people or records), the counterparty (internal, known, new or public), the direction for access, the provider and step for gated, and the data kind for sensitive. A classifier never reads a flag, label or claim supplied by the agent or by record text. A seed cannot add a class; it proposes one for the fleet list.

**Acceptance.**
1. Every tool in `tools / list` carries its possible classes in `_meta`, equal to the Agent surface table.
2. For each tool, fixture calls cover every class it can carry, and the computed classes and facts equal the fixture's expected values.
3. An argument or record text asserting a class or a confirmation (`internal: true`, `confirmExternal: true`) leaves the computed classes unchanged.
4. Money calls carry amount and currency, external calls their counterparty and recipient count, access calls their direction, and destructive calls their item count.
5. No tool in `tools / list` declares a class outside the fleet list, and `rer check` fails on one.
6. A refused call's audit row still records its computed classes.

#### BASE-AGENT-007 — The company's policy decides, at one chokepoint

*Tier:* Agent surface

**Requirement.** Every agent door calls one decision function: MCP, the integration API with agent tokens, and the seed's embedded agents. It evaluates the call's classes against the company's policy, as above. The seed ships no dispositions and fills no gap with one: agent access opens only under a complete policy that setup has asked for (RISK-POLICY.md), and before then every agent call returns `policy_unset` with the setup link and changes nothing. *Autonomous* runs the call. *Review* runs it and adds it to the review feed. *Approval* saves a pending action with server-computed facts and returns `input_required`, with a URL-mode elicitation to the seed's approval page and a pending handle. Each person the rule names approves the exact saved revision in a signed-in browser, and changed inputs need a new approval. The retried call returns the result and a receipt. A rejection returns `approval_rejected`, and a lapse past the wait the rule sets returns `approval_expired`. *Blocked* returns `policy_blocked`, naming the class, rule and revision.

**Acceptance.**
1. The Base harness runs each tool under each disposition for every class it can carry, and sees it run, run and enter the review feed, wait with no effect, or be refused.
2. Before setup is complete, the setup page lists every class the seed's tools carry with examples and no answer pre-selected, an agent call returns `policy_unset` with the setup link and changes nothing, and an incomplete revision cannot be confirmed; a `*` rule completes it, and a tool an upgrade adds with an unanswered class appears in `tools / list` once that class is answered, while the other tools keep running.
3. Under "money autonomous up to $500, approval up to $10,000, blocked above", calls of $400, $600 and $20,000 run, wait and are refused; a per-day cap sends the call that crosses it to the next rule.
4. A call carrying two classes takes the stricter disposition.
5. An approval shows server-computed facts and an expiry, returns the URL elicitation and a handle, and completes once after the named approver approves; a changed input needs a new approval, and a rejection or lapse leaves no effect.
6. The same call through MCP, the integration API and an embedded agent gets the same decision.
7. A policy change applies to the next call within 60 seconds, and the audit cites the new revision.
8. A policy document with a bad signature or another Business's id is rejected, and the door keeps the last valid revision.

#### BASE-AGENT-008 — Truthful attribution

*Tier:* Agent surface

**Requirement.** Every agent act is recorded and shown as `"<agent> for <person>"`, and mail and messages an agent sends outside name it that way as their sender. An approval, a review mark, a confirmation (a warning dialog, a typed-field confirmation, a delivery confirmation), a decision or a signature attributed to a person comes only from that person's signed-in session. When an agent does the equivalent act, the record names the agent, and the act carries its own class; a binding decision or a signature is commitment. Agent doors ignore arguments that stand for a person's confirmation. No tool solves a bot check, or enters a person's own password or 2FA code at an outside service. A provider step that demands a person goes to a person, whatever the policy says; the gated class marks such steps before they run.

**Acceptance.**
1. An agent call carrying a person-confirmation flag is classified and decided exactly as without it.
2. Approving, marking reviewed or answering a policy question with an agent or device token returns 403 and changes nothing.
3. A form-mode elicitation "accept" never completes an approval.
4. Where an agent's decision, signature or field confirmation runs without a person, it reads `"<agent> for <person>"` in the record, the activity view, exports and any certificate, never as the person's own act.
5. After a person approves an agent's prepared action, the record shows the person as approver and the agent as preparer.
6. Activity and exports at 1440 and 390 show `"<agent> for <person>"` for every agent act.
7. Mail an agent sends to an outside address names `"<agent> for <person>"` as its sender.

#### BASE-AGENT-009 — Every agent action is audited with its class and decision

*Tier:* Agent surface

**Requirement.** Extending BASE-OPS-005, each call that reads private data or changes anything records the agent client, name and specialist, and the run or task id (`traceparent` when sent); the sponsoring person, the grant, the tool and the targets; the classes and their facts, and the policy revision and rule; the decision (autonomous, review, approval, blocked, unset or self_escalation) and the outcome (done, refused, pending or failed); the approval or review id and person, and the idempotency key. For a period, the seed's Agents page shows actions by class and decision with the notable ones, the review feed (Mark reviewed, Flag, and Undo where reversible), pending approvals, steps waiting for a person and setup questions. Business shows the same across seeds.

**Acceptance.**
1. One write leaves a complete audit row.
2. Refused, pending, unset and self-escalation calls are audited.
3. The Agents page's counts by class and decision equal the audit rows on a fixture week.
4. The review feed lists exactly the calls decided as review; Mark reviewed records the person, and Undo restores a reversible one.
5. Filtering by agent or class lists only those rows, and export includes every field.
6. Removing the agent keeps its rows and its name.
7. The Agents page works at 1440 and 390 with no serious or critical axe findings.

#### BASE-AGENT-010 — Agents can follow changes

*Tier:* Agent surface

**Requirement.** The seed emits a typed event for every record change and for every approval, review and policy decision. Each event carries a stable id, a type, the record URI, the actor (a person, or an agent acting for a person) and a time. Events never carry secrets or more than the subscriber may read. Agents can read events three ways: `subscriptions / listen`, an `events.list` tool with a cursor, and signed webhooks from Base `integrations` using the same ids. Every channel delivers at least once and filters by access at delivery.

**Acceptance.**
1. A subscribed record changed in the UI produces a notification within 10 seconds.
2. `events.list` returns the same event id the webhook carries.
3. Replaying from a cursor returns the same ids in order.
4. After access is revoked, no channel delivers events about that record.
5. A failed webhook is visible and replays without duplicate effects.
6. `approval.pending`, `approval.decided`, `review.flagged` and `policy.adopted` carry the class and decision and nothing the subscriber may not read.

#### BASE-AGENT-011 — Limits are policy, and Pause stops everything

*Tier:* Agent surface

**Requirement.** Business limits are rules in the company's policy: per-call and per-day thresholds on any class's measure, such as money moved, outside recipients or items destroyed; spend caps on provider cost (models, SMS, email) per seed, specialist or agent, which setup asks with the classes; "no cap" is an answer. Tools with provider cost declare an estimate before they run, and an exhausted cap returns `budget_exhausted` before any partial effect. The seed's capacity limits (request rate, body and byte sizes) protect the installation: they bound rate and size, never daily business volume, are documented and are not policy. A grant carries budgets only when the person granting it sets them. A **Pause agents** control in the seed, and Pause all agents in Business when paired, refuses every agent token within 60 seconds until a person resumes; browser sessions and devices keep working.

**Acceptance.**
1. A rate overrun returns 429 with `Retry-After`.
2. A per-day cap of three outside recipients sends the fourth to the rule that applies past the cap.
3. An exhausted spend cap returns `budget_exhausted` with no partial effect and shows the spend.
4. Under the answer "no cap", a spending call runs and its spend shows in usage; a call that spends nothing is unaffected by any cap.
5. The usage view shows calls, decisions by class, money moved and provider spend per agent.
6. Pause and Pause all agents each stop the next call within 60 seconds, and resume restores access.
7. An agent token cannot resume.

#### BASE-AGENT-012 — Writes are idempotent and conflict-safe

*Tier:* Agent surface

**Requirement.** Every mutating tool requires an idempotency key and takes an optional expected revision. The same key with the same arguments returns the first outcome for at least 24 hours; the same key with different arguments returns `idempotency_conflict`; a stale revision returns `revision_conflict` with the current revision. Long work returns a job handle and a status tool, with no dependence on the Tasks extension.

**Acceptance.**
1. Two calls with one key give one effect and equal results.
2. A retry with a new JSON-RPC id and the same key, after a dropped stream, returns the recorded outcome.
3. The same key with different arguments returns a conflict and no effect.
4. A stale revision returns a conflict naming the current revision.
5. A job handle used by another person's token reads as not found.

#### BASE-AGENT-013 — Manifest, docs and the conformance journey

*Tier:* Agent surface

**Requirement.** `server / discover` instructions and an on-site `/docs/agents` page are generated from the action registry. The page lists tools by job, with each tool's classes, the test that adds each computed class, its scopes, resource templates, event types, capacity limits and error codes, and the specialist role. `prompts / list` carries the specialist's jobs. Base ships the conformance journey, a harness that `rer verify` runs against `rer dev` and seeds run in CI. It is an MCP client; a signed-in test person takes a person's steps (setup answers, approvals, review marks, resume) through the URLs the door returns, and the same browser leg runs the UI-parity actions and the page checks at 1440 and 390. It runs every acceptance point of BASE-AGENT-001 to 012 and of the seed's SURFACE clauses under two company policies: *all autonomous* (`*`), and *held* (standard review, every other class the seed declares approval, which the test person grants), plus the single-class variants a point names. A point that names no disposition passes under both.

**Acceptance.**
1. The docs list exactly the names in `tools / list` and `resources / templates / list`.
2. Each tool's classes, and the test behind each computed one, are documented.
3. The harness fails on any of: a tool without a schema; an effect under approval or blocked, or before setup is complete; a computed class that differs from its fixture; a flag that changes a class or completes a person's step; a role-parity mismatch; a wrong-audience token being accepted; a duplicate effect on retry.
4. Every acceptance point runs under both policies, every decision matches the policy in force, and under all autonomous no call waits for a person or is refused by policy.
5. A stranger agent given only the seed URL completes the specialist journey through MCP.

after1.text: # Blotter Blotter is practice management for a small bookkeeping and accounting firm: recurring client jobs with their due dates, document requests that clients answer through a private upload link, reviewer sign-off, staff capacity, and time exported for your own billing. It runs in your own Cloudflare account. 100% free and open source, MIT licensed. Blotter's contract is the practice manager a US firm moves to from Karbon, TaxDome or Canopy: US firm setup in USD, calculated federal and state deadlines, IRS e-file signatures, invoices and payments. [CONTRACT.md](CONTRACT.md) and the run site's [/contract](https://run-blotter.com/contract) page show what the code does today and what is next. Today's release records new amounts in US dollars (records from the first release keep their Australian dollars), takes due dates entered by people with their source, and does not file returns, calculate tax, keep client books or give advice. ## Run Blotter You need macOS, Linux or Windows with WSL2, and Git. These are the two steps on [run-blotter.com/run](https://run-blotter.com/run). Install rer (it brings its own Node if you have none; if the installer ends with a line to run, run it): ```sh curl -fsSL https://runeditrun.com/install.sh | sh ``` Then start Blotter: ```sh rer dev just-every/run-blotter ``` Already have Node 22 or later? `npx -y @runeditrun/rer dev just-every/run-blotter` does both steps in one line. To start it again later, run `cd run-blotter && rer dev`. `rer dev` installs the locked dependencies, selects pinned Node 22.20.0 and pnpm 10.12.4, prepares a local D1 database and starts the app on a free port. The first launch takes several minutes; if it is interrupted, run it again. It prints `RER_READY` with the address and `RER_OPEN` with a sign-in link. Open the `RER_OPEN` link on this computer: you are signed in as the principal. Confirm **Finish setup**, then open the workspace at `/app`. The link is a local credential; keep it private. If `rer dev` says the server limit is reached, stop a server you no longer need with the command it prints, or start with `RER_SERVER_LIMIT=8 rer dev`. Stop Blotter with `rer dev --stop`. ### Try the other roles locally Local mail is suppressed, so team members sign in as local personas instead of by email. In **Team & safety**, save `reviewer@dev.localhost` as a reviewer and `preparer@dev.localhost` as a preparer. Then stop the app and restart as one of them: ```sh rer dev --stop rer dev --as reviewer # or: rer dev --as preparer ``` Open the new `RER_OPEN` link. `rer dev` with no `--as` returns to the principal. The run site is live at [https://run-blotter.com](https://run-blotter.com), and its run page is [https://run-blotter.com/run](https://run-blotter.com/run). The local run entrypoint is `/run` in the static site built by `rer build --site`. The [documentation](docs/README.md) is maintained as repository Markdown and ships as `/docs` and its guide pages in that same static build. ## Do the first jobs 1. **Team & safety:** set your own hourly rate (in cents, before tax; `15000` is $150.00), add a reviewer and a preparer, and set their rates. On a deployed installation, **Send an invitation** emails them a sign-in link. 2. **Clients & templates:** add a client with a contact email, and save the prefilled **Quarterly sales-tax return** template (checklist, document requests, fixed fee). Under **Start a job**, choose the client, template, period start (for example `2026-07-01`), the due date you have checked, where it comes from, the preparer and the reviewer. 3. **Jobs → open the job → Client documents:** **Send a reminder with an upload link.** Blotter mails the client the link (on a deployed installation) and shows it to you once. Open the link in a private window: that is the client's view. Upload a file for each request, then back in the job **Accept** each one or **Ask again**. For larger packets, staff use **Document packets → Add a packet or corrected version**: up to 20 MiB and 2,000 declared pages, with confirmed-byte progress, pause/resume for seven days, immutable prior versions, internal page notes and review. Select the exact original to resume. Client details also expose searchable document folders by client/period. New packets start internal; corrections retain preceding contact grants and create no share links. 4. **Checklist:** tick every step and **Submit for review**. As the assigned reviewer (or the principal, for someone else's work), choose **Sign off** with a note. Signing off closes the upload link. 5. **Roll forward:** on the signed-off job, record the next period's due date under **Roll forward to the next period**. Blotter creates the next period's job with the same client, template and people. It refuses a second copy. 6. **Time & billing:** record time on a job (**Time** section; it uses your current rate). In **Time & billing**, choose items, **Prepare export**, then as the principal **Approve** it with a note and **Download CSV**. An approved export cannot change; each time entry or fixed fee can be exported once. 7. **Preparations:** create an agent key in **Team & safety** and give it to your agent with [API.md](API.md). Its roll-forwards, reminders and exports wait here until you **Approve** or **Decline**; decisions are recorded. 8. **Move in:** load [the documented fixture](fixtures/client-list.csv) or your own list, map source columns, **Preview (dry run)**, review any duplicate choices and preview again, then **Import these clients**. **View journal** shows the original file and progress; **Undo import** removes the untouched imported clients/contacts while keeping native work and edited records. Native matches add source provenance without changing permissions. See [IMPORTING.md](IMPORTING.md) for the CSV shape. 9. **Team & safety:** **Download practice archive**, and **Erase a client file** by typing its name and a reason. The exact first-release scope is in [ACCEPTANCE.md](ACCEPTANCE.md). ## Backup and restore The archive holds clients, templates, jobs, document requests and files, time, exports, imports and the audit log. Sign-in accounts, sessions, agent keys and client upload links are not included: create new keys and send new reminders after a move. Restore only into an empty installation, from **Team & safety** or the command line: ```sh rer export --output exports/practice.rer # In a new, empty checkout: copy the archive into its exports/ folder first; # --input must be a path inside the checkout. rer import --input exports/practice.rer --yes rer dev ``` The restored checkout gets a new local owner; your practice data, exports and history come back unchanged. After erasing a file, make a new archive and retire older ones. An older archive is refused unless you also supply the newer archive that carries the erasure journal (`--journal exports/newer.rer`, or the second file field in **Restore**). `rer reset --yes` deletes local data; export first. ## Deploy your installation You need a Cloudflare account with Workers and D1, a sending address verified with Resend, and a Resend API key for email sign-in and reminders. Never put credentials in Git, commands, screenshots or chat. 1. Stop local serving (`rer dev --stop`) and commit your changes. In `deploy.json`, set `MAIL_FROM` to your verified sending address. Keep the project, package, Worker and D1 names unchanged, and keep `AUTH_LOCAL` `false`. 2. In your shell's private environment, supply `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` and `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`, and `OWNER_EMAIL`, `SESSION_SECRET`, `SETUP_TOKEN` and `MAIL_API_KEY`, plus `VAULT_KEY` to use the client credential vault. Generate the session, setup and vault values as independent random strings of at least 32 characters, with your secret manager; keep `VAULT_KEY` with your backups, since archived credentials open only under the same key. 3. Run `rer deploy --dry-run` to build and check the plan without provider calls (it already needs the variables from step 2), then `rer deploy`. It creates or reuses the D1 database, applies the migrations, deploys the Worker and its assets, checks health and prints the URL. 4. Open the printed address's `/signin`, request a link for the owner email and follow it. Confirm **Finish setup**, then open `/app`. [RUN-LOCALLY.md](RUN-LOCALLY.md) and [SEED-COMMAND-CONTRACT.md](SEED-COMMAND-CONTRACT.md) describe every `rer` command. [OPERATIONS.md](OPERATIONS.md) covers running it. ## Develop `rer verify` builds the Worker, typechecks, runs the integration flows in `tests/` against the built Worker (only the mail provider is faked) and checks the hosted output. [SOURCES.md](SOURCES.md) records where the code came from.
