# Crank target contract

Target approved scope: **16 October 2026**. Category: **workflow automation (iPaaS)**. Crank is an owned Zapier/Make/Workato replacement: a connector library with managed OAuth credentials, webhooks/app events/polling/schedules, visual multi-step branching workflows with durable execution, AI agent steps and optional human approval where the action warrants it. It also targets the control and agent capabilities buyers seek in n8n, Gumloop and Pipedream.

The buyer connects the business’s applications so recurring work completes without copying data or supervising every step. Approval and idempotent HTTP delivery are one useful part of this whole job. This target replaces the old first-release exclusions of connectors, credential custody, schedules and live SaaS calls; it does not claim they already exist. No homepage, UI, manifest, code, test or workflow changes are authorized by this document.

Core records are workspaces, members/roles, connections and grants, workflows and immutable versions, steps/subflows/templates, trigger subscriptions/cursors, queues/runs/attempts, mapped inputs/outputs, remote effects, approvals, obligations, usage, import provenance, audit and erasure journals. All future capabilities below remain in scope even when marked missing. Each sibling remains its own product; Crank owns cross-app orchestration and integrates neighboring systems.

Acceptance journeys are repeated in [ACCEPTANCE.md](ACCEPTANCE.md). They run through UI, HTTP/CLI/SDK/MCP or provider doors, using fakes only at the network/paid edge in automated tests. A local edge test does not establish real provider consent, hosted operation, migration compatibility or customer acceptance. Live sandbox/provider journeys are required before a connector or migration can be called complete.

Status starts from the category code audit at `11db081906aa18bfb1c89e261d910196cffd3660`, also current main when this target was authored. No product source changed between the audit and this base. **done** means the entire stated bounded clause is implemented with cited code/test evidence; **partial** identifies the implemented subset and what is absent; **missing** has no product implementation. Vendored generic modules alone do not prove product adoption. The table at the end is a gap map, not a release certification. After the first switching-buyer review (16 October 2026), TRIG-001 widened to third-party webhook senders and moved from done to partial; sixteen clauses were added for the named everyday-app connectors, general HTTP requests, trigger latency, flood holds, hosted email, built-in mail/SMS, publish authority, reviewer edits, collect-data steps and MCP tools. After the second review (16 October 2026), TRIG-007 (feed and URL polling triggers) and WORK-010 (digest steps) were added, and WORK-002 now commits line-item arrays and a line-itemizer with per-line USD reconciliation, tested through CONN-006, CONN-007, CONN-008 and CONN-018. After the third review (16 October 2026), WORK-011 (search-step outcomes and find-or-create) and WORK-012 (built-in no-code transforms at Formatter breadth) were added; CONN-001, CONN-006, CONN-011, CONN-015, WORK-002, WORK-007, EXEC-006 and MIG-001–003 now cite them, WORK-004 adds named delay queues and EXEC-003 adds automatic pause on a sustained error rate. After the fourth review (16 October 2026), WORK-013 (the filter and path condition language: typed operators, AND/OR groups, exclusive or parallel paths with fallback and always-run branches, type mismatches and `stopped by filter`) and CONN-019 (live account pickers, dependent inputs, field refresh and custom values) were added; WORK-001, WORK-002, WORK-011, CONN-001, EXEC-003, EXEC-005 and MIG-001–003 now cite them, CONN-003 adds Gmail search, label and attachment triggers, and WORK-007 adds table-record triggers and atomic counters and lists. After the fifth review (16 October 2026), TRIG-008 (updated-record triggers on watched fields) and WORK-014 (step tests on real samples) were added. After the sixth review (16 October 2026), CONN-007 commits named QuickBooks Online, Xero and NetSuite triggers (paid invoice, payment, due and overdue invoice, updated invoice), searches with find-or-create, and actions (final invoices, send invoice and estimate, record payment, sales receipt, credit memo, void, attach file), unattended under publish authority; CONN-001 reports an operation of an app outside Zapier’s popular-apps list native only when its connector clause names it; CONN-004 names Slack, Nook and Teams triggers, direct messages, bot identity and searches. After the seventh review (16 October 2026), CONN-008 names Shopify and Stripe triggers (including abandoned checkout, inventory threshold and updated order), searches with find-or-create and actions (customers, tags, products and variants, inventory, draft orders and orders, fulfillments, captures, gift cards), and CONN-009 names Zendesk and Jira Software Cloud triggers (ticket in view, updated ticket, issue status changed, JQL), searches with find-or-create and actions, with loop prevention; TRIG-008, CONN-001 and MIG-002 cite them, CONN-005 adds append row and rows, and CONN-018 adds find-or-create searches and stock updates. After the eighth review (17 October 2026), AI-001 takes PDF (including scanned), image, audio and video file references and URLs with type and size bounds, a publish-time model support check and the named error `model input unsupported`, and names built-in operations (send prompt and conversation, extract structured data with line items, analyze and classify, transcribe, translate, extract content from URL, search content across URLs, generate image, model files); CONN-001 maps Zapier’s ChatGPT (OpenAI), Anthropic (Claude) and AI by Zapier steps to them, MIG-001–003 migrate those steps and Make and n8n OpenAI and Anthropic modules, and CONN-015 names Facebook Pages, Instagram and LinkedIn posting.

## Product target

Crank is the owned workflow-automation product a US small or mid-size business buys instead of Zapier, Make or Workato, with the control and agent capabilities buyers now look to n8n, Gumloop and Pipedream for. This contract describes that product, which is what Crank is being built into.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Category | Workflow automation (iPaaS) |
| Incumbents a buyer switches from | Zapier, Make, Workato, n8n, Gumloop, Pipedream |
| First buyer | A US operations lead at a 5–100 person business replacing Zapier, Make or Workato, whose recurring work runs through QuickBooks Online, HubSpot, Slack, Shopify and Stripe; costs in USD, US business calendars and timezones, the buyer's own Cloudflare account |

## Published clauses

### Workspace and HTTP delivery

#### WORK-001 — Visual multi-step workspace.

An operations lead creates, names, folders, searches, duplicates and connects workflows in a visual node-and-edge editor without code: steps are filled by picking account resources and fields by name (CONN-019) and routes are built with WORK-013 conditions, never by typing IDs or writing expressions. Each workflow has an owner, description, trigger, typed steps and enabled state; its graph shows branches, data lineage and validation errors. Every edge shows real sample data from WORK-014 step tests (recent records loaded from the connected account, the next real delivery, an earlier run, an action’s real response, or an explicitly labeled manual sample), with that sample’s source, so a builder sees what a field actually contains before mapping it. Draft edits and sample tests cannot send production actions unless explicitly authorized: a live action test needs its own WORK-014 confirmation naming the effect and account. Publishing a version is itself the authorization for that version’s declared steps on its bound connections (TEAM-004); limits and approval steps are opt-in.

**Acceptance evidence:** From the builder, connect a new lead trigger to a filter, CRM lookup, invoice draft and notification; test the trigger to load recent real leads from the connected test account and pick one, test each step and inspect the sample data and its named source at every edge, correct a missing required field, save and reopen the same graph, then publish it deliberately and observe its next triggered run complete with no further authorization step.

#### HTTP-001 — Authorized HTTP dispatch.

The existing custom HTTP connector delivers the immutable approved JSON body to the deployment-authorized exact origin, adds the run’s stable idempotency key, refuses redirects and binds success to the receiver’s returned effect ID and matching key. Failure or lost acknowledgment remains visible. One owner-controlled replay uses the same bytes/key; a compliant receiver records one effect. This connector’s manual mode remains available beside future standing-grant and app steps.

**Acceptance evidence:** Create and activate a flow through the HTTP API, prepare an event without sending, concurrently approve twice, lose the receiver acknowledgment, replay once and inspect one receiver effect; reject another run and refuse a foreign or credential-bearing destination.

### Run history and recovery

#### EXEC-004 — Replay any eligible step safely.

Operators retry/resume any eligible failed or incomplete step or selected batch items using retained versioned input and scoped authority. Preview shows what would run, prior effects and idempotency/reconciliation status. A corrected payload creates an attributable new revision; successful side effects are not silently repeated. Bulk replay has selection preview and limits. Until TEAM-001 adds an operator role, the owner replays. Eligible steps are the failed steps (and failed loop items) of a failed workflow run, plus failed loop items of a succeeded continue-on-error run, on a published, adopted workflow; a paused run resumes with run resume, an interrupted static read restarts by itself, and an interrupted or lost-response write is listed as uncertain with its operation key and goes to EXEC-006 reconciliation, never blind replay. Items that failed in a loop set to continue belong to a run that succeeded and whose later steps used its results; they are repaired with a linked new run on the same still-published version. The same digest-bound preview and selection limit apply; the source history stays unchanged. A repair retains completed checkpoints (including later steps), reopens only the selected failed items and their enclosing loops, and records `repair_of` and the selected paths. A path claimed by a repair is no longer eligible on its source, including concurrent decisions and after that repair is erased; the source retains the path claim until the source itself is erased; a failed repair is retried on that repair run. Unselected historical failures cannot be replayed through the copied checkpoints. The preview lists the eligible steps with their retained input, error, operation key and revision count, the uncertain writes and the completed effects that will not run again, and carries a digest; a replay names the selected paths (at most 100) and that digest, and a changed run refuses it. An uncorrected replay reuses the step’s retained input and operation key; a corrected input becomes revision N with operation key `<original>#rN`. Every revision keeps the replaced input, error and operation key beside the new input, with the owner and time, and the replay is audited with its paths and version. Completed steps and items keep their checkpoints and never run again; unselected failed items stay failed; each dispatch still checks live publish authority. Revisions are portable records under DATA-001 and erased with their run under DATA-002.

**Acceptance evidence:** Fail the fourth step after three committed effects, restart, preview and resume that step, then replay selected failed items with corrected data; verify the first three effects persist once and the original and corrected inputs remain distinguishable. Also finish a continue-on-error loop with two failed items and a successful later effect: preview and correct one failed item as a linked repair, verify the source history and later effect stay unchanged, the other item stays failed, concurrent decisions create only one repair, and its original and corrected inputs, operation identities, audit and restore links remain inspectable. Replay an uncorrected failed item and verify identical retained input and operation key.

#### EXEC-005 — Searchable run history and debugging.

#### WORK-004 — Durable delay and event waits.

A named delay queue has exactly one spacing policy. A second workflow declaring the same queue with different spacing fails visibly at declaration and leaves existing queued work unchanged. Pausing blocks new, queued and running next-step dispatch. Replacement permits only runs actually waiting or awaiting approval at replacement whose old version chose `continue`, on that frozen graph with live connection and authority checks at every step. Pause, unpublish and version replacement end test dispatch without production waiting-run exceptions. Tests are labelled in history and audit, excluded from production operations reports, notices, auto-pause counts and OPS-002 usage limits, and restore without execution authority under DATA-001. Comparison returns the exact draft/published/retained graphs and changed field paths. Builders compare changes, run selected authorized samples against test accounts, promote with a change record and roll back. Draft step tests follow WORK-014 and are never production runs: a draft bound to declared test accounts tests without confirmation, while a live test against a production connection needs its own confirmation naming the effect and account, is recorded as a test run and grants no production authority; publishing a version (TEAM-004) remains the only production authorization. In-flight runs retain their original version; environment promotion requires explicit connection binding and cannot inherit broader authority. Rollback is one owner action naming an earlier version number: it publishes that version’s exact graph as a new version whose change record (`rollback_of`) names the restored version, under the same publish checks as any publish (TEAM-004), audited as a publish, and leaves the draft as it was; rolling back to the version already published is refused. The workflow’s history lists every saved draft edit, newest first, with its author, time, the fields it changed (name, description, folder, graph, settings), the SHA-256 digest of the saved draft graph and the published version it started from.

**Acceptance evidence:** Start a production run, edit and test its mapping in a draft, promote the draft and roll back; verify the in-flight run uses its original graph, tests use test accounts and all three deployments remain attributable. Test a draft action live against a production connection: verify the named confirmation, a test-labeled history and audit entry, no production run or usage counted, and that the next production run still uses the published version. Save five draft edits and verify each is listed in the workflow’s version history with its author, time and change; roll back with one action from the history to an earlier published version and verify the rollback is in the audit and the next run uses that version’s graph.

#### WORK-009 — Collect-data human steps.

A collect-data step pauses a run to ask a person for typed fields (text, number, USD amount, date, choice, checkbox, file) before later steps continue. The builder sets the form, assignees (workspace members, a role, or an external recipient by email link that grants access to that one request only), a due time on a business calendar, reminders and an escalation target. Assignees are notified by email, Slack, Microsoft Teams or Nook and mobile push, each with an authenticated link. Answers are validated, recorded with the answering person and time, and map into later steps by field; the run resumes the exact paused step once. Unanswered requests remind, then escalate, then follow the configured timeout branch; late or duplicate answers after resolution are recorded and ignored.

DATA-001 applies before this capability ships: include its collected human data in the versioned portable inventory and restore them without execution or receiving authority.

AGENT-004 inheritance: every added human question/fact kind inherits all AGENT-004 obligations and acceptance before shipping, including proof of owner-named native contact authority, calendar/cadence limits, unanswered escalation, revocation and deactivation fencing, exactly one authorized human continuation, late/duplicate refusal, takeover/cancellation, audited contacts, and complete inactive portability/erasure through named public-door journeys. Routing grants no workflow access or approval rights.

**Delivered native slice (c33, owner-only answer default pending ct):** A collect step declares text, finite JSON number, USD decimal string (canonical cents; no rounding of extra precision), actual YYYY-MM-DD date, explicit choice or checkbox fields. The native owner answers through the existing digest-bound decision form; no role, person or external email-link assignment is implied. The existing owner-authorized native-inbox follow-up retains business calendars, cadence, escalation and revocable contact authority without granting read/answer rights to a contact. One typed answer resumes the original step; duplicate or resolved-late submissions are audited without another continuation. A declared calendar timeout produces a separate timeout outcome, never an answer or approval. Question values use the existing per-class sealed run/wait inventory, immediate blind indexing, retention and run erasure; archived waits restore without receiving authority. File fields, role/external assignments, rich typed form controls and the complete provider journey remain unbuilt; WORK-009 is partial.

**Acceptance evidence:** Publish a workflow with a collect-data step requesting a PO number and a USD amount from a sales role; trigger it late on a Friday, restart the service over the weekend and observe the Monday reminder and then the escalation to the configured manager; answer through the emailed link, verify the run resumes the exact step and the provider readback shows the answered values; submit the same link again and verify one continuation; let a second request pass its deadline and verify the timeout branch runs. Export and restore these collected human data, compare their full portable records and assert inactive receiving state under DATA-001.

#### WORK-010 — Digest steps that collect across runs.

A digest step accumulates entries across many runs and releases them together. Each digest has a name, an entry template (text, or structured fields kept as a list) and a release rule: daily, weekly or monthly at a chosen time and day in an IANA timezone, when a count threshold is reached, or manual only. Steps can **append entry**, **find digest** (read the current entries and count without releasing) and **release now**; release either clears the digest or keeps its entries. Each release is one durable run with a stable occurrence identity, so a restart, redeploy or DST change neither drops nor double-releases a digest, and an entry appended during a release lands in exactly one release. The released text or list maps into later steps (a Slack post, an EXEC-007 email, a sheet row); entries keep their source run links, an empty digest follows a builder-chosen skip or send-empty policy, and digests have retention and erasure under DATA-002/DATA-003.

DATA-001 applies before this capability ships: include its digest state in the versioned portable inventory and restore them without execution or receiving authority.

**Acceptance evidence:** Publish a “new lead → append to Today’s leads” workflow with a daily 5 p.m. America/Chicago release to Slack; append 7 lead entries through the day, restart the service before 5 p.m. and verify one Slack message lists all 7 and a find-digest step then shows it empty; append during a release and verify the entry appears in exactly one release; cross a DST change with a daily digest and verify one release per day; release a manual-only digest on demand and verify a keep-entries release leaves its entries; migrate a Zap whose Digest by Zapier step uses a weekly schedule and verify the coverage report calls it native and its parity test passes. Export and restore these digest state, compare their full portable records and assert inactive receiving state under DATA-001.

#### WORK-011 — Search steps: found, not found, several found, and find or create.

Every search operation, in every native connector, every CONN-011 custom connector and every WORK-007 workflow table, has three declared settings that a builder sets without code and that run history records on each run:

- **Create if not found:** an optional write on the same connection with its own mapped fields (WORK-002 and WORK-012), which turns the search into a find-or-create step. The step outputs the record plus an outcome of `found` or `created` that later steps, filters and paths can test, and run history shows which one happened.
- **No-match outcome:** either *halt*, which ends the run with the non-error status `stopped by search` (shown and filterable in EXEC-005 run history, counted apart from failures in OPS-001, and sending no EXEC-003 failure notice), or *continue*, which passes an explicit empty result with the outcome `not found` that WORK-013 filters and paths can branch on. A provider error, denied scope, rate limit or timeout is never reported as no match; it is a failure under EXEC-002 and EXEC-003.
- **Multi-match outcome:** *first*, by a declared sort field and direction (for example most recently updated); *stop*, with the named outcome `multiple matches`, which halts or routes to a branch as the builder chooses; or *all*, which returns every match up to a declared bound (paginating the provider) as an array for WORK-003 loops or WORK-002 line items, with the match count as an output and a named outcome when the bound truncates results.

Search keys are typed. Exact or case-insensitive matching is declared per field, emails compare case-insensitively after trimming, and a search whose key resolves to an empty value is a named validation error, never a match-all. A find-or-create is a mutating step under EXEC-006: its create carries a stable operation identity and the provider’s idempotency or unique key where one exists; if a create’s response is lost, Crank reads back by the search key before any retry; and concurrent runs for the same connection and normalized key are serialized, so they produce one record, with one run reporting `created` and the others `found`. A create the provider refuses as a duplicate (for example HubSpot’s existing-contact conflict) is resolved by readback to `found`, not raised as a failure. MIG-001, MIG-002 and MIG-003 carry these settings across from n8n, Zapier and Make search steps.

**Acceptance evidence:** Using a HubSpot sandbox, publish a workflow with a “Find or create contact by email” step: a new email creates the contact, run history shows `created` and readback shows one contact; the same email in a second run reports `found` and creates nothing; two concurrent runs for a third new email produce exactly one contact, one reporting `created` and one `found`; lose the create response on a fourth email and verify readback by email before any retry and one contact. Set a no-match search to halt and verify the run ends as `stopped by search` with no EXEC-003 failure notice; set the same search to continue and verify it routes to a “not found” path. Search for a company name matching 3 companies: it returns the first by the declared sort when set to first, stops with the named `multiple matches` outcome when set to stop, and drives a 3-iteration WORK-003 loop when set to all. Make the provider return 500 during a search and verify a failure, not `not found`; map an empty email as the key and verify a named validation error and no search. Repeat the halt and continue settings on a WORK-007 table lookup and a CONN-011 custom connector search with the same outcomes. Migrate a Zap whose HubSpot search uses “create if it doesn’t exist” and verify the coverage report calls it native and its parity test passes.

#### WORK-012 — Built-in no-code transforms.

Transform steps, and the same functions inline in any field mapping, provide without code at least the operations of Zapier Formatter’s four families:

- **Text:** split by a separator or by a name rule (first word and the rest, or last word and the rest) with a segment choice of first, last, by index or all as a list; extract email, URL, phone number (normalized to E.164, US default region), number and regular expression with capture groups (first match or all); find and replace, literal or by pattern; case (upper, lower, title, sentence); trim and collapse whitespace; truncate with an optional ellipsis; strip HTML to plain text, keeping line breaks and link text; Markdown to HTML and HTML to Markdown; default value when empty; URL-encode and URL-decode; length and word count.
- **Numbers:** arithmetic (add, subtract, multiply, divide, negate) and spreadsheet-style formulas (SUM, ROUND, ROUNDUP, ROUNDDOWN, MIN, MAX, ABS, IF) over mapped values in exact decimal arithmetic with a declared scale and rounding mode (half-up by default for USD, half-even selectable); parse a number or amount from formatted text such as `$1,234.50`; format a number (separators, decimals) and a currency (USD by default, any ISO 4217 code).
- **Date/Time:** parse from ISO 8601, Unix time and common US formats with a declared input timezone; format to a chosen pattern in an IANA timezone; add or subtract years, months, weeks, days, hours and minutes, and business days on the WORK-004 business calendar (weekends and that calendar’s holidays skipped); compare two dates for earlier, later or equal and their difference in a chosen unit.
- **Utilities:** lookup table with a default value, either static in the step or backed by a WORK-007 table; pick from list (first, last, by index, random); text to list and list to text with a chosen separator; count items; remove duplicates; and the WORK-002 line-itemizer.

Every transform is typed: its inputs and output have declared types, the builder previews its output on the step’s WORK-014 sample data, with the sample’s source named, before saving, and a value that cannot be parsed (a date, number, amount or phone number) raises a named validation error that halts or routes under EXEC-003, instead of writing an empty string, zero or the raw input downstream. Transforms are deterministic and run in the workflow engine with no code step, model call or external request. MIG-002 maps each Zapier Formatter transform and option to one of these or names it as a manual conversion in the coverage report; MIG-003 and MIG-001 do the same for Make’s built-in functions and n8n’s built-in transformation nodes.

**Acceptance evidence:** Build one workflow from a web form sample with no WORK-005 code step and no AI step that splits “Mary Ann O’Neil” into first name “Mary Ann” and last name “O’Neil” by the last-word rule; extracts the email and phone from a free-text message, the phone normalized to E.164; maps “TX” to its sales rep through a lookup table and an unknown state to the default rep; computes a due date of close date + 30 days (20 November 2026 → 20 December 2026) and close + 10 business days on a US federal holiday calendar across Thanksgiving (→ 7 December 2026) in America/Chicago; computes 3 × $19.99 × 1.0825 = $64.92 exactly; and strips HTML from an email body. Preview each step on the sample before saving, run the published workflow and verify each output by readback of the destination record. Send an unparseable date and verify a named validation failure and no write. Migrate a Zap using Formatter split, lookup table, add/subtract time and perform math and verify the coverage report calls each step native and its parity test passes. Map a missing company to “Individual” with default value when empty and verify a lead without a company writes “Individual” while a lead with one keeps its company.

#### WORK-013 — Filter and path condition language.

Every filter step, every path rule, and every routing condition on a WORK-011 search outcome, a WORK-007 table lookup or an EXEC-003 error branch uses one condition language that a builder sets without code. Each rule names a mapped field, an operator and an operand (typed, picked or mapped from an earlier step), and the operator set is:

- **Text:** contains, exactly matches, is in a list (typed in the rule or mapped as a list), starts with, ends with and matches pattern (regular expression), each with its negation (does not contain, does not exactly match, is not in a list, does not start with, does not end with, does not match pattern). Text rules are case-insensitive by default with a per-rule case-sensitive switch, and leading and trailing whitespace is ignored unless the builder chooses otherwise.
- **Number and USD amount:** greater than, less than, equal to, not equal to, greater than or equal to and less than or equal to. Operands are parsed with the WORK-012 number and amount rules (so `$1,234.50`, `1234.5` and `100` are numbers) and compared as exact decimals, never as text: `100` is greater than `99`.
- **Date/time:** after, before, equals, on or after and on or before, comparing instants or, when the builder chooses day precision, calendar days. Both sides resolve in a declared IANA timezone (the workspace default unless set on the rule). Operands may be relative: now, today, start of this week or month, now plus or minus N minutes, hours, days, weeks or months, and plus or minus N business days on the WORK-004 business calendar.
- **Boolean:** is true and is false, accepting the field type’s declared true and false forms (true/false, yes/no, 1/0).
- **Existence:** exists and does not exist (the field is absent or null), and is empty and is not empty (present as an empty string, whitespace only or an empty list), keeping WORK-002’s distinction between missing, null and empty; the rule trace shows which of the three the value was.
- **Lists:** for an array field, any item matches or every item matches the inner rule, and list length compared as a number.

**Rule groups.** Rules combine with AND inside a group, and groups combine with OR. A filter or path rule allows at least 50 rules per group and 20 OR groups; the limits are stated in the editor and are never below these.

**Paths.** A path group holds at least 20 branches (Zapier allows 10) and nests at least 5 levels deep (Zapier allows 3). Each group is **exclusive**, running only the first matching branch in the declared order, or **parallel**, running every matching branch as its own branch of the same run with its own step history and an optional WORK-003 join. Each group may have one **fallback** branch, which runs only when no other branch matches, or one **always-run** branch, which runs whatever else matches, but not both. The editor warns before publish when a group has no fallback, and a run in which no branch matches and no fallback exists ends as `stopped by filter`.

**Type mismatches.** A value that cannot be read as the rule’s type (text in a number or USD rule, an unparseable date, a list in a boolean rule) produces the named outcome `type mismatch`, which names the rule, the field and the value. The builder chooses per filter or path group whether a type mismatch halts the run as a validation failure under EXEC-003 (the default) or routes to a declared branch. It is never a silent pass or fail.

**Preview.** Before saving, the editor shows each rule’s resolved operands and pass or fail, and each group’s and branch’s result, on the step’s WORK-014 samples, naming each sample’s source.

**Run history.** A run that a filter stops, or in which no path branch matches, ends with the non-error status `stopped by filter`. Run history (EXEC-005) shows the stopping group, each rule’s resolved operands and its result, and the status is filterable there, counted apart from failures in OPS-001, sends no EXEC-003 failure notice and does not count toward EXEC-003 auto-pause. Every path group in a run records which branch or branches ran and the rule results that chose them. The builder previews each rule’s result on the step’s sample data before saving.

**Migration.** MIG-002 maps every Zapier filter and path rule operator (text, number, date/time, boolean and exists rules), each AND/OR group, and each fallback and always-run branch to a committed operator here. MIG-003 maps every Make filter operator (text, numeric, date, time, array and boolean operators, their case-insensitive variants, matches pattern, exists and does not exist) and router fallback routes. MIG-001 maps n8n IF, Filter and Switch conditions (string, number, date, boolean, array and object operators, the AND/OR combinator, ignore case, loose type validation and the Switch fallback output). An operator with no committed equivalent is named as a manual conversion in the coverage report, never dropped.

**Acceptance evidence:** Build a lead workflow with no WORK-005 code step and no AI step, in America/Chicago: path A is “state is in TX, OK, LA” AND “amount greater than 5000”; path B is “close date after today” OR “email ends with .gov”; a fallback branch catches the rest. In parallel mode send 6 sample leads (TX $6,000 closing yesterday; CA $100 closing tomorrow; OK $7,500 closing tomorrow; NY $200 closed last week at an agency.gov address; FL $300 closed last week; LA amount “5000” closed last week) and verify by readback that they took A; B; A and B; B; fallback; and fallback respectively. Switch the group to exclusive and verify the OK lead runs only A. Send “100” against “greater than 99” and verify a numeric pass; send “abc” against a number rule and verify the named `type mismatch` outcome and no write. Verify “email contains ACME.com” matches a lower-case address at the domain acme.com by default and not once the rule is case-sensitive; verify a missing field, a null field and an empty string give distinct exists and is-empty results. Add an always-run branch to a second group and verify it runs alongside the matching branch, and verify the editor refuses a group with both a fallback and an always-run branch. Verify a filtered-out run appears in run history as `stopped by filter` with the stopping rule and its resolved operands, sends no EXEC-003 notice, and that 20 such runs do not auto-pause the workflow. Migrate a Zap with an AND/OR filter and a Paths group with a fallback branch, a Make scenario whose router has a fallback route and a numeric filter, and an n8n workflow with an IF node and a Switch node with a fallback output: verify the coverage report calls each native and each parity test passes.

#### WORK-014 — Step tests on real samples.

Every step in the builder has a **test** that produces the sample later steps map from, and the editor always shows where each sample came from (connected account, live delivery, earlier run, action response, connector schema or manual). Samples are real data from the buyer’s own accounts wherever the step can produce one:

- **Polling and app trigger tests:** testing a trigger loads at least the three most recent records from the step’s bound connection, newest first, each labeled with its source record ID and its created or modified time, with every field value shown as loaded under CONN-019 (hidden form fields, custom properties and file references included). A **find new records** action fetches fresher ones, and the builder chooses which record becomes the step’s sample. For updated-record triggers (TRIG-008) a sample carries the watched fields’ previous and current values where the provider or snapshot holds them. Loading samples is read-only: it starts no run, advances no polling cursor or TRIG-008 snapshot, and is never counted against production deduplication.
- **Webhook, form, inbound-email and feed trigger tests:** the editor shows the draft’s URL or address (TRIG-001 secret URL, TRIG-006 alias, WORK-007 form link) and waits for the next real delivery, then offers it as the sample with its parsed fields, raw body, headers, query and files; TRIG-007 feeds and URL polls load their latest items. A delivery received in test mode starts no production run. A typed or pasted sample is allowed only as an explicit **manual sample**, labeled as such in the editor, in every preview built on it and in the test record.
- **Earlier runs as samples:** any retained EXEC-005 run of the workflow, including history captured during MIG-001, MIG-002 or MIG-003 migration, can be loaded as the trigger sample or as a step’s sample output. Loading obeys DATA-003 retention and EXEC-005 payload read permissions: a builder without payload access cannot load the run, and redacted fields stay redacted in the sample.
- **Action tests:** testing a create, update, delete or send step either runs live against the step’s bound connection after a confirmation that names the exact effect, the target app and the account (for example “Create 1 contact in HubSpot account Acme Sales”), or, with no confirmation, runs against a declared test-account binding (WORK-008). The provider’s real response (record IDs, URLs and returned fields) becomes the step’s sample output, mappable in later steps. Every test write is recorded in the SEC-003 audit and in run history as a **test run** attributed to the builder; it is never shown as a production run in OPS-001, never counts toward OPS-002 usage limits or spending controls, never raises EXEC-003 production alerts or auto-pause, and authorizes nothing in production (TEAM-004). A live test write is still bound by TEAM-002 limits: a test above a limit requires the same approval as a production run.
- **Search and read tests:** WORK-011 search steps, lookups and other read-only steps test against the live connection with no confirmation and no write; a find-or-create test asks for confirmation only when its create branch would run.
- **Untested steps:** a builder may skip an action test; later steps then map from the connector’s declared output schema with typed example values, labeled **schema sample, not tested**, and the publish check lists every step whose mapping relies on one.
- **Previews and freshness:** every downstream preview (WORK-002 mappings, WORK-012 transforms, WORK-013 rule and branch results, WORK-011 outcomes) runs on the chosen samples and names their source. After a CONN-019 refresh fields or a change to the step’s connector schema version, a sample older than the step’s current schema is flagged **stale**, naming the fields it lacks, until it is reloaded.

DATA-001 applies before this capability ships: include its sample records in the versioned portable inventory and restore them without execution or receiving authority.

**Acceptance evidence:** On a draft Typeform → HubSpot → Slack workflow, test the Typeform trigger and verify it loads the last 3 real responses from the test account, newest first, with their response IDs and times, and that loading them started no run; pick the second response and verify its hidden UTM value appears in a downstream WORK-012 preview labeled with that response’s ID. Submit a new response, use find new records and verify it appears at the top. Test a webhook trigger and verify the editor waits for and captures a real form-encoded POST to the draft URL as the sample with no production run; type a sample by hand and verify it is labeled manual sample in the editor and in a downstream preview. Load a 3-day-old run from history as the trigger sample, then verify a reader without payload access cannot load it. Test the HubSpot “create contact” step: verify the confirmation names the HubSpot account, exactly one contact is created and verified by readback, a test-labeled audit entry and test run are recorded, and the returned contact ID is mappable in the Slack step; rebind the step to a declared test account and verify the test runs with no confirmation and the contact exists only in the test account. Test a WORK-011 search step and verify no write and no confirmation. Verify none of these tests appear as production runs in OPS-001, count toward OPS-002 usage limits or raise an EXEC-003 alert. Add a question to the Typeform, refresh fields and verify the earlier sample is flagged stale naming the new question until a new record is loaded. Skip the Slack step’s test and verify the publish check lists it as relying on a schema sample. Export and restore these sample records, compare their full portable records and assert inactive receiving state under DATA-001.

### Connections and triggers

#### CONN-001 — Discoverable connector library.

The catalog describes each app’s supported triggers/actions, searchable objects and custom fields, authentication, scopes, pagination, attachments, API version, limits and known restrictions. Builders select reusable personal or team connections and test access before activation. Every input that names an account resource is a CONN-019 live picker, and discovered custom fields load as mappable step inputs through CONN-019. Unsupported actions are explicit and have a custom-connector path; a generic HTTP form is not a native app connector. Every search operation in the catalog follows WORK-011: it offers create-if-not-found where the app has a matching create action, and declares its no-match and multi-match outcomes.

Breadth is a stated commitment, not an aspiration. Every app on Zapier’s popular-apps list ([zapier.com/apps](https://zapier.com/apps)) as of 16 October 2026 has a named native connector with at least one trigger, one search and one action: Google Sheets, Google Drive (CONN-005); Gmail, Microsoft Outlook (CONN-003); Slack (CONN-004); HubSpot, Salesforce (CONN-006); Stripe (CONN-008); Facebook Lead Ads, Google Forms, Typeform, Jotform, Gravity Forms (CONN-012); Google Calendar, Calendly (CONN-013); Notion, Trello, monday.com, Google Docs (CONN-014); Mailchimp, LeadConnector (CONN-015); Airtable (CONN-005). Everyday SMB apps beyond that list are also named: Microsoft Excel, OneDrive and SharePoint (CONN-005), Zoom (CONN-013), Asana and ClickUp (CONN-014), Pipedrive (CONN-015), Dropbox, Box, DocuSign and PandaDoc (CONN-016), Twilio SMS (CONN-017), and Square, PayPal and WooCommerce (CONN-018). Zapier’s built-in tools map to named clauses: Webhooks catch hooks and requests (TRIG-001, HTTP-002), Webhooks Retrieve Poll and RSS (TRIG-007), Email (TRIG-006, EXEC-007), Formatter text, numbers, date/time and utilities (WORK-012), Filter/Paths with their full rule language, fallback and always-run branches (WORK-013), Formatter Line-itemizer and line-item fields (WORK-002), search steps with “create if it doesn’t exist” and their no-match and multiple-result settings (WORK-011), Digest (WORK-010), Delay (WORK-004), Schedule (TRIG-002), Transfer (TRIG-002 historical runs), Code (WORK-005), Looping (WORK-003), Sub-Zaps (WORK-006), Storage/Tables/Forms/Interfaces (WORK-007), AI by Zapier (Analyze and Return Data to AI-001 analyze and classify, Extract Content From URL to AI-001 extract content from URL, Search Content Across URLs to AI-001 search content across URLs), Human in the Loop (TEAM-005, WORK-009) and MCP (PLATFORM-002). For the long tail, an agent builds a connector on demand from the provider’s public API documentation or OpenAPI description under CONN-011, with the same sandbox acceptance as a native connector.

AI apps are named native connectors too, run by AI-001 on a CONN-002 model connection:

- **ChatGPT (OpenAI):** Send Prompt, Conversation and Write an Email map to send prompt and conversation; Extract Structured Data to extract structured data; Analyze Images and the other analysis actions to analyze and classify; Create Transcription to transcribe; Create Translation to translate; Generate An Image to generate image; and its file searches and Find or Create File to model files.
- **Anthropic (Claude):** Send Message maps to send prompt and conversation; Upload File and its file searches map to model files.

The same mapping applies to Make’s and n8n’s OpenAI and Anthropic modules and nodes. An AI step reports native only when AI-001 supports its exact operation and its input type (text, file, image, audio or URL); any other operation of these apps reports agent-buildable under CONN-011, never native.

A coverage report reads a buyer’s automation inventory (a Zapier JSON export, the itemized MIG-002 inventory, a Make/Workato/n8n/Pipedream export, or a typed list of apps and events) and reports for each app and each trigger/action used: **native** (named connector and operation exist), **agent-buildable** (public API and supported auth exist; CONN-011 build with its estimated scope), or **blocked** (with the reason, such as partner-only API or no public API, and the buyer’s workaround through HTTP-002 or a provider partner). For every app outside that popular-apps list, operation depth is set by its connector clause: an operation reports native only when the clause that names the app (CONN-003 to CONN-018) names that trigger, search or action, and any other operation of a named app reports agent-buildable under CONN-011 or blocked, never native. A search used with a create-if-not-found or outcome setting, a Formatter transform, a filter or path rule, and a chosen account resource each report native only when WORK-011, WORK-012, WORK-013 or CONN-019 respectively supports that exact setting, operator or resource.

**Acceptance evidence:** Find a CRM connector by a business action, connect a test account, discover custom fields and see them load as mappable step inputs through a CONN-019 picker, test a paginated lookup and inspect the exact action scope and unsupported-operation message before publishing. Feed the coverage report a 60-Zap SMB inventory built only from Zapier’s 22 popular apps, using a fixed operation list committed with the test: for each app, every trigger, search and action used by that app’s ten most-used Zapier templates as captured on 16 October 2026, plus the built-in tools mapped above (including RSS, Retrieve Poll, Digest, Line-itemizer, every Formatter transform those templates use, every filter and path rule operator and fallback they use, every chosen account resource, and every search with “create if it doesn’t exist” or a no-match or multiple-result setting): every app, operation and setting reports native. Add three long-tail apps (one with a public OpenAPI description, one with documented REST but no OpenAPI, one with a partner-only API) and verify agent-buildable, agent-buildable and blocked-with-reason respectively. #### CONN-002 — Managed OAuth, keys and connection lifecycle.

Owners authorize multiple accounts through provider OAuth or scoped API keys; Crank encrypts credentials under installation-controlled custody, refreshes tokens, rotates keys, tracks consent and permits team ownership transfer. Revocation stops new work, records in-flight uncertainty and tells affected workflow owners how to reconnect. Secrets never appear in graphs, logs, prompts, exports or browser reads; new scopes need fresh consent.

EXEC-002 currently keys request rate/concurrency buckets per connection, never by an editable name or credential text. When this clause adds provider-verified stable account identity, connections with the same provider app and verified account ID must share that account’s rate/concurrency bucket before the capability ships.

**Delivered renewal semantics (c33):** A scheduled run renews an expired OAuth token without an owner session. Connection state and the owner-only history expose the previous expiry, renewal time and new expiry without tokens. Concurrent requests serialize rotating-token exchanges; a late exchange cannot overwrite a revoked or rotated credential. A provider-returned scope outside the existing grant requires fresh consent and pauses access; an unconfirmed or interrupted exchange requires reconnection rather than blind refresh reuse. Renewal leases are installation-local and excluded from archives. This slice adds no provider-verified account identity: admission remains per connection until the verified provider-app/account capability ships.

**Acceptance evidence:** Connect two accounts, select one per step, expire and refresh OAuth, rotate an API key, revoke the connection during a run and reconnect with a narrower grant; verify dependent workflows pause visibly and no secret appears in API state, exports or agent context. Let a connected OAuth account’s access token expire overnight with no one signed in: verify the next scheduled run refreshes it before its provider call and succeeds with no owner action, and that the connection’s history shows the expiry time and the automatic renewal. Search run history, step logs, the audit and an export for the stored secret and the refreshed token and find neither.

#### CONN-011 — Custom, enterprise and private app connections: custom connectors, private gateways and pipelines.

Technical teams build versioned custom connectors from documented APIs/OpenAPI with typed inputs, pagination, OAuth/key declarations, webhook verification and reusable tests. PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, SFTP and S3-compatible data-pipeline recipes use typed connectors or reviewed custom connectors, authenticated customer-controlled private gateways and incremental checkpoints; large files stream with explicit bounds. Workato-class deployment includes environment separation and scoped service accounts.

**Private gateway rules (ct, 21 October 2026).** Only the owner enrolls a gateway, in a native browser session after the fresh email-link step-up within the preceding five minutes, with a single-use 256-bit enrollment code shown once, stored only as its SHA-256 hash, expiring after 15 minutes and naming one installation, one environment and the gateway. The gateway program generates an Ed25519 key pair on the customer host; Crank keeps only the public key and fingerprint. The gateway connects only outward to Crank over HTTPS, signs every request over method, path, body digest, timestamp and a single-use nonce, and accepts only installation-signed jobs. A gateway serves exactly one installation and one environment. It does nothing until the owner grants it one connector at an exact version, named operations and named private destinations; a new connector version needs a new grant, and every grant change bumps the TEAM-001 authority revision. Database, SFTP and storage credentials stay on the gateway host, referenced by name, and never reach Crank, run history, logs, audit or archives. Crank and the gateway each check status, environment, grant revision, connector version, operation and destination on every dispatch; the gateway runs only the granted version's typed operations against granted destinations after its own resolution, follows no redirect, always refuses link-local and metadata addresses and is never an arbitrary network proxy. Owners and admins revoke a gateway or grant without step-up, effective from the next dispatch; later results are withheld and the run fails with `gateway revoked`. A request for another environment's gateway, connection or secret is refused, audited and shown as a named access decision. A scoped service account is an owner-minted non-person credential bound to one environment and to workflow and connection scopes no wider than the owner's live authority, shown once, stored only as a hash, expiring (365 days by default, 730 at most), suspended when its authority ends and never transferred. SEC-003 audits codes, grants, revocations and refused dispatches without secrets or payloads; archives carry no code, gateway key or grant authority, so a restore brings gateways back revoked and grants inactive. SEC-002, SEC-003, TEAM-001, TEAM-003, DATA-001, DATA-002, BASE-003, WORK-011 and CONN-020 inherit these rules.
