#### TRIG-001 — Scoped, deduplicated webhook admission.

Every workflow can receive webhooks from senders that cannot add custom headers or wrap their payload. Each flow has one or more inbound URLs with an embedded random secret that the owner can revoke and rotate (old and new URLs overlap for a chosen window), plus optional header credentials (the existing scoped bearer trigger credential). Builders can require provider signature verification: HMAC-SHA256/SHA1 over the raw body or a signed timestamped payload with replay tolerance, with presets for Stripe, Shopify, Calendly, GitHub, Typeform and Twilio. The URL accepts POST, PUT and GET with JSON, form-encoded, multipart (with files) or raw bodies; a raw mode exposes the body text, headers and query string to mapping alongside the parsed fields. Deduplication uses a builder-chosen key path (for example `data.id` or a header) or, when the payload has no ID, a SHA-256 digest of the normalized body within a stated window (default 24 hours, configurable from 1 minute to 30 days). The response is configurable: an immediate status/body/headers, or a synchronous response produced by the workflow within a bounded timeout. Crank’s `{event_id,input}` envelope remains one supported mode: stable source event identity deduplicates equal payloads, rejects changed payloads under the same ID and respects an erased-event fence. No inbound credential can read workspace data, approve or activate work, and revocation takes effect at the server.

Secret-URL envelope identities are permanent within their workflow: the same canonical input returns its existing run (or held decision), and changed input under that ID is a conflict even after the ordinary body-digest window. Header delivery metadata does not change that identity. Query-only GET fallback identities hash the method and normalized query; other body fallback identities hash the normalized body and file contents. Ordinary identities become eligible again when their receipt time is at or before the current time minus the configured window; still-held items remain deduplicated until decided. Admission commits the identity, uploaded files and either its queued run or held item together, repeating current hook/version and erased-event authority inside that transaction. Interrupted admission leaves no accepted identity without durable work.

Owner erasure of a terminal multi-step run requires its workflow paused (`POST /api/crank/data/erase`, `workflow_run_id`, `confirm:"ERASE"`). An opaque event-key digest permanently fences its webhook redelivery, including after restart and portable restore. Erasure preserves the audit chronology with its run subject anonymized and sensitive detail removed; payload/decision copies in linked run, step, wait, attempt, hold and obligation rows are removed. This does not claim complete subject/operator/file erasure under DATA-002.

**Acceptance evidence:** Call the public trigger endpoint with an active flow key, resend the same event, change its payload, send to another flow and revoke the key; verify a single pending run, conflicts/refusals and no unauthorized reads. Send a form-encoded POST with no auth header and no event ID to a flow’s secret URL and verify exactly one run with the fields mapped; resend it inside the dedup window and verify no run; send it after the window and verify a new run; send a Stripe-signed event with a valid and then a tampered signature and verify one run and one refusal; send a GET with query parameters and a multipart POST with a file in raw mode and inspect headers, query and file as mapped data; configure a synchronous JSON response and verify the sender receives it; rotate the URL and verify the old URL stops after the overlap.

#### TRIG-002 — Schedules and on-demand runs.

Owners start a run on demand or schedule intervals, daily/weekly business times and calendar-aware recurrence in an IANA timezone. A historical run applies a published workflow to existing source records the owner selects by filter or date range (for example last quarter’s closed deals), with a preview of the count, sample records and estimated USD cost before any effect (as in TRIG-005), runs selected or all items once each by source ID, and reports per-item outcomes. DST behavior, missed-run catch-up/skip policy and concurrent-run policy are inspectable. Due occurrences have stable identities, continue unattended and do not duplicate after restart or clock movement.

Historical runs currently read complete, bounded JSON lists through an authorized HTTP source connection (or a public source), keeping an immutable snapshot of the selected records and published version. Source IDs are strings (safe integer IDs convert to decimal strings), deduplicated within that snapshot; identical duplicate records collapse and conflicting records fail the preview. The selected record is the run’s trigger payload unchanged. A new preview is an explicit new historical batch; repeat or concurrent release of one batch never reruns a source ID. Every record/list door added under CONN-003–019 or WORK-007 inherits this count/sample/cost/selection and release obligation before it ships.

Selection uses WORK-013 filters on `trigger.<field>` at the preview’s recorded clock and timezone. Date-range bounds are inclusive UTC instants; date-only bounds cover the entire UTC day. Cost components for orchestration, connectors, models and executors are explicit owner-supplied USD per-run estimates with assumptions, labeled **owner estimate; not provider-verified**; no zero price is invented. Components are summed exactly, multiplied by the selected count and rounded half-up to cents once. The owner releases selected IDs or all remaining records with the preview fingerprint. Paused/replaced versions cannot start a release; per-item outcomes link to the actual runs. Resource bounds fail visibly rather than showing a truncated count (1,000 source records, 50 pages, 2 MiB per response and 4 MiB retained payload; narrower queries can be prepared as separate batches).

**Acceptance evidence:** Configure weekday 9 a.m. America/New_York execution, an interval and an on-demand run; cross both DST changes and restart during a due occurrence, then inspect the planned and actual times and exactly one admitted run per due occurrence. Start a historical run over last quarter’s 40 closed test deals: verify the preview shows 40 items and an estimated USD cost with no effects, run 10 selected items and then the rest, and verify exactly 40 runs, one per deal, with per-item outcomes.

#### TRIG-003 — App, polling and email triggers.

Native event subscriptions and polling discover new/changed app records and incoming email automatically. Verified signatures, renewable subscriptions, paginated cursors, overlap windows, source IDs and deduplication handle delayed/out-of-order deliveries and outages. The owner chooses initial backfill and can see the last successful poll and next due action. Every updated-record trigger follows TRIG-008: watched fields or an explicit any-field choice, optional changed-to values, previous and current values in the run, provider change events or per-record snapshots, and a declared dedup identity. Polling frequency and trigger latency are committed in TRIG-004, burst holds in TRIG-005, mailbox-free email triggers in TRIG-006, and feed and arbitrary-URL polling in TRIG-007.

**Acceptance evidence:** Activate an email and CRM polling workflow, return overlapping pages and out-of-order webhook events, expire a subscription and restart polling after an outage; verify no lost admitted records, duplicate business actions or silent subscription failure. Edit an unwatched property of a CRM record whose trigger watches its stage and verify no run (TRIG-008).

#### TRIG-004 — Polling frequency and trigger latency.

Each polling workflow has its own interval, chosen from 1, 2, 5, 15, 30 and 60 minutes or a longer schedule; the 1-minute floor is available on every installation with no plan gate, and a provider whose rate limit cannot sustain the chosen interval shows the slowest safe interval before publish. With a healthy executor each poll starts within 30 seconds of its due time. Instant triggers (webhooks, app subscriptions, form submissions and inbound email) admit an event and start its run within 10 seconds of receipt at the 95th percentile. Every run records its trigger-to-start latency (source event time where the provider supplies one, receipt time and run start), and OPS-001 reports latency percentiles per workflow against the configured interval, flagging late polls with their cause (provider rate limit, executor backlog, outage).

**Acceptance evidence:** Publish a “new HubSpot deal → Slack” workflow at a 1-minute interval and an instant Typeform workflow; create 30 deals and 30 submissions spread over an hour; verify every deal run starts no later than 1 minute 30 seconds after the deal’s creation, every form run starts within 10 seconds of receipt at p95, and each run’s history shows its measured latency; throttle the HubSpot test edge with 429s and verify the late polls are flagged with “provider rate limit” in OPS-001; choose an interval faster than a provider allows and verify the pre-publish warning.

#### TRIG-005 — Flood protection for bursts of trigger events.

Each workflow has a burst threshold (default 100 new records in one poll, or 100 instant events in one minute; configurable from 1 to 10,000). When a poll or burst exceeds it, Crank creates no business effects for the excess: it holds the whole burst as one reviewable batch, notifies the workflow owner (EXEC-003 channels), and shows the count, source, sample records and estimated USD cost. The owner can run all, run selected items, or discard; held events stay deduplicated by source ID and retained until decided, with reminders and an optional owner-chosen expiry. Releases are attributable and partial releases leave the rest held. Activation backfill (TRIG-003) remains a separate explicit choice.

The current held-batch review door is `GET /api/crank/holds/:id`: source, item count, retained samples/items, decision attribution and USD estimate state are returned together. Before any release, the owner quotes all four per-run components (orchestration, connectors, models and executors), including explicit zero quotes where applicable, with assumptions through `POST /api/crank/holds/:id/estimate`. Amounts are nonnegative USD decimals with at most eight decimal places; components sum exactly, multiply by the batch or selected item count, and round half-up to cents once. Estimates are labeled **owner estimate; not provider-verified**, as in TRIG-002. Missing pricing is labeled **cost estimate required** and releases stay blocked; no provider charge or zero is invented. OPS-002 separately owns measured usage, forecasts and spending controls.

A release supplies the reviewed `estimate_fingerprint`, binding the quoted assumptions and owner/time to the current published version and all remaining held source IDs and payload digests. New items, payload changes, a partial decision or version replacement require a fresh review. The owner may discard without a quote. A release commits its attributable decision and durable queued runs atomically; interruption before that commit leaves all selected items held, while executor loss afterwards leaves queued runs that resume once. Email is the current owner-notice channel; each notice channel added under EXEC-003 and CONN-004 inherits held-batch notices before shipping.

**Acceptance evidence:** With a threshold of 100, return 500 new contacts from one poll of a CRM test edge to a welcome-email workflow; verify zero emails and zero downstream writes, one held batch with 500 deduplicated items and an owner notice; release 20 selected items and verify exactly 20 runs and emails; return the same 500 records on the next poll and verify no new hold or duplicate items; discard the remainder and verify they never run; send 150 instant webhooks in one minute and verify the same hold.

#### TRIG-006 — Hosted inbound email addresses.

Each workflow can have its own inbound email address on the installation’s inbound domain (Cloudflare Email Routing to the Worker, or MX records the buyer points at Crank on a subdomain), so staff can forward or CC messages and vendors that can only email can start a run without mailbox OAuth. Addresses use a revocable, rotatable alias; an optional sender allowlist (addresses or domains) and SPF/DKIM/DMARC results gate admission; messages over the stated size limit (25 MB including attachments) are refused with a bounce. The parsed sender, recipients, subject, plain and HTML body, headers, forwarded-original fields and attachments (as file references under CONN-005 rules) are mappable. The Message-ID deduplicates within the TRIG-001 window, and each received message is visible in run history with its admission decision.

**Acceptance evidence:** Forward a vendor email with a PDF attachment to a workflow’s alias; extract the PO number from the body with a mapping or AI-001 node, attach the PDF to a HubSpot test record and verify one run and the record by readback; resend the same message and verify no second run; send from a non-allowlisted domain and an oversized message and verify both are refused and visible; revoke the alias and verify mail to it bounces.

#### TRIG-007 — Feed and URL polling triggers.

Two built-in triggers start runs when something new appears at a URL with no app connector. The **feed trigger** watches one or several RSS 2.0, Atom or JSON Feed URLs and starts one run per new item, deduplicated by GUID/id, falling back to the link, then to a digest of title and date; a re-published or edited item with the same identity starts no run, and an item’s title, link, summary, content, author, categories, dates and enclosures are mappable, with the source feed named when several feeds share a trigger. The **URL poll trigger** sends a GET (with mapped headers and query parameters, and authentication from a stored connection under HTTP-002 rules) to any endpoint and reads a JSON array at a chosen path, or XML/HTML items selected by XPath; the builder chooses the dedup key path (`id` by default, or any path such as `data.ref`, or a digest of the whole item), and cursor, page or link-header pagination is followed. Both triggers use TRIG-004 intervals (1-minute floor) and latency reporting, TRIG-003 activation backfill (start from now, or process existing items) and TRIG-005 flood holds; requests obey SEC-002 egress rules, so private-network, link-local and metadata addresses and redirects into them are refused, response size and parse time are bounded, and fetch, parse and auth failures are visible on the trigger with EXEC-003 notices rather than silent skips. A URL poll’s header and query values are literal text or map `{{poll.since}}` (the start of the last successful poll, ISO 8601 UTC), `{{poll.now}}` (this poll’s start) and `{{poll.interval_minutes}}`; any other mapping is refused when the workflow is saved, and a value that maps to nothing is left out, so the first poll sends no `since`. Parse time is bounded by bounding the work, because a Worker’s clock does not advance during synchronous parsing: each response is at most 2 MiB, an XML or HTML document at most 200,000 nodes, and a poll at most 10 pages; exceeding a bound is a visible trigger error with the owner notice.

**Acceptance evidence:** Publish a feed trigger on an RSS fixture at a 1-minute interval: verify the first activation follows the chosen TRIG-003 backfill option, two new items start exactly two runs, and a re-published item with the same GUID starts none; add an Atom and a JSON Feed URL to the same trigger and verify each new item names its source feed. Publish a URL poll trigger on a JSON endpoint whose records have no `id` field, deduplicated on `data.ref`, with a bearer connection and two pages: verify one run per new record across both pages and none on the next unchanged poll; poll an XML endpoint selected by XPath and verify one run per new item; point the trigger at a private-network address and at a URL that redirects to one and verify both are refused with no request sent past the refusal; return malformed JSON and verify a visible trigger error and owner notice.

#### TRIG-008 — Updated-record triggers on watched fields.

Every “updated” or “changed” trigger defines what counts as an update: in every native connector (CONN-003 to CONN-018, including CONN-005 Sheets, Excel and Airtable rows and SharePoint list items, CONN-006 leads, contacts, companies and deals, CONN-007 invoices (status, balance, due date) and customers or contacts, CONN-008 Shopify orders, customers, products and inventory levels and Stripe subscriptions and customers, CONN-009 Zendesk tickets and Jira issues, CONN-014 work items, CONN-015 subscribers, contacts, opportunities and deals, and CONN-018 orders, payments and disputes), every CONN-010 Run Edit Run product trigger, every CONN-011 custom connector trigger and WORK-007 table triggers.

- **Watched fields:** the builder chooses one or more watched fields (sheet or Excel columns, Airtable and table fields, CRM object and custom properties, a pipeline and its stage, an order, payment, fulfillment or dispute status, an inventory level, a ticket’s priority or an issue’s status) with CONN-019 pickers, or explicitly chooses **any field**. A new update trigger cannot publish without that choice, and choosing any field shows a warning that every edit starts a run. A run starts once per change to a watched field’s value; edits to unwatched fields start nothing and count as nothing.
- **Changed to and changed from:** optionally, the value or set of values a watched field must change to (stage = Closed Won, Status in {Approved}), and optionally the value it must change from, set with WORK-013 operators. A change to any other value starts nothing.
- **Change payload:** each run carries, as mappable data, the record ID, which watched fields changed, each watched field’s previous and current value, and the change time: the provider’s modified or property-history timestamp where supplied, otherwise the detecting poll’s time, labeled as such.
- **Detection:** where the provider sends property-change events or keeps property history (HubSpot property-change subscriptions and property history, Salesforce Change Data Capture and field history, Pipedrive webhooks with previous values, Zendesk ticket event webhooks and Jira issue changelogs), Crank uses them. Shopify, Stripe, Square, PayPal and WooCommerce webhooks say which record changed and carry its current state, so Crank compares them against the snapshot below. Where it does not (Google Sheets, Excel, Airtable without a last-modified field, QuickBooks Online and Xero change notifications, which name the changed record but not its previous values, polled lists and items), Crank keeps a per-record snapshot of the watched fields only and compares on each TRIG-004 poll, starting runs only for differences. Activation seeds the snapshot from current values under the TRIG-003 backfill choice, so existing values start no run unless the owner chose backfill. Snapshots are workspace data under DATA-003 retention and DATA-002 erasure, and are re-seeded with no runs when a new version changes the watched fields.
- **Dedup identity:** by default record + field + new value + change time, so a Status that goes Approved → Pending → Approved runs again on the second Approved. The builder may instead choose **first time this value is seen** (record + field + value), Zapier’s trigger-column behavior, under which a value already seen for that record never runs again. Repeated or out-of-order deliveries of one change start one run (TRIG-003), and several watched fields changing in one edit start one run that lists every changed field.
- **Partial entry:** Sheets and Excel row triggers offer an optional **settle delay** (1 to 60 minutes): a new or changed row runs only once its watched and mapped columns have stayed unchanged for the delay, with the values at release, so a row typed cell by cell is not sent half filled. An optional “required columns filled” condition holds a row until those columns are non-empty.
- **Migration:** MIG-002 maps Zapier’s trigger column (and “any column”), each Property Change trigger’s property, and Updated Deal Stage’s pipeline and stage onto watched fields and changed-to values, using the first-time-seen identity where the source used a trigger column. MIG-003 maps Make watch modules’ field and “changed” options, and MIG-001 maps n8n trigger options such as the Google Sheets Trigger’s columns to watch. Any other update setting is a named manual conversion, never a silent widening to any field.

**Acceptance evidence:** In a Google Sheets sandbox, publish “Status changes to Approved → QuickBooks Online draft invoice” with Status as the watched column and changed to Approved. Set a row’s Status to Approved and verify one draft invoice by readback; edit that row’s notes and phone cells and verify no run and no invoice; change Status to Pending and verify no run; change it back to Approved and verify exactly one more run under the default identity, and none when the trigger uses first time this value is seen. Type a new row cell by cell with a 2-minute settle delay and verify one run carrying every cell filled. Activate the trigger with “start from now” on a sheet holding 50 rows already Approved and verify no run. Verify an update trigger with no watched-field or any-field choice cannot publish. In HubSpot and Pipedrive sandboxes, move a deal to Closed Won and verify one run carrying the previous and new stage and the change time; edit that deal’s amount and description and verify no run. Publish a HubSpot Contact Property Change trigger on lifecycle stage: edit the contact’s phone and verify no run, then set lifecycle stage to SQL and verify one run. Migrate a Zap using a Google Sheets trigger column and one using HubSpot Updated Deal Stage: verify each reports native, keeps its watched column or stage by name and passes its parity test. In a Shopify development store, add a note to an order and verify no run on a trigger watching fulfillment status, then fulfill it and verify one run; in a Zendesk sandbox, add an internal note and verify no run on a trigger watching priority, then change the priority and verify one run carrying the previous and new value.

### Operate recurring work

#### EXEC-001 — Durable queues and execution checkpoints.

Activated workflows execute without a person per run under published authority and any applicable grants. Durable queues show queued/running/waiting/dead-letter states, depth, oldest age, priority and owner. Atomic claims, per-step checkpoints, concurrency limits and cancellation survive executor loss and deployment; lease expiry records uncertainty before recovery. Pausing states whether it stops intake, dispatch or both, and cancellation identifies already-started effects.

Execution priority is an integer from -100 to 100 (default 0), higher first, then receipt time and stable run ID. Each admitted version freezes `max_concurrency` (1–100, default 1); its claim counts every unexpired running lease of the same workflow across versions. Waiting, approval and paused runs occupy no execution slot. A saturated workflow is filtered before the scheduler’s candidate limit.

The Operations live inventory is independent of historical date bounds and respects its workflow/team filters; depth counts the complete inventory, with the first 100 runs shown by execution order. Dead letters are retained terminal failed runs (including uncertain writes), with their checkpoints and error category, and never dispatch automatically. An expired lease atomically marks in-flight mutating checkpoints uncertain before recovery. Cancellation fences the lease and all later dispatch, preserves completed checkpoints, and labels an already-started write uncertain because it may still complete; it does not undo effects. Paused workflows hold new trigger intake and refuse on-demand starts. New/queued/running step dispatch stops, except existing waits permitted by TEAM-004’s frozen continuation policy; those waits still check live authority and connections.

**Acceptance evidence:** Queue a multi-step batch, stop the executor before and after a remote write, restart and inspect its checkpoints and oldest pending work; verify safe continuation, cancellation and no duplicate completed effect. Also inspect queued, running, waiting and dead-letter depth, oldest receipt, published priority and accountable owner; cancel both queued and in-flight runs, inspect already-started effects, and verify paused intake and dispatch across restart.

#### EXEC-002 — Rate limits, backoff and exhaustion.

Connector workflow execution distinguishes proven-not-sent/transient failures from uncertain effects and permanent errors. Retries honor Retry-After, exponential backoff with jitter, provider/account rate limits, concurrency and attempt/time budgets. Exhausted work stays durable with its next owner action; throttling one account does not starve another. Outside runs, trigger polling/historical fetch (TRIG-003/004/007), connection consent/test/token lifecycle (CONN-002) and operational log delivery (OPS-001) retain their own lifecycle policies.

All shipped workflow request operations conform: general HTTP, public file downloads and native Slack, including pagination and readback. Safe reads default to 6 attempts: backoff is 60 seconds × 2^(completed attempts − 1) plus uniform 0–250 ms jitter, saturating at one hour. A step may explicitly set `retry_policy.read_attempts` (1–10) and `retry_policy.base_delay_ms` (1–3,600,000). Retry-After (delta seconds or HTTP date) is a lower bound; an absent/invalid header uses backoff. A provider-required wait beyond one hour durably exhausts instead of sending early. HTTP 429/502/503/504 and transient network failures retry safe reads; permanent auth errors stop. Slack POST reads declare read safety in their request identity. A mutating HTTP request makes at most 2 attempts only after a lost response with an explicit provider idempotency header; its default backoff starts at 500 ms plus the same jitter. Slack writes make one attempt. A lost write without that guarantee resumes its declared readback or remains uncertain, never blind replay. Multipart retries retain identical bytes, MIME boundary and operation key across restart.

Each request has a 60-second active wall-clock budget per execution slice. Waits of 30 seconds or less sleep in-request within that budget. Longer waits persist the exact input, immutable version, operation identity, completed-response checkpoints, original request budget identity and attempt count, park the run, and release its workflow execution slot. The first Cron tick at or after due queues it, rounding the wait up by less than one minute; workflow concurrency may delay actual execution further. History distinguishes earliest scheduled retry, Cron release and actual resume. A recorded park starts a fresh active slice on actual resume; restart without a park retains its original slice deadline. Every resumed dispatch still checks current publish authority and connections. Each actual parked interval, including Cron rounding and capacity delay, is capped at one hour; intervals are summed across the run's requests with a 24-hour total cap. Crossing either cap durably exhausts with the budget reason and next owner action. Parked runs count toward workflow concurrency only while executing.

Private, bounded completed-response checkpoints stored in 64 KiB chunks reconstruct earlier pages without refetching changed records and resume a lost write's readback phase without repeating the write. They exclude credential headers and credential query URLs, keep the existing 2 MiB HTTP, 1 MiB file and 4 MiB Slack response bounds, participate in subject-erasure review, and are deleted atomically when their step/run settles or is erased. They are portable under DATA-001 and restore inactive without receiving authority. Request identity remains a value-free digest. Retry parameters are frozen on each published/test version; existing immutable versions keep their prior defaults, and rollback retains the restored version's parameters.

Requests enforce the catalog default of 100 requests per 10-second half-open rolling window and 4 simultaneous requests per connection. Unconnected requests share an origin bucket. Retries, pagination, file downloads and readback consume the same capacity. Completed admissions remain counted for the full window after their response, so slow requests cannot create a later burst; abandoned concurrency leases expire after the bounded request deadline plus 2 seconds. Transient value-free admissions are not portable authority. CONN-002 inherits shared-account buckets when provider-verified account identity exists. CONN-003–019, HTTP-002, EXEC-007, WORK-005, AI-001 and PLATFORM-002 inherit this clause for each added workflow request capability before it ships.

**Acceptance evidence:** Run two accounts while one returns 429, then transient 503 and a permanent auth error; inspect spaced retry times, bounded attempts and a dead-letter outcome. Lose a mutating response and verify no blind retry before reconciliation. With a connector whose catalog declares 100 requests per 10 seconds per account and no builder rate setting, queue 300 steps on one account: verify no 10-second window holds more than 100 provider requests and the provider returns no 429; fail one step transiently and verify its retries wait growing, jittered gaps shown in the run's attempts. Exercise the unconfigured 1/2/4/8/16-minute backoff and a 90-second Retry-After with real elapsed time across restart. Verify slot release, due-only/concurrent Cron release, immutable input/version/operation identity, cancellation, live credential refusal, exact page/readback/multipart continuation, inactive portable restore, credential exclusion and terminal checkpoint cleanup. Restore historical one-hour/24-hour waits and an expired active slice: each exhausts without another send; retained-version and rollback parameters remain frozen.

#### EXEC-003 — Error routes, alerts and escalation.

Builders choose per-step stop, continue, fallback business branch, compensate or resume behavior without hiding the original error. Error workflows deliver deduplicated email, Slack, Nook or Teams notices containing a safe run link, failure category, accountable owner and due action. Unresolved failures escalate on a business calendar; restored work resolves the alert and stops reminders. An **auto-pause policy**, on by default with owner-set thresholds, pauses a workflow whose failure rate passes a threshold over a window (default: at least 20 runs and 95 % failed within 24 hours); runs ended by a WORK-011 `stopped by search` halt or a WORK-013 `stopped by filter` end do not count as failures. The pause stops dispatch, holds new trigger events as a TRIG-005 batch, notifies the workflow owner once with the failure categories, and on re-enable lets the owner run or discard the held events.

**Delivered slice (c33, notice-consent default pending ct):** Email and explicitly owner-consented per-workflow Slack notices are deduplicated, carry only operational kind/category, owner reference, due action and authenticated run links, and retain channel attempts. No Slack destination is enabled implicitly; changing/revoking consent cancels pending old-destination delivery. Known non-deliveries retry on minute Cron after 1/2/4/8 minutes, at most five attempts. Uncertain responses and expired send claims stop for reconciliation without automatic resend. Provider acceptance is labelled separately from development-mail suppression and does not claim mailbox receipt or a human read. Answered approvals stop pending notice delivery. Delivery/attempt history restores inactive without routes or send leases and follows run erasure. Teams/Nook and later EXEC-007/CONN-004 notice channels inherit these safety rules before shipping.

**Acceptance evidence:** Cause validation, credential and provider failures in a published workflow, exercise stop/continue/error branches, fail the alert provider and restore it, then resolve the business exception; inspect the durable error, alert delivery history and end of escalation. Fail 20 consecutive runs of one workflow and verify it auto-pauses, the owner is notified once, new trigger events are held with no effect, and re-enabling runs the selected held events once; verify 20 `stopped by search` halts do not pause a workflow. Verify a failure notice and a waiting-approval notice each reach the owner by email and in Slack within 60 seconds of the run needing them, each with a working safe run link.

#### EXEC-007 — Built-in email and SMS steps.

A send-email step works without connecting a mail provider: it sends from the installation’s own sending identity on a domain the owner verifies, through the installation’s configured transactional mail transport. Setup shows the exact SPF include, DKIM selector/key and DMARC records to publish and checks them before the first production send. The step supports mapped To/CC/BCC (bounded recipient count), reply-to, subject, plain and HTML body, and attachments by file reference; delivery, bounce and complaint events are recorded on the run, and hard-bounced or complained addresses are suppressed for later sends. A send-SMS step sends through the buyer’s Twilio connection (CONN-017) with its opt-out and registration rules; internal alerts to the workflow owner or team need no SMS account, through EXEC-007 email, Slack/Teams/Nook (CONN-004) or UX-001 mobile push. Both steps feed EXEC-003 notices and obey TEAM-004/TEAM-002 recipient and rate limits.

Recipient actions inherit TEAM-004: count actual mapped destinations (including duplicates), apply both workspace and step caps using the stricter bound, and pause only excess actions for an exact-input approval; no approval means no out-of-cap send.

Before shipping any added workflow request operation, this clause inherits EXEC-002’s provider/account admission, bounded retries and parked budgets, exact continuation/readback and uncertain-write safety, with a named public-door acceptance journey.

Before shipping added capabilities, this clause inherits BASE-001: prove owned operation and inactive, credential-free restoration, preserve input/file safety, and disclose each outgoing recipient, purpose, field category, required credential, region and retention (provider-controlled terms labelled unverified).

**AI-003 receiver duty (ct scope-review-54):** Recurring invoice-follow-up customer contact through this clause obeys AI-003's configured cadence and stops on paid, closed or void invoices, human takeover, cancellation, owner pause, expired authority or budget hold. Recipients come only from the invoice's billing contact. Re-read the connected invoice in the same dispatch before every contact, block the next dispatch after tool revocation, and retain a contact operation key to prevent duplicate sends, with one active run per invoice. The first external send of a new skill/objective version requires human approval unless a TEAM-002 standing grant covers it; the agent never approves. This receiving duty is required before this clause's contact can satisfy AI-003; it is not delivered evidence.

**Acceptance evidence:** Verify a test sending domain’s SPF, DKIM and DMARC records in setup, then send a mapped email with a PDF attachment from a published workflow with no mail connection and verify receipt, a passing DKIM signature and the delivered event on the run; send to a hard-bouncing address and verify the bounce is recorded and the next send is suppressed; attempt a production send before the records verify and see a named setup requirement; send an SMS step through a Twilio test number and see its delivery status; route a failure alert to the workflow owner with no Twilio connection and verify it arrives by email and mobile push. Test an inclusive recipient bound, one excess destination, duplicate destinations and rejection: only the excess action waits, rejection sends nothing, and approval sends exactly the reviewed list under TEAM-004. For AI-003 customer follow-up through this transport, use a live connected invoice, verify configured cadence and billing-contact-only recipients, and change the invoice before dispatch to prove a same-dispatch read stops paid/closed/void contact. Exercise takeover, cancellation, owner pause, authority expiry and budget hold, and revoke a tool before its next dispatch: assert no further send. Retry/restart/concurrently dispatch the same operation and assert one customer contact and one active run per invoice. Require human approval for a new version's first external send unless its standing grant covers it, refuse an agent's approval and verify the provider receipt/readback. AI-003 stays missing until its full journey passes.

#### OPS-001 — Operations reporting and external logs.

Owners see workflow throughput, queue age, latency, success/failure/uncertainty, outstanding business obligations and connector health by workflow/team/time. Reports export CSV and stream redacted operational/audit events to buyer-selected Datadog, Splunk, S3-compatible storage or authorized HTTP sinks with delivery lag and failure visibility. The operations report counts a business outcome as complete only when a named owner explicitly confirms an independent check against the business record and records the evidence, labeled "owner attestation" in the API, docs and UI. HTTP or workflow success alone never counts as business completion, and an uncertain effect blocks it. Automated provider readback belongs to AGENT-001; this report never claims AGENT-001 verification.

**Acceptance evidence:** Generate passing, failed, waiting and uncertain runs; filter an operations report, export it and stream events to an unavailable then restored sink; reconcile counts to run history and show incomplete business outcomes separately. Verify HTTP and workflow success alone leave business completion unchanged, an uncertain effect blocks it, and only a named owner’s explicit confirmation of an independent business-record check with recorded evidence counts the outcome as complete. Verify the API, docs and UI label this "owner attestation" and do not claim AGENT-001 verification; automated provider readback remains AGENT-001’s acceptance work. On the operations home, verify that today’s run count and failed count, for the business day in the workspace timezone, equal that day’s runs and failures in run history, and that it shows how many active workflows ran today out of all active workflows and names any scheduled workflow whose due run did not happen.

#### OPS-002 — USD usage, forecasts and spending controls.

Before activation the buyer sees estimated per-run/workflow USD costs and assumptions for orchestration, connectors, models and external executors; actual usage remains labeled measured or estimated by source. Account/team/workflow budgets, task/credit exhaustion notices and authorized overage policies pause or resume predictably, retaining due work and preventing runaway loops or agent spending.

The owner quotes all four components, including any explicit zero, before publishing a workflow or activating an approval flow. The graph-bound quote is labelled **owner estimate; not provider-verified**, with its assumptions, actor and time; a changed graph requires review again. Published versions keep immutable estimates; rollback displays and reuses the selected version's original estimate. USD input has at most eight decimal places, summed exactly in 10^-8 USD units. Batch estimates sum the components and multiply the count before rounding half-up to cents. Forecasts extrapolate the UTC month's admitted work and owner estimates over the elapsed portion of that month; they are labelled estimates, never invoices. Observed production step paths and physical requests are counts Crank actually recorded, not invented USD charges. Only source-reported USD is shown as provider charges: an executing HTTP endpoint may report `x-crank-usage-usd`, attributed to its origin and response header as self-reported, without independent provider verification. Missing charges remain **not reported**, never zero; an invalid report is an explicit unknown and does not discard a valid execution response.

An account budget means this installation's workspace; team budgets use OPS-001 team assignments, snapshotted when a run is admitted. The owner sets recurring monthly USD limits per workspace, team or workflow (including approval flows), in UTC calendar months. Each new production run atomically reserves its complete immutable per-run estimate against every applicable active budget. An admission that would exceed a limit is held, including a zero-priced admission when the limit is already exhausted. Budget debit is the maximum of that run's reserved estimate and its cumulative source-reported charges, with no double debit; late reports update the month of admission. A run whose reported charges exceed its reservation starts no further request while an applicable budget is exhausted. Threshold notices at 80% and 100% are recorded atomically and delivered to the owner, with delivery state retained. At 100% new admissions stop into the TRIG-005 reviewable hold, retaining exact event identity/input and deduplication; budget holds never auto-expire. Polls retain all unadmitted items, schedules retain each due occurrence, and manual/legacy events are held as well. Replenishing a budget grants no release authority: the owner reviews and releases held items separately. A legacy hold release creates pending approval runs and never dispatches them. Extra overage requires an audited owner USD allowance and reason for the current UTC month. Test runs (WORK-008/014) are excluded from production usage and limits. Existing EXEC-001 execution caps remain, and every run additionally has a durable ceiling of 10,000 distinct expanded step paths, configurable downward with `settings.max_steps`; resuming a checkpoint does not consume the same path twice. A pre-metering unfinished run without a reservation retains its history and dispatches nothing; the owner quotes/reactivates and prepares fresh work.

The obligations apply to all current workflow and approval-flow execution. AI-001 and AGENT-001/002/003/004, WORK-005, EXEC-007 and each new provider or executor inherit source-labelled charging, budget admission and step limits before shipping. DATA-001 applies before usage records ship: quotes, immutable version estimates, budgets, owner allowances, per-run reservations, value-free scope/month spending totals, observed paths/requests, source charges, reporting failures and notices all travel in archives. Restored budgets, allowances and pending usage notices are inactive; workflows and approval flows retain DATA-001's execution fence. The receiving owner saves a budget and grants any fresh allowance explicitly. DATA-002 erases run-linked usage/observations/charge details while retaining only value-free per-scope UTC-month debit totals, disclosed in the erasure receipt, so erasure cannot replenish an allowance.

**Acceptance evidence:** Estimate a batch, run it against metered provider test edges, approach and exhaust a budget and replenish it; verify timely notices, no unauthorized overage, preserved backlog and a report separating estimates, observed usage and provider charges. Export/restore all usage records and assert inactive receiving state under DATA-001.

### People, authority and data

#### TEAM-001 — Team workspaces and permissions.

Owners invite/deactivate members and assign owner, administrator/builder, operator, approver and viewer roles, with workflow/folder/environment and connection-use scopes. Team-owned flows survive employee departure. Enterprise group/SCIM provisioning through Auth or the buyer’s IdP applies the same environment/project policy and revokes sessions and service access when membership ends. Server-side access limits sensitive payloads and production writes; audit readers and billing administrators need not receive credentials or customer data.

**Approved role policy (ct, 20 October 2026 20:20Z):** Owner, admin, builder (may publish), operator, approver and viewer are layered on Base roles, with per-workflow and per-connection scopes. Connection secrets are never readable after creation. A run starter cannot approve that run’s spend or side effect. Scope changes are audited and apply on the next request. The current scoped-role slice does not complete the legacy unassigned Base-role and approval-flow scope/separation-of-duties obligations, folder/environment policy, SCIM/group provisioning, full operator recovery/admin powers, delegated creation, or the audit-reader/billing-admin exclusion obligation: audit readers and billing administrators need not receive credentials or customer data. These remain gaps, without narrowing the role or enterprise requirements.

**Scope-review-54 ruling (ct, 21 October 2026):** Access is the union of explicit grants, with deny by default. One grant must cover both the action and resource; separate grants cannot combine into a wider permission. Deactivation, environment isolation, owner-only decisions and starter-never-approves override every grant. The starter never approves their own run, including the owner and legacy admins, in both workflow runs and legacy approval flows (`crank_flows`). Roles include admin with delegated access administration only up to their own grants, builder with draft-test rights, operator with replay rights, approver, status-only viewer, auditor and billing admin. Audit-reader and billing-admin duties retain the exclusion of credentials and customer data.

Folders are authority records with grants covering descendants. Moving a workflow requires rights on both source and destination and takes effect on the next request. Environments are isolated; existing records belong to production. Every role, scope or group change bumps an authority revision, fencing the next request and any late commit admitted under the old revision. Published runs continue under their immutable version's publish authority (TEAM-004). A one-time migration replaces every unscoped Base-role fallback with exact explicit grants and a zero-widening report proving nobody gained access; only then is the fallback removed. Legacy approval flows obey the same policy.

Native SCIM 2.0 uses an owner-issued credential limited to SCIM. People match by IdP issuer plus external id, never email alone. New users have no grants; groups confer grants only through owner-set mappings. Updates are idempotent and replay-safe, and deactivation revokes sessions and service access; the owner cannot be deprovisioned. Access grants are never restored. Okta, Entra and Auth compatibility remains unverified until the owner provisions a real IdP tenant. These are remaining obligations, not completion evidence; TEAM-001 stays partial.

Name one approver for a workflow’s approval step: verify that approver can decide it while another approver and a builder cannot, a builder can edit and publish but not approve, and a viewer can read runs but cannot edit, publish or approve, each refusal enforced at the server. Verify audit readers and billing administrators can perform their respective duties without receiving credentials or customer data; this exclusion remains unimplemented and TEAM-001 stays partial. Attempt self-approval as a scoped approver, owner and legacy admin in workflow and legacy approval flows and verify refusal. Exercise delegated admin access only up to their grants, a builder draft test and an operator replay within scope, plus auditor and billing-admin duties without credentials or customer data. Grant a folder and verify descendants, refuse a move lacking either side, then complete an authorized move and verify the next request uses its new scope. Refuse cross-environment access and place existing records in production. Change roles, scopes and group mappings during an admitted request and verify next-request and late-commit refusal while published work keeps its version authority. Migrate each unscoped Base person once, inspect the zero-widening report and verify the fallback is removed without losing exact authorized access. Through native SCIM 2.0, prove owner-issued SCIM-only credentials, issuer/external-id identity without email merging, new users with no grants, owner-mapped group grants, idempotent/replayed updates, session/service revocation and owner deprovisioning refusal. Restore without access grants. Real Okta/Entra/Auth interoperability awaits the owner's IdP tenant; local proof cannot establish it. Status stays partial.

#### TEAM-004 — Publishing authorizes a workflow’s declared steps.

When a member with publish rights publishes a workflow version, that version is authorized to run exactly its declared steps, with their mapped fields, on the connections bound to it, for every triggered run, with no expiry, no per-run approval and no separate grant to author. The authority is recorded on the version (publisher, time, steps, connections) and ends when the version is unpublished, replaced, or a bound connection is revoked. It does not extend to steps added later, other connections, or anything an AI/agent node decides beyond its declared tools (AI-001). Limits are opt-in: builders add approval steps (TEAM-005) or per-step caps, and owners may set optional workspace default caps (for example a USD refund ceiling or a maximum recipients per email) that pause only actions outside the cap for approval while in-cap actions continue unattended.

Pausing blocks new, queued and running next-step dispatch. Only runs actually waiting or awaiting approval at the pause retain a frozen continuation when their version chose `continue` (the default when omitted) or `cancel_on_new_version`; `cancel_on_pause` cancels them. Replacement permits only runs actually waiting or awaiting approval at replacement whose old version chose `continue`, on that frozen graph with live connection and authority checks at every step. These exceptions are persisted at the pause or replacement, never inferred from a historical wait. Unpublishing retires the version and stops every old dispatch and wait with no exception.

Workspace caps use `{category,max_usd?,max_recipients?}`; step caps use `{max_usd?,amount?,max_recipients?,recipients?}`. An action obeys the stricter workspace and step bound, inclusively. Recipients resolve to an array or one address, without delimiter parsing; every entry, including a duplicate, counts. For generic HTTP actions the graph declares the recipient mapping beside the mapped request. Approval covers the exact input and effective caps; rejection sends nothing. Every currently shipped action conforms, and EXEC-007, CONN-003, CONN-004 and CONN-017 carry these obligations when adding recipient operations; typed sends must count their actual expanded destination list.

**Acceptance evidence:** Build or import 10 ordinary workflows (lead to CRM, Slack notice, Sheets row, draft invoice and similar), publish each, and observe their triggered runs complete unattended with no grant authoring, approval or other step beyond publish; verify each run’s audit names the publishing member and version. Add a workspace USD refund cap of $200 and trigger refunds of $150 and $350: verify only the $350 action pauses for approval while the $150 one completes. Add a step to a draft and verify the published version cannot run it until republished; revoke a bound connection and verify new runs pause with a reconnect notice.

#### SEC-001 — Native authentication and origin-bound writes.

Private product routes require a current native operator session or a specifically scoped machine credential. Authorization is enforced in handlers and durable write predicates; browser mutations require the configured exact Origin. Owner-only data/access/import decisions cannot be obtained by an admin, member, trigger or preparation agent. Access decisions are inviting a person, deactivating or reactivating them, changing their role and ending another person’s sessions; until TEAM-001 adds narrower roles, only the owner makes them, admins may read the people list, and everyone may list and end their own sessions. A write admitted before its session or credential is revoked, signed out or demoted is refused when it commits. Local development identity remains local and is excluded from deployed assets.

**Acceptance evidence:** Sign in through the ordinary email-link journey, call private HTTP doors signed out and with each lower role, send a foreign-Origin mutation and revoke a session/credential before a guarded write; verify denial without product effects and the build’s dev-identity exclusion.

#### SEC-002 — Bounded network and untrusted content.

HTTP/custom connectors, callbacks, code, files and agent tools validate authorized egress destinations on every redirect/resolution, refuse private/metadata targets unless an explicit private gateway grant applies, bound bytes/time and keep secrets server-side. Input text, imported graphs and tool results cannot execute HTML/scripts or override agent policy. File types and access are checked before forwarding.

**Acceptance evidence:** Through workflow and import doors submit hostile HTML, credential-bearing URLs, redirect and DNS-rebinding targets, oversized payloads and prompt-injection text; verify literal display or named refusal, no unintended network requests and no secret in stored output.

#### SEC-003 — Permanent attributable audit.

An exportable, append-only audit records connection consent/rotation, grant changes, deployments, approvals, executions, replays, imports, exports, erasures and administrative actions with actor, time, version and value-free subject identity. Agents and automated work identify the policy authorizing them. Erasure anonymizes actors and removes sensitive payload copies without rewriting action history; external log delivery is observable. Until TEAM-001 adds an auditor role, the owner is the authorized auditor: only the owner reads or exports the audit, no caller can change or delete a record (the door answers 405 and the database refuses), and each export first records itself. The export is one JSON object per line, oldest first by time then id. Today’s grant changes are agent and trigger credential issue and revocation; access decisions (invite, deactivate or reactivate, role change) are recorded with the person’s operator id, never an email address. A draft edit names the published version it started from and the SHA-256 digest of the saved draft graph; an execution names its published version and publish authority. Erasing a workflow run or flow run replaces that run’s audit subject link with an opaque label and clears its detail while keeping each record’s id, time, actor, action and version; the run’s not-yet-delivered log events are erased with it. TEAM-002 (standing grants), DATA-002 (subject and operator erasure, which must anonymize the erased person’s actor ids) and every later clause that adds an action kind must add its audit records before shipping.

**Acceptance evidence:** Change a grant, publish, execute, approve, replay and erase a run; read/export the audit as an authorized auditor, deny a builder’s audit mutation and verify anonymized records retain chronology without erased payloads or secrets. Verify the audit lists a draft edit, a run and an approval of the same workflow, each with actor, time and version.

#### DATA-003 — Explicit retention and sensitive-data policy.

Owners choose payload, attachment, model-context and history retention with dry-run deletion scope and legal holds. Defaults and automatic cleanup are disclosed; limits on displayed pages never masquerade as deletion policy. Durable outcomes, audit and value-free receipts outlive expiring payloads, and incomplete obligations are not silently erased. Health/financial/customer data use scoped encryption, regional/provider controls and required agreements before production processing.

- **Defaults and periods:** nothing expires until the owner sets a period. Payload, attachment and history retention are each empty (kept until erased) or a whole number of days from 1 to 3650, counted from the instant the run finished (a flow run: its last update), in UTC; history must be at least the payload and attachment periods. The per-minute Cron maintenance pass expires at most 25 runs of each kind per minute, each run in one atomic batch, so a restart resumes where it stopped. Saving periods requires the digest of their current dry run; every change is audited.
- **Model context:** Crank stores no model context today. AI-001, AI-003, WORK-009 and AGENT-001–AGENT-004 inherit a model-context retention period under these rules before they ship.
- **What expires:** payload expiry clears a finished run's trigger data, response, step input, output and trace, step-revision inputs, wait proposals and decisions, held and historical event copies and resumable request responses, and reduces each failure to its category; the run, its step statuses, times, business key, source event id, audit and a value-free receipt stay, and the run can no longer be replayed. Attachment expiry deletes the run files named by that run, and files no run names once older than the period. History expiry removes the whole run through DATA-002's erasure (event-digest fence, value-free receipt carrying its workflow, outcome and cutoff). Every expiry advances the portability redaction checkpoint and file deletions fence their rows, so an archive made before the expiry is refused against this installation or a later archive supplied as the journal (`erasure_epoch`).
- **Always kept:** unfinished runs, runs waiting for a decision, runs with an unverified business obligation (OPS-001), runs with an uncertain write to reconcile (EXEC-006), runs with a repair in progress (EXEC-004) and held runs never expire; the dry run lists each with its reason.
- **Dry run:** shows, for the chosen periods, every run and file the maintenance pass would remove now (or as of a chosen time) and every kept run with its reason, and deletes nothing.
- **Legal holds:** the owner holds one exact identifier (3 to 500 characters, matched case-insensitively the way DATA-002 matches a subject) or one whole workflow, with a reason. A held run never expires and its DATA-002 erasure is refused (409) until the owner releases the hold; release keeps the hold's record and digest and removes the identifier. Placing and releasing are audited.
- **Disclosure:** the Data screen states the defaults, the periods, the cleanup that already runs on its own (request-rate admission windows after their window, a paused workflow's held events at the expiry chosen for that hold, resumable request responses when their step finishes) and that run lists page the newest runs while older runs are kept.
- **Sensitive data:** the owner sets each workflow's data class (none, customer, financial or health). A financial or health workflow publishes or resumes only while the owner's attestation for that class is recorded, naming each provider agreement in place (for example a BAA) and where the data is held; it is labelled owner-attested and Crank never claims to have verified or certified it. Withdrawing an attestation pauses every published workflow of that class at once.
- **Scoped encryption (ct 19 Oct 17:20Z and 17:42Z):** Crank itself encrypts every payload value of a customer, financial or health workflow: trigger data, the webhook response, step input, output, trace and failure detail, replay and repair inputs, approval proposals and decisions, held and historical event copies, and run files. Each value is AES-256-GCM ciphertext under the installation's key for that data class, bound to its workflow and key; beside it stay only value-free routing facts (the file ids it names, an HTTP step's method, a failure's category, code, HTTP status and uncertainty, retry ids and times). Each installation makes its own random key per class on first use and seals it under the installation secret, like connection credentials; the blind-index HMAC-SHA-256 key is derived from the same key. Values are sealed on write; the per-minute Cron pass brings at most 25 runs, 50 held or historical copies and 10 files a minute to their workflow's current form, each run in one atomic batch that a concurrent write or execution defers: this migrates existing payloads when a workflow is classified, re-seals them on rotation and returns them to plaintext when a workflow leaves both classes. The owner rotates a class key at once (typed ROTATE); new values use the new key, the pass re-seals and re-indexes everything, and the old key is destroyed (its material deleted, the event audited) once no value, digest or run refers to it and 15 minutes have passed since it retired. Key creation, rotation, destruction, export and import are audited. Customer data needs no attestation; financial and health data also need the attestation above.
- **Blind index:** the owner declares a sealed workflow's identifier fields (up to 20 property names). Their text or number values, trimmed and lower-cased, found at any depth of the trigger, step input or step output, are kept only as HMAC-SHA-256 digests under the class key. DATA-002 subject erasure and subject legal holds match a sealed run by its business key or when the identifier exactly equals one of those values; free text inside sealed values is never matched, and run search says that text search does not reach encrypted payloads. While any run waits for the pass to seal or re-index it, or is sealed under a key this installation does not hold, the subject preview names that and erasure waits. Payload expiry deletes a run's digests with its values; run erasure deletes them with the run.
- **Archives and keys:** keys never travel in an archive; an archive carries the ciphertext and digests. After a fresh email-link confirmation (step-up), the owner downloads a key file holding every key not yet destroyed, wrapped with AES-256-GCM under a key derived from the owner's passphrase (12 to 500 characters; PBKDF2-SHA-256, 100,000 iterations). Restored on another installation without it, runs, outcomes and audit restore and each sealed value shows as sealed and labelled; after its own step-up, that installation's owner imports the key file with the passphrase, the values read again, and its pass re-seals them under that installation's own key and then destroys the imported one.
- **Later capabilities:** AI-001, AI-003, AGENT-001 to AGENT-004 (model context and agent memory), WORK-007 (tables and forms), WORK-009 (collected answers), WORK-010 (digest entries), TRIG-006 (inbound email) and EXEC-007 (sent messages) store payload values and must seal them for customer, financial and health workflows under these rules before they ship.

**Acceptance evidence:** Configure short payload retention and a held subject, run the maintenance job across its boundary and restart; verify only eligible sensitive data expires, held records remain, unfinished work is visible and pre-erasure snapshots respect fences. Classify a published workflow as health data and verify it cannot publish or resume until the owner records the agreements and data location, labelled owner-attested, and that withdrawing the attestation pauses it. Encrypt a financial workflow's payload values under a per-installation, per-data-class key, rotate the key, and erase a subject matched through a keyed blind index.

#### AI-001 — Inspectable AI and agent nodes.

Builders add LLM classification/extraction/generation and tool-using agent nodes using buyer-selected OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini or authorized model endpoints, or with no model key at all through the installation’s default model (Cloudflare Workers AI on the installation’s own account, which the owner can replace with any configured endpoint), whose usage is metered in USD under OPS-002. Each node declares typed outputs, model/version, allowed data, tools, MCP servers, iteration/time/USD budgets and failure policy. Prompts, files and external documents are untrusted data; agents cannot acquire new scopes, change grants, send out-of-policy messages or hide tool calls. Invalid structured output is a visible step failure.

**File, image, audio and URL inputs.** AI node inputs accept WORK-002 file references as well as text, so a node reads the file itself rather than text pasted from it:

- documents: PDF (including scanned pages, read through the model’s vision or the installation’s document-to-text conversion), DOCX, XLSX, CSV, HTML and plain text;
- images: PNG, JPEG, HEIC, WebP and GIF;
- audio and video: MP3, M4A, WAV, MP4, MOV and WebM, with video read through its audio track for transcription.

Any step that produces a file reference feeds an AI node: a CONN-003 or TRIG-006 attachment, a CONN-012 form upload, a CONN-017 MMS image, a CONN-013 Zoom recording, a CONN-005 or CONN-016 stored file, or a WORK-002 fetched URL. Default bounds are shown in the step and owners can change them within the model’s own limits: documents up to 50 MB and 500 pages, images up to 20 MB, and audio or video up to 500 MB and 4 hours, with long media split into chunks whose timestamps stay continuous. File type is checked by content as well as extension under SEC-002 before any model call. Before publish, the step editor shows which input types and operations the chosen model supports; mapping a file type the chosen model cannot read blocks publishing with a named error. A file that arrives at run time with an unsupported type, over the bounds or unreadable fails the step with the named error `model input unsupported`, naming the type, size and model, and no later step writes.

**Built-in AI operations.** Each operation is a native step with typed inputs and outputs. Each runs on the installation’s default model where that model supports it (Workers AI speech-to-text, vision, document-to-text conversion and image generation) and on any buyer-selected OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini or authorized endpoint that supports it:

- **Send prompt and conversation:** text generation with optional file inputs and system instructions, and an optional conversation key whose earlier turns persist across runs until cleared.
- **Extract structured data:** from text or a file into builder-declared typed fields, with line items returned as WORK-002 line-item arrays in exact decimal cents. Each extracted field records the page it came from, and lines that do not reconcile to the extracted total route to WORK-002’s named validation failure instead of writing.
- **Analyze and classify:** answer an instruction about text, an image or a document, returning typed fields or one category from a declared list.
- **Transcribe:** audio or video to text with segment timestamps, speaker labels where the model provides them, and the detected language.
- **Translate:** text, or audio, into translated text in a chosen language.
- **Extract content from URL:** fetch a web page, PDF, image, audio or video at a URL under SEC-002 egress rules and return its text, title and content type. Private, metadata and DNS-rebinding targets are refused before any request is sent; bytes and time are bounded; pages become readable text without running their scripts; and media go through the transcribe or analyze operation.
- **Search content across URLs:** answer one question from up to 10 URLs fetched as above, with the URL each statement came from.
- **Generate image:** from a prompt, returning a WORK-002 file reference with name, type and size.
- **Model files:** upload a file to the selected provider’s file store, find a file, and find or create one under WORK-011.

Every operation records model, version, input types, tokens or media seconds, and USD usage under OPS-002. CONN-001 maps Zapier’s ChatGPT (OpenAI), Anthropic (Claude) and AI by Zapier steps to these operations.

### Product delivery and boundaries

#### UX-001 — Accessible mobile operation.

Builders and operators use responsive web interfaces and iOS/Android mobile access for run search, notifications, approvals, pause, safe replay and takeover; full workflow editing remains usable on desktop and accessible on small screens. Keyboard/screen-reader labels, textual states, focus and action errors meet the WCAG 2.2 AA target. Notifications never expose secrets; poor connectivity shows stale state and reconciles a decision before permitting another.

Decision connectivity semantics: an offline approval is not sent; an interrupted response is labelled unconfirmed because it may have reached the server. Both freeze the displayed approval controls until a fresh server page is read, automatically on reconnection or through an explicit check. Checking only reads current state; it never resends a decision. A failed check keeps the proposal labelled stale and the controls frozen. The same rule covers approval flows and workflow approval steps.

**Acceptance evidence:** At 1440px and 390px with realistic long names/payloads, create and inspect work, approve/reject, pause and resolve a failure using keyboard and touch; interrupt connectivity during approval and verify one decision and clear stale/error state. #### PLATFORM-001 — Public API, webhooks, SDK and MCP.

The product exposes documented, versioned APIs, paginated reads, outgoing signed run/outcome webhooks, SDKs and an MCP server for authorized workflow/run/connection operations. Idempotent writes, scoped service accounts, event retries, subscription rotation and public error contracts support app and agent integrations. Remote clients have the same grants and audit trail as UI operators and cannot bypass approval. Connected-app actions exposed to the buyer’s own AI clients are covered by PLATFORM-002.

**Delivered slice semantics:** `/api/crank/v1` versions the existing workflow/flow JSON doors and their public error codes; `/api/crank/v1/mcp` adapts the same doors without extending caller authority. Draft create/save accept an optional 1–200 visible-ASCII-character `Idempotency-Key`, scoped to the current credential, operation and target workflow. Canonically identical JSON retries retain one workflow, draft snapshot and audit write; changed reuse is a conflict. A replay returns the current workflow plus the original draft receipt, so it cannot undo a later edit. Receipts contain hashes and record IDs only, stay installation-local and are erased with their operator; portable drafts and history restore inactive. Granted task starts also accept the optional key, scoped to that execution grant. Concurrent or restarted identical requests create one task version, run and audit entry, with one dispatch; retries return current progress without re-executing work or bypassing pending/rejected approval. Changed request reuse conflicts. The caller’s task_id remains a source label, not a deduplication key. Task receipts follow the same installation-local hash/ID-only custody and operator-erasure policy; after run-history erasure, the receipt refuses reuse instead of launching effects again. Publish and rollback accept the same optional key under distinct operation/target namespaces. Canonical retries create one immutable publication version and one publish audit, including concurrent calls and lost-response recovery. They return the original version beside the current workflow state without republishing a newer draft, replacing a later version, resuming a pause or repeating restore adoption. Replay requires current publish authority and workflow scope. Publication receipts use the same local hash/ID-only custody and operator erasure; archives omit them. Duplication accepts the same optional key, scoped to the current credential and source workflow under a separate operation. Concurrent, lost-response and restarted retries retain one inert destination draft and creation audit. A retry reads that destination's current state without copying a later source revision, overwriting destination edits, publishing or starting work. The native preparation and source-scope checks still apply. Duplication receipts share the existing local hash/ID-only custody and erasure rules; archives omit them, so a fresh receiving-owner duplication creates a new inert draft. Other writes keep their existing semantics and are not automatically retried. No completion webhook subscription or delivery is claimed by this slice.
