Direct booking displays and records acknowledgment of the required-versus-requested distinction. **Acceptance evidence:** Book with a required accessible table and requested patio, submit a 16-person inquiry, have a manager reply and convert it; verify guest acknowledgment of what is guaranteed.

- **DIST-001 — Reserve with Google.** Placemat completes eligible Actions Center partner onboarding and certification, publishes availability to Google Search/Maps, receives bookings/modifications/cancellations and reconciles inventory with channel attribution. A link alone is labeled a link until the actual end-to-end integration is live. Before shipping, this capability must inherit SERVICE-005 arrival/service/concurrent/area pacing and SERVICE-007 warning, reasoned override and hard physical-capacity obligations; public and agent allocations never override. **Acceptance evidence:** Through Google’s approved test/production partner journey, publish a venue, book on Google, change and cancel there, and verify matching reservation IDs and released local inventory; exercise feed rejection and outage recovery.

- **DIST-002 — Instagram and Facebook booking.** Owners connect Instagram/Facebook booking actions where partner support permits and publish trackable profile links elsewhere. Bookings preserve social/referrer/campaign provenance and real inventory; revoked profiles and unsupported account types receive actionable setup guidance. Before shipping, this capability must inherit SERVICE-005 arrival/service/concurrent/area pacing and SERVICE-007 warning, reasoned override and hard physical-capacity obligations; public and agent allocations never override. **Acceptance evidence:** Connect a supported profile, follow its reservation action at phone width, book and inspect social attribution; disconnect and prove existing bookings remain manageable.

- **DIST-003 — Diner discovery and partner distribution.** Searchable venue pages expose location, cuisine, menus, images, experiences and live availability; diner discovery and approved concierge/travel/marketplace distribution bring bookable demand. Partners use allocated inventory or the shared live ledger, with source fees visible and no assumption of inherited OpenTable/Resy network reach. Before shipping, this capability must inherit SERVICE-005 arrival/service/concurrent/area pacing and SERVICE-007 warning, reasoned override and hard physical-capacity obligations; public and agent allocations never override. **Acceptance evidence:** Find a venue by neighborhood and cuisine, book an experience from a partner listing and reconcile its source, fee and remaining tables; reject a duplicate partner callback.

- **DIST-004 — Channel inventory and attribution.** Managers allocate protected tables/covers by direct, Google, social, discovery, phone and partner channels, with release times, direct-booking priority and source/campaign attribution that survives modification. A channel outage cannot oversell shared physical inventory. Before shipping, this capability must inherit SERVICE-005 arrival/service/concurrent/area pacing and SERVICE-007 warning, reasoned override and hard physical-capacity obligations; public and agent allocations never override. **Acceptance evidence:** Reserve two four-tops for direct until 5 p.m., exhaust partner allocation, release it on schedule and inspect original source after a guest changes time. The reservation book shows each party’s channel and totals covers by channel (website, Google, Instagram, phone) that reconcile to its rows, including after a guest changes time.

- **DIST-005 — Guest accounts and repeat booking.** **Status: done.** CT judged DIST-005 at `90fbab254ae525906eded2f2f27752c1799dda30` on 27 October 2026 and accepted it as done. Diners can optionally keep verified contact details, favorite restaurants, manage upcoming reservations and rebook prior visits across devices, with saved preferences controlled per restaurant. Guest checkout remains available and identity never merges distinct people solely because they share a phone. **CT ruling, 26 October 2026 — APPROVE WITH RIDERS; DIST-005 remains PARTIAL.** A diner explicitly proves access to the selected booking’s current recorded email before attaching that booking. Thirty-two-byte random one-use codes are stored only as digests and expire after fifteen minutes; independent device bearers are stored only as digests and expire after twenty-four hours. Each additional booking needs its own current-contact proof. Shared phone numbers confer no identity, booking or account authority. Favorites and preferences are controlled per restaurant; verification grants no staff role, marketing permission, review eligibility or group-sharing permission. Sends are explicit, bounded and audited, with provider acceptance distinguished from mailbox delivery. Logout revokes the selected device; account forget revokes all account sessions without cancelling reservations. DATA-003 portability, DATA-002 erasure fences and AUDIT-001 accountability apply to these records, while verification and device custody remain excluded from archives. The complete diner-facing favorite, repeat-booking and upcoming-reservation management target across devices remains binding. Group sharing remains the separate GUEST-006 target. **CT update ruling, 26 October 2026 — APPROVE WITH RIDERS; DIST-005 remains PARTIAL.** The earlier DIST-005 ruling remains binding. Pending email proof may retain the private booking, guest and current-contact references needed to validate that single booking, while storing the random code only as a digest, expiring it after fifteen minutes and consuming it once. Failed or uncertain mail does not establish delivery or successful verification. An independent digest-only device session expires after twenty-four hours and grants management only for individually verified bookings whose current recorded contact still matches. Every change, reconfirmation or cancellation requires a fresh booking-specific preview and explicit diner confirmation; the preview is bound to that device, booking and current state, is revocable and is excluded from archives. Capacity failure, stale state, replay, revoked access or changed contact grants no mutation authority. Recorded payment obligations require manager review and remain unchanged through this diner door; this grants no charge, refund, fee waiver or automatic message authority. Current-contact, custody, audit, portability and erasure riders remain binding. This update accepts no completion. **Acceptance evidence:** Book without an account, verify a diner account, attach only the verified booking, rebook a favorite on another device and revoke saved preferences.

- **DIST-006 — Verified diner reviews and restaurant replies.** Diners whose reservation was seated or completed (or matched to a POS check) can rate and review the venue once per attended visit on its Placemat venue page and booking widget; no-shows, cancellations and staff cannot review. Reviews show the visit date, averages show only above a minimum count, and the restaurant can post and edit one public reply per review and report abuse for moderation under published guidelines. Neither the restaurant nor Placemat removes or hides a review because of its rating, and review invitations follow CRM-005’s no-gating rule. Before shipping, DIST-006 inherits DIST-005’s explicit current-contact proof for each attached booking. A verified diner account alone establishes neither an attended visit nor review eligibility and authorizes no review invitation or publication. Prove booking identity separately from this clause’s attended-visit, once-only review and invitation-permission requirements. **Acceptance evidence:** Complete a visit, receive the review invitation, submit a four-star review and see it with its visit date on the venue page and widget. Refuse a review for a no-show and a second review for the same visit. Reply as manager and see the reply public; report an abusive review and read the moderation outcome; prove a manager cannot delete a one-star review.

### The host stand and floor

- **FLOOR-002 — Rooms and editable floor plans.** Managers arrange rooms, indoor/outdoor areas, bars and numbered tables with shapes, seats, accessibility and joinable combinations. Changes are previewed against future commitments; retired tables retain history and live occupancy is visible without manual page reload. Before richer table attributes ship, preserve FLOOR-009 direct move/swap/lock fit, access and history obligations. Rooms have indoor, outdoor or bar types; numbered tables use round, square, rectangle or bar shapes, exact access tags and percentage positions within a room. A floor-change preview lists every affected commitment, replacement, conflict and disabled combination; a manager approves the exact venue, rooms, floor, services, observations and bookings snapshot. Active commitments retain their room, confirmed times, fit and access needs. Locked assignments must be unlocked explicitly; arrived, seated or unbussed parties must be resolved before retirement. Retirement removes a table from new availability and selection, disables its joins and keeps the table plus historical bookings and attributed replacement history. Open host devices check the authorized floor version every three seconds and update without a page reload; focused or unsaved forms defer replacement and show the pending change, and failed checks show an unavailable warning. FLOOR-008 inherits offline reconciliation and richer synchronization; FLOOR-004 inherits sections, server capacity and serving history. Current and future allocation doors inherit retirement, fit and access guards before shipping (BOOK-002, BOOK-005, DIST-001–DIST-004, VOICE-001, AGENT-001). **Acceptance evidence:** Draw dining room and patio, retire a booked table with an approved replacement, book both areas and watch occupancy update on a second host device.

- **FLOOR-003 — Approved table combinations.** Managers explicitly permit which adjacent tables can join, their combined capacity, accessible fit and setup buffer. Allocation cannot combine distant or incompatible tables merely because their seats sum to the party size. Before explicit join definitions ship, enforce FLOOR-009 permitted combinations on direct and prepared moves as well as all booking doors. Managers confirm adjacency explicitly for an exact set; joins can cross named areas only when explicitly approved, while a booking’s required area must match every constituent. Approved capacity is an integer no greater than the constituent seats, and every approved access tag must exist on every constituent. Setup is 0–120 whole elapsed minutes immediately before arrival, within the service, with half-open occupancy from setup start through the preserved turn/reset and any ongoing overrun; single tables need no setup. Current public search/booking, staff walk-ins, waitlist seating, direct move/swap/lock and prepared assignments all enforce these definitions. Active booked/seated commitments freeze join settings and setup; disabling prevents new assignments while preserving those commitments, and structural edits wait until they finish. Changes to join configuration invalidate prepared publication or reassignment review. Future booking doors (BOOK-002, BOOK-005, DIST-001–DIST-004, VOICE-001, AGENT-001) inherit exact joins and full setup before shipping. **Acceptance evidence:** Permit T1+T2 but prohibit T1+T8; request six guests, verify the permitted join is used and reject a host attempting the prohibited join.

- **FLOOR-004 — Server sections and fair covers.** Managers create shift-specific sections, assign servers and tables, record breaks and cap covers per server. Hosts see seated/expected covers and rotation, while reassignment preserves the serving history and checks kitchen and server capacity. Before server sections ship, expose assigned server filtering in the FLOOR-005 timeline and enforce FLOOR-009 server capacity and serving history on moves. Servers are named shift roster entries, not new sign-in roles. Each table belongs to at most one section per service, and an assignment or join must fit wholly within one section once sections are configured. Server and configured kitchen-area caps count overlapping booked or seated dining covers in half-open arrival-to-forecast-departure intervals; setup and cleanup still reserve physical tables separately. Ongoing seated parties remain counted past forecast departure. Expected covers total the shift’s booked and seated parties; seated covers total its currently seated parties, with exact booking drilldowns and missing seating history labeled. Each party counts against every kitchen area containing its assigned tables. Breaks exclude new assignments and seating, while an existing seated party can retain its server during a same-section move. Rotation considers a requested party size and live fitting tables, breaks and caps, then orders eligible servers by seated covers, oldest last seating (never seated first) and stable server id. Active section mappings cannot silently change; move or finish affected parties before changing their mapping. New reservations, walk-ins, waitlist seating, status reacquisition, direct moves/swaps, reviewed proposals and retirement replacements all enforce these capacities and retain attributed serving events. FLOOR-008 inherits offline staffing reconciliation, ROLE-003 inherits server-specific sign-in visibility, and SERVICE-005/007 inherit wider interval pacing and permitted overrides; BOOK-002/005, DIST-001–DIST-004, VOICE-001 and AGENT-001 inherit staffing constraints before their new doors ship. **Acceptance evidence:** Assign two sections and servers, seat uneven parties, put one server on break and move a table; verify cover totals, suggested rotation and attributed service history. SERVICE-007 carries signed, reasoned exceptions to the configured concurrent kitchen-area cap; server caps and breaks remain hard.

- **FLOOR-005 — Timeline and overdue turns.** A searchable day/service timeline shows arrivals, assigned tables, expected/actual seating and departure, cleanup, late arrivals and overdue turns. Hosts zoom or filter by room/server and resolve an overrun by moving the next arrival in one host action (FLOOR-009) or accepting a proposed replacement, never silently moving a confirmed reservation. Current observations are staff-recorded, not POS verification. An extension changes only the expected departure, retains the originally confirmed seating/departure/reset and appends actor, receipt time, prior/new forecast and reason; no reservation moves until a separate direct host command or reviewed agent proposal is accepted. The original cleanup duration follows the extended forecast, and an ongoing seated party remains physically occupied even past its forecast. Late means an actual arrival after the promised start, or an unarrived booked party past that start; overdue means an ongoing seated party past expected departure. Raw elapsed minutes are returned, while labels round to the nearest minute. The inclusive next window is now through now plus the selected elapsed minutes; seated/due/average totals use the displayed filtered parties. Average actual turn is the mean corrected seating-to-completed duration for parties actually completed today in venue time; missing actual timestamps are excluded and an empty mean stays unknown. Each total opens its exact party ids. Search matches guest name/contact, reservation id, service and tables without changing identity. The selected date is the venue-local service-start date. Current room/area and time-scale filters work on existing tables; FLOOR-004 inherits populated server assignments and server filtering before sections ship. Corrections retain both original observations and restored facts. **Acceptance evidence:** Seat a late six-top, extend its actual turn and inspect the collision with the next arrival; move the next arrival to a fitting replacement as a host in one action and read both histories. The host header shows seated covers now, covers due within a configurable next window and the average actual turn so far today, each opening its parties.

- **FLOOR-006 — Service statuses and handover.** Hosts manage confirmed, reconfirmed, arrived, partially arrived, seated, ordering, check open, paid, clearing, completed, late, canceled and no-show states. Status changes carry timestamps and actor; POS observations cannot falsely mark a dirty table ready. Current owner/admin staff and owner-granted FLOOR-009 hosts record service observations; ROLE-003 carries further host/server rights before those roles ship. Current observations are explicitly staff-recorded, including paid, which does not claim a POS payment. POS-007 inherits all status, timestamp, dirty-table and correction obligations before connected observations ship. Service and floor histories append the actor and server receipt time; a correction requires a reason, restores only the latest observation’s prior state and retains both rows, refusing physical clashes. Paid and completed leave the table needing bussing; only staff ready permits another seating. Future online reservations still use the promised turn/reset, and ready never shortens that protected interval. Floor timers show elapsed whole minutes since the last course/floor change; missing legacy observations are labeled not recorded. A read of shift handover shows current stages and their full observations, including corrections. **Acceptance evidence:** Run a reservation from arrival through paid and clearing to ready, correct an accidental state with a reason and inspect the next shift’s handover. The floor plan marks each table reserved, seated, mains, dessert, check dropped or needs bussing with a timer since its last transition, from host taps or POS signals (POS-007), and a legend names the same states.

- **FLOOR-007 — Busy-service search and shift handover.** Hosts find guests, bookings, phone numbers and table labels quickly, filter by service/source/status and see VIP, allergy, access and unpaid-policy alerts with PAY-010 deadlines. A handover lists unresolved guest requests, late parties and promised callbacks with owners and due times. **Acceptance evidence:** Find an arriving guest by phone suffix, resolve their access request, hand over an unpaid deposit exception and prove the next host can complete the promised callback. Current timeline search uses GUEST-002 case/accent-normalized name/email and normalized US phone suffix matching, plus case-insensitive booking-ID, service-name and table-label substrings. Venue-local service-start date, service, source and booking-status filters combine; an empty filter includes every value. It displays existing VIP/regular facts, guest-supplied allergy/accommodation requests and required table access/area, without certifying food safety or claiming a payment. Ct policy (21 October 2026): An active owner-granted host or a manager creates a follow-up and assigns it to themself or another active host or manager. A host reassigns only items they hold; a manager reassigns any. The current assignee or a manager completes it. Every active host and manager sees each open item's kind, booking, guest, due time, assignee and state. Free text is shown only to managers and the current assignee, never to agents or preparation keys, and leaves the SEC-002 stand page on lock or switch. **Ct assertions:** host A hands to B; C sees the item without its text; B completes it on the stand; after a switch to C, B's text is absent from response and DOM. All acceptance points pass. Hosts create and hand over their own work; active hosts retain booking/kind/guest/assignee/due/state metadata, while current assignment controls free text in live and historical reads. Manager-defined USD deposit requests supply real unpaid deadlines and overdue exceptions; transferring their callback transfers the follow-up owner. Completion records an operational outcome and never marks a deposit paid. PAY-010 retains delivered notices, policy automation, waivers and live sandbox proof in its own partial clause.

- **FLOOR-008 — Concurrent devices and operational outage.** Host devices reconcile live changes, identify stale edits and show last successful sync. During an outage staff can read an encrypted, time-stamped service sheet and capture pending actions; reconnect requires conflict review before pending seats or reservations affect live inventory. **Acceptance evidence:** Seat from two tablets, disconnect one, record a pending walk-in and reconnect after its table is sold; refuse silent overwrite and reconcile to a different table. With the reservation book open on one device, make a booking from the guest page and see it arrive within seconds with a “new since” count and marker, without a reload and without overwriting a stale edit. The live reservation book counts and marks reservations absent from the first successful state snapshot of that open staff page, scoped to the selected service. Unrelated updates, assignment changes and explicit refresh retain that baseline; reopening the page starts a fresh baseline. The count includes every current reservation status and source, with no persistent guest or browser tracking. Focused or unsaved forms defer replacement and show the pending change; sync failures show an unavailable warning and the last successful sync remains visible.

Ct policy (23 October 2026): **Access.** "Staff" means the owner, active managers (admin) and owner-granted hosts, plus seating leads within their ROLE-002 grant. They may use outage mode on a personal session or under their PIN session on a registered SEC-002 stand. The owner turns this on with one explicit, audited and revocable venue setting (before/after recorded). The owner-only mode stays available. Servers, finance, plain members, group admins, agents and preparation keys are always refused. **Device keys.** Each person who will use a sheet on a device enrols their own outage passphrase (at least 16 characters) while online. This wraps the sheet key for that person, and the enrolment is audited. There is no shared passphrase, and a SEC-002 PIN is never an offline key. Offline unlock, capture and discard are attributed to the unlocking person. That attribution is marked "device-attributed" until a person with live authority signs the reconciliation. **Offline data.** Every role gets one minimised projection, never more than FLOOR-012's host projection: per booking, the guest name as booked, a short booking reference, the last four digits of the US phone, party size, arrival and reset end, tables/section/server, status, required access tags, and guest-supplied allergy/dietary/access requests labelled unverified. It holds no email, no full phone, no guest notes, tags, VIP level, visit count, occasion, preferences, deposit or payment state, and nothing from other services. Erased guests appear only as "Erased guest". Pending reservations and waitlist entries may hold the name and one contact that staff type, under the same encryption and expiry. **Pending actions.** Staff can capture walk-ins, pending reservations, waitlist adds, seating an existing reservation, and marking a reservation arrived, finished or no-show. Each action has a UUID, a device capture time and the capturing person. **Retention.** The sheet expires at the earlier of 12 hours or one hour after service end, and is deleted on the next page activity or unlock. It is also deleted when the last pending action is reconciled or discarded, and the next time the page is online after any of these: sign-out, session revocation, removal of the host grant, device revocation, or the owner turning outage mode off. While online, unreconciled actions show a persistent warning before expiry. When a draft expires with unreviewed actions, the next online contact records an audit row holding only their count and creates a manager-visible follow-up (FLOOR-007). **Locking.** Five idle minutes lock the sheet on a personal session. On a stand, SEC-002's two-minute inactivity lock and any switch also lock it, so the stricter rule applies. Leaving the page clears the key. **Offline open.** An installed offline app shell must open the locked sheet after a reload or restart with no connection. **Reconnect.** Nothing applies automatically. A person with live authority for that action reviews the current floor and the exact alternatives. They sign a five-minute review bound to actor, action and floor version, and every live seating, access, turn, combination, hold, pacing and staffing guard is checked again. The action then commits atomically through its normal door, exactly once, including replay after a lost response or erasure. Hard conflicts are never bypassed. A SERVICE-007 override is offered only to its grant holders, through the existing reviewed path. Capture time stays an observation. A party that has already left is recorded only through an explicit, reviewed "already finished during outage" action that carries device-observed times labelled as such. **Audit.** The log records the venue setting, each sheet preparation (person, device, service, expiry, field-scope version), passphrase enrolments, and each commit: UUID, capturing and reconciling persons, capture time, original and final tables, and the conflict. It also records expired-unreviewed counts and discards reported on reconnect. Offline reads cannot be server-audited, and the clause says so.

**Remaining gaps (FLOOR-008 stays PARTIAL):**

| Gap | Remaining |
| --- | --- |
| G1 | host, manager and seating-lead access, plus SEC-002 stand use, behind the owner setting |
| G2 | per-person key wrapping and offline attribution |
| G3 | the minimised named projection (today the sheet is anonymous only, so hosts cannot greet an arriving party) |
| G4 | pending reservations, waitlist adds, seat-existing and arrived/finished/no-show actions, plus the reviewed "already finished" action |
| G5 | offline app shell (today "reloading needs a connection") |
| G6 | the extra deletion triggers and the expired-unreviewed audit row and follow-up |
| G7 | a SERVICE-007 override for grant holders. |

- **FLOOR-009 — Direct host table moves, swaps and locks.** A host or manager moves a booked, arrived or seated party to a free fitting table or permitted combination, swaps two parties’ tables, or locks an assignment, each in one direct action (drag on the floor plan or timeline, or Change assignment on the reservation) on tablet, phone and web. No manager approval is needed. At commit each action checks the live floor version, physical fit, overlapping turns, permitted joins and required access needs, refuses a move into an occupied or clashing table with the reason, and writes one audit row with actor, before/after tables, time and optional reason. A locked assignment is never changed by automatic allocation, reflow or agent proposals until a person unlocks it. The prepare→approve path of PLAN-001 remains for preparation keys and agent proposals only. The owner grants or revokes the venue host capability for an active native member; native account roles remain unchanged. Hosts use direct assignment, service-observation and WAIT-002 intake/party-update commands, never proposal approval, venue administration or bulk guest export. Every direct assignment command requires the exact current floor version. Current combinations must stay in one dining area and each selected table must contain every exact required access tag recorded on the booking. FLOOR-002 and GUEST-003 inherit richer table/access attributes; FLOOR-003 inherits explicit permitted adjacent joins and setup buffers; FLOOR-004 inherits server capacity and serving-history constraints before those capabilities ship. Current and future allocation and agent doors must retain locked assignments until an explicit human unlock; humans also unlock before a direct move or swap. An atomic swap validates the final two-party floor, then writes one audit row containing both parties. Assignment reasons and guest-linked access tags follow DATA-002 erasure. **Acceptance evidence:** Signed in as a host, not a manager, move a seated four-top to a free fitting table, swap two booked parties and lock a third assignment, each in one HTTP command and one floor-screen gesture at 1440 and 390 widths; read the three audit rows. Refuse a move into an occupied table and into a table whose next turn clashes. Book a new party and prove automatic allocation leaves the locked assignment untouched. Prove a preparation key can still only prepare a `table.assign` proposal.

- **FLOOR-010 — Counter seats and unassigned bar pools.** Managers define bars and chef’s counters as seat-level inventory (a 10-seat counter where a two-top takes 2 seats, adjacent where required) and lounge or bar areas as unassigned cover pools with their own pacing and turn times. Counter seats are chosen at booking or assigned at arrival; a pool reservation holds covers without a table until the host seats it. Seats and pools share the one capacity ledger, turns and pacing with tables, and hosts can move a pool or counter party to a table under FLOOR-009. **Acceptance evidence:** Define a 10-seat counter and a 20-cover lounge pool; book five two-tops at the counter and refuse a sixth for the same turn; seat two adjacent counter guests and prove those seats are not sold twice across overlapping turns. Book a lounge reservation, seat it at assigned bar seats on arrival and then move it to a table, reading pool and table occupancy after each step. Before counter seats or pools ship, include their assignments on FLOOR-012 screen, print and PDF and assert the chef’s-counter acceptance there. Current inventory settings and identities are immutable for history. Counter units are physical one-person seats; pool units are anonymous cover holds, not physical seats. Pool inventory requires explicit area selection; hosts assign physical seats before seating, then may transfer to a table while retaining confirmed times and required access. Transfers refuse a destination requiring a longer turn. Counters count individually in physical-seat utilization; anonymous pool capacity is reported separately. Existing correction histories and immutable report publication apply.

- **FLOOR-011 — Late arrivals, holds and the no-show workflow.** Past a configurable grace time a booked party shows as late on the floor and timeline. A host (or the service agent inside a person-approved policy) logs each contact attempt, an outbound call or text, against the booking with its outcome: answered, no answer, voicemail, delivered or failed. When a guest says they are running late, the table is held to a stated time only if the next turn on it allows; otherwise the host sees the clash and the fitting alternatives. A person marks the no-show; the timeline records each step with actor and time, the party’s capacity returns to the shared ledger, the PAY-004 fee policy runs on recorded consent and the freed table is offered to fitting waiting parties under WAIT-004 with a stated hold window. A guest who arrives after release is seated at the next fitting table, never over a reassigned one. **Acceptance evidence:** Book a four-top for 7:15, reach the grace time with no arrival, log two unanswered calls and mark the no-show at 7:30 as a host; read the timeline with each step, actor and time; verify the table returns to availability, one PAY-004 fee is recorded and a fitting waiting party receives a table-ready text with its hold window and is seated. Text “running 15 late” for another booking and verify its table is held to the stated time; refuse an extension that would clash with the next booking on that table.

- **FLOOR-012 — Printable pre-shift sheet.** Before service a host or manager opens one sheet for the service date, printable from the browser, downloadable as PDF and readable on host devices. It lists the guests to know (VIP and regular status with visit count, occasion, declared allergies and access needs from GUEST-003, seating preference and the notes the viewer’s role may see), deposits and card guarantees held with amounts (PAY-002, PAY-003) and unpaid PAY-010 deadlines, the server sections with their tables and expected covers (FLOOR-004), the pacing limits (SERVICE-005) and the kitchen notes of FLOOR-013. It reflects bookings and changes up to the moment it is opened and shows when it was generated. Roles without rights (ROLE-003, ROLE-004) never see restricted notes or contact details on it, and erased guests (DATA-002) never appear with personal values. **Acceptance evidence:** Prepare a Friday with a shellfish-allergic anniversary regular, an eight-top with a deposit and a chef’s-counter booking; open the pre-shift sheet as manager and print it to PDF; read each guest’s flags, deposit and section; change a booking and reopen to see the change and a new generated time; open it as a server and find restricted notes absent; erase one guest and prove a new sheet holds none of their values. Under ct’s 21 October 2026 ruling, FLOOR-012 is done when every existing capability conforms: owner/admin get the full current sheet; owner-granted hosts get names, VIP/regular level, recorded attended visit count, occasion, unverified guest-supplied dietary/allergy/access requests, seating preferences, table/section/server and pacing only. Hosts receive no contact, guest notes or tags. Plain members and preparation keys are refused. One server-side projection feeds HTML, print and on-demand PDF; no sheet or PDF is stored. The date is venue-local; every service starting on that date is included, with current non-canceled/non-no-show bookings and a generated instant. Erased guests show only “Erased guest”, time, party size and table. Saved deposit requests show protection state and their pay-by deadline in the live sheet, print and PDF for managers and hosts; only server-verified paid state establishes protection. No card guarantee or held-deposit amount is inferred; PAY-002 and PAY-003 retain their amount/guarantee duties. Before their capabilities ship, PAY-002, PAY-003, PAY-010, FLOOR-013, GUEST-003, FLOOR-010, ROLE-003 (server acceptance step) and ROLE-004 each inherit their full sheet duties and acceptance in both documents. The deposit eight-top, chef’s-counter and server acceptance steps remain binding in those receivers; current proof uses an ordinary eight-top, guest-supplied requests and a granted host.

- **FLOOR-013 — Service notes and kitchen notes.** Managers attach free-text shift notes (for example “regular booked Thursday, seat in Ana’s section”) and kitchen notes to a service date. Every host device and the pre-shift sheet (FLOOR-012) show them, and edits keep author, time and history. The kitchen view of a service shows the arrival pacing limit and covers expected per interval (SERVICE-005), large parties, counts of dishes, add-ons or tasting choices that guests supplied at booking (BOOK-007, EXP-002) totaled by item, and each declared allergy and access need by table (GUEST-003) with no diagnosis and no statement that food is safe. Counts come only from guest-supplied booking data or manager entry and say which; Placemat never estimates portions. **Acceptance evidence:** As manager add the kitchen note “Halibut: 12 portions” and a shift note; as host open the floor on a second device and read both; collect a halibut pre-order on three bookings and see the item total with its source; record a shellfish allergy for the Table 12 booking and read it in the kitchen view beside the arrival pacing limit; edit the note and read author, time and history; open the kitchen view as a server and find only that server’s section allergies. Before service notes ship, feed current authorized shift/kitchen notes into FLOOR-012 through its one server-filtered projection for screen, print and PDF. FLOOR-013 retains unpaid ordinary-reservation dish pre-orders from a manager-published list; paid or ticketed add-ons belong to EXP-002. FLOOR-013 must add DATA-003 CSV/archive coverage, DATA-001 restore validation and DATA-002 erasure before shipping. Under ct’s 21 October 2026 ruling, FLOOR-013 is done when every current capability conforms: unpaid dish pre-orders are captured on ordinary public reservations from the manager-published per-service list, with integer quantities and the item name preserved. Withdrawn dishes refuse new requests and retain previous quantities. Guest-supplied quantities and manager-entered counts are shown separately, never estimated or treated as a paid order. Kitchen totals and covers include booked, seated and completed reservations, excluding cancelled/no-show parties; large parties are eight or more. Service-date notes use the venue-local date on which the service starts. Owner/admin write notes and publish dishes/counts; owner/admin and granted hosts read shift notes, while owner/admin, granted hosts and plain members read the identity-free kitchen view; preparation keys cannot open it. Note edits append text, actor and instant history; hosts receive live changes through the existing floor version, and the kitchen has live updates plus explicit refresh. Authorized shift and kitchen notes feed FLOOR-012’s one screen/print/PDF projection. Kitchen allergy/access fields are unverified guest-supplied requests by table, with no guest identity/contact fields, diagnosis or safety claim. Paid/ticketed add-ons and tasting choices inherit item/source totals and sheet coverage in EXP-002 before shipping. ROLE-003 inherits server sign-in with own-section allergies, including the full server kitchen acceptance step; GUEST-003 inherits declared/acknowledged allergy and access sources before shipping. Notes/history, published lists, manager counts and booking quantities export in DATA-003 CSVs and structured archives; DATA-001 validates their dates, shapes and relationships before restore. DATA-002 clears the erased guest’s booking quantities/needs and shared note text/history on their booked service dates, redacts the corresponding audit snapshots and fences older archives. Anonymous counts, dates, actors and instants remain. Current tests assert manager/host/member/key boundaries, three guest pre-orders, per-table needs, pacing/large parties, note history/live reads, pre-shift HTML/PDF, portable restore, invalid-reference refusal and erasure. The future server and acknowledged-needs acceptance remains binding in those receivers.

### Waitlist and cancellation demand

- **WAIT-002 — Remote and walk-up joining.** Guests join by QR, website or host intake, state party size, preferred time/area, access needs and contact consent, receive a secure queue-status link and leave or update their party. Duplicate active entries are explained; online joining can be paused independently of staff intake. The QR and website open the same /queue public door; joining reserves no table. An online join requires email for the existing normalized exact-email guest lookup, while staff intake can record a guest without email. Same name or phone never merges people. An active duplicate means the same existing guest id in the same service in queued, offered, accepted or arrived state (including legacy waiting); public refusals give one generic next action without disclosing contact existence. Each intake returns a new private status link once; 32 random bytes form the bearer and only its SHA-256 digest is persisted. The fragment link scopes read, update and leave to that one entry, never guestbook/contact/history reads; rotation replaces its hash and immediately invalidates the old link. The guest saves/copies the link: no email or text send is claimed. Online pause is an owner/admin service setting and affects new public joins only; owner-granted hosts can add a staff party or change its party preferences while paused, but cannot pause intake, approve plans, administer the venue or export guests. Public-created entries and no-phone follow-ups have an active native owner; guest actions are labeled guest-supplied, not verified identity. Preferred times are offset instants inside the service (start inclusive, end exclusive), preferred areas name existing areas, and declared required access tags are exact case-sensitive strings carried into capacity-checked seating and FLOOR-009 assignment. Preferences do not promise a table. Contact permission is an explicit optional boolean for this queue, independent of marketing and of joining; changes keep source, actor and receipt time. SERVICE-004 channel checks govern public join/update and SERVICE-006 full-turn/reset checks still govern actual seating. Resolved entries remain readable by their link but cannot be changed or rotated. DATA-002 erasure clears the link hash and guest-linked preference/contact-permission/history values; the link then returns the same generic unavailable response as an unknown link, while anonymous timing and accountability remain behind existing restore fences. **Acceptance evidence:** Join by phone QR and staff intake, refuse a duplicate, change party size and pause online intake while allowing a host entry. WAIT-002 queue intake stays open at pacing caps, labelled “queued only; no table or time promised”; pacing is enforced when a person seats, books or allocates from the queue.

- **WAIT-003 — Quoted waits and queue updates.** Hosts quote a range with timestamp and basis, distinguish reservation requests from same-day walk-ins and update guests when the estimate changes. Queue order accounts for fit and promises with a visible reason; never label a forecast as a guaranteed table. **Acceptance evidence:** Quote 20–30 minutes, delay a turn, revise the range and inspect the delivered update and guest status; seat a later fitting two-top while documenting the six-top’s retained priority.

- **WAIT-004 — Table-ready conversations and offer expiry.** A fitting party receives a table-ready SMS with reply/arrival window and status link. Yes, no, late, free-text and unanswered replies reach the host; expiring an offer releases its hold before the next party is offered it. **Acceptance evidence:** Notify two matching parties sequentially; let the first expire and have both reply yes together, proving only the still-valid offer seats and the other receives a clear response.

- **WAIT-005 — Future cancellation notifications.** Guests request alerts for sold-out dates, party sizes and experiences separately from the live queue. Managers control offer priority, eligible inventory and response windows; notify requests expire or stop on opt-out and fulfilled requests close automatically. **Acceptance evidence:** Request Saturday experience availability, cancel one ticket, notify eligible guests in the configured order and turn the accepted offer into one paid reservation. Cancel a same-day table and verify the freed table is offered to fitting waiting parties and notify requests in the configured order, and the book shows how many tables were offered and how many were filled.

- **WAIT-006 — Waitlist accountability.** Hosts see queued, offered, accepted, arrived, seated, declined, expired and abandoned states with wait quoted versus realized. Manual priority changes, no-contact parties and missed offers have reasons and owners; service close resolves every remaining entry. Current owner/admin staff manage queue statuses, quotes, priority, seating and close; owner-granted WAIT-002 hosts may add intake and update party preferences. ROLE-003 carries broader host queue rights before they ship. Offers and replies here are explicitly staff-recorded observations, never claimed provider sends or table holds; WAIT-004 inherits actual delivery and expiring inventory holds before shipping. New entries record intake time; quoted ranges retain basis and observation time. Actual wait is elapsed intake-to-seat or intake-to-terminal-disposition minutes (shown rounded to the nearest tenth); legacy missing intake times remain unknown. Higher numeric priority sorts first and changes keep the acting manager, reason and prior value. Closing the service expires offered/accepted entries and abandons other unresolved parties, retaining seated history and assigning follow-up; new booking/intake doors refuse the closed service. Queue text follows DATA-002 erasure. **Acceptance evidence:** Close a shift containing an unanswered offer, a no-phone party and a seated party; inspect dispositions, actual waits and assigned follow-up with no unresolved ghost offers.

### Delivered communications and follow-up

- **MSG-002 — Twilio SMS and WhatsApp connection.** Owners connect a venue’s Twilio sender with US A2P registration and WhatsApp business/template approval where required. Signed inbound/status webhooks attach provider IDs to guest threads; sender setup distinguishes pending, failed and usable channels. **Acceptance evidence:** Connect approved test senders, send a table-ready SMS and WhatsApp template, ingest signed delivery/reply events and reject a forged webhook; surface unregistered sender failure to the manager.

- **MSG-003 — Resend email connection.** Owners verify a sending domain with Resend, configure reply routing and receive signed delivery, bounce and complaint events. Transactional guest mail uses the restaurant’s identity, safe templates and recorded provider outcomes; authentication mail alone does not count as booking delivery. **Acceptance evidence:** Verify the domain, send a booking email to a controlled mailbox, reply to it and process bounce/complaint callbacks; show the guest thread and delivery state without leaking secrets.

- **MSG-004 — Booking and cancellation delivery.** Reservation creation, meaningful changes and cancellation automatically enqueue the selected SMS/email notices with local time, party size, policy, location and manage-booking link. Capture queued/sent/delivered/failed outcomes independently; a booking stays visible if delivery fails. **Acceptance evidence:** Book online, modify and cancel; inspect three distinct provider receipts and the guest’s messages, then fail one delivery and find a staff follow-up without a duplicate booking.

- **MSG-005 — Scheduled reminders and reconfirmations.** Managers set reminder offsets, preferred channels, quiet hours and reconfirmation deadlines per service. Guests reconfirm or cancel by link or by replying C or X to the SMS; replies resolve against that guest’s active booking through MSG-006 and an ambiguous reply goes to the host. Jobs stop for cancellation, avoid repeats after restart and record confirmed/unanswered/failed outcomes with a host queue before service. **Acceptance evidence:** Schedule a 24-hour reconfirmation and 2-hour reminder, confirm one booking by link and another by replying C, cancel a third by replying X and restart the scheduler; verify correct recipients, no repeats and an owned unanswered task.

- **MSG-006 — Unified two-way guest inbox.** Hosts read and reply to email, SMS and WhatsApp in one guest/reservation thread, assign conversations, set due times, use templates and resolve/reopen them. Incoming replies to old bookings are clearly labeled; two staff cannot unknowingly answer the same active claim. **Acceptance evidence:** Receive a late-arrival text, assign it to a host, reply from the inbox, receive an email follow-up and resolve it; verify both channels and reservation context in one history.

- **MSG-007 — Delivery retry and failed-contact ownership.** Provider timeouts, throttling, bounces and unknown outcomes have bounded retry and idempotency rules. Unknown sends are reconciled before retry, permanent failures create an assigned contact task, and alternate channels require appropriate permission rather than bypassing opt-out. **Acceptance evidence:** Timeout after a provider accepts a send, replay its callback and restart the job; prove one message, then bounce another address and complete the assigned phone-contact task.

- **MSG-008 — Consent and US messaging policy.** Store transactional and marketing permissions separately by channel, venue, purpose, source and time. Honor STOP/HELP, unsubscribe, suppression and quiet hours immediately across imports, jobs and agents; keep policy evidence and never infer marketing consent from a reservation. **Acceptance evidence:** Book without marketing consent, attempt a campaign, then opt in and send; reply STOP while another job is queued and prove the queued send is suppressed without losing booking management. GUEST-004 inheritance: permissions remain tied to their own email/phone and channel, venue and purpose; a merge never grants unknown permission or overrides the more restrictive value or suppression. Prove this on every future provider/job/agent send door.

- **MSG-009 — Templates and guest communication preferences.** Managers preview and version restaurant-branded templates in supported guest languages with accessible text, US date/phone conventions, exact cancellation terms and safe substitutions. Guests can select supported channels; missing translations and unusable contacts become explicit tasks. **Acceptance evidence:** Preview and deliver an English/Spanish reminder with long names and special characters, then change the template; prior messages retain their actual rendered content and policy version.

- **MSG-010 — Guest text actions: confirm, reschedule and captured requests.** Reminder and confirmation texts carry plain reply actions: C confirms, R starts a reschedule and X cancels (MSG-005 defines C and X; this clause adds R). Replies resolve against the guest’s active booking. R sends a scoped manage-booking link (BOOK-004) offering nearby times (BOOK-003) and reaches a host when none fits. A free-text reply that states an occasion or request (“It’s our anniversary, candle on dessert”) is stored on the booking as a guest-supplied tag and note with source, time and the original text, shown to hosts and on the pre-shift sheet (FLOOR-012); a host can correct or remove it. A reply that states an allergy or access need goes to the host as an unresolved request to acknowledge and record under GUEST-003, never as a silent tag, and no reply creates a diagnosis or marketing consent. Anything ambiguous goes to the host inbox (MSG-006). **Acceptance evidence:** Send a reminder; reply “C! It’s our anniversary, candle on dessert” and verify the booking is confirmed with an anniversary tag and candle-on-dessert note sourced to the guest reply; reply R on another booking and complete a reschedule through the link; reply “I’m allergic to shellfish” on a third and verify it reaches the host as an unresolved request rather than a structured allergy; reply STOP and verify no further send (MSG-008).

- **MSG-011 — Instagram and Facebook direct messages.** Owners connect their Instagram professional account and Facebook Page messaging through Meta’s approved messaging API. Direct messages arrive in the guest and reservation thread of MSG-006 with the account, time and provider message ids. Hosts, and under an approved policy the service agent (AGENT-001), answer inside Meta’s messaging window. A booking made in a DM uses the shared live inventory, carries the social source (DIST-004) and is confirmed in the same thread and the guest’s chosen channel. Outside the window, or where the account type lacks access, the sender gets an explanation and a booking link rather than silence; a revoked or unauthorized connection shows as an owned setup task. **Acceptance evidence:** Connect a Meta test page, receive a DM asking for a table for two, reply from the inbox with 9:15 at the bar and book it; see one booking assigned to the bar with source Instagram and the confirmation in the thread. Let the window lapse and verify the reply is refused with a booking-link fallback; deliver a replayed webhook and find one message; revoke the connection and find an owned task.

### Payments and table protection

- **PAY-001 — Stripe merchant connection and token custody.** The restaurant connects its own Stripe account for USD charges, deposits and refunds, completes merchant onboarding and sees capability/revocation state. Hosted fields/Checkout collect payment details; Placemat stores references and never raw PAN/CVC or merchant funds. **Acceptance evidence:** Connect a Stripe test merchant, collect a hosted payment method, inspect redacted product records and disconnect; existing obligations stay visible while new charges are blocked.

- **PAY-002 — Deposits and partial prepayment.** Managers require fixed or per-person deposits by service, party size, experience or channel, disclose terms before checkout and link the receipt to one capacity-held reservation. Failures and abandoned checkout release holds; deposit balance is available for POS settlement. Before shipping, this capability inherits BOUND-001: each payment is tied to one named booking or event, shown as a balance against it and refunded under PAY-005; it is nontransferable, cannot be topped up and cannot be redeemed outside that booking or event or spent as a general balance. **Ct ruling, 25 October 2026 — APPROVED WITH RIDERS; PAY-002 remains PARTIAL.** The interim workflow uses existing personal owner or native admin-manager authority to create fixed-USD or per-person booking-bound deposit requests and explicitly close collection. For a per-person request, preserve the original booking reference, party count, integer-cent USD rate, total and saved deadline; later booking or policy changes do not rewrite that request or authorize another collection through its original scope. Existing PAY-010 host authority, including a live authorized host PIN session, may issue or copy the saved request and use existing status-verification doors without acquiring request-setting, waiver, refund, payment-administration or ledger authority. Stripe retains payment credentials and money movement; Placemat retains restricted references and recorded outcomes, not PAN/CVC or merchant funds. Creating or copying a hosted link establishes neither delivery nor guest receipt or consent, collected money, bank settlement, POS credit, seating release or refund. Paid/protected claims require matching authenticated provider facts. PAY-002 pre-checkout disclosure, BOOK-004 financial-consequence consent, applicable PAY-003/PAY-004 agreement and MSG-008 channel-permission duties remain separate and binding. This slice authorizes no automatic send, reservation release, refund or seating settlement. Unresolved Checkout collection preserves the reservation; collection closure and any permitted booking cancellation remain separate explicit actions under BOOK-006. The complete original payment, refund, capacity, display and seating acceptance remains binding. **Acceptance evidence:** Require a $25-per-person deposit for four guests, pay $100, retry the callback and inspect one paid booking; fail another payment and verify its table becomes bookable. Each deposit held shows on the booking, the confirmation and the pre-shift sheet (FLOOR-012) with its amount, per-guest rate and the card’s last four digits, and states what happens at seating; seating the booking applies it to the check (PAY-008) or releases the hold exactly once and shows which. Prove the inherited BOUND-001 boundary: inspect the booking/event-bound balance and PAY-005 refund, and refuse transfer, top-up, redemption against another booking/event and general-balance spending. Before deposits ship, FLOOR-012 shows held deposit amounts on its manager sheet and only amounts permitted by the receiving role policy; assert the deposited eight-top in its screen, print and PDF.

- **PAY-003 — Card guarantees and authorization expiry.** Guests provide a tokenized card guarantee or supported authorization with explicit no-show terms. The venue sees authorization expiry and recollection tasks; a saved card is not described as an indefinite card hold and the restaurant must use the approved mandate for later charging. **Ct expiry ruling, 25 October 2026 — APPROVED WITH CHANGES for the expiry foundation.** Expiry restricts authority and creates none: ownership, owner attestation, a saved card or a successful setup alone never authorize a fee. The original booking, guest, dated service, arrival, party count, immutable policy, USD-cent amount and fixed or per-person basis remain binding; material changes need matching fresh agreement. Save a finite deadline no later than that dated service's absolute end instant and display it in venue time. Earlier revocation or an applicable guest or provider limit wins. Shortening the service permanently shortens authority; extending or rescheduling never extends saved authority. A violation before expiry permits no new charge attempt after expiry. A previously submitted reserved decision may reconcile its known provider operation after expiry without a replacement decision, key or charge; an uncertain operation without a known provider reference needs manual reconciliation once authority expires. Legacy unbounded authority expires on upgrade; missing or invalid expiry is refused or conservatively expired on restore. Historical archives restore neither credentials nor charging authority. Explicit recollection is attributable owner-held work for an upcoming active retained booking; it sends nothing, changes no expiry and establishes no renewal. Erasure fences, attributable history, role-safe sheets and DATA-001 through DATA-004 remain binding. BOOK-004, BOOK-006, PAY-004, PAY-010, MSG-008, FLOOR-012, GUEST-004 and AUDIT-001 retain their receiving duties. This foundation ruling does not approve the later merchant and guest-collection default or certify a provider mandate. **CT ruling, 26 October 2026 — APPROVE WITH RIDERS; PAY-003 remains PARTIAL.** The merchant collection, guest mandate, manual authorization and explicit capture default is approved subject to the 25 October expiry riders. A personal owner explicitly enables collection; the guest accepts exact immutable booking-bound terms before hosted setup or authorization. Integer-cent USD authorization cannot exceed the agreed maximum fee. Authority ends at the earliest saved guest limit, dated service end, owner revocation or verified provider deadline, and later changes never extend it. A fresh explicit owner decision for a matching actual violation may capture only the original verified authorization within its permitted amount and deadline. Uncertainty reserves the original operation; it permits observation, not a replacement charge. Unconfirmed release retains the last verified held amount, and renewed authorization waits for confirmed release of the earlier hold and fresh applicable agreement. Recollection remains attributable owner-held work without an automatic message or renewed authority. Personal-owner restrictions on staff financial projections remain in force. The complete guarantee and permitted-fee acceptance remains binding; this ruling grants no completion or legal certification. **Acceptance evidence:** Create a guaranteed reservation, expire an authorization and request renewed collection; prove an expired hold is not reported as protected and inspect guest consent to a permitted later fee. Before card guarantees ship, FLOOR-012 shows held guarantee amounts only to permitted roles in the live sheet, print and PDF, without card credentials.

- **PAY-004 — No-show and late-cancellation fees.** Versioned policies define cutoffs in venue local time, per-person/fixed fees, grace, exemptions and required evidence. Authorized people approve exceptional fees, waivers and disputes; normal policy execution uses recorded consent and cannot charge the same violation twice. Before shipping, PAY-004 adds charged and waived fee figures, with reservation drilldowns and CSV/PDF columns, to the REPORT-007 end-of-service snapshot fixed at close. **Acceptance evidence:** Cancel before and after a DST-aware cutoff, mark a no-show, waive one fee and charge another through Stripe; replay requests and inspect one charge plus the deciding person and policy. Close the service and reconcile the charged and waived fees in its REPORT-007 report, CSV and PDF.

- **PAY-005 — Full and partial refunds with notices.** Authorized staff preview refundable balances, select full/partial amounts and reasons, follow manager limits and submit one processor refund. Pending, succeeded and failed states reconcile from signed events; guest SMS/email receipts name amount, remaining balance and actual outcome. Before shipping, PAY-005 adds refunded fee figures, with reservation drilldowns and CSV/PDF columns, to the REPORT-007 end-of-service snapshot fixed at close. PAY-005 inherits ROLE-002: A limit is integer USD cents. No recorded limit means no refund authority, and owners are uncapped. It caps the sum of pending and succeeded refunds that person submits against one booking's charges, so splitting cannot exceed it. PAY-005 refuses an excess before any processor call. Only an owner sets limits, with AUDIT-001 before/after history. **Ct assertions:** with a 10000 limit, refunding $60 then $40 of $150 succeeds and a further $0.01 is refused; a manager with no limit is refused. **Acceptance evidence:** Refund $40 of a $100 deposit, replay its webhook, refund the remaining $60 and refuse a further cent; verify processor references, delivery receipts and failed-refund follow-up. Refund a no-show fee and reconcile it in the closed service’s REPORT-007 report, CSV and PDF.

- **PAY-006 — Money ledger and processor reconciliation.** An immutable minor-unit USD ledger relates reservation, charge, deposit, fee, transfer, refund, dispute and payout references. Signed webhooks are deduplicated and out-of-order events reconciled; finance can resolve unmatched settlements without changing historical amounts. **Ct ruling, 25 October 2026 — APPROVED WITH RIDERS; PAY-006 remains PARTIAL.** Only a full personal venue owner may use the interim ledger-read, payout-import and explicit unmatched-attribution doors. This neither enlarges nor withdraws ROLE-004's existing limited charge/refund finance read/export authority; scoped finance settlement reconciliation remains a contracted target. Payout import retrieves the complete provider settlement through read-only provider requests and reconciles USD gross, fees and net; incomplete or inconsistent retrieval establishes no reconciled payout. An attribution correction appends a separately identifiable human decision linking an existing unmatched transaction to an existing booking. It may change derived attribution, never historical amounts, currency, fees, net, processor references, payout snapshots or economic-event history. The original provider facts and the actor/time/source of the human decision remain distinguishable and inspectable, with AUDIT-001 before/after and reason-when-recorded duties. Attribution is not provider confirmation of an absent booking reference. It cannot hide an amount or lifecycle discrepancy, manufacture a balancing entry or make a financial difference disappear by marking an item matched. These doors grant no charge, refund, send, deletion or automatic provider-write authority. The complete original reference relationships, signed-event deduplication, out-of-order reconciliation, finance delegation, audit, portability, correction and DATA-004 retention obligations remain binding. **Acceptance evidence:** Deliver refund before charge callbacks, duplicate both and reconcile a Stripe payout to its bookings, fees and net amount; correct an unmatched item with a new adjustment record.

- **PAY-007 — Tax gratuity and service-charge disclosure.** Experience checkout itemizes base price, add-ons, discounts, US sales tax through Stripe Tax or configured approved tax rules, mandatory service charge and optional gratuity. Guests see total before payment and receipts preserve the applied rates/basis; refunds reverse allocated amounts correctly. **Acceptance evidence:** Buy two $95 tickets with add-ons, tax, service charge and tip, inspect line-level USD totals and partially refund one ticket including its allocated tax and eligible charges.

- **PAY-008 — Deposit redemption at the POS.** A seated guest’s eligible deposit/prepaid balance is handed to the mapped POS check with a stable redemption reference. Partial use, split checks, check voids and provider outages reconcile without double credit; unreconciled amounts remain in a finance queue. **Acceptance evidence:** Seat a $100-deposit booking, apply $60 to one check and $40 to a second, void one check and reconcile; prove the guest never receives duplicate credit.

- **PAY-009 — Disputes and payment operations.** Managers receive failed-card, dispute and chargeback tasks with deadlines, consent/attendance/message evidence and processor links. They approve responses, review refunds and fee exposure, and export finance records for QuickBooks Online or the separate Pantry accounting product. **Acceptance evidence:** Open a test dispute, assemble the booking/policy/message evidence, approve a response and export its ledger to accounting; trace a rejected sync back to an owned task.

- **PAY-010 — Staff-requested card and deposit links.** When a host or manager creates or changes a phone, concierge, in-house or inquiry-converted reservation that a deposit or card-guarantee policy covers (PAY-002, PAY-003), Placemat sends the guest a scoped, expiring link by SMS and/or email to Stripe-hosted collection, showing the amount or guarantee terms, the policy text and a pay-by deadline in venue local time. Staff can resend, change channel or copy the link, and never key card numbers into Placemat. Until collected the booking shows as unprotected with its deadline on the floor, timeline and reservation list; a staff reminder task is created at a set lead time and an optional guest reminder is sent. At the deadline the venue policy either releases the table and cancels the booking with a delivered guest notice, or flags it for a person to decide. Paying before release marks the booking protected and links the receipt. A permitted role can waive the requirement with a recorded reason, and waivers are reported. **Acceptance evidence:** As a host, book a six-top by phone under a $25-per-person deposit policy; read the delivered SMS and email provider receipts carrying a link to Stripe-hosted test collection with a deadline; pay and see the booking marked protected with its receipt. Book a second party and leave it unpaid: see the unprotected flag and the staff reminder task, advance past the deadline and verify the table is released, the booking canceled and the guest notified; replay a late payment callback and verify the booking is not resurrected without a person and the payment is refunded or flagged. Waive a third party’s requirement with a reason and read its audit row. Before payment requests ship, FLOOR-012 shows unpaid deadlines and protection state only to permitted roles in its live sheet, print and PDF.

### Experiences and ticketed dining

- **EXP-001 — Experience catalog and event inventory.** Restaurants publish free, deposit-backed or fully prepaid dining experiences, tasting menus and one-off events with images, menu, dates, seating areas, ticket classes, quantity limits and cancellation rules. Experience inventory shares physical tables and pacing with ordinary reservations. Experience-specific turn duration, cleanup and last seating conform to SERVICE-006 before publication. Before this capability ships, its experience filter inherits BOOK-003 search, exact fit and stale-result reselect. Current catalog pricing describes required terms; free experiences book through the shared guest reservation and hold doors, while deposit and prepaid listings explicitly take no payment or reservation until EXP-002 supplies checkout. Class limits count guest covers per dated service, including active and completed reservations and live checkout holds. Experience dining time is a minimum with longer table, area and party rules preserved; cleanup uses the longer reset and last seating respects both policies. Frozen booking terms survive catalog edits. EXP-002 inherits these allocation, full-turn, reset, quantity and checkout-hold semantics before paid tickets ship. **Acceptance evidence:** Publish a tasting dinner and a free patio event, book both beside normal reservations and prove the same table cannot be sold through two catalogs and that its experience-specific turn and reset fit SERVICE-006.

- **EXP-002 — Ticketed checkout and add-ons.** Guests select ticket quantities and per-person dietary choices, wine pairings or other prepaid add-ons, see availability and an itemized USD checkout, pay through Stripe and receive a scoped ticket receipt. Limited add-ons have their own inventory and cannot be oversold. Ticket checkout fits its experience-specific SERVICE-006 turn and cleanup in the shared physical inventory. Before shipping, this capability inherits BOUND-001: each payment is tied to one named booking or event, shown as a balance against it and refunded under PAY-005; it is nontransferable, cannot be topped up and cannot be redeemed outside that booking or event or spent as a general balance. Current zero-charge ticket options use manager-published stable add-on identities, per-service stock shared across classes, and optional numbered guest dietary choices. Active holds and booked, seated and completed reservations consume stock; expiry, explicit abandonment and cancellation release it. Confirmed carts keep original quantities and names; erasure clears personal choices while retaining anonymous stock facts. Kitchen and pre-shift projections retain current role and server-section boundaries. Adopted pending ct: paid self-service is denied by default; catalog publication confers no payment execution authority. EXP-002 retains its full paid acceptance and PAY-007 money allocation, BOUND-001 financial limits, PAY-005 refund and BOOK-006 processor recovery duties. **Acceptance evidence:** Buy four tasting tickets with two pairings and one limited supplement, race the last supplement from another checkout and verify one sale plus accurate remaining capacity and an experience-specific SERVICE-006 turn and reset. Prove the inherited BOUND-001 boundary: inspect the booking-bound or event-bound balance and PAY-005 refund, and refuse transfer, top-up, redemption against another booking or event and general-balance spending. Paid or ticketed pre-order add-ons inherit guest-supplied item totals in FLOOR-013 and the authorized FLOOR-012 sheet before shipping; unpaid ordinary-reservation dish pre-orders remain FLOOR-013’s current duty. Before experience checkout ships, it inherits BOOK-006 short-lived inventory holds, visible expiry, safe release and stable booking and payment recovery.

- **EXP-003 — Experience guest management.** Hosts see attendee names, purchaser versus attendee contacts, questionnaire answers, tickets, dietary constraints and paid balances, check guests in and manage authorized transfers or exchanges without duplicating seats or broadening consent. **Acceptance evidence:** Transfer one ticket to a new attendee, exchange another to a later seating with a price difference, then check in by scoped ticket and refuse a reused ticket.

- **EXP-004 — Experience cancellation and event settlement.** Managers cancel or reschedule an event with a preview of affected guests, refund/credit choices and outreach. Reports reconcile ticket sales, discounts, taxes, gratuities, fees, refunds, attendance and net receipts by event and seating. **Acceptance evidence:** Reschedule one seating, refund guests who decline, notify all affected purchasers and reconcile the resulting attendance and settlement report to the Stripe ledger.

- **EXP-005 — Prepaid pickup experiences.** Tock-style packaged dining/take-home experiences can sell a bounded pickup slot and optional add-ons with prepaid capacity, confirmation and pickup status, handing item fulfillment to the venue’s POS/order system. Full kitchen ordering and delivery dispatch remain separate systems. Before shipping, this capability inherits BOUND-001: each payment is tied to one named booking or event, shown as a balance against it and refunded under PAY-005; it is nontransferable, cannot be topped up and cannot be redeemed outside that booking or event or spent as a general balance. **Acceptance evidence:** Publish a Thanksgiving take-home pickup experience, pay for a 4 p.m. slot, transfer its line items to the connected POS and mark pickup complete; reject a sold-out slot and refund a canceled order. Prove the inherited BOUND-001 boundary: inspect the booking/event-bound balance and PAY-005 refund, and refuse transfer, top-up, redemption against another booking/event and general-balance spending.

### Guest relationships and repeat visits

- **GUEST-002 — Searchable profiles and structured preferences.** Hosts search normalized phone, email and name, maintain guest tags, VIP level, seating preferences and dated service notes, and see reservation/visit history in one profile. Imported versus guest-supplied versus staff-observed facts keep provenance and restricted notes obey role rights. Current owner/admin operations staff perform the host workflow until ROLE-003 adds the host role; current member/preparation-key readers retain ACCESS-001 guest-note visibility. Explicit facts keep guest-supplied, imported or staff-observed provenance; missing legacy source or original import date is labeled not recorded. Search normalization does not change exact-email identity matching. Every future restricted fact, role and access scope introduced by GUEST-003, ROLE-003, ROLE-004 and DATA-004 must conform in profile, search, arrival and backup doors before shipping. **Acceptance evidence:** Find a returning guest by US phone, add a VIP tag and seating preference, then book again and view the preferences and their sources at arrival.

- **GUEST-003 — Allergy and accessibility handoff.** Guest-declared allergies, dietary and access needs are separate explicit fields with date/source and staff acknowledgment. Host/server handover and the connected POS show the relevant facts without an AI inventing a diagnosis or declaring food safe; stale or conflicting notes require clarification. Before richer access needs ship, enforce FLOOR-009 required access constraints on direct/prepared moves, swaps and booking allocation. **Acceptance evidence:** Book a nut-allergic guest requiring step-free seating, acknowledge both at check-in, send the declared facts to POS and correct an outdated note with its author/date retained. Before acknowledged allergy/access facts ship, feed them with their declared/acknowledged source into FLOOR-012 screen, print and PDF; keep the guest-supplied/unverified distinction and no safety claim. Before this capability ships, FLOOR-013’s kitchen view inherits declared/acknowledged allergy and access sources by table, retaining the no-diagnosis/no-safety-claim distinction; assert the acknowledged-needs kitchen step as well as its pre-shift receivers.

- **GUEST-004 — Duplicate review and household separation.** Potential duplicate profiles are suggested from normalized identities and visit context, with a preview of conflicts, linked bookings, consent and spend before an authorized merge. Shared household numbers do not auto-merge people; merges are traceable and mistaken merges can be reversed safely. **Acceptance evidence:** Import two emails for one guest and a shared family phone, review suggestions, merge only the true duplicate and reverse it without losing visits or changing anyone’s marketing permissions. Matching follows ct scope51 (21 October 2026): email is trimmed/lowercased only; US phone is normalized to +1; names compare exactly after accent/case normalization. Suggest only the same email or the same phone plus name; shared phone with a different name is a household and is never mergeable. Imports retain distinct source IDs with collision warnings, never automatic merging. Owner/admin previews choose the surviving profile; typed confirmation and current profile/linked-record versions fence each atomic mutation. Selected profile fields remain selected; both originals, provenance, notes and visits remain in the manager-only journal, alternate contacts retain their source identity, and approved reminders retain their original recipients. Queue consent stays bound to the original phone; the most restrictive recorded value wins for a shared phone, unknown never grants, and unrelated household permission stays separate. Marketing permission and spend remain not recorded. Unmerge restores only unchanged records and lists later edits/new records for manual assignment without overwriting them or restoring more permissive consent. Journal CSV and structured archives include snapshots, aliases, contact provenance and pending assignments with relationship validation. Erasing a merged identity erases its reviewed aliases and unresolved profiles still carrying that identity pending assignment, purges related journal snapshots and linked audit/operational personal values, and permanently blocks reversal and pre-erasure restore. MSG-008 inherits contact/channel/purpose-specific consent and suppression; GUEST-005 inherits POS visit/payment relationship reassignment before those capabilities ship.

- **GUEST-005 — POS-linked visit and item history.** Profiles link attended reservations to checks, item/category spend, discounts, tips and refunds, distinguishing payer from companions and ambiguous matches. Historical imports preserve their original source; unmatched or split checks never inflate guest lifetime spend. **Acceptance evidence:** Seat a returning party, split its POS bill, refund an item and inspect the payer’s visit/spend history; leave ambiguous companions unassigned until a person resolves them. - **CRM-001 — Visit-based segments and audiences.** Managers build saved segments from visit frequency, recency, experience, source, VIP tags, no-shows, feedback and POS spend, previewing inclusion reasons and channel eligibility.
