- **CRM-002 — Retention and win-back automation.** Owner-approved workflows trigger welcome, birthday/anniversary, first-to-second visit, lapsed-guest and experience invitations from recorded guest facts and completed visits. Frequency caps, quiet hours, stop conditions and campaign attribution apply; draft preview names recipients and the exact offer. **Acceptance evidence:** Approve a post-first-visit workflow, finish two visits and cancel a third, then advance the scheduler and inspect the right delivered messages and repeat bookings; suppress a guest who opts out mid-run.

- **CRM-003 — Campaign creation and conversion reporting.** Managers compose branded campaigns, test renders, preview recipients/cost, schedule send and pause/cancel remaining sends. Delivery, clicks, unsubscribes, attributed reservations, attended covers and actual POS revenue are separate measures with explicit attribution windows. **Acceptance evidence:** Send a controlled campaign, book from one tracked link, cancel another booking and reconcile delivered count, attended covers and realized revenue without crediting canceled or unpaid visits.

- **CRM-004 — Mailchimp audience handoff.** Owners connect Mailchimp and map only permissioned guest fields, tags and segments. Subscribe/unsubscribe and deletion changes reconcile both ways with source/timestamps and failure tasks; syncing a list cannot upgrade an unknown consent state or resend suppressed guests. **Acceptance evidence:** Sync an opted-in segment, unsubscribe one contact in Mailchimp and erase another in Placemat; retry a failed sync and verify neither contact is reintroduced into a campaign.

- **CRM-005 — Post-visit feedback and manager follow-up.** *Cites:* DATA-002, DATA-003, ROLE-003. Completed visits trigger consent-appropriate surveys; feedback links are scoped to the visit and duplicate responses are handled. Poor feedback creates an assigned recovery case with SLA, guest reply thread and closure outcome; public-review requests avoid filtering guests by sentiment. **Acceptance evidence:** Complete two visits, submit low feedback on one and positive feedback on the other, verify consistent public-review invitation rules and resolve the manager’s recovery case with a delivered reply.

- **POS-001 — Toast connection.** The owner completes Toast partner/merchant authorization and maps restaurant, service areas, tables, checks and guest identities. - **POS-003 — Clover connection.** Owners connect their Clover merchant account and map dining tables, orders, customers, payments and refunds. Missing table identifiers become explicit reconciliation tasks; staff can confirm a candidate match without importing unrelated merchant/customer data. **Acceptance evidence:** Connect a Clover test merchant, match a table’s open order to its seated booking, settle and refund it; resolve an order lacking table metadata and inspect attributed spend.

- **POS-004 — Lightspeed connection.** Placemat supports the restaurant’s declared Lightspeed Restaurant edition through its approved API/partner access, maps floor/check identities and consumes item, payment and table progress. Backfilled checks retain original service times and cannot mark current tables ready from old events. **Acceptance evidence:** Disconnect the Aloha bridge during dinner, complete two checks, reconnect and inspect backfill spend while proving yesterday’s close event does not clear today’s occupied table.

- **POS-006 — Guest and check matching controls.** Deterministic links use reservation/table/time/location and verified guest identity; probable matches show confidence/reasons for human review. Split/combined checks, multiple payers, table moves and walk-ins preserve provenance, with reversible corrections and unmatched-check queues. **Acceptance evidence:** Move a party between tables, combine two checks and split payment; review an ambiguous guest match, correct it and compare both profiles’ spend before and after.

- **POS-007 — Live check and kitchen pace.** POS check/course status, actual turn progress, server staffing and permitted kitchen-load signals inform availability and proposed pacing. Stale signals are clearly aged, paid does not mean clean, and kitchen/host limits always constrain an automatic status update. **Acceptance evidence:** Open, course, pay and clear a check, slow a kitchen signal and inspect suggested availability; drop the POS feed and prove the last observed state is labeled stale instead of assumed ready.

### Service and commercial reporting

- **REPORT-001 — Covers cancellations and no-shows.** Managers filter historical/current/future reservations by venue, local service date, shift, area, source, status and party size (inclusive bounds from 1 to 500, the largest supported party; no bound means every size); reports distinguish booked, attended, canceled and no-show covers and rates with visible denominators and downloadable row drilldown. Dates are inclusive venue-local service-start dates; period uses the service interval, with end ≤ now past and start ≤ now < end current. Booked covers include every reservation status, attended means seated/completed, and canceled/no-show/attended rates use all filtered booked covers as denominator (zero gives no rate). A combined-table booking counts once. Every existing venue, area and source is included; additional venues (ROLE-001), floor areas (FLOOR-002) and channels (DIST-001–DIST-004, BOOK-005, VOICE-001, AGENT-001) inherit these filters and reports before shipping. **Acceptance evidence:** Run two shifts with cancellations and no-shows, filter one local date, drill a total to its bookings and reconcile its CSV to attended versus booked covers.

- **REPORT-002 — Turns waits and server performance.** Reports compare expected/actual turns, arrival lateness, quoted/actual waits, abandoned queues, seating utilization, interval pacing, staff pacing overrides and server/section covers, with sample sizes and missing observations shown. Staff corrections remain traceable rather than rewriting prior published results. Current staff-recorded observations use raw elapsed minutes; labels round to two decimals. Missing facts stay unknown and carry sample/missing counts; distributions show mean, median, nearest-rank p90 and exact observation drilldowns. Expected turn preserves the original confirmed interval; actual turn uses corrected seating-to-completion, and departure delay separately compares completion (or an ongoing party at report generation) to the original departure. Quotes are recorded ranges; deviation is negative below the lower bound, zero within it and positive above the upper bound. Historical attended covers belong to the server and section recorded at the corrected seating instant; current assigned expected covers are separate, and missing seating assignments are explicit. Utilization is unioned occupied physical table-seat minutes divided by available physical table-seat minutes within service bounds, with known ongoing observations identified and setup/cleanup excluded. Managers publish immutable, attributed snapshots and can compare later live corrections or publish a new snapshot; histories retain original and correcting events without guest names, contacts, notes or reasons. Existing observations all conform; WAIT-003 provider estimates, POS-007 observations and FLOOR-010 seat/pool inventory inherit these reporting and correction obligations before shipping. **Acceptance evidence:** Complete a service with two overruns and a waitlist abandonment, inspect turn/wait distributions and server totals and trace an outlier back to its status history.

- **REPORT-003 — Channels spend and repeat business.** Owners compare direct/Google/social/partner campaign conversion, cover/source fees, average check, spend per cover, repeat-visit cohorts, retention and realized revenue. Paid, refunded and merely reserved revenue remain distinct; attribution rules and unmatched POS data are visible. **Acceptance evidence:** Book from three sources, attend two, refund one and revisit another month; reconcile source cost, net revenue and repeat cohort to the booking and check ledger.

- **REPORT-004 — Experience and payment performance.** Event/seating dashboards reconcile ticket inventory, sold/held/refunded tickets, add-ons, attendance, deposits, no-show recovery, processor fees and outstanding liabilities with the immutable payment ledger. **Acceptance evidence:** Close a partly refunded tasting event, export settlement and inspect drilldowns from net receipts to Stripe transactions and from occupancy to check-ins.

- **REPORT-005 — Scheduled exports and group reporting.** Managers download reservation/guest/finance CSV reports across past, current and future periods and schedule authorized email deliveries. Groups compare locations using consistent local dates and timezones; exports obey field permissions, consent and erasure. **Acceptance evidence:** Schedule a weekly group cover report for a permitted manager, export future bookings and historical visits, then revoke access before the next scheduled delivery and prove it is blocked. Ct APPROVED PARTIAL, 25 October 2026 at 20:08Z: a personal venue-wide owner or admin explicitly approves each native group recipient. External recipients require owner approval of that exact address through an owner-created schedule; an admin may only reuse that recorded identity and address approval. Changed addresses require renewed owner approval. Current schedule-owner authority, recipient identity and every selected venue grant are checked on each delivery attempt and authenticated download; removal, changed recipient email, disconnection or an unreachable venue refuses. Email contains only an authenticated link, never an anonymous or bearer link or report snapshot. No report snapshot is retained. Private schedule and attempt metadata is owner-exportable but excluded from restorable archives, so restore cannot resume sends. Uncertain submission remains “delivery unconfirmed” for explicit manual resend. Recipient approval, attempts and every recheck or foreign-identity refusal are audited. Group comparisons use ROLE-001 read-only tokens with member-to-home checks on every call and identical inclusive local service-date labels in each venue timezone. Operational CSVs inherit current manager service scopes; guest personal and finance fields retain their existing restricted export doors, consent and erasure. DATA-001, DATA-002 and DATA-003 continue to govern these records; MSG-003 and MSG-007 inherit authenticated report custody and uncertain-send handling before richer delivery receipts or retries ship.

- **REPORT-008 — Scheduled recurring report delivery.** Scheduled recurring report delivery remains missing beyond the approved partial REPORT-005 slice. **Acceptance evidence:** Schedule authorized recurring reservation, guest and finance reports; prove field permissions, consent, erasure and access revocation on each delivery.

- **REPORT-006 — Local performance benchmarking.** Restaurants optionally contribute de-identified aggregates to comparable-market benchmarks for covers, demand, no-shows and turns, with cohort size/date freshness shown and small cohorts suppressed. A venue can opt out without losing its own history. **Acceptance evidence:** Opt in a controlled cohort, view a sufficiently sized comparison, shrink its cohort below privacy rules and verify suppression, then opt out and retain internal reporting.

- **REPORT-007 — End-of-service report.** Closing a service produces a report fixed at close and never rewritten by later edits: covers booked, walk-in and waitlist-seated, attended, canceled and no-show covers with visible denominators, fees charged, waived and refunded (PAY-004, PAY-005), average actual turn against expected, quoted versus actual waits (WAIT-003), covers recovered from cancellations and no-shows (counted only once the replacement party is seated, whether by the agent or by staff), and pacing-override counts (SERVICE-007). Each figure drills to its reservations and the report prints and downloads as PDF and CSV. A correction after close is a new traceable adjustment beside the original. Current operational snapshots commit atomically with service.close in the existing performance archive. The original CSV keeps its exact close-time population and statuses; later service observations are identified by event IDs, retaining actor, time and before/after facts without rewriting the snapshot. Missing financial and recovery facts are never inferred from attendance. Recovered covers follow one exact rule. A freed reservation is a cancelled or no-show reservation of the service, released at the latest staff observation that recorded that status; without such an observation its release is not recorded and nothing is attributed to it. A replacement is another reservation of the same service created at or after that release, sharing at least one of its tables, whose reserved interval overlaps the freed one (half-open), and which is seated or completed; offered, booked and waiting parties never count. Each replacement counts once, for the earliest-starting freed reservation it matches (then booking id), and a freed reservation recovers at most its own party size. The report shows recovered against freed covers, split into cancellations and no-shows, and drills to both reservations; the CSV gives each row its recovered covers and the reservation it recovers, and managers see the same figure live on the performance report before close. Every current seating is staff-recorded; AGENT-002 inherits agent-seated recovery attribution before an agent seats anyone. PAY-004/PAY-005 now record charged, waived, succeeded-refund and pending fee amounts with reservation drilldowns and CSV/PDF columns inside the close transaction. Older snapshots keep their original absent or not-recorded financial state; no historical fee is inferred. The fixed report also downloads as a PDF and prints from the browser with every drilldown open. **Acceptance evidence:** Run a service with two no-shows, two refills from the waitlist, a walk-in and a no-show fee; close it; reconcile every figure to its bookings and the CSV; verify a refilled table counts as recovered only after its party is seated; correct one status after close and see the original report unchanged with a dated adjustment beside it. Until payments ship no fee can be taken: the report states fees were not recorded, and PAY-004 and PAY-005 carry this journey’s fee step into their own acceptance.

- **COST-001 — Predictable operating costs.** Owners see USD subscription/hosting, per-cover distribution, messaging, voice, payment and optional provider costs with actual usage, budget alerts and forecasts before enabling a channel or campaign. Direct guest records remain exportable regardless of channel pricing. **Acceptance evidence:** Preview 1,000 reminders and a promoted event, inspect projected provider/cover cost, set a budget alert and reconcile the bill to usage and processor fees.

### Rights, APIs and daily operation

- **ROLE-001 — Owner and group-administrator rights.** Owners control restaurant configuration, billing/provider connections, people and capability grants, exports, erasure and backup/restore. Group central management is deferred to ROLE-010. Group admins get explicit per-venue rights without becoming owner; sensitive access and financial changes require recorded personal authority. Before additional venues ship, approved sister-venue alternatives inherit BOOK-003 search, exact fit and stale-result reselect. **Acceptance evidence:** As owner connect two venues, grant a scoped group admin, revoke it and prove direct API access stops; deny a venue manager an owner export, erasure and provider credential change. Group model (ct approved as the first slice, 23 October 2026): each venue stays its own installation. An owner issues a one-use invitation and the other venue's owner joins with it, choosing the most any group admin may read there; the home owner grants a native member explicit per-venue rights, read-only and never above that ceiling (reservation report, host pre-shift projection). A short-lived token is checked by the member venue against its home on every call, so revocation or disconnection stops access at once and an unreachable home refuses. Group rights cannot write in this slice, and every grant, export, erasure, refund, person and provider-credential change stays the venue's own owner or manager's personal authority, recorded in the audit history with before/after visible to the owner only. Connections, grants and tokens are never restored from a backup; DATA-003 exports links and grants without secrets. Central management, group-wide configuration and billing (ROLE-010), sister-venue alternatives (BOOK-003), shared guest profiles (GUEST-006) and group reports (REPORT-005) are deferred, not excluded, and inherit this model.

- **ROLE-002 — Manager and shift-lead rights.** Managers configure approved shifts, publish services, assign sections, resolve guest recovery, approve policy exceptions and refunds within limits, and see allowed reports. Shift leads may resolve operational exceptions without changing payment credentials, owners or guest export rights. **Acceptance evidence:** Give a manager a $100 refund limit and a lead seating-only override; test each direct operation, refuse the excess refund and provider change, and record a permitted decision. Ct policy (21 October 2026): owner-issued separate seating-lead grant, reviewed seating/rule/pacing exceptions with hard conflicts never bypassed, no owner/provider/guest-export/financial mutation rights for leads, and explicit service scopes for lead report reads. Leads receive reservation/performance JSON only, no exports or publication. Existing managers keep venue-wide reports until explicitly scoped; explicit scopes cover every report door and immutable snapshots. Owner-recorded refund authority uses USD cents ($100 = 10000). A limit is integer USD cents. No recorded limit means no refund authority, and owners are uncapped. It caps the sum of pending and succeeded refunds that person submits against one booking's charges, so splitting cannot exceed it. PAY-005 refuses an excess before any processor call. Only an owner sets limits, with AUDIT-001 before/after history. **Ct assertions (PAY-005 inherits them):** with a 10000 limit, refunding $60 then $40 of $150 succeeds and a further $0.01 is refused; a manager with no limit is refused. All acceptance points pass under the final ct policy. Owner-only integer-cent limits are audited; pending plus succeeded refunds submitted by one manager across one booking's charges consume that authority. With a 10000 limit, $60 then $40 of $150 succeed and a further cent is refused before any processor call. Managers with no limit are refused; owners are uncapped within the charge balance. Reviewed lead seating, hard physical conflicts, scoped reports and denial of owner/provider/export/financial changes remain proven. ROLE-001/ROLE-004 retain future venue/group/provider scoping.

- **ROLE-003 — Host server and read-only rights.** Hosts manage reservations, arrivals and queues within their venue, directly move, swap and lock table assignments (FLOOR-009) and, when granted, override pacing (SERVICE-007); servers see their section and service-relevant dietary/access notes; read-only staff can view permitted operations but never mutate. Guest exports, bulk marketing and sensitive notes are separately permissioned. **Acceptance evidence:** Sign in as host, server and read-only member, seat, move and swap tables as host without approval, inspect only the server’s section and refuse member mutations and all three actors’ bulk guest exports. Before server sign-in ships, enforce own-section FLOOR-012 and FLOOR-013 visibility on the server; assert the pre-shift server step with restricted notes/contact absent from HTML, print and PDF. Current owner-granted hosts receive only FLOOR-012’s enumerated host projection; ordinary read-only members are refused the sheet. Before server sign-in ships, assert FLOOR-013’s full server acceptance: open the kitchen as a server and find only that server’s own-section allergy/access requests, with no other section, guest identity/contact or shift-note values in the response or page. Server identity model (ct approved, 23 October 2026): only the owner grants a native member the separate server capability (never together with host or shift-lead; revoking removes every shift link), and a manager links that person to one shift server. A signed-in server reaches only their own pre-shift sheet (HTML, print, PDF) and kitchen view for shifts they are linked to, limited to their own sections' tables and parties; no contact, guest notes, tags, payments, shift notes, other sections, pacing or dish totals. Every other door answers 403. Hosts keep reservation, arrival, queue and assignment rights. Host guest conversations are carried by ROLE-009. Restored grants and links remain inactive until the owner confirms the native identity and shift link. MSG-006, GUEST-003 and POS-007 inherit the server view; DATA-003 covers the grant and link.

- **ROLE-009 — Host guest conversations.** Hosts manage reservations, arrivals, queues and guest conversations within their venue; guest conversations beyond BOOK-007 inquiries stay with MSG-006, and inquiry replies stay manager-only until MSG-006 / BOOK-007 reply authority is built. Carved verbatim from ROLE-003 under ct’s 23 October 2026 ruling.

- **ROLE-010 — Group central management.** Group central management provides one shared directory of several venues inside one installation, group-wide configuration and billing. This requirement is carved verbatim from ROLE-001 under ct’s 23 October 2026 ruling; group writes are deferred, not excluded. A later grant may add explicitly consented per-venue write rights.

- **ROLE-004 — Finance marketing and integration rights.** Finance users reconcile charges/refunds/settlements and export finance reports without private allergy notes; marketing users manage consented segments/campaigns without seating or charging rights. Integration and agent credentials are least-privilege, venue/purpose scoped, revocable and incapable of approving their own proposals. **Acceptance evidence:** Grant finance, marketing and integration identities, run permitted jobs and deny direct unrelated reads/writes; revoke an integration credential during a queued job and prove the job cannot proceed. Before finance, marketing or execution identities ship, enforce FLOOR-012 field and sheet access for each scoped identity on the server across HTML, print and PDF; preparation keys remain refused. Finance identity (default ADOPTED pending ct, c38): only the owner grants a native member the separate read-only finance capability (never with host, shift-lead or server); it reaches only reconciliation of charges against pending and succeeded refunds in USD cents, the payment-request, refund-charge, refund and refund-event CSVs (the owner export schema) and its own page, never guest notes, requests, the floor, sheets, writes or refunds, and every other door answers 403. Marketing identities, scoped integration or execution credentials with job-time revocation, and settlement reconciliation await CRM-001 to CRM-003, PAY-006 and a job queue, which do not exist.

- **SEC-001 — Identity and session lifecycle.** Native invitations, suspension, recovery and session revocation support restaurant teams, with MFA/step-up for high-impact owner/finance changes and optional Google Workspace/Microsoft Entra SSO for groups. Terminated staff lose browser/API access promptly and retained audit uses stable actor identities. **Acceptance evidence:** Invite and suspend a host, revoke an active session, test direct access, then require step-up for an owner export/refund policy change and provision a scoped SSO user.

- **SEC-002 — Shared host-stand device and quick staff switch.** An owner registers a host-stand tablet as a venue device that stays available with limited rights. Each staff member switches in with a personal PIN or badge in seconds; every action is attributed to that person, the device locks after inactivity or on switch, and restricted notes, refunds, waivers, payment settings, exports and administration require the individual’s full session or step-up (SEC-001). PINs are per person, throttled after failed attempts and revoked with the person or the device. **Acceptance evidence:** Register a host iPad as a venue device, switch between two hosts by PIN, seat and move parties and read audit rows attributed to each host. Let it idle and see it lock; enter wrong PINs until throttled; suspend one host and refuse their PIN; refuse a guest export from a PIN session without step-up; revoke the device and refuse its next request. Ct policy (21 October 2026): owner-only one-use registration (10 minutes), 30-day installation-local device lease, personal 6–12 digit PIN and two-minute inactivity lock. A PIN session carries the person's live host authority: FLOOR-009, WAIT-002, SERVICE-007 when granted, FLOOR-007, phone and walk-in booking create/change, and sending PAY-010 links. It never carries restricted notes, refunds, waivers, payment settings, exports or administration. Staff tap their name on a roster of active enrolled hosts, then enter the PIN. PINs are HMAC-SHA256-keyed with a versioned Worker-secret pepper, then PBKDF2-SHA256 at the platform maximum with a per-PIN salt. Pepper version and iterations are stored per PIN and upgraded on successful unlock. Common, repeated and sequential PINs are refused. Ten consecutive failures disable a PIN until a full-session reset, with an owner/manager security event. The owner renews a lease for at most 30 more days, warned from day 23. Claim, switch and lock sign out personal sessions left in the browser; PIN mode also refuses native account-administration and sign-in/setup routes and has no full-session fallback. Device credentials and personal PIN credentials remain excluded from archives. PIN replacement, native suspension/version changes, host-grant removal and device revocation invalidate authority, including in-write invalidation fences. **Ct assertions:** phone booking and walk-in made by PIN; export refused; 123456 refused; the 10th failure disables the PIN and a correct 11th entry is refused; a digest does not verify without the pepper; a renewed stand works past day 30. All acceptance points pass under the final ct policy. PIN sessions use the live host grants with in-write device fences; unsupported financial, restricted-note, export and administration doors refuse without personal-session fallback. Ten consecutive failures disable the personal PIN across stands until a full-session reset, recorded in manager-visible security events. Versioned Worker-secret HMAC then platform-maximum PBKDF2, per-PIN salt, predictable-PIN refusal and successful-unlock upgrades are proven. The day-23 warning and owner-only renewal preserve the server lease bound. SEC-001 retains future step-up duties.

### Agent surface (Base-delivered)

#### BASE-AGENT-001 — One MCP door per seed

*Tier:* Agent surface

**Requirement.** Every seed, hosted or self-hosted, serves one remote MCP endpoint at `/mcp` over Streamable HTTP. It speaks the current revision (2026-07-28) and accepts 2025-11-25 clients through the twelve-month deprecation window. It implements `server / discover`, tools, resources and prompts. Lists are deterministic and carry `ttlMs` and `cacheScope: "private"`. Roots, Sampling and Logging are not served.

**Acceptance.**
1. `server / discover` returns the supported versions, capabilities, `serverInfo` and instructions.
2. A 2026-07-28 request works with no handshake, and a 2025-11-25 client completes `initialize` and lists the same tools.
3. An unsupported version returns `UnsupportedProtocolVersion`.
4. Two `tools / list` calls return the same order, with cache fields.
5. A foreign Origin returns 403, and a header and body method mismatch returns `HeaderMismatch`.
6. An oversized body returns 413 with no effect.

#### BASE-AGENT-002 — The seed's jobs are tools, through the UI's own actions

*Tier:* Agent surface

**Requirement.** Each Core job a person does in the product is a tool. Where one is not, the Agent surface says why: it runs on a device, it is a person's interactive screen, it belongs to a connector or the import door, or it is an installation fact. Risk is never the reason: a risky job is a tool with its class (BASE-AGENT-006). Tools are named `<seed>.<area>.<verb>` and declare input and output schemas and truthful annotations. Each calls the same server action as the UI, so validation and authorization are written once, and the seed's embedded agents use the same registry. A business refusal returns `isError` with the seed's stable error code.

**Acceptance.**
1. The Core clause ids in each tool's `_meta`, with the not-a-tool reasons that `server / discover` serves, cover every Core clause in the contract, and no reason is risk; the harness and `rer check` fail on a gap.
2. Each tool's fixture result validates against its `outputSchema`.
3. Read tools declare `readOnlyHint`; tools that can carry destructive declare `destructiveHint`, and tools that can carry external declare `openWorldHint`.
4. A refusal returns the same error code the UI gets for the same action.
5. The UI action and its tool, on the same fixture, give the same record state and the same audit event type.
6. The seed's embedded agents appear in the audit as calls to the same tools.

#### BASE-AGENT-003 — Records are resources

*Tier:* Agent surface

**Requirement.** Each primary record type has a URI template, and tools return `resource_link`s to the records they touch. A read returns exactly the fields the caller's role sees in the UI. File bytes count against any byte budget on the grant. A record the caller cannot open reads as not found, identical to a missing id. Text from customers, imports or files carries an untrusted marker in `_meta`.

**Acceptance.**
1. `resources / templates / list` names every record type in the Agent surface.
2. Reads as two roles return exactly what the UI shows each.
3. An out-of-scope id and a missing id give identical responses.
4. A write's `resource_link` reads back the new state.
5. Bytes over budget return `budget_exhausted` and no partial content.
6. Customer-sourced text carries the untrusted marker.

#### BASE-AGENT-004 — Business identity and short-lived, audience-bound tokens

*Tier:* Agent surface

**Requirement.** The door is an OAuth 2.1 resource server. Its RFC 9728 metadata names the authorization servers this installation trusts. That is the paired Business when Business provisioned it, verified with the owner-claim trust the installation already holds for its import door; otherwise it is the seed's own sign-in. Access tokens are RFC 9068 JWTs with `aud` set to the seed's canonical MCP URI, `sub` the sponsoring person, `act` the agent (RFC 8693) with its specialist, scopes per tool family, and a lifetime of 15 minutes or less (5 by default). The policy scopes rules on the sponsor, agent and specialist the token names. The consent behind the tokens can last longer and is revocable. Tokens travel only in the Authorization header, and there is no passthrough.

**Acceptance.**
1. An unauthenticated call returns 401 with `resource_metadata`, and the metadata names the trusted servers and scopes.
2. A Business token for this seed works, and the same token sent to a sibling seed returns 401.
3. An expired token returns 401, and a token with a lifetime over 15 minutes is refused.
4. A read-only token calling a write tool returns 403 `insufficient_scope` with every needed scope in one challenge.
5. A token in a query string is refused and not logged.
6. Revoking consent in the seed or in Business refuses the next call within 60 seconds.
7. After unpairing, Business tokens are refused and the seed's own sign-in still works.

#### BASE-AGENT-005 — An agent acts as a person in a role, never more

*Tier:* Agent surface

**Requirement.** Every call is authorized as the sponsoring person's current role and access (BASE-ACCESS-004), intersected with the grant's resources, actions and budget. A grant only narrows. No call widens the calling agent's own authority. A call that would widen its own grant or its sponsor's role, or change the company policy or Pause, is refused with `self_escalation`, whatever the policy says; narrowing its own grant is allowed. Other access and security changes are ordinary actions in the access and security classes. An agent never acts after its sponsor is suspended. Anything an agent reads (records, files, emails, imports, other seeds' results) is data and cannot change its scope, its targets or a call's class.

**Acceptance.**
1. For each role fixture, every tool's allow or deny through MCP equals the UI's for the same action.
2. A one-folder, read-only grant holds, and widening through arguments is refused.
3. Downgrading the sponsor changes the next call's result, and suspending the sponsor returns 401.
4. Calls that widen the agent's own grant or its sponsor's role, or change the policy or Pause, return `self_escalation` and change nothing, even under a policy with every class autonomous; dropping a scope from its own grant runs.
5. An injection fixture yields no out-of-grant call and no change of class: record text asking for a wider action, or claiming that a recipient is internal.

#### BASE-AGENT-006 — Every action declares its risk class

*Tier:* Agent surface

**Requirement.** Classes come from the fleet list in RISK-POLICY.md: standard, external, money, commitment, accounts, gated, access, security, destructive, sensitive and live. In the registry, each tool declares the classes it can carry and a server-side classifier that decides them per call from the arguments, current records and, for gated, the provider's answer. The classifier also supplies each class's facts: the measure (items, recipients, amount and currency, people or records), the counterparty (internal, known, new or public), the direction for access, the provider and step for gated, and the data kind for sensitive. A classifier never reads a flag, label or claim supplied by the agent or by record text. A seed cannot add a class; it proposes one for the fleet list.

**Acceptance.**
1. Every tool in `tools / list` carries its possible classes in `_meta`, equal to the Agent surface table.
2. For each tool, fixture calls cover every class it can carry, and the computed classes and facts equal the fixture's expected values.
3. An argument or record text asserting a class or a confirmation (`internal: true`, `confirmExternal: true`) leaves the computed classes unchanged.
4. Money calls carry amount and currency, external calls their counterparty and recipient count, access calls their direction, and destructive calls their item count.
5. No tool in `tools / list` declares a class outside the fleet list, and `rer check` fails on one.
6. A refused call's audit row still records its computed classes.

#### BASE-AGENT-007 — The company's policy decides, at one chokepoint

*Tier:* Agent surface

**Requirement.** Every agent door calls one decision function: MCP, the integration API with agent tokens, and the seed's embedded agents. It evaluates the call's classes against the company's policy, as above. The seed ships no dispositions and fills no gap with one: agent access opens only under a complete policy that setup has asked for (RISK-POLICY.md), and before then every agent call returns `policy_unset` with the setup link and changes nothing. *Autonomous* runs the call. *Review* runs it and adds it to the review feed. *Approval* saves a pending action with server-computed facts and returns `input_required`, with a URL-mode elicitation to the seed's approval page and a pending handle. Each person the rule names approves the exact saved revision in a signed-in browser, and changed inputs need a new approval. The retried call returns the result and a receipt. A rejection returns `approval_rejected`, and a lapse past the wait the rule sets returns `approval_expired`. *Blocked* returns `policy_blocked`, naming the class, rule and revision.

**Acceptance.**
1. The Base harness runs each tool under each disposition for every class it can carry, and sees it run, run and enter the review feed, wait with no effect, or be refused.
2. Before setup is complete, the setup page lists every class the seed's tools carry with examples and no answer pre-selected, an agent call returns `policy_unset` with the setup link and changes nothing, and an incomplete revision cannot be confirmed; a `*` rule completes it, and a tool an upgrade adds with an unanswered class appears in `tools / list` once that class is answered, while the other tools keep running.
3. Under "money autonomous up to $500, approval up to $10,000, blocked above", calls of $400, $600 and $20,000 run, wait and are refused; a per-day cap sends the call that crosses it to the next rule.
4. A call carrying two classes takes the stricter disposition.
5. An approval shows server-computed facts and an expiry, returns the URL elicitation and a handle, and completes once after the named approver approves; a changed input needs a new approval, and a rejection or lapse leaves no effect.
6. The same call through MCP, the integration API and an embedded agent gets the same decision.
7. A policy change applies to the next call within 60 seconds, and the audit cites the new revision.
8. A policy document with a bad signature or another Business's id is rejected, and the door keeps the last valid revision.

#### BASE-AGENT-008 — Truthful attribution

*Tier:* Agent surface

**Requirement.** Every agent act is recorded and shown as `"<agent> for <person>"`, and mail and messages an agent sends outside name it that way as their sender. An approval, a review mark, a confirmation (a warning dialog, a typed-field confirmation, a delivery confirmation), a decision or a signature attributed to a person comes only from that person's signed-in session. When an agent does the equivalent act, the record names the agent, and the act carries its own class; a binding decision or a signature is commitment. Agent doors ignore arguments that stand for a person's confirmation. No tool solves a bot check, or enters a person's own password or 2FA code at an outside service. A provider step that demands a person goes to a person, whatever the policy says; the gated class marks such steps before they run.

**Acceptance.**
1. An agent call carrying a person-confirmation flag is classified and decided exactly as without it.
2. Approving, marking reviewed or answering a policy question with an agent or device token returns 403 and changes nothing.
3. A form-mode elicitation "accept" never completes an approval.
4. Where an agent's decision, signature or field confirmation runs without a person, it reads `"<agent> for <person>"` in the record, the activity view, exports and any certificate, never as the person's own act.
5. After a person approves an agent's prepared action, the record shows the person as approver and the agent as preparer.
6. Activity and exports at 1440 and 390 show `"<agent> for <person>"` for every agent act.
7. Mail an agent sends to an outside address names `"<agent> for <person>"` as its sender.

#### BASE-AGENT-009 — Every agent action is audited with its class and decision

*Tier:* Agent surface

**Requirement.** Extending BASE-OPS-005, each call that reads private data or changes anything records the agent client, name and specialist, and the run or task id (`traceparent` when sent); the sponsoring person, the grant, the tool and the targets; the classes and their facts, and the policy revision and rule; the decision (autonomous, review, approval, blocked, unset or self_escalation) and the outcome (done, refused, pending or failed); the approval or review id and person, and the idempotency key. For a period, the seed's Agents page shows actions by class and decision with the notable ones, the review feed (Mark reviewed, Flag, and Undo where reversible), pending approvals, steps waiting for a person and setup questions. Business shows the same across seeds.

**Acceptance.**
1. One write leaves a complete audit row.
2. Refused, pending, unset and self-escalation calls are audited.
3. The Agents page's counts by class and decision equal the audit rows on a fixture week.
4. The review feed lists exactly the calls decided as review; Mark reviewed records the person, and Undo restores a reversible one.
5. Filtering by agent or class lists only those rows, and export includes every field.
6. Removing the agent keeps its rows and its name.
7. The Agents page works at 1440 and 390 with no serious or critical axe findings.

#### BASE-AGENT-010 — Agents can follow changes

*Tier:* Agent surface

**Requirement.** The seed emits a typed event for every record change and for every approval, review and policy decision. Each event carries a stable id, a type, the record URI, the actor (a person, or an agent acting for a person) and a time. Events never carry secrets or more than the subscriber may read. Agents can read events three ways: `subscriptions / listen`, an `events.list` tool with a cursor, and signed webhooks from Base `integrations` using the same ids. Every channel delivers at least once and filters by access at delivery.

**Acceptance.**
1. A subscribed record changed in the UI produces a notification within 10 seconds.
2. `events.list` returns the same event id the webhook carries.
3. Replaying from a cursor returns the same ids in order.
4. After access is revoked, no channel delivers events about that record.
5. A failed webhook is visible and replays without duplicate effects.
6. `approval.pending`, `approval.decided`, `review.flagged` and `policy.adopted` carry the class and decision and nothing the subscriber may not read.

#### BASE-AGENT-011 — Limits are policy, and Pause stops everything

*Tier:* Agent surface

**Requirement.** Business limits are rules in the company's policy: per-call and per-day thresholds on any class's measure, such as money moved, outside recipients or items destroyed; spend caps on provider cost (models, SMS, email) per seed, specialist or agent, which setup asks with the classes; "no cap" is an answer. Tools with provider cost declare an estimate before they run, and an exhausted cap returns `budget_exhausted` before any partial effect. The seed's capacity limits (request rate, body and byte sizes) protect the installation: they bound rate and size, never daily business volume, are documented and are not policy. A grant carries budgets only when the person granting it sets them. A **Pause agents** control in the seed, and Pause all agents in Business when paired, refuses every agent token within 60 seconds until a person resumes; browser sessions and devices keep working.

**Acceptance.**
1. A rate overrun returns 429 with `Retry-After`.
2. A per-day cap of three outside recipients sends the fourth to the rule that applies past the cap.
3. An exhausted spend cap returns `budget_exhausted` with no partial effect and shows the spend.
4. Under the answer "no cap", a spending call runs and its spend shows in usage; a call that spends nothing is unaffected by any cap.
5. The usage view shows calls, decisions by class, money moved and provider spend per agent.
6. Pause and Pause all agents each stop the next call within 60 seconds, and resume restores access.
7. An agent token cannot resume.

#### BASE-AGENT-012 — Writes are idempotent and conflict-safe

*Tier:* Agent surface

**Requirement.** Every mutating tool requires an idempotency key and takes an optional expected revision. The same key with the same arguments returns the first outcome for at least 24 hours; the same key with different arguments returns `idempotency_conflict`; a stale revision returns `revision_conflict` with the current revision. Long work returns a job handle and a status tool, with no dependence on the Tasks extension.

**Acceptance.**
1. Two calls with one key give one effect and equal results.
2. A retry with a new JSON-RPC id and the same key, after a dropped stream, returns the recorded outcome.
3. The same key with different arguments returns a conflict and no effect.
4. A stale revision returns a conflict naming the current revision.
5. A job handle used by another person's token reads as not found.

#### BASE-AGENT-013 — Manifest, docs and the conformance journey

*Tier:* Agent surface

**Requirement.** `server / discover` instructions and an on-site `/docs/agents` page are generated from the action registry. The page lists tools by job, with each tool's classes, the test that adds each computed class, its scopes, resource templates, event types, capacity limits and error codes, and the specialist role. `prompts / list` carries the specialist's jobs. Base ships the conformance journey, a harness that `rer verify` runs against `rer dev` and seeds run in CI. It is an MCP client; a signed-in test person takes a person's steps (setup answers, approvals, review marks, resume) through the URLs the door returns, and the same browser leg runs the UI-parity actions and the page checks at 1440 and 390. It runs every acceptance point of BASE-AGENT-001 to 012 and of the seed's SURFACE clauses under two company policies: *all autonomous* (`*`), and *held* (standard review, every other class the seed declares approval, which the test person grants), plus the single-class variants a point names. A point that names no disposition passes under both.

**Acceptance.**
1. The docs list exactly the names in `tools / list` and `resources / templates / list`.
2. Each tool's classes, and the test behind each computed one, are documented.
3. The harness fails on any of: a tool without a schema; an effect under approval or blocked, or before setup is complete; a computed class that differs from its fixture; a flag that changes a class or completes a person's step; a role-parity mismatch; a wrong-audience token being accepted; a duplicate effect on retry.
4. Every acceptance point runs under both policies, every decision matches the policy in force, and under all autonomous no call waits for a person or is refused by policy.
5. A stranger agent given only the seed URL completes the specialist journey through MCP.

## Push further with service agents

- **AGENT-001 — Live voice and message booking agent.** A disclosed service agent answers phone, SMS, WhatsApp and permitted email inquiries using the restaurant’s approved menu/policies and current shared inventory. It books/changes/cancels only inside person-approved rules, obtains contact/policy consent and hands unknowns, urgent safety concerns and exceptions to people with context. Existing preparation keys remain unable to execute or self-approve; a separately scoped dispatcher enforces approved policy. Before shipping, this capability must inherit SERVICE-005 arrival/service/concurrent/area pacing and SERVICE-007 warning, reasoned override and hard physical-capacity obligations; public and agent allocations never override. **Acceptance evidence:** Call and message concurrently for the last accessible four-top, ask a menu question outside the knowledge base and request a fee exception; prove one fitting booking, a delivered confirmation, no invented answer and successful human transfer.

- **AGENT-002 — Cancellation refill through completed conversations.** The agent watches actual cancellations, table combinations and opted-in guest preferences, ranks eligible waitlist/Notify requests under manager-approved fairness rules, converses with each guest and completes a replacement reservation. Holds/expiry prevent competing accepts; incentives and contacts stay inside approved budgets and consent. Before an agent seats a replacement, AGENT-002 inherits REPORT-007’s recovered-cover rule and labels agent-seated recoveries apart from staff-recorded ones. **Acceptance evidence:** Cancel a six-top, offer to matching guests, let the first timeout and complete a second guest’s reply and booking; race a late first acceptance and report only realized recovered covers.

- **AGENT-003 — Honest waits from actual service pace.** The agent combines seated/arrival timestamps, POS course/check progress, staffing, kitchen-load limits and fitting tables to estimate wait ranges with confidence and source freshness. It proposes revised quotes and seating changes; hosts approve moves and promises outside authorized bands and managers own capacity. **Acceptance evidence:** Slow kitchen progress and extend a six-top’s turn, inspect the changed estimate and proposed move, reject it as host and verify no unauthorized guest promise or extra kitchen load. Each suggestion lists actions a host applies in one step, such as holding named tables to a later time, seating a quoted walk-in at a stated time or sending a waiting party who consented to texts an offer for bar seating, and shows the kitchen signal behind it; applying it records the host as decider.

- **AGENT-004 — Feasible seating and booking improvements.** Using demand, approved table joins, access needs, turns, staffing and pacing, the agent proposes explainable table allocations, protected direct inventory and shift adjustments. It previews affected bookings and expected covers/waits, never moves a committed guest or changes a published service without required person approval. Current direct inventory protects exact half-open table intervals (setup through cleanup) for the website booking channel; walk-in, waitlist and their reassignment doors must use other inventory until a manager approves release or the interval ends. DIST-004 and every future distribution door inherit that protection before shipping. Protection previews preserve all current bookings and do not reduce recorded queue feasibility. Current shift suggestions extend the end by 30, 60 or 90 minutes, keep total service duration within 24 hours, refuse overlap with another open published service, and retain existing bookings, staffing, turns and pacing. The approving manager confirms the recorded team and kitchen remain available through the displayed end. Projections use recorded queue order and current constraints and are conditional feasibility, not guest promises or unrecorded demand. **Acceptance evidence:** Provide a service with an avoidable stranded four-top, prepare two alternatives, approve one and reject a stale plan after another host seats a walk-in; compare actual utilization without breaking access constraints.

- **AGENT-005 — No-show risk and reconfirmation assistance.** The agent uses this venue’s observed booking/attendance history, lead time and reconfirmation outcomes to explain uncertain no-show risk and suggest contact or policy review. It never infers protected traits, auto-cancels a guest or imposes an unconsented fee; managers approve policy changes and monitor false positives. The shipped assistant uses deterministic, fact-cited review prompts, never a probability: a prior recorded no-show or a booked reservation without a recorded reconfirmation raises a flag. Lead time is the raw elapsed minutes from booking creation to arrival (displayed to two decimals) and remains context rather than evidence of nonattendance. Attendance and reconfirmation references distinguish native observations from imported dated history; missing facts remain unknown. Only existing booking, attendance and reconfirmation facts are assessed, with no protected traits or free-text profile inference. Owner/admin managers accept or decline contact or policy-review work with an attributed reason; accepted work has a manager owner and an explicit-offset due time. Completion records a staff-reported outcome and claims no provider delivery. Accepting a policy-review task does not approve or apply a policy change: the existing person-approved policy workflow remains required, and this assistant never changes a guest’s table, terms, consent or fees. Managers monitor distinct bookings with flagged reviews against later attended, no-show and pending outcomes; attendance is a potential false positive, with no causal claim. Guest erasure clears linked task reasons and outcomes and excludes the guest from new assistance reads. MSG-005 and PAY-004 inherit these fact, uncertainty, approval and unchanged-commitment obligations before adding provider reconfirmation or fee-policy assistance. **Acceptance evidence:** Flag controlled risky/unconfirmed bookings, inspect cited facts and missing-data caveats, accept a reconfirmation task and decline a policy change; prove the guest retains their table and original terms.

- **AGENT-006 — Evidence-based guest recovery.** The agent reads verified feedback, visit notes, consent and POS check facts to draft recovery outreach, propose permitted compensation, arrange a return visit and chase unresolved follow-up. Managers approve sensitive replies and compensation; no invented apology facts, inferred allergy or unsubscribed outreach is allowed. **Acceptance evidence:** Receive poor feedback, inspect a fact-cited draft, approve a bounded offer, complete the guest conversation and return booking and track attendance; opt out another guest and prove no contact occurs.

- **AGENT-007 — Permissioned guest enrichment and next visit.** The agent proposes tags and repeat-visit segments from recorded preferences, declared occasions and spend with per-fact provenance, confidence and sensitive-field exclusions. Approved low-risk rules can run unattended; managers can reject/undo enrichments and preview any campaign before sending. **Acceptance evidence:** Process ambiguous notes and refunded spend, review proposed tags, reject an inferred dietary condition and approve a visit-frequency tag; undo it and verify downstream audience membership changes.

- **AGENT-008 — Measured reversible service experiments.** The agent proposes pacing, deposit or reminder experiments using accepted bookings, attended/recovered covers, quoted/actual waits, no-shows, refunds, guest complaints and POS contribution. Managers approve dates, policy terms, audiences and controls, can stop/roll back immediately, and see sample sizes, uncertainty and harms as well as gains. **Acceptance evidence:** Approve a two-week pacing experiment with a control period, record realized covers/waits and kitchen overload, stop it mid-service and inspect unchanged prior commitments plus a report distinguishing observed improvement from unsupported causal claims.

## Honest boundaries and separate products

Placemat owns reservations, restaurant guest relationships, dining experiences, host operations and their follow-through. It connects to Toast, Square for Restaurants, Clover, Lightspeed and NCR Aloha for orders, kitchen execution, checks and loyalty; those systems keep POS, menu fulfillment and payroll jobs. Separate payroll: [Envelope](https://github.com/just-every/run-envelope). EXP-005 covers prepaid pickup experiences through that integration, rather than turning Placemat into delivery dispatch or a general POS.

Stripe is the restaurant’s processor. Placemat delivers the payment workflows in PAY-001–PAY-010 and experience clauses, including onboarding and reconciliation, while Stripe retains card custody, underwriting, bank settlement and processor dispute decisions. Sales-tax calculation uses the named tax connection and restaurant-approved configuration; policy/accounting decisions belong to the restaurant and its advisers. No missing provider approval removes a payment clause.

The restaurant CRM is part of this product. The general sales CRM remains [Orbit](https://github.com/just-every/run-orbit); general accounting remains [Pantry](https://github.com/just-every/run-pantry), which receives PAY-009’s finance handoff. [Crank](https://github.com/just-every/run-crank) owns general cross-tool workflow automation, [Uptime](https://github.com/just-every/run-uptime) monitors availability and [Oncall](https://github.com/just-every/run-oncall) coordinates responders. Observability: [Porthole](https://github.com/just-every/run-porthole). API-002 and OPS-001 supply the respective handoffs. No unowned category gap is absorbed here.

Google/Meta distribution and POS/voice partner access require actual approved accounts, certification and operational support. DIST-001–DIST-004 and the named POS/voice clauses include that engineering/commercial work. Placemat does not inherit an incumbent’s diner audience, but discovery and distribution remain target product work. It uses carriers and voice providers rather than operating a telephone network; agents transfer emergencies and safety issues to people and never present restaurant booking as an emergency service. Restaurant staff remain responsible for food preparation and the truth of menu/allergy information.

Two statements the homepage makes about what Placemat is are clauses here, so the page and the product are tested against the same words.

- **OSS-001 — Free and open source, MIT licensed.** Placemat’s source is MIT licensed in its public repository and Placemat itself charges no license fee and sets no paywall, plan, seat or cover limit. Restaurants run it on their own computer or in their own Cloudflare account. Third-party providers (Stripe processing, Twilio messaging and voice, Google, Meta, POS and partner fees) bill the restaurant directly under their own terms; COST-001 shows those costs before a channel is enabled, and they are never called free or folded into a Placemat charge. **Acceptance evidence:** Read `LICENSE` (MIT) and the license line on the homepage, README and /run; install with the /run command and run a complete service with no payment, plan or license prompt; enable a provider channel and prove the cost shown is that provider’s own (COST-001) and that Placemat bills nothing. Today OSS-001 is done when every capability that exists conforms and the public installation completes a service without license, plan or payment setup. Before any restaurant provider channel ships, COST-001 and each introducing clause (MSG-002, MSG-003, PAY-001, DIST-001–DIST-004, POS-001–POS-005 and VOICE-001) inherit provider-owned cost disclosure before enablement and no Placemat charge; those future provider journeys remain required in their own clauses. Authentication and hosting may have their own external costs and are never described as free provider service.

- **BOUND-001 — Stated boundary: online ordering, gift cards and the POS.** The homepage says “Not in Placemat: online ordering, gift cards or the POS itself”, and the product says the same. Placemat sells no gift cards, stored-value cards or vouchers, takes no online food orders and is not the point of sale. A PAY-002 deposit, an EXP-002 prepaid ticket and an EXP-005 pickup experience are each tied to one named booking or event, shown as a balance against it and refunded under PAY-005; none is transferable, can be topped up or spends as a general balance. Gift cards, online ordering and check taking stay in the restaurant’s POS or its payment provider’s own gift-card and ordering products, and a Toast, Square or Clover loyalty program stays there too (CRM-006 syncs only identity and redemption status). The homepage names no gift-card provider, so the docs give the same line without naming one. Today’s capabilities must conform to this boundary. Before their capabilities ship, PAY-002, EXP-002 and EXP-005 each inherit the booking/event-bound balance, PAY-005 refund, nontransferability, no-top-up and no-general-spending obligations and their payment acceptance points. Those payment journeys remain missing in their own clauses; BOUND-001 is done when all capabilities that exist today conform. **Acceptance evidence:** Read the homepage boundary line, this clause and the owner docs and find the same three exclusions and the same pointer to the venue’s POS or payment provider; search the staff app, public booking page, `docs/HTTP-CONTRACT.md` routes and exports for gift-card, stored-value, voucher and ordering surfaces and find none; pay a deposit and a prepaid ticket and prove neither can be transferred, topped up or redeemed outside its booking; a site test fails if the homepage names a gift-card or ordering capability this clause excludes, or this clause names one the page omits.

before1.text: # Placemat Every table, filled. Placemat is restaurant reservations, the host stand, the waitlist and guest history for US restaurants: a 100% free, open source alternative to OpenTable, Resy and SevenRooms, MIT licensed, on your own computer or in your own Cloudflare account. [CONTRACT.md](CONTRACT.md) is the product it is being built towards; [ACCEPTANCE.md](ACCEPTANCE.md) says which journeys work today. This release has no payments, deposits, card holds or provider sends. Not in Placemat: online ordering, gift cards or the POS itself. Placemat sells no gift cards, stored-value cards or vouchers and takes no online food orders. Gift cards, online ordering and check taking stay in the restaurant’s POS or its payment provider’s own products; connected loyalty stays there too. This release has no payment collection or booking balances. A staff-recorded “ordering” or “paid” stage is only a service observation, never an order or processor payment. The owner guides are in [docs/](docs/site.json), starting with [Getting started](docs/getting-started.md); the run site publishes them at `/docs`. The run site is at https://run-placemat.com. Its run page, https://run-placemat.com/run, gives the install and `rer dev` steps; to run it on your own computer, follow **Clone and run** below. ## Clone and run You need Git and internet access on macOS, Linux or Windows with WSL2. RER selects this project's pinned Node **22.20.0** and pnpm **10.12.4**; you do not need to change your global Node version. Install rer, the Run Edit Run command, then start Placemat. These are the same two lines as https://run-placemat.com/run: ```sh curl -fsSL https://runeditrun.com/install.sh | sh rer dev just-every/run-placemat ``` The installer adds rer for you alone, with its own Node if you have no Node 22 or later; if it prints an `export PATH=…` line, run that line before the second. Already have Node 22 or later? `npx -y @runeditrun/rer dev just-every/run-placemat` does both steps in one line. To start it again later, run `cd run-placemat && rer dev`. The first run installs dependencies, applies every D1 migration and creates a local review owner. Give it up to ten minutes. Open the printed `RER_OPEN` link on this computer, check the owner on **Finish setup**, tick its confirmation and click **Finish setup**. You arrive at `/app`. Keep `RER_OPEN` private: it signs you in. Local development sends no email. A fresh installation is empty. If `rer` is not on your shell's PATH after installation, run `export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"`. Start again with `rer dev` in the `run-placemat` folder; it resumes a partial launch. The saved port is printed as `RER_READY`; use that address throughout, not a guessed port. Stop with `rer dev --stop` or Ctrl-C. For an installation belonging to a real person, run `npx -y @runeditrun/rer setup just-every/run-placemat` in place of the one line and answer its owner-email prompt, then `cd run-placemat && rer dev`. Setup preserves existing data on reruns. `rer dev --as admin` and `rer dev --as member` provide local manager and read-only personas; `rer dev --as signed-out` opens the guest view. Return to the owner with `rer dev --as owner`. ## Run Friday dinner 1. In **Settings**, save the venue name and an IANA timezone, for example `America/New_York`. The app displays and accepts venue time even when your computer uses another timezone. Set it before creating a service. 2. In **Services & tables**, add four two-seat tables, T1–T4, at distinct floor positions such as 15%, 38%, 61% and 84% across, 40% down. Create a future **Friday dinner**, 6:00 PM–10:00 PM, 90-minute turns and eight covers. Click **Prepare publication**, follow **Approvals & reminders**, expand **Exact plan**, and **Approve plan**. A draft is private until approved. 3. Open **Guest booking page** (`/book`) in a private browser window. Book three parties of two at 6:00 PM with distinct guest emails. Each success displays its booking reference. The page lists only available 15-minute starts that fit a complete turn. Staff click **Refresh** to see new bookings. 4. In **Floor & bookings**, expand **Add a walk-in** and seat a fourth party of two at 6:00 PM. Leave Tables empty for automatic assignment. The floor shows booked and seated tables at the selected time. Table combinations are automatic when one table cannot fit a party; table clashes and the service's cumulative cover limit cannot be overridden. 5. In **Waitlist**, add the next party. In the bookings list change one booked party to **no-show**. Seat the waiting party at 6:00 PM. The no-show stays in guest history and its freed capacity is available. Staff can mark a booked guest seated, then completed; cancelled and no-show bookings remain in history. 6. Under **Approvals & reminders**, **Prepare reminder batch**, review its exact bookings and approve it. **Download reminders CSV** gives contacts and approved messages for your venue's own sender. Placemat records approval and export; it does not deliver email or SMS. Cancelled/no-show/erased guests are omitted. Each booking also has a **Calendar** download. 7. Under **Guests**, expand a guest to read visits and save notes. Owners can explicitly erase personal details there. Staff cannot erase guests. Publication fixes the service's hours, cover limit and turn duration. To offer another sitting, create another service. Draft edits invalidate old publication proposals. Tables with booking history are kept unchanged; add a new table when the physical layout changes. ## Move in and undo In **Move in**, choose [`fixtures/tablein-guests.csv`](fixtures/tablein-guests.csv), click **Preview import**, inspect guests, diagnostics and counts, then **Apply reviewed import**. No guest is written by the preview. The journal records the exact source and checkpoint; a partial job can be resumed by applying the same reviewed CSV. **Review undo** opens the exact job; type `UNDO` and submit. A guest edited after import blocks strict undo and the staff edit survives. This is a **Tablein-shaped guest and historical-visit kit**, using invented data. It has not been tested against a real Tablein export. It never creates active future reservations or assumes marketing consent. See [MOVE-IN.md](docs/MOVE-IN.md) for its documented columns, limits and HTTP commands. ## People and agents The owner can invite people under **Settings → People & invitations**. **Owner** controls move-in, erasure, backups and agent keys; **admin** is the floor manager; **member** can read venue operations. Every private server handler checks its session and role. Guests can only read published availability and create their own booking. An owner creates a preparation key under **Settings → Agent preparation keys**, copies it once into private agent storage, and can revoke it there. A bearer key can read `/api/state` and POST `/api/commands` with `proposal.prepare`. It cannot approve, change the floor directly, erase, import or back up. Plans are `service.publish`, `table.assign` and `reminders`. A native owner/admin approves from the UI; changed plans or clashes require another proposal. [AGENTS-API.md](docs/AGENTS-API.md) documents the requests. ## Backup, restore and erasure **Settings → Backup & restore** downloads a Base portability JSON archive. On an empty product installation, choose it, type `RESTORE` and submit. Restores check integrity, schema, relationships, emptiness and erasure fences. If restoring an older backup elsewhere, also choose a trusted later backup in the optional journal field. Auth identities, agent secrets, rate-limit state, local settings and mail outboxes are excluded. Set up a fresh owner separately. For a complete native local transfer, stop the server first: ```sh rer dev --stop rer export --output exports/venue.rer # In a fresh checkout with no product data: rer import --input /absolute/path/venue.rer --yes rer dev ``` Both interfaces use the same product policy. Keep archives private and outside public/server folders. Erasure anonymizes a guest's live history, notes and import custody, withdraws affected original CSVs, and records contact hashes that block reimport. Known older backups are refused. When restoring an offline backup elsewhere, supply a trusted later archive via `rer import --journal /path/to/later.rer`; an isolated old backup cannot know later erasures. Erasure cannot delete files already downloaded outside the installation. Do not use `rer reset` as an erasure or migration workflow: it removes local owner/data/settings after confirmation. ## Deploy to your Cloudflare account No domain purchase is needed for the Worker app. `rer deploy` uses Base's owner-account deploy kit, creates its declared D1, applies numbered migrations and checks the deployed health and assets. It does not run tests. Deployment needs your Cloudflare account/token and a verified mail sender; no credentials are included here. 1. Stop local dev. In `deploy.json`, set `vars.MAIL_FROM` to your verified sending address and select the matching `MAIL_PROVIDER` (default `resend`). Keep the declared project, Worker and D1 identities. Commit source changes before a real deployment. 2. Create a private mode-0600 `.env.deploy` using an editor, with `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`, `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`, `OWNER_EMAIL`, `SESSION_SECRET`, `SETUP_TOKEN` and `MAIL_API_KEY`. Session and setup secrets must be separate strong random values of at least 32 characters. The Cloudflare token must be scoped to your intended account with Worker and D1 deployment permissions. Never commit this file or put values into CLI arguments. 3. Run: ```sh rer deploy --dry-run --env-file .env.deploy rer deploy --env-file .env.deploy rer signin --env-file .env.deploy ``` The dry run builds and validates without provider calls. The real deploy prints its Worker URL. Open the one-time owner link printed by `rer signin`, complete **Finish setup**, and use `/app`. Keep the link private. Ordinary sign-in uses your configured email provider; confirm its sending-domain setup first. Provider setup is described in [OPERATIONS.md](OPERATIONS.md) and the installed `node_modules/@runeditrun/rer/modules/deploy-kit` documentation. A local passing check does not claim real provider delivery. ## Development checks ```sh rer dev --stop pnpm test:api rer verify ``` The six HTTP integration tests run the real workerd/D1 implementation, with only the paid mail boundary faked. They cover the Friday flow, direct auth and CSRF, person approvals, concurrent table claims, import/undo, erasure and restore. The emitted-Worker smoke check and the run site check (`pnpm test:site`: `rer build --site`, the homepage's Run Placemat opens `/run`, every guide in `docs/site.json` is published) also run on pushes. GitHub **Verify** runs source, API, run-site and built-runtime shards in parallel; installer journeys run on release tags and nightly. No tests run during build or deploy. The suite remains below the 200-test budget. Pinned RER: **0.2.42**. Foundation: [`runeditrun/base@c7cb0613`](https://github.com/runeditrun/base/tree/c7cb0613120074c5ffca63f610533802afbda6bd). Reuse and known shared-module gaps are documented in [SOURCES.md](docs/SOURCES.md).
