# Placemat product contract

Target edition: **17 October 2026**. Placemat fills tables and runs restaurant guest relationships from first inquiry to the next attended visit. A US owner/GM switching from OpenTable, Resy, SevenRooms or Tock gets direct and distributed booking, the host stand, live queues, delivered guest conversations, deposits and prepaid dining, POS-connected profiles, retention and service economics. Eat App and Loman AI set additional expectations for automation and voice intake. This is the product being built towards; a missing implementation never narrows the destination.

## Product target

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Category | Restaurant reservations, waitlist and guest management |
| Incumbents a buyer switches from | OpenTable, Resy, SevenRooms, Tock; Eat App and Loman AI |
| First buyer | The US owner or general manager of a 30–150 seat independent restaurant, with hosts, servers and a finance/marketing lead, operating in USD and US time zones; restaurant groups can add venues and shared guest relationships |

The whole job is to turn direct, Google, social, phone and discovered demand into feasible seated covers, protect scarce tables, keep service promises and earn repeat visits using actual guest and check facts. The product includes its own diner-facing booking/discovery experience and restaurant CRM. Acquisition, provider certification, approved POS access, US messaging registration, native clients and payment onboarding are work to deliver, not scope exclusions.

The existing contract had seven unnumbered guarantees. The Published foundations below give them stable IDs, preserve their capacity/authority/data guarantees and retain the first-release CSV reminder mode. Other clauses extend that foundation. Definitions state buyer behavior and acceptance through a screen, public HTTP door, download, command or provider event. [ACCEPTANCE.md](ACCEPTANCE.md) lists every journey with the same status. Local tests do not establish live provider onboarding, real customer migration or native mobile acceptance.

## Operating rules

- The owner’s restaurant starts empty. Test fixtures stay in tests; real service, guest and provider records are created or migrated by the restaurant.
- Every booking channel shares one capacity ledger. A table, combination, experience ticket or waitlist hold cannot create another physical seat. A stale view must reconcile before it can commit.
- Existing preparation keys can read and prepare only. People approve exact plans; edits invalidate approval. New unattended transaction workflows require a person-approved policy enforced by a separately scoped execution service. An agent cannot approve its own proposal, grant access, alter policy or exceed a financial/compensation limit.
- Amounts use USD integer minor units with explicit tax, service charge, tip and refund allocations. Stripe owns payment credentials and money movement. Venue-local times carry an unambiguous offset and IANA timezone through booking, policy cutoffs, import and reporting.
- Transactional permission, marketing consent and sensitive guest facts are distinct. Unknown imported consent is unknown; a booking never implies a marketing opt-in. Accessibility needs and declared allergies constrain service decisions and are never inferred as medical conclusions.
- An automated send, payment or booking is complete only when its actual outcome is reconciled. A queued job, CSV, draft message or provider timeout is not a delivered message, collected payment or recovered cover. Failures have a named human next action.
- The public contract promises the target. The final Status table judges current code at the named commit, starting from the 16 October inventory audit and rechecking changed source/test paths; it is not a claim that missing provider work already ships.

## Published foundations

- **ACCESS-001 — Native sessions and preparation authority.** Private product routes require an active native owner, admin or member session, or an owner-issued unrevoked preparation key. Owner/admin operate the floor and approve plans; members read only unless the owner grants the product host capability in FLOOR-009. That capability permits direct assignment changes, staff service observations and WAIT-002 intake/party updates; a separate SERVICE-007 pacing grant adds walk-in/waitlist seating and reasoned overrides, never plan approval or venue administration. Only an owner person manages keys, move-in, erasure and backups. Every handler enforces authority and browser writes require the venue origin. **Acceptance evidence:** Call state, commands, downloads, import and backup directly while signed out, as member, admin and preparation key; refuse unauthorized writes and cross-origin requests; revoke a key and refuse its next read.

- **PRIVACY-001 — Public guest isolation.** Guests see published services and their own new-booking confirmation. Public availability and other guests’ confirmations never expose guest contact data, notes or private history. When BOOK-002 analytics is on, the booking page and widget ask once per visit before anything leaves for GA4 or Meta: nothing is sent before Accept, on Decline or without an answer, the answer is never stored, no provider script loads on the page, and accepted events carry no guest name or contact data, IP address, cookies, booking reference or reservation date/time. **Acceptance evidence:** Create two guests through the public booking door; inspect availability and both confirmations while signed out and prove neither response contains the other guest’s details. With BOOK-002 analytics on, book once without answering the analytics question and once after Accept; prove the first sends nothing and the second’s provider events carry no guest details.

- **BOOK-001 — Live assigned reservations.** Guests read current published availability and immediately create a booking assigned to a fitting table or combination. Full or concurrently claimed capacity returns a conflict rather than a false confirmation. **Acceptance evidence:** Publish a service, make three public reservations and race the final fitting combination from two guest requests; exactly one succeeds and the next availability read reflects it.

- **FLOOR-001 — Conflict-safe physical capacity.** Half-open UTC intervals, full-turn fit, starts on the service slot interval (15 minutes by default, configurable under SERVICE-004), distinct table combinations and cumulative service covers protect allocation. A physical table cannot be sold twice across overlapping services. Writes compare the floor version; stale plans require renewed review. **Acceptance evidence:** Book a combined table through HTTP, reject too few or duplicate tables and over-capacity arrivals, finish a turn and book a later one; attempt a clash across services and require refusal.

- **SERVICE-001 — Reviewed dated service publication.** An owner or manager configures venue timezone, positioned tables, a dated service, turn time and cover limit. A person publishes its exact prepared venue, service and floor snapshot; a later draft edit invalidates approval. **Acceptance evidence:** Create tables and a Friday service through commands, prepare publication, edit it, refuse stale approval and approve a fresh plan; only the published service becomes bookable.

- **PLAN-001 — Exact plans and accountable decisions.** Publication, prepared table-reassignment and reminder proposals preserve exact inputs, preparer, reason and the deciding person. A person’s own direct table move, swap or lock is not a plan: FLOOR-009 commits it at once with an audit row, so the approval path binds preparation keys and agent proposals. Preparation keys cannot approve. Changed inputs and physical clashes refuse approval; readable actor names identify people and keys. **Acceptance evidence:** Prepare with an owner-issued key, refuse key approval, change a draft, refuse stale approval, then approve a fresh plan as manager and read its identities; prepare and approve a valid table move.

- **MSG-001 — Approved reminder CSV custody.** People can approve exact reminder batches and download them for their own sender. Exported rows retain approval attribution, render the venue-local time in US format (for example “Sat, Oct 17, 2026, 7:30 PM PDT”) and exclude no-shows and erased guest contact values. A CSV export records preparation and export, never provider delivery. **Acceptance evidence:** Book guests, mark one no-show, approve remaining reminders and download CSV with US-formatted local times; erase a booked guest and download again, proving the guest’s personal values are absent.

- **WAIT-001 — Staff walk-ins and waiting parties.** Managers seat fitting walk-ins, add a party to the service waitlist and seat it when capacity is released. Booked, seated, completed, canceled and no-show transitions are guarded against impossible state changes. **Acceptance evidence:** Run the Friday HTTP journey with online bookings, a walk-in, a waiting party and a no-show; seat the waiting party and refuse completion before seating.

- **GUEST-001 — Guest visit history.** Guest contact records, editable service notes, current reservation statuses and imported dated visit history remain linked to the guest, including cancellations and no-shows. **Acceptance evidence:** Book a guest, change its service status, import dated visits and read guest/state through an authorized session; update notes and find both current and imported history.

- **MIG-001 — Reviewed Tablein-shaped move-in.** Base import-kit accepts the documented eight-column guest/history CSV shape with a no-write dry run, exact fingerprint confirmation, atomic native/journal batches, durable provenance and undo that refuses later edited rows. This existing fixture is explicitly shape-only, not verified against a real customer export. **Acceptance evidence:** Upload the fixture through dry-run, reject a wrong fingerprint, apply, read the journal, undo unchanged rows and refuse undo after a staff edit while keeping that edit.

- **DATA-001 — Validated empty-destination backups.** Owner backups use Base portability with integrity, relationship and empty-destination checks. Restore never overwrites a working venue; corrupt archives fail without partial product writes and refusals give a plain-language next step. A restore brings back BOOK-002 analytics settings but never their GA4 or Meta keys, so the restored venue asks no analytics question and sends nothing until the owner enters the keys again. **Acceptance evidence:** Export a booked venue through the owner backup endpoint; restore into an empty installation, compare records, then refuse overwrite and a modified archive without changing destination data. Restore a venue with analytics on and prove nothing is offered or sent until the owner re-enters both keys.

- **DATA-002 — Guest erasure and restore fences.** Owner erasure removes live and import-custody personal values, suppresses known erased identities and fences known older backups. An isolated offline restore needs a trusted later erasure journal to learn erasures it has never seen. **Acceptance evidence:** Import, back up and erase a guest; verify guest and retained archive custody no longer contain personal values, refuse reimport and refuse a pre-erasure restore when given the trusted later journal.

- **SITE-001 — Runnable product and owner guides.** The run site built with rer build --site serves its homepage, a Run Placemat action opening /run and all listed owner guides at /docs. The installed root remains the Lobby and a fresh installation starts without sample restaurant data. **Acceptance evidence:** Build the run site and follow homepage to /run and /docs; open the installed root after fresh setup and reach empty restaurant operations. The homepage’s Run Placemat and Read the docs buttons and its Run it yourself command (`npx -y @runeditrun/rer dev just-every/run-placemat`) match `src/site/run.json`, README and /run exactly; run that command in a clean directory and reach owner setup.

## Target clauses

These clauses extend the published foundations to the complete category job. Each states the behavior a buyer gets and the journey that proves it.

### Venue setup and service policy

- **SETUP-001 — US restaurant onboarding.** The owner sets legal/trading name, address, US phone, contact channels, logo, booking policies, USD currency and an IANA venue timezone. Setup previews a realistic service without creating fake production guests; Los Angeles and New York daylight-saving gaps and repeated hours require explicit resolution. **Acceptance evidence:** Finish onboarding for a 72-seat US restaurant, preview its booking page and create services across both DST changes; refuse nonexistent local times and disambiguate repeated times. Under ct scope51 (21 October 2026), completing restaurant setup saves editable defaults for new dated and recurring services: online parties 1–8 with inquiry above the maximum, 60 inclusive venue-local days ahead, inclusive 16:00 same-day cutoff, 30 elapsed minutes lead and 15-minute slots. Walk-in and waitlist defaults have no cutoff and zero lead. Every rule applies together; owner/admin may override party, horizon and lead with a recorded reason, never a cutoff or physical capacity. The owner acknowledges the exact summary, recorded with a monotonically increasing version, actor and instant; edits require a fresh acknowledgment. Existing services retain their own policies, and pre-onboarding installations retain their existing rules until the owner completes restaurant setup. Contact channels are the restaurant’s phone, email and optional HTTPS website; saving them claims no provider validation or send. PNG/JPEG/WebP restaurant logos are uploaded locally. USD is the edition currency. A transient preview uses the entered service and real floor through the current search/capacity engine and creates no service, guest, booking or proposal. Service creation and recurring generation refuse a DST gap and name its next valid local minute; repeated start or end times require an actual valid offset choice. Venue-local input resolves on the server and stored timestamps remain unambiguous instants. Restaurant fields, exact policies and acknowledgment export and restore under DATA-003 and DATA-001.

- **SERVICE-002 — Recurring shifts and seasonal schedules.** Managers define weekly breakfast, lunch and dinner templates, seasonal date ranges and special holiday shifts. They preview generated services, conflicts and capacity before publication; editing a template never silently rewrites existing guest commitments. Seasons and preview dates are inclusive venue-local calendar dates; dated exceptions replace the weekly shift, including opening a normally closed day. End time at or before start means the following local day. Nonexistent DST times refuse generation and repeated times require an explicit valid UTC offset. Preview shows physical seats (active tables only; retired tables are history, not seats), service covers and overlapping services, and publication binds the exact schedules, venue, floor, services and bookings. A template edit marks changed future generated services for renewed approval; only explicitly selected unbooked services can be renewed or closed by that reviewed batch. Booked services and historical services remain unchanged and affected bookings require the separately reviewed SERVICE-003 change workflow. Batches cover up to 31 dates each and successive batches cover a longer season. **Acceptance evidence:** Create a recurring dinner template and Thanksgiving exception, preview and publish a week, then change the template and inspect which future services need renewed approval.

- **SERVICE-003 — Closures and emergency service changes.** Managers close dates, rooms or arrival windows, hold inventory for private use and safely amend a published service. Affected bookings become a named outreach and reaccommodation queue with delivery outcomes and explicit refund decisions; closure cannot make them disappear. Owner or admin reviews each closure or relocation action. A closure message goes only to guests with recorded contact permission and covers only their own booking. Relocation changes a booking only after the guest accepts; unanswered bookings stay unchanged and visible to the owner. Refunds follow PAY-005: owner or admin authority, exact cents, recorded reason and no refund claimed before provider confirmation. Contact details and messages follow existing guest-data retention and erasure; every action records actor and time. Current closure restrictions use half-open intervals: room, full-service and private holds cover setup through cleanup across shared physical tables; arrival-window closures compare arrival instants. Existing reservations retain all commitments. Existing direct, swapped and prepared assignment doors refuse unaccepted changes to an affected booking’s tables; an outstanding follow-up cannot bypass acceptance. A personal manager reviews an exact offer without changing the booking, then explicitly sends once to its recorded permitted email. A scoped digest-only link expires at the earliest of 24 hours or either arrival, rotates on renewed review and is consumed on a decision. Acceptance rechecks the original booking, full turn, cleanup, access, physical capacity, staffing and pacing atomically. Provider acceptance remains distinct from mailbox delivery; opening the private link records guest-opened. Staff follow-up observations remain distinct from these delivery outcomes. Portable history strips live capabilities and guest erasure clears linked permission, free text and personal snapshots. **Acceptance evidence:** Close a room with three future bookings; preview impacts, confirm the change, relocate one, cancel and refund another and track failed outreach for the third to staff ownership.

- **SERVICE-004 — Party and advance-booking rules.** Per service/channel rules control minimum and maximum party size, advance-booking horizon, same-day cutoff, lead time, slot interval and large-party inquiry routing. Staff overrides of party, horizon and lead-time rules require a permitted role and a reason and cannot violate physical capacity; pacing and cover-limit overrides follow SERVICE-007. Current online, walk-in and waitlist-seating channels each store their own rules. Horizon is an inclusive count of venue-local calendar days, lead time is elapsed minutes (zero disables the staff-seating lead check; public bookings always require a future time), the same-day cutoff is inclusive HH:MM in venue time, blocked starts are exact UTC instants, and slots align to service start. Current owner/admin managers may override party, horizon and lead-time checks with a recorded reason; public and preparation-key requests cannot. Large parties above the inquiry threshold are directed to contact the venue and are never falsely confirmed. BOOK-007 inherits the full inquiry workflow; BOOK-002, BOOK-005, DIST-001–DIST-004, WAIT-002, VOICE-001 and AGENT-001 inherit channel rules before their new booking doors ship. **Acceptance evidence:** Configure different lunch/dinner rules; try early, late, oversized and blocked public requests, then authorize a lead-time override and inspect its audit.

- **SERVICE-005 — Arrival pacing and concurrent covers.** Managers set covers and parties per arrival interval, total service covers, simultaneous seated covers and kitchen pacing by area. Public, widget, Google, social, partner, voice and agent allocations are refused at these limits with clear reasons. Staff bookings see the same limits as a warning and proceed past them only through a reasoned, audited SERVICE-007 override. Current limits are per service. Arrival intervals use whole elapsed minutes aligned to service start and half-open bounds; booked, seated and completed arrivals count, cancelled/no-show parties do not. Total service covers use those same statuses. Simultaneous dining covers count overlapping booked/seated dining intervals, with ongoing seated parties counted past their forecast. Each party counts once per arrival interval and once against each configured area containing its assigned tables. Whole-number limits are 1–500 and intervals 5–120 minutes; absent older pacing settings add no arrival or simultaneous limit beyond the existing service-cover and FLOOR-004 kitchen caps. Managers configure the policy at service creation or with an attributed service.pacing command; existing commitments remain, and assignment changes cannot increase an exceeded limit without a new reviewed allocation. Current online booking, walk-in and waitlist seating, status reacquisition, direct/prepared assignments and retirement replacements retain pacing and every hard physical/server guard. New widget/phone/distribution/voice/agent doors (BOOK-002, BOOK-005, DIST-001–DIST-004, VOICE-001, AGENT-001) inherit these obligations before shipping. WAIT-002 queue intake stays open at pacing caps, labelled “queued only; no table or time promised”; pacing is enforced when a person seats, books or allocates from the queue. **Acceptance evidence:** Set a 12-cover arrival limit and 48 simultaneous covers, book through two channels concurrently and prove the next public party is refused despite a physically free table, while a staff booking at the same moment receives a warning and needs a SERVICE-007 override. The reservation book shows covers against the limit for each arrival interval and marks a full interval, whose next public request is offered alternatives (BOOK-003).

- **SERVICE-006 — Turn and cleanup rules.** Managers set turn duration by party size, table, dining area, experience and service, plus cleanup buffers and last-seating rules. Availability fits the whole promised turn and reset; changes preview affected guests and preserve approved reservations. Current service, party-size, table and dining-area rules apply to every existing booking door. A table rule takes precedence over its area, then the matching non-overlapping party range, then the service default; a combination uses its longest constituent turn. Cleanup occupies the same tables through a separate cleanupEndAt, including a completed booking with a reset, and both the full turn and reset must fit service hours. Last seating is an inclusive offset instant. Reviewed policy edits preview each existing reservation, require renewed review if the service, floor or bookings change, and affect only future bookings; confirmed turns and resets remain unchanged. EXP-001 and EXP-002 inherit experience-specific duration and cleanup before publishing experiences; BOOK-002, BOOK-005, DIST-001–DIST-004, WAIT-002, VOICE-001 and AGENT-001 inherit full-turn/reset allocation before their new booking doors ship. **Acceptance evidence:** Configure 90-minute two-tops, 120-minute six-tops and a 15-minute reset; search last seating, book both sizes and verify adjacent turns and a policy edit.

- **SERVICE-007 — Staff pacing overrides with warnings.** Permitted staff (managers by default, hosts when granted) can knowingly book or seat a party past an arrival-interval, simultaneous-cover, area-pacing or service-cover limit, or into a blocked timeslot, from the reservation book, a phone booking, a walk-in or waitlist seating. Before commit the screen and HTTP response name each limit exceeded and by how much; the staff member confirms with a reason. The override is audited with actor, limit, excess and reason, flagged on the booking and timeline, and counted separately in pacing and cover reports (REPORT-002). Public, widget, Google, social, partner, voice and agent allocations never override and stay refused; WAIT-002 queue intake remains queued-only as SERVICE-005 states. No override can breach physical table capacity, overlapping turns or permitted combinations (FLOOR-001, FLOOR-003). Current owner/admin managers configure and override by their existing rights. An owner grants or revokes a separate pacing capability for an active FLOOR-009 host; it adds walk-in and waitlist seating with reasoned pacing overrides, never plan approval or venue administration. Each command rechecks the current grant. A native authenticated no-write preview names every limit/current/projected/excess and returns a five-minute HMAC review bound to the actor, command, exact payload, floor version and expiry. Commit needs that unchanged review, an explicit confirmation and a reason, and rechecks live fit. Review tokens are never stored or archived. Booking and audit retain actor/time/limit/excess/reason, the timeline flags the exception, and pacing and cover reports count and drill to overridden reservations separately (including later cancellations). Guest erasure clears linked override reasons in bookings, audit and retained proposal snapshots. Server caps/breaks, physical fit, access, joins and occupied turns always remain hard. BOOK-005 inherits future phone/concierge reservation-book creation; other new doors named in SERVICE-005 inherit these rules before shipping. **Acceptance evidence:** With a full 12-cover 7:30 interval and a physically free four-top, have a public request and an agent request refused. As a host without the grant, be refused. As a granted host, see the warning naming the limit and excess, confirm with a reason and book; read the audit row, the flag on the timeline and the override count in the pacing report. Attempt an override onto an occupied table and be refused. Configured FLOOR-004 concurrent kitchen-area caps are area-pacing warnings eligible for that same signed exception; server cover caps and breaks stay hard. Unrelated roster changes preserve existing reviewed kitchen exceptions; changing the kitchen cap itself still validates existing commitments.

### Booking and distribution

- **BOOK-002 — Branded website booking widget.** Restaurants embed a responsive, accessible booking widget on their own WordPress, Squarespace, Wix or custom website with venue branding, locale, party/date/time search and policy disclosure. The standalone booking page and embed share inventory and preserve source attribution. Owners can switch on consent-aware Google Analytics 4 and Meta Pixel/Conversions API events for search, checkout start and completed booking (with party size and source, never guest contact data). Before shipping, this capability must inherit SERVICE-005 arrival/service/concurrent/area pacing and SERVICE-007 warning, reasoned override and hard physical-capacity obligations; public and agent allocations never override. Embedding follows ct’s 20 October 2026 ruling: the owner alone manages an explicit list of up to 20 exact `https` website origins for the `/book?embed=1` widget (no wildcards, credentials, paths, `http`, `localhost` or loopback addresses, in any environment), and every change is audited with actor, time and the before/after list. Only that widget response names the list in CSP `frame-ancestors`, and it omits `X-Frame-Options`, which cannot express a list; an empty list answers `frame-ancestors 'none'` with `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, as does every other response, so staff pages, the standalone page, the queue and inquiry pages stay unframeable. The widget never submits on its own: a booking needs the guest’s own Confirm booking press. It accepts no messages from the host page, posts only its height to the listed origin and shows no staff link or data. Widget bookings use the public booking door with the online channel’s rules, turn/reset, joins, staffing, pacing and physical capacity, never an override, and record `attribution` `{door: widget, origin}` (the listed origin the widget reported: attribution, not proof); other public bookings record `{door: booking-page}`. The widget uses this installation’s own branding and venue name, US English with venue-local times in the venue’s IANA time zone, and the standalone page’s request terms, availability re-check and inquiry routing; both list each searched service’s online booking rules (party range, large-party inquiry threshold, horizon, same-day cutoff, lead time and arrival interval) before the guest confirms. Analytics follows ct’s 20 October 2026 ruling. Only the owner switches Google Analytics 4 (Measurement Protocol: measurement ID and API secret, optional `debug_mode` test mode) and Meta (Conversions API to the owner’s Pixel/dataset ID: access token, optional `test_event_code`) on or off; every change is audited with actor, time and before/after settings. Switching a provider off stops its events; its saved key stays until the owner enters a new one or removes it. Following ct’s 21 October 2026 ruling, the owner alone (as one of the owner’s own controls; no finance or staff role) can press Remove saved key for each provider: it deletes the stored GA4 API secret or Meta access token, leaves that provider’s other settings unchanged and is audited under AUDIT-001 with actor, time and `keySaved` false, never the key. While a provider is on without a key it sends nothing, the guest is not asked about it, and the settings say a key is needed; restores never bring a key back (DATA-001, DATA-003). The GA4 API secret and Meta access token are write-only: no state response, backup, archive, business CSV, audit row or log contains them (DATA-003 names the exclusion), so a restored installation sends nothing until the owner enters them again (DATA-001). While a provider is on and holds its key, `/book` and the widget ask once per page visit with Accept and Decline, naming each provider that is on and saying what is sent; the answer lives only in that page’s memory and is never stored or carried to another visit. Nothing is sent before Accept, on Decline or without an answer. After Accept the page creates a random visit ID, and Placemat’s server, never a script on the page, sends search (after each search the guest runs), checkout start (when the guest selects a time) and completed booking (after the booking commits) with exactly party size, booking source (`widget` with the listed origin, or `booking-page`) and the visit ID (Meta receives its SHA-256 as `external_id`), plus for Meta the browser user agent, the source page as `event_source_url` and the send time; never guest name or contact data, IP address, cookies, booking reference or reservation date/time. The visit ID is never stored on the booking or anywhere else. Sends run after the guest’s response with no retry queue, so a slow or failing provider never blocks or delays a booking. The owner sees each provider’s latest HTTP answer: GA4 never confirms an event (check DebugView) and Meta reports `events_received`; Placemat never claims a provider verified an event. **Acceptance evidence:** Embed on an allowed test website, search and book at 1440 and 390 widths, navigate by keyboard and verify the same slot disappears on the standalone page; observe the GA4 and Meta test events for the completed booking with no guest contact data, then decline analytics consent and observe none. Test events are observed where GA4 and Meta receive them, at Placemat’s outbound network edge, in each provider’s test mode (`debug_mode`, `test_event_code`): provider-sandbox evidence with the provider edge faked in tests, never hosted or production acceptance.

- **BOOK-003 — Reservation search and availability alternatives.** Guests search by date, party size, area and experience and see honest nearby times or approved sister-venue alternatives when full, including accessible seating constraints. Empty and stale results explain the next available action without collecting a false booking. Current search covers every published open service and existing dining area with exact required access tags. Dates are venue-local arrival dates; nearby alternatives include the requested date through seven later calendar days, inclusive, ordered by actual arrival instant. A selected area and every access tag are required fit constraints at search, booking and later reassignment; availability is not a hold, and a failed commit preserves contact inputs but requires an explicit new selection. Empty results ask the guest to change date or filters or contact the venue, without making a booking. EXP-001 inherits experience filtering and ROLE-001 inherits approved sister-venue alternatives in these same search and commit doors before those capabilities ship. **Acceptance evidence:** Search a full Friday for an accessible four-top, select a Saturday alternative and complete it; race a stale result and receive a clear reselect path.

- **BOOK-004 — Secure guest modification and cancellation.** A scoped expiring manage-booking link lets a guest change time, size or contact details, reconfirm or cancel only their reservation. Show fee/refund consequences before consent and replace inventory atomically; changed links and replays cannot expose other guests. **Acceptance evidence:** Use a delivered link to move a two-top to four, fail an unavailable move without losing the old booking, cancel with policy acknowledgment and refuse an expired or foreign token. Ct approved as adopted with riders (22 October 2026, 18:30Z): an owner or a native admin manager holding reservation authority explicitly sends or reissues to the reservation's recorded email, with an actor audit on every issue. Hosts, shared-device sessions and agents cannot issue. At most five issues per reservation per venue-local calendar day, including reissues and failed-delivery attempts; refusal happens before email. A 32-byte random bearer is stored only as a digest, expires at the earlier of 24 hours and service start, and rotates on successful writes without extending expiry. Reissue or a changed reservation invalidates the prior link. Changing the recorded email closes link access; sending to the new address requires the same explicit issue action. This door sends email only; MSG-008 must establish SMS consent before any future SMS send. No automatic payment, refund or outbound retry occurs. Reservations with payment obligations remain unchanged in manager review until PAY-004 (PARTIAL fee/cancellation policy) and PAY-005 (PARTIAL refund execution) ship their financial-consequence duties. Zero-money management is implemented and proven through public HTTP and the guest page. **Live delivery proof:** `scripts/booking-management-sandbox.mjs` — “BOOK-004 delivered-link zero-money journey”, controlled receiver receipt 3af92aa1-6a2c-4694-87e2-fb245c71cc37 at 2026-10-22T15:15:04.327Z (DMARC pass), proves actual delivery, private-link use, two-to-four change, unavailable preservation, acknowledged cancellation and replay refusal. Fresh controlled receiver receipt 6502906c-1114-40aa-83e7-dffcf3fd7922 at 2026-10-22T19:38:50.261Z repeats that journey with DMARC pass.

- **BOOK-005 — Staff telephone and concierge reservations.** Hosts create future reservations for phone callers, hotel concierges and offline inquiries with source, contact preference and special requests. A permitted role can override party, lead-time or pacing rules with a reason (SERVICE-004, SERVICE-007). When a deposit or card-guarantee policy covers the booking, it sends the PAY-010 payment request link with a deadline. They search existing guests and quote live rules; booking confirmation reaches the guest in the selected channel. Before shipping, this capability must inherit SERVICE-005 arrival/service/concurrent/area pacing and SERVICE-007 warning, reasoned override and hard physical-capacity obligations; public and agent allocations never override. **Acceptance evidence:** As host, book next Friday for a returning caller, identify the concierge source, confirm by SMS and read the booking in the same floor schedule as online guests; book a six-top under a deposit policy and see the PAY-010 request delivered.

- **BOOK-006 — Booking holds and duplicate submissions.** Short-lived checkout/experience holds reserve scarce inventory across channels, display expiry and release on abandonment or failed payment. Stable request identity ensures reloads and retried submits return the same reservation; no guest can be charged for a lost slot. **Acceptance evidence:** Two guests start checkout for the final four-top, expire one hold, complete the other and retry its booking/payment request after a network interruption; find one booking and one charge. Current public checkout holds last at most five minutes, bind an exact booking payload to a client-generated random capability, and count against current channel, physical, turn/reset, pacing, staffing and seat-inventory allocators. Expiry does not renew on replay. Explicit abandonment releases a hold; conversion atomically saves the reservation and consumes its allocation. Reload and interrupted-response recovery return that same reservation. Recovery records contain no guest contact or request text and never travel in archives; guest erasure ends recovery. Payments start only after the reservation exists. An unresolved Checkout attempt protects its reservation until a personal owner or manager recovers the stable processor request and observes an authoritative terminal state; local deadlines and uncertain expiry acknowledgments cannot release it. Closing collection and cancelling a reservation remain separate explicit actions. EXP-002 inherits this hold and duplicate-submission obligation before experience checkout ships.

- **BOOK-007 — Special requests and group inquiries.** Booking captures occasion, stroller/highchair, wheelchair access, dietary/allergy notes and seating preferences with explicit required versus requested distinctions. Large groups and private-dining inquiries have an owner, status, reply due date and conversion to a capacity-checked reservation. The approved guest door shows a cryptographically random 32-byte inquiry token once, stores only its SHA-256 digest, and scopes reads/replies/offer acceptance to that inquiry. Replies are posted on the guest page with no delivery claim; conversion requires explicit guest acceptance of the current exact offer and a fresh physical, access, turn, staffing, pacing and channel-rule check. The token expires on closure or conversion. Current inquiries begin owned by an active venue owner, due 24 elapsed hours after submission; owner/admin managers may reassign to an active native owner/admin and set a future offset-timestamp deadline. Converted inquiries bypass only the large-party inquiry-routing threshold; every other online rule and hard fit remains. Offered party size and required area/access cannot be weakened; changed timing or required guarantees require a new offer and guest acceptance. Only required area/access, party size and offered timing are guaranteed; occasion, stroller/highchair, wheelchair accommodation, dietary/allergy notes and seating preferences are recorded guest requests, with no claim that food is safe. Direct booking displays and records acknowledgment of the required-versus-requested distinction. **Acceptance evidence:** Book with a required accessible table and requested patio, submit a 16-person inquiry, have a manager reply and convert it; verify guest acknowledgment of what is guaranteed.

- **DIST-001 — Reserve with Google.** Placemat completes eligible Actions Center partner onboarding and certification, publishes availability to Google Search/Maps, receives bookings/modifications/cancellations and reconciles inventory with channel attribution. A link alone is labeled a link until the actual end-to-end integration is live. Before shipping, this capability must inherit SERVICE-005 arrival/service/concurrent/area pacing and SERVICE-007 warning, reasoned override and hard physical-capacity obligations; public and agent allocations never override. **Acceptance evidence:** Through Google’s approved test/production partner journey, publish a venue, book on Google, change and cancel there, and verify matching reservation IDs and released local inventory; exercise feed rejection and outage recovery.

- **DIST-002 — Instagram and Facebook booking.** Owners connect Instagram/Facebook booking actions where partner support permits and publish trackable profile links elsewhere. Bookings preserve social/referrer/campaign provenance and real inventory; revoked profiles and unsupported account types receive actionable setup guidance. Before shipping, this capability must inherit SERVICE-005 arrival/service/concurrent/area pacing and SERVICE-007 warning, reasoned override and hard physical-capacity obligations; public and agent allocations never override. **Acceptance evidence:** Connect a supported profile, follow its reservation action at phone width, book and inspect social attribution; disconnect and prove existing bookings remain manageable.

- **DIST-003 — Diner discovery and partner distribution.** Searchable venue pages expose location, cuisine, menus, images, experiences and live availability; diner discovery and approved concierge/travel/marketplace distribution bring bookable demand. Partners use allocated inventory or the shared live ledger, with source fees visible and no assumption of inherited OpenTable/Resy network reach. Before shipping, this capability must inherit SERVICE-005 arrival/service/concurrent/area pacing and SERVICE-007 warning, reasoned override and hard physical-capacity obligations; public and agent allocations never override. **Acceptance evidence:** Find a venue by neighborhood and cuisine, book an experience from a partner listing and reconcile its source, fee and remaining tables; reject a duplicate partner callback.

- **DIST-004 — Channel inventory and attribution.** Managers allocate protected tables/covers by direct, Google, social, discovery, phone and partner channels, with release times, direct-booking priority and source/campaign attribution that survives modification. A channel outage cannot oversell shared physical inventory. Before shipping, this capability must inherit SERVICE-005 arrival/service/concurrent/area pacing and SERVICE-007 warning, reasoned override and hard physical-capacity obligations; public and agent allocations never override. **Acceptance evidence:** Reserve two four-tops for direct until 5 p.m., exhaust partner allocation, release it on schedule and inspect original source after a guest changes time. The reservation book shows each party’s channel and totals covers by channel (website, Google, Instagram, phone) that reconcile to its rows, including after a guest changes time.

- **DIST-005 — Guest accounts and repeat booking.** **Status: done.** CT judged DIST-005 at `90fbab254ae525906eded2f2f27752c1799dda30` on 27 October 2026 and accepted it as done. Diners can optionally keep verified contact details, favorite restaurants, manage upcoming reservations and rebook prior visits across devices, with saved preferences controlled per restaurant. Guest checkout remains available and identity never merges distinct people solely because they share a phone. **CT ruling, 26 October 2026 — APPROVE WITH RIDERS; DIST-005 remains PARTIAL.** A diner explicitly proves access to the selected booking’s current recorded email before attaching that booking. Thirty-two-byte random one-use codes are stored only as digests and expire after fifteen minutes; independent device bearers are stored only as digests and expire after twenty-four hours. Each additional booking needs its own current-contact proof. Shared phone numbers confer no identity, booking or account authority. Favorites and preferences are controlled per restaurant; verification grants no staff role, marketing permission, review eligibility or group-sharing permission. Sends are explicit, bounded and audited, with provider acceptance distinguished from mailbox delivery. Logout revokes the selected device; account forget revokes all account sessions without cancelling reservations. DATA-003 portability, DATA-002 erasure fences and AUDIT-001 accountability apply to these records, while verification and device custody remain excluded from archives. The complete diner-facing favorite, repeat-booking and upcoming-reservation management target across devices remains binding. Group sharing remains the separate GUEST-006 target. **CT update ruling, 26 October 2026 — APPROVE WITH RIDERS; DIST-005 remains PARTIAL.** The earlier DIST-005 ruling remains binding. Pending email proof may retain the private booking, guest and current-contact references needed to validate that single booking, while storing the random code only as a digest, expiring it after fifteen minutes and consuming it once. Failed or uncertain mail does not establish delivery or successful verification. An independent digest-only device session expires after twenty-four hours and grants management only for individually verified bookings whose current recorded contact still matches. Every change, reconfirmation or cancellation requires a fresh booking-specific preview and explicit diner confirmation; the preview is bound to that device, booking and current state, is revocable and is excluded from archives. Capacity failure, stale state, replay, revoked access or changed contact grants no mutation authority. Recorded payment obligations require manager review and remain unchanged through this diner door; this grants no charge, refund, fee waiver or automatic message authority. Current-contact, custody, audit, portability and erasure riders remain binding. This update accepts no completion. **Acceptance evidence:** Book without an account, verify a diner account, attach only the verified booking, rebook a favorite on another device and revoke saved preferences.

- **DIST-006 — Verified diner reviews and restaurant replies.** Diners whose reservation was seated or completed (or matched to a POS check) can rate and review the venue once per attended visit on its Placemat venue page and booking widget; no-shows, cancellations and staff cannot review. Reviews show the visit date, averages show only above a minimum count, and the restaurant can post and edit one public reply per review and report abuse for moderation under published guidelines. Refuse a review for a no-show and a second review for the same visit. Reply as manager and see the reply public; report an abusive review and read the moderation outcome; prove a manager cannot delete a one-star review.

### The host stand and floor

- **FLOOR-002 — Rooms and editable floor plans.** Managers arrange rooms, indoor/outdoor areas, bars and numbered tables with shapes, seats, accessibility and joinable combinations. Changes are previewed against future commitments; retired tables retain history and live occupancy is visible without manual page reload. Before richer table attributes ship, preserve FLOOR-009 direct move/swap/lock fit, access and history obligations. Rooms have indoor, outdoor or bar types; numbered tables use round, square, rectangle or bar shapes, exact access tags and percentage positions within a room. A floor-change preview lists every affected commitment, replacement, conflict and disabled combination; a manager approves the exact venue, rooms, floor, services, observations and bookings snapshot. Active commitments retain their room, confirmed times, fit and access needs. Locked assignments must be unlocked explicitly; arrived, seated or unbussed parties must be resolved before retirement. Retirement removes a table from new availability and selection, disables its joins and keeps the table plus historical bookings and attributed replacement history. Open host devices check the authorized floor version every three seconds and update without a page reload; focused or unsaved forms defer replacement and show the pending change, and failed checks show an unavailable warning. FLOOR-008 inherits offline reconciliation and richer synchronization; FLOOR-004 inherits sections, server capacity and serving history. Current and future allocation doors inherit retirement, fit and access guards before shipping (BOOK-002, BOOK-005, DIST-001–DIST-004, VOICE-001, AGENT-001). **Acceptance evidence:** Draw dining room and patio, retire a booked table with an approved replacement, book both areas and watch occupancy update on a second host device.

- **FLOOR-003 — Approved table combinations.** Managers explicitly permit which adjacent tables can join, their combined capacity, accessible fit and setup buffer. Allocation cannot combine distant or incompatible tables merely because their seats sum to the party size. Before explicit join definitions ship, enforce FLOOR-009 permitted combinations on direct and prepared moves as well as all booking doors. Managers confirm adjacency explicitly for an exact set; joins can cross named areas only when explicitly approved, while a booking’s required area must match every constituent. Approved capacity is an integer no greater than the constituent seats, and every approved access tag must exist on every constituent. Setup is 0–120 whole elapsed minutes immediately before arrival, within the service, with half-open occupancy from setup start through the preserved turn/reset and any ongoing overrun; single tables need no setup. Current public search/booking, staff walk-ins, waitlist seating, direct move/swap/lock and prepared assignments all enforce these definitions. Active booked/seated commitments freeze join settings and setup; disabling prevents new assignments while preserving those commitments, and structural edits wait until they finish. Changes to join configuration invalidate prepared publication or reassignment review. Future booking doors (BOOK-002, BOOK-005, DIST-001–DIST-004, VOICE-001, AGENT-001) inherit exact joins and full setup before shipping. **Acceptance evidence:** Permit T1+T2 but prohibit T1+T8; request six guests, verify the permitted join is used and reject a host attempting the prohibited join.

- **FLOOR-004 — Server sections and fair covers.** Managers create shift-specific sections, assign servers and tables, record breaks and cap covers per server. Hosts see seated/expected covers and rotation, while reassignment preserves the serving history and checks kitchen and server capacity. Before server sections ship, expose assigned server filtering in the FLOOR-005 timeline and enforce FLOOR-009 server capacity and serving history on moves. Servers are named shift roster entries, not new sign-in roles. Each table belongs to at most one section per service, and an assignment or join must fit wholly within one section once sections are configured. Server and configured kitchen-area caps count overlapping booked or seated dining covers in half-open arrival-to-forecast-departure intervals; setup and cleanup still reserve physical tables separately. Ongoing seated parties remain counted past forecast departure. Expected covers total the shift’s booked and seated parties; seated covers total its currently seated parties, with exact booking drilldowns and missing seating history labeled. Each party counts against every kitchen area containing its assigned tables. Breaks exclude new assignments and seating, while an existing seated party can retain its server during a same-section move. Rotation considers a requested party size and live fitting tables, breaks and caps, then orders eligible servers by seated covers, oldest last seating (never seated first) and stable server id. Active section mappings cannot silently change; move or finish affected parties before changing their mapping. New reservations, walk-ins, waitlist seating, status reacquisition, direct moves/swaps, reviewed proposals and retirement replacements all enforce these capacities and retain attributed serving events. FLOOR-008 inherits offline staffing reconciliation, ROLE-003 inherits server-specific sign-in visibility, and SERVICE-005/007 inherit wider interval pacing and permitted overrides; BOOK-002/005, DIST-001–DIST-004, VOICE-001 and AGENT-001 inherit staffing constraints before their new doors ship. **Acceptance evidence:** Assign two sections and servers, seat uneven parties, put one server on break and move a table; verify cover totals, suggested rotation and attributed service history. SERVICE-007 carries signed, reasoned exceptions to the configured concurrent kitchen-area cap; server caps and breaks remain hard.

- **FLOOR-005 — Timeline and overdue turns.** A searchable day/service timeline shows arrivals, assigned tables, expected/actual seating and departure, cleanup, late arrivals and overdue turns. Hosts zoom or filter by room/server and resolve an overrun by moving the next arrival in one host action (FLOOR-009) or accepting a proposed replacement, never silently moving a confirmed reservation. Current observations are staff-recorded, not POS verification. An extension changes only the expected departure, retains the originally confirmed seating/departure/reset and appends actor, receipt time, prior/new forecast and reason; no reservation moves until a separate direct host command or reviewed agent proposal is accepted. The original cleanup duration follows the extended forecast, and an ongoing seated party remains physically occupied even past its forecast. Late means an actual arrival after the promised start, or an unarrived booked party past that start; overdue means an ongoing seated party past expected departure. Raw elapsed minutes are returned, while labels round to the nearest minute. The inclusive next window is now through now plus the selected elapsed minutes; seated/due/average totals use the displayed filtered parties. Average actual turn is the mean corrected seating-to-completed duration for parties actually completed today in venue time; missing actual timestamps are excluded and an empty mean stays unknown. Each total opens its exact party ids. Search matches guest name/contact, reservation id, service and tables without changing identity. The selected date is the venue-local service-start date. Current room/area and time-scale filters work on existing tables; FLOOR-004 inherits populated server assignments and server filtering before sections ship. Corrections retain both original observations and restored facts. **Acceptance evidence:** Seat a late six-top, extend its actual turn and inspect the collision with the next arrival; move the next arrival to a fitting replacement as a host in one action and read both histories. The host header shows seated covers now, covers due within a configurable next window and the average actual turn so far today, each opening its parties.

- **FLOOR-006 — Service statuses and handover.** Hosts manage confirmed, reconfirmed, arrived, partially arrived, seated, ordering, check open, paid, clearing, completed, late, canceled and no-show states. Status changes carry timestamps and actor; POS observations cannot falsely mark a dirty table ready. Current owner/admin staff and owner-granted FLOOR-009 hosts record service observations; ROLE-003 carries further host/server rights before those roles ship. Current observations are explicitly staff-recorded, including paid, which does not claim a POS payment. POS-007 inherits all status, timestamp, dirty-table and correction obligations before connected observations ship. Service and floor histories append the actor and server receipt time; a correction requires a reason, restores only the latest observation’s prior state and retains both rows, refusing physical clashes. Paid and completed leave the table needing bussing; only staff ready permits another seating. Future online reservations still use the promised turn/reset, and ready never shortens that protected interval. Floor timers show elapsed whole minutes since the last course/floor change; missing legacy observations are labeled not recorded. A read of shift handover shows current stages and their full observations, including corrections. **Acceptance evidence:** Run a reservation from arrival through paid and clearing to ready, correct an accidental state with a reason and inspect the next shift’s handover. The floor plan marks each table reserved, seated, mains, dessert, check dropped or needs bussing with a timer since its last transition, from host taps or POS signals (POS-007), and a legend names the same states.

- **FLOOR-007 — Busy-service search and shift handover.** Hosts find guests, bookings, phone numbers and table labels quickly, filter by service/source/status and see VIP, allergy, access and unpaid-policy alerts with PAY-010 deadlines. A handover lists unresolved guest requests, late parties and promised callbacks with owners and due times. **Acceptance evidence:** Find an arriving guest by phone suffix, resolve their access request, hand over an unpaid deposit exception and prove the next host can complete the promised callback. Current timeline search uses GUEST-002 case/accent-normalized name/email and normalized US phone suffix matching, plus case-insensitive booking-ID, service-name and table-label substrings. Venue-local service-start date, service, source and booking-status filters combine; an empty filter includes every value. It displays existing VIP/regular facts, guest-supplied allergy/accommodation requests and required table access/area, without certifying food safety or claiming a payment. Ct policy (21 October 2026): An active owner-granted host or a manager creates a follow-up and assigns it to themself or another active host or manager. A host reassigns only items they hold; a manager reassigns any. The current assignee or a manager completes it. Every active host and manager sees each open item's kind, booking, guest, due time, assignee and state. Free text is shown only to managers and the current assignee, never to agents or preparation keys, and leaves the SEC-002 stand page on lock or switch. **Ct assertions:** host A hands to B; C sees the item without its text; B completes it on the stand; after a switch to C, B's text is absent from response and DOM. All acceptance points pass. Hosts create and hand over their own work; active hosts retain booking/kind/guest/assignee/due/state metadata, while current assignment controls free text in live and historical reads. Manager-defined USD deposit requests supply real unpaid deadlines and overdue exceptions; transferring their callback transfers the follow-up owner. Completion records an operational outcome and never marks a deposit paid. PAY-010 retains delivered notices, policy automation, waivers and live sandbox proof in its own partial clause.

- **FLOOR-008 — Concurrent devices and operational outage.** Host devices reconcile live changes, identify stale edits and show last successful sync. During an outage staff can read an encrypted, time-stamped service sheet and capture pending actions; reconnect requires conflict review before pending seats or reservations affect live inventory. **Acceptance evidence:** Seat from two tablets, disconnect one, record a pending walk-in and reconnect after its table is sold; refuse silent overwrite and reconcile to a different table. With the reservation book open on one device, make a booking from the guest page and see it arrive within seconds with a “new since” count and marker, without a reload and without overwriting a stale edit. The live reservation book counts and marks reservations absent from the first successful state snapshot of that open staff page, scoped to the selected service. Unrelated updates, assignment changes and explicit refresh retain that baseline; reopening the page starts a fresh baseline. The count includes every current reservation status and source, with no persistent guest or browser tracking. Focused or unsaved forms defer replacement and show the pending change; sync failures show an unavailable warning and the last successful sync remains visible.

Ct policy (23 October 2026): **Access.** "Staff" means the owner, active managers (admin) and owner-granted hosts, plus seating leads within their ROLE-002 grant. They may use outage mode on a personal session or under their PIN session on a registered SEC-002 stand. The owner turns this on with one explicit, audited and revocable venue setting (before/after recorded). The owner-only mode stays available. Servers, finance, plain members, group admins, agents and preparation keys are always refused. **Device keys.** Each person who will use a sheet on a device enrols their own outage passphrase (at least 16 characters) while online. This wraps the sheet key for that person, and the enrolment is audited. There is no shared passphrase, and a SEC-002 PIN is never an offline key. Offline unlock, capture and discard are attributed to the unlocking person. That attribution is marked "device-attributed" until a person with live authority signs the reconciliation. **Offline data.** Every role gets one minimised projection, never more than FLOOR-012's host projection: per booking, the guest name as booked, a short booking reference, the last four digits of the US phone, party size, arrival and reset end, tables/section/server, status, required access tags, and guest-supplied allergy/dietary/access requests labelled unverified. It holds no email, no full phone, no guest notes, tags, VIP level, visit count, occasion, preferences, deposit or payment state, and nothing from other services. Erased guests appear only as "Erased guest". Pending reservations and waitlist entries may hold the name and one contact that staff type, under the same encryption and expiry. **Pending actions.** Staff can capture walk-ins, pending reservations, waitlist adds, seating an existing reservation, and marking a reservation arrived, finished or no-show. Each action has a UUID, a device capture time and the capturing person. **Retention.** The sheet expires at the earlier of 12 hours or one hour after service end, and is deleted on the next page activity or unlock. It is also deleted when the last pending action is reconciled or discarded, and the next time the page is online after any of these: sign-out, session revocation, removal of the host grant, device revocation, or the owner turning outage mode off. While online, unreconciled actions show a persistent warning before expiry. When a draft expires with unreviewed actions, the next online contact records an audit row holding only their count and creates a manager-visible follow-up (FLOOR-007). **Locking.** Five idle minutes lock the sheet on a personal session. On a stand, SEC-002's two-minute inactivity lock and any switch also lock it, so the stricter rule applies. Leaving the page clears the key. **Offline open.** An installed offline app shell must open the locked sheet after a reload or restart with no connection. **Reconnect.** Nothing applies automatically. A person with live authority for that action reviews the current floor and the exact alternatives. They sign a five-minute review bound to actor, action and floor version, and every live seating, access, turn, combination, hold, pacing and staffing guard is checked again. The action then commits atomically through its normal door, exactly once, including replay after a lost response or erasure. Hard conflicts are never bypassed. A SERVICE-007 override is offered only to its grant holders, through the existing reviewed path. Capture time stays an observation. A party that has already left is recorded only through an explicit, reviewed "already finished during outage" action that carries device-observed times labelled as such. **Audit.** The log records the venue setting, each sheet preparation (person, device, service, expiry, field-scope version), passphrase enrolments, and each commit: UUID, capturing and reconciling persons, capture time, original and final tables, and the conflict. It also records expired-unreviewed counts and discards reported on reconnect. Offline reads cannot be server-audited, and the clause says so.

**Remaining gaps (FLOOR-008 stays PARTIAL):**

| Gap | Remaining |
| --- | --- |
| G1 | host, manager and seating-lead access, plus SEC-002 stand use, behind the owner setting |
| G2 | per-person key wrapping and offline attribution |
| G3 | the minimised named projection (today the sheet is anonymous only, so hosts cannot greet an arriving party) |
| G4 | pending reservations, waitlist adds, seat-existing and arrived/finished/no-show actions, plus the reviewed "already finished" action |
| G5 | offline app shell (today "reloading needs a connection") |
| G6 | the extra deletion triggers and the expired-unreviewed audit row and follow-up |
| G7 | a SERVICE-007 override for grant holders. |

- **FLOOR-009 — Direct host table moves, swaps and locks.** A host or manager moves a booked, arrived or seated party to a free fitting table or permitted combination, swaps two parties’ tables, or locks an assignment, each in one direct action (drag on the floor plan or timeline, or Change assignment on the reservation) on tablet, phone and web. No manager approval is needed. At commit each action checks the live floor version, physical fit, overlapping turns, permitted joins and required access needs, refuses a move into an occupied or clashing table with the reason, and writes one audit row with actor, before/after tables, time and optional reason. A locked assignment is never changed by automatic allocation, reflow or agent proposals until a person unlocks it. The prepare→approve path of PLAN-001 remains for preparation keys and agent proposals only. The owner grants or revokes the venue host capability for an active native member; native account roles remain unchanged. Hosts use direct assignment, service-observation and WAIT-002 intake/party-update commands, never proposal approval, venue administration or bulk guest export. Every direct assignment command requires the exact current floor version. Current combinations must stay in one dining area and each selected table must contain every exact required access tag recorded on the booking. FLOOR-002 and GUEST-003 inherit richer table/access attributes; FLOOR-003 inherits explicit permitted adjacent joins and setup buffers; FLOOR-004 inherits server capacity and serving-history constraints before those capabilities ship. Current and future allocation and agent doors must retain locked assignments until an explicit human unlock; humans also unlock before a direct move or swap. An atomic swap validates the final two-party floor, then writes one audit row containing both parties. Assignment reasons and guest-linked access tags follow DATA-002 erasure. **Acceptance evidence:** Signed in as a host, not a manager, move a seated four-top to a free fitting table, swap two booked parties and lock a third assignment, each in one HTTP command and one floor-screen gesture at 1440 and 390 widths; read the three audit rows. Refuse a move into an occupied table and into a table whose next turn clashes. Book a new party and prove automatic allocation leaves the locked assignment untouched. Prove a preparation key can still only prepare a `table.assign` proposal.

- **FLOOR-010 — Counter seats and unassigned bar pools.** Managers define bars and chef’s counters as seat-level inventory (a 10-seat counter where a two-top takes 2 seats, adjacent where required) and lounge or bar areas as unassigned cover pools with their own pacing and turn times. Counter seats are chosen at booking or assigned at arrival; a pool reservation holds covers without a table until the host seats it. Seats and pools share the one capacity ledger, turns and pacing with tables, and hosts can move a pool or counter party to a table under FLOOR-009. **Acceptance evidence:** Define a 10-seat counter and a 20-cover lounge pool; book five two-tops at the counter and refuse a sixth for the same turn; seat two adjacent counter guests and prove those seats are not sold twice across overlapping turns. Book a lounge reservation, seat it at assigned bar seats on arrival and then move it to a table, reading pool and table occupancy after each step. Before counter seats or pools ship, include their assignments on FLOOR-012 screen, print and PDF and assert the chef’s-counter acceptance there. Current inventory settings and identities are immutable for history. Counter units are physical one-person seats; pool units are anonymous cover holds, not physical seats. Pool inventory requires explicit area selection; hosts assign physical seats before seating, then may transfer to a table while retaining confirmed times and required access. Transfers refuse a destination requiring a longer turn. Counters count individually in physical-seat utilization; anonymous pool capacity is reported separately. Existing correction histories and immutable report publication apply.

- **FLOOR-011 — Late arrivals, holds and the no-show workflow.** Past a configurable grace time a booked party shows as late on the floor and timeline. A host (or the service agent inside a person-approved policy) logs each contact attempt, an outbound call or text, against the booking with its outcome: answered, no answer, voicemail, delivered or failed. When a guest says they are running late, the table is held to a stated time only if the next turn on it allows; otherwise the host sees the clash and the fitting alternatives. A person marks the no-show; the timeline records each step with actor and time, the party’s capacity returns to the shared ledger, the PAY-004 fee policy runs on recorded consent and the freed table is offered to fitting waiting parties under WAIT-004 with a stated hold window. A guest who arrives after release is seated at the next fitting table, never over a reassigned one. **Acceptance evidence:** Book a four-top for 7:15, reach the grace time with no arrival, log two unanswered calls and mark the no-show at 7:30 as a host; read the timeline with each step, actor and time; verify the table returns to availability, one PAY-004 fee is recorded and a fitting waiting party receives a table-ready text with its hold window and is seated. Text “running 15 late” for another booking and verify its table is held to the stated time; refuse an extension that would clash with the next booking on that table.

- **FLOOR-012 — Printable pre-shift sheet.** Before service a host or manager opens one sheet for the service date, printable from the browser, downloadable as PDF and readable on host devices. It lists the guests to know (VIP and regular status with visit count, occasion, declared allergies and access needs from GUEST-003, seating preference and the notes the viewer’s role may see), deposits and card guarantees held with amounts (PAY-002, PAY-003) and unpaid PAY-010 deadlines, the server sections with their tables and expected covers (FLOOR-004), the pacing limits (SERVICE-005) and the kitchen notes of FLOOR-013. It reflects bookings and changes up to the moment it is opened and shows when it was generated. Roles without rights (ROLE-003, ROLE-004) never see restricted notes or contact details on it, and erased guests (DATA-002) never appear with personal values. **Acceptance evidence:** Prepare a Friday with a shellfish-allergic anniversary regular, an eight-top with a deposit and a chef’s-counter booking; open the pre-shift sheet as manager and print it to PDF; read each guest’s flags, deposit and section; change a booking and reopen to see the change and a new generated time; open it as a server and find restricted notes absent; erase one guest and prove a new sheet holds none of their values. Under ct’s 21 October 2026 ruling, FLOOR-012 is done when every existing capability conforms: owner/admin get the full current sheet; owner-granted hosts get names, VIP/regular level, recorded attended visit count, occasion, unverified guest-supplied dietary/allergy/access requests, seating preferences, table/section/server and pacing only. Hosts receive no contact, guest notes or tags. Plain members and preparation keys are refused. One server-side projection feeds HTML, print and on-demand PDF; no sheet or PDF is stored. The date is venue-local; every service starting on that date is included, with current non-canceled/non-no-show bookings and a generated instant. Erased guests show only “Erased guest”, time, party size and table. Saved deposit requests show protection state and their pay-by deadline in the live sheet, print and PDF for managers and hosts; only server-verified paid state establishes protection. No card guarantee or held-deposit amount is inferred; PAY-002 and PAY-003 retain their amount/guarantee duties. Before their capabilities ship, PAY-002, PAY-003, PAY-010, FLOOR-013, GUEST-003, FLOOR-010, ROLE-003 (server acceptance step) and ROLE-004 each inherit their full sheet duties and acceptance in both documents. The deposit eight-top, chef’s-counter and server acceptance steps remain binding in those receivers; current proof uses an ordinary eight-top, guest-supplied requests and a granted host.

- **FLOOR-013 — Service notes and kitchen notes.** Managers attach free-text shift notes (for example “regular booked Thursday, seat in Ana’s section”) and kitchen notes to a service date. Every host device and the pre-shift sheet (FLOOR-012) show them, and edits keep author, time and history. The kitchen view of a service shows the arrival pacing limit and covers expected per interval (SERVICE-005), large parties, counts of dishes, add-ons or tasting choices that guests supplied at booking (BOOK-007, EXP-002) totaled by item, and each declared allergy and access need by table (GUEST-003) with no diagnosis and no statement that food is safe. Counts come only from guest-supplied booking data or manager entry and say which; Placemat never estimates portions. **Acceptance evidence:** As manager add the kitchen note “Halibut: 12 portions” and a shift note; as host open the floor on a second device and read both; collect a halibut pre-order on three bookings and see the item total with its source; record a shellfish allergy for the Table 12 booking and read it in the kitchen view beside the arrival pacing limit; edit the note and read author, time and history; open the kitchen view as a server and find only that server’s section allergies. Before service notes ship, feed current authorized shift/kitchen notes into FLOOR-012 through its one server-filtered projection for screen, print and PDF. FLOOR-013 retains unpaid ordinary-reservation dish pre-orders from a manager-published list; paid or ticketed add-ons belong to EXP-002. FLOOR-013 must add DATA-003 CSV/archive coverage, DATA-001 restore validation and DATA-002 erasure before shipping. Under ct’s 21 October 2026 ruling, FLOOR-013 is done when every current capability conforms: unpaid dish pre-orders are captured on ordinary public reservations from the manager-published per-service list, with integer quantities and the item name preserved. Withdrawn dishes refuse new requests and retain previous quantities. Guest-supplied quantities and manager-entered counts are shown separately, never estimated or treated as a paid order. Kitchen totals and covers include booked, seated and completed reservations, excluding cancelled/no-show parties; large parties are eight or more. Service-date notes use the venue-local date on which the service starts. Owner/admin write notes and publish dishes/counts; owner/admin and granted hosts read shift notes, while owner/admin, granted hosts and plain members read the identity-free kitchen view; preparation keys cannot open it. Note edits append text, actor and instant history; hosts receive live changes through the existing floor version, and the kitchen has live updates plus explicit refresh. Authorized shift and kitchen notes feed FLOOR-012’s one screen/print/PDF projection. Kitchen allergy/access fields are unverified guest-supplied requests by table, with no guest identity/contact fields, diagnosis or safety claim. Paid/ticketed add-ons and tasting choices inherit item/source totals and sheet coverage in EXP-002 before shipping. ROLE-003 inherits server sign-in with own-section allergies, including the full server kitchen acceptance step; GUEST-003 inherits declared/acknowledged allergy and access sources before shipping. Notes/history, published lists, manager counts and booking quantities export in DATA-003 CSVs and structured archives; DATA-001 validates their dates, shapes and relationships before restore. DATA-002 clears the erased guest’s booking quantities/needs and shared note text/history on their booked service dates, redacts the corresponding audit snapshots and fences older archives. Anonymous counts, dates, actors and instants remain. Current tests assert manager/host/member/key boundaries, three guest pre-orders, per-table needs, pacing/large parties, note history/live reads, pre-shift HTML/PDF, portable restore, invalid-reference refusal and erasure. The future server and acknowledged-needs acceptance remains binding in those receivers.

### Waitlist and cancellation demand

- **WAIT-002 — Remote and walk-up joining.** Guests join by QR, website or host intake, state party size, preferred time/area, access needs and contact consent, receive a secure queue-status link and leave or update their party. Duplicate active entries are explained; online joining can be paused independently of staff intake. The QR and website open the same /queue public door; joining reserves no table. An online join requires email for the existing normalized exact-email guest lookup, while staff intake can record a guest without email. Same name or phone never merges people. An active duplicate means the same existing guest id in the same service in queued, offered, accepted or arrived state (including legacy waiting); public refusals give one generic next action without disclosing contact existence. Each intake returns a new private status link once; 32 random bytes form the bearer and only its SHA-256 digest is persisted. The fragment link scopes read, update and leave to that one entry, never guestbook/contact/history reads; rotation replaces its hash and immediately invalidates the old link. The guest saves/copies the link: no email or text send is claimed. Online pause is an owner/admin service setting and affects new public joins only; owner-granted hosts can add a staff party or change its party preferences while paused, but cannot pause intake, approve plans, administer the venue or export guests. Public-created entries and no-phone follow-ups have an active native owner; guest actions are labeled guest-supplied, not verified identity. Preferred times are offset instants inside the service (start inclusive, end exclusive), preferred areas name existing areas, and declared required access tags are exact case-sensitive strings carried into capacity-checked seating and FLOOR-009 assignment. Preferences do not promise a table. Contact permission is an explicit optional boolean for this queue, independent of marketing and of joining; changes keep source, actor and receipt time. SERVICE-004 channel checks govern public join/update and SERVICE-006 full-turn/reset checks still govern actual seating. Resolved entries remain readable by their link but cannot be changed or rotated. DATA-002 erasure clears the link hash and guest-linked preference/contact-permission/history values; the link then returns the same generic unavailable response as an unknown link, while anonymous timing and accountability remain behind existing restore fences. **Acceptance evidence:** Join by phone QR and staff intake, refuse a duplicate, change party size and pause online intake while allowing a host entry. WAIT-002 queue intake stays open at pacing caps, labelled “queued only; no table or time promised”; pacing is enforced when a person seats, books or allocates from the queue.
