- **API-002 — Scoped integration lifecycle.** Owners create least-privilege, location-aware application credentials, rotate and revoke them, set permitted event subscriptions and inspect usage and failures. Pagination, schema versions and documented rate responses make integrations operable without exposing full owner data. Semantics (API-002 scope set, ct-approved 20 Oct; attendance approved 21 Oct under wording-audit-49-final.md A2, owner hold discharged 21 Oct 01:42Z): this clause's target is exactly the catalogue below and the lifecycle around it; further read scopes (such as contact details or money) and any write scope each need their own owner-approved clause and acceptance before they join the catalogue. Only the native human owner's session manages integration keys, and secrets are issued only in the app: the Integrations page form creates a key and rotates its secret (`integration.create`, `integration.rotate`), the JSON command door refuses both even for the owner (403 `integration_secret_in_app_only`), and the owner revokes a key or changes its events on the page or through the owner command door (`integration.revoke`, `integration.events`); agent keys, integration keys, members, instructors and kiosks are refused with no writes. A key's secret is 256 random bits shown once; Strap stores only its SHA-256 hash, as for agent keys, and a key works only while the owner who created it keeps the same active owner access. The fixed read-only catalogue holds `roster:read` and the separately granted `attendance:read`. The `roster:read` scope returns classes (id, title, service, UTC start and end, capacity, published or cancelled) with each booking's id, status (booked, waitlisted, offered or cancelled) and the attendee's first name plus last initial; it never carries attendance, money, packs, payments, fees, balances, contact details, notes, cancellation reasons or instructor names. The separate GET resource `/api/strap/integration/attendance` requires `attendance:read`, which is off by default and granted explicitly by the owner only when creating a new key on Integrations. Scopes stay fixed for a key's life: no existing key gains attendance and rotation never widens scopes. For a key created before API-003 shipped it uses the roster's class paging and returns only each class id and each currently booked booking's `bookingId` and `attended` boolean. True means its current outcome is attended, by check-in or owner correction; false covers unrecorded, no-show and excused without distinguishing them. Waitlisted, offered and cancelled bookings are omitted. No names, outcome labels, times, actors, channels, kiosk ids, fees, credits, reasons, corrections or notes appear; a key also granted `roster:read` may join on bookingId. Naming no-show, excused or cancellation outcomes, or a member reference, is API-003, which applies only to keys created after it shipped. Every API-002 rule applies to both scopes, including the owner-only lifecycle, check order, shared per-key rate limit, logs, rotation, revocation, location, erasure and restore fences. Every key covers the studio's one location (the Studio settings location) until STUDIO-002 adds location scopes. The integration door (`/api/strap/integration/`) answers GET only: any other method is refused 405 `read_only`, and any resource outside the key's scopes, including payments, balances, packs and people, 403 `scope_not_granted`, with no writes. Every request names `strap-schema-version: 1`; a missing or unknown version is refused 400 with the supported versions. Roster pages hold 1–100 classes (default 50) in UTC start-then-id order after an opaque cursor; an invalid limit or cursor is refused, never clamped. Each key may make 60 counted requests in any rolling 60 seconds: every request with a live secret counts, whatever its outcome, except those refused by the limit, which are answered 429 `rate_limited` with `Retry-After` in whole seconds (1–60) until the oldest counted request leaves the window. Strap checks the secret, then the limit, the method, the schema version and the scope. Rotation commits the new secret and the old secret's revocation together; revocation stops every secret of the key at once, and a revoked key cannot be rotated or resubscribed. The owner who created a key reads its usage and failures: the newest 100 requests per key with time, method, path, status and refusal code, never a query string, member data or secret; a request with an unknown secret cannot be attributed and is not logged. A key subscribes only to events its scopes permit (`roster:read`: `class.changed` and `booking.changed`; `attendance:read`: `attendance.changed`); Strap records the subscriptions and labels them not delivered until INT-008 delivers signed events. Keys, secrets, subscriptions, logs and rate counts never travel in native archives or the portable exit, so a restored studio has no integration keys and refuses every old secret (ARCHIVE-001, MOVE-011); erased people never appear in either scope. Named carriers inherit these rules with their own before-shipping acceptance: STUDIO-002 (location scopes), INT-008 (signed delivery of subscribed, scope-permitted events) and SEC-003 (used-member erasure leaves both scopes). **Acceptance evidence:** Create a read-roster integration for one location, traverse paginated results, attempt financial data and writes, rotate/revoke the key and inspect failures and rate-limit behavior. A roster-only key is refused attendance with 403 and its roster still has no attendance; a dual-scope key created before API-003 shipped reads true for check-in and owner-corrected attendance, false for no-show and excused, and no money or reason fields. Erased people are absent and a native restored studio refuses the key; `docs/INTEGRATIONS.md` documents the separate scope.

- **API-003 — Attendance outcome sharing.** Owners let another application, such as a front-desk display or a studio dashboard, read who booked, attended, missed or cancelled each class through a separate explicit `attendance:read` scope on a new integration key, with a stable per-key member reference and short names, and without reasons, notes, health answers, money or contact details. GET `/api/strap/integration/attendance` returns, for each class on the page, its id, title, service, UTC start and end and status (published or cancelled), and for each seat with an outcome a row of exactly: `bookingId`, `memberRef`, `attendee`, `outcome`, `checkedInAt`, `checkInChannel`, `cancelledAt`, `cancelledBy`, `corrected`, `correctedFrom`, `correctedAt` and `source`. `outcome` is one of `booked` (a confirmed seat nobody has checked in or marked), `attended`, `no_show`, `excused`, `late_cancel` and `early_cancel`; the outcome is the booking's current state, and a late arrival is not a state, so a consumer compares `checkedInAt` with the class start. A waitlisted or offered place has no outcome and is omitted, as is a cancellation that was not a late or early cancel choice (a move, an expired offer, a waitlist release, or the studio cancelling the class, which the class status shows). `checkedInAt` and `checkInChannel` are set only for a real check-in (roster or kiosk) and are null when the owner corrected the seat to attended. `cancelledAt` and `cancelledBy` (`member`, `staff` or `system`) are set only on a cancelled seat. `corrected` is true when the owner corrected the outcome, `correctedFrom` is the outcome before the latest correction (`no_show` or `late_cancel`) and `correctedAt` its UTC time, never the reason. `source` is `native`, or `imported` for a row that MOVE-009 brings in. `attendee` is the first name plus last initial, as in the roster. `memberRef` is `mref_` plus the first 128 bits, in hex, of HMAC-SHA-256 over the person id under a random secret held only by that key: it is the same for one member in every class and across secret rotation, differs between members, and cannot be joined across two keys or to a person id. The resource never carries correction, cancellation or waiver reasons, notes, staff alerts, waiver state, intake or health answers, contact details, kiosk ids, check-in codes, full names, person ids, money, fees, credits, packs, balances, instructor names or pay, or an erased person. A key subscribed to `attendance.changed` is told it is recorded and labelled not delivered until INT-008 delivers signed events. Carriers inherit these rules with their own before-shipping acceptance: INT-008 (the event carries only these fields), SEC-003 (used and imported member erasure removes the rows and the reference), STUDIO-002 (location scopes), MOVE-009 (imported rows and their source) and LEAD-006, MEM-001 and MEM-006 (a member sharing opt-out, if one is added, removes that member's rows). The owner’s explicit grant on a new key remains required. MEM-006 now also lets a member remove their rows from existing integration keys; it never widens a key’s scope. **Acceptance evidence:** A new key created on Integrations with `attendance:read` (the form lists the fields; a roster-only key is refused the resource with 403 and its roster, even after rotation or crafted scope fields, carries no attendance) reads classes and rows with the exact field allowlist; asserts booked, attended (check-in), no_show, excused (owner correction), late_cancel and early_cancel with `cancelledBy`, `corrected`, `correctedFrom` and `correctedAt` (a late cancel corrected to early reads early_cancel, corrected from late_cancel), no check-in time for a corrected attendance, waitlisted, offered and studio-cancelled seats omitted, `source` imported once a row is marked, `memberRef` equal for one member across classes and rotation and different between members and between two keys, full name, email, phone, ids of people, reasons, money and instructor absent, an erased person absent, paging, the shared rate limit and usage log, `attendance.changed` recorded not delivered, and a key created under API-002 alone still reading booleans only. Native restore refuses the key (API-002 archive journey).

### Security custody and operating boundaries

- **SEC-001 — Private records and operational recovery.** Studios retain deployment and data custody, encrypted transport, protected provider credentials and least-privilege access, with tested backup recovery, actionable integration diagnostics and clear stale/error states. Logs redact member notes and payment secrets and every export requires explicit rights. **Acceptance evidence:** Deploy to a controlled studio account, exercise role-separated exports and provider failure diagnostics, inspect logs for planted secrets and restore a backup to a recovery installation.

- **SEC-002 — Durable staff and automation audit.** Record actor, role, policy/version, time, source and before/after effect for staff access, member changes, billing attempts, autopay skips and postponements, staff-made contract freezes, freeze ends, terminations and canceled terminations with their type or reason code and comment, cash drawer adjustments, refunds, entitlements, attendance corrections, imports, exports, messages and agent execution. Every staff action on a member's behalf through a STAFF-006 staff door is recorded as staff-made with the acting staff member, role, STAFF-001 right used, member, channel (desk, phone, inbox or staff device) and any reason: bookings, cancellations with their early or late type, fee waiver and notice suppression, moves, restores, waitlist actions, spot and guest bookings, makeups, check-ins, sales and card-on-file charges, invoices and receipts sent, payment collections, retries and payment-method changes, plan changes, freezes and terminations, signing sessions launched, and profile, household, intake, preference, referral and privacy-request records. Authorized owners search/export the audit by member, staff member, right and action; erasure retains only permitted pseudonymous financial evidence. **Acceptance evidence:** Change staff rights, correct attendance, run a renewal and approved refund, export and erase a member; inspect the complete ordered audit and verify agents and staff cannot rewrite it. As front desk, cancel one member's booking late, early-cancel another with a waiver reason, move and restore bookings and charge a card on file; filtering the audit by member and by right shows each action once as staff-made with its right, channel and reason. SCHED-014 obligation before this capability ships: SCHED-014 staff-made action records in searchable and exportable durable audit history; assert the inherited behavior through its public doors. STAFF-006 obligation before this capability ships: every member action here must ship its table-mapped staff door and named right, the same preview, policy, notice and once-only identity, any member-owned authorization step, and one canonical staff-made actor/member/channel/before/after entry; assert the member/staff pair through HTTP and the 390-pixel staff view, including denied/revoked rights under STAFF-001. Current partial search/export semantics: the native owner filters existing canonical staff-made history by exact member, acting staff member, right, channel and command and inclusive studio-local from/through dates. Newest UTC event comes first, with event identity as the tie-breaker; the screen, JSON and CSV select the same records. JSON/CSV preserve event identity, time, actor and role, member, command/action, named right, channel, reason and before/after facts; replay payloads and command results are excluded. CSV uses JSON-valued data cells, with before/after objects encoded as JSON text; erased profile values remain null under the existing unused-identity policy. The HTTP doors are read-only and keep existing owner-only authority. This does not claim complete studio auditing or change retention policy. Personal-copy requests and delivery outcomes remain distinguishable from signature completion. Credentials stay outside audit records and document content remains in restricted evidence storage.

Record a phoned-in access request, verify identity and deliver the export; the request and its outcome are audited, and a manager without the privacy right is refused. - **SEC-004 — Multi-factor sign-in for privileged roles: owners, factors, recovery and reset.** Owners enroll a second factor (passkey or TOTP authenticator) before reaching refunds, payouts, pay, exports, staff rights or provider connections. Recovery codes are single use, a factor reset requires another owner and is audited, and members may opt in. Strap's own factors protect Base sign-in. **Doors:** a person who must have a factor and has none is refused every gated page, form, JSON and download with 403 `mfa_enrollment_required`; ordinary work stays open. Anyone with a working factor (required or opted in) is held at every gated door with `mfa_required` until the session presents one, lasting that session. Gated today: revenue and teaching-pay reports; every CSV, XLSX, text and exit download; staff history; pay rules and every pay view other than an instructor's own; staff rights (inviting, deactivating, reactivating, changing a role, and the owner's finance-report grant); agent keys; integration keys; kiosk pairing; the member-email connection; factor resets. Refunds (BILL-008), payouts (BILL-011), Stripe (BILL-001), payroll and provider connections (STAFF-003–005, INT-001–009, MSG and CHANNEL connections) join before they ship. Agent, integration and kiosk keys never satisfy, perform or bypass a factor check. **Factors:** TOTP RFC 6238 (SHA-1, six digits, 30 seconds, one step either side, each step once per factor), secret sealed AES-256-GCM under a dedicated `MFA_KEY` generated at setup (never the session secret), setup refused while `MFA_KEY` is absent, factor active after one valid code. Passkeys use WebAuthn with user verification required, the installation host as RP, ES256 or RS256, single-use challenges expiring after five minutes, and any attestation accepted without claiming the maker checked. **Enroll/remove:** a first factor needs Base fresh email-link step-up; adding or removing beside a working factor needs the session's check; a person who must have a factor cannot remove their last. **Recovery:** ten codes shown once, hashed, each once in one transaction, counting only while a working factor exists; regenerating after a factor check voids the old set. Five wrong since the last right code pauses that person's checks for 15 minutes. **Reset:** only another owner, in a factor-checked session, after Base step-up and with a required reason; removes factors and recovery codes and ends all their sessions. Nobody resets their own; a sole owner recovers only with a recovery code, with no support or installation bypass. **Audit:** SEC-002 staff history records every enrollment, removal, reset (actor, subject, time, reason, factors removed), recovery-code use, regeneration and pause; never a secret, code or credential. **Archives:** factor secrets, passkeys and recovery hashes never enter a native archive or MOVE-011 exit; a restored studio sends everyone to enrollment, and a changed `MFA_KEY` does the same for authenticator apps with the reason shown. **Finance-report grant:** gives a member read of the revenue and collections report and its downloads only; it is not STAFF-001's finance role, which replaces it when STAFF-001 ships. STAFF-001's manager and finance roles reach gated doors only through SEC-005, and no right grants reset power. SEC-001, SEC-002, SEC-003, MOVE-011, API-002, API-003 and APP-001 inherit these protections before their new doors ship. **Acceptance evidence:** Enroll a passkey and a TOTP app and sign in with each; use one recovery code twice (second refused); have one owner reset another's factor and inspect the audit record. Before enrollment, attempt an owner export, a teaching-pay adjustment, a staff role change and an integration-key creation (each refused with nothing written); verify a replayed TOTP code, a sixth wrong code within 15 minutes, a self-reset and an agent or integration key on a gated door are refused, factor data is absent from a native archive and the exit, and a member who opts in is asked for the factor at each new sign-in.

- **SEC-005 — Multi-factor sign-in for privileged roles: managers, finance staff and payouts.** Managers and finance staff enroll a second factor (passkey or TOTP authenticator) before reaching refunds, payouts, pay, exports, staff rights or provider connections. Every SEC-004 rule applies unchanged to STAFF-001's manager and finance roles and to BILL-011's payout report. **Acceptance evidence:** Invite a finance user and attempt a payout report before enrollment (refused), then enroll and open it; invite a manager and attempt an export before enrollment (refused).

## Push further

- **SUCCESS-001 — Detect explainable attendance drop-off.** The member-success agent joins real booking/attendance patterns, membership/freeze state, available classes, cancellations and consent to explain a deviation from a member's own routine. It cites dates and uncertainty, excludes unavailable opportunities and queues outreach under owner frequency limits. **Acceptance evidence:** Run an approved member journey through public booking/attendance doors, remove visits for one routine and freeze another member; inspect cited risk reasons, no false freeze alert and no message without permitted policy. Semantics (SUCCESS-001): native owners and connected preparation keys use the source rules and exclusions in LEAD-004 to prepare immutable explanations of completed weekly class routines. Proposals cite dated attended bookings and classes, elapsed missed opportunities, cancellation and unavailable-week exclusions, current plan and freeze identities, independently recorded channel permission and uncertainty about why visits stopped. No health diagnosis or consent is inferred. Only the native human owner confirms a private outreach-review task after recomputing the booking and membership sources, current channel permission and the explicitly configured per-member rolling 30-day task cap inside the DATA-001 revision fence. Changed sources, permission revisions or limits require a fresh proposal; an opt-out cannot be undone by replaying an old capture. One permanent task identity covers the member, routine and last attended booking, and every confirmed task counts against the cap across channels. AGENT-001 preparation keys cannot confirm, read the private queue or gain private appointment sources through this workflow. Confirmation retains the owner, time, exact evidence and note; identical capture replay retains one task, while a changed replay is refused. The task is private review work and sends no member message or payment. MEM-006 supplies the existing channel-permission rule; AUTO-001 inherits automatic triggers and MSG-001–009 retain actual external delivery and their provider boundaries before any outbound capability ships.

- **SUCCESS-002 — Offer a workable attendance plan.** Using member-provided schedule preferences, travel and location choices, class eligibility, remaining credits, live capacity and actual visits, the agent offers feasible class times and a plan change or freeze request when useful. It never invents availability or diagnoses health. **Acceptance evidence:** Give a member a narrow available schedule and no entitlement to reformer classes; inspect only eligible available choices, accept one and verify the offered class remains feasible after a concurrent booking. STAFF-006 obligation before this capability ships: every member action here must ship its table-mapped staff door and named right, the same preview, policy, notice and once-only identity, any member-owned authorization step, and one canonical staff-made actor, member, channel, before and after entry; assert the member and staff pair through HTTP and the 390-pixel staff view, including denied or revoked rights under STAFF-001. Semantics (SUCCESS-002): the member alone records dated availability intervals and chosen locations. An owner, connected preparation key or explicitly scoped front-desk user prepares at most ten chronological published choices, citing class identities, current eligible packs and actual attended booking identities. The entire class must fit an interval and chosen location; current credits, plan hours, freeze and cancellation state, intake, waiver, booking windows, existing overlapping bookings and online capacity are checked. Offers hold no seat and send nothing. No eligible choice is stated honestly, with the existing member plan-change and freeze request doors; those retain their own human approval requirements. Member acceptance or the booking-right staff pair rechecks current source details and eligibility inside the ordinary booking transaction; a changed preference, changed class or filled seat refuses without partial booking or credit use. Replay preserves one booking and its ordinary confirmation. A separate owner-granted attendance booking scope and enabled member-record scope must both name the member and location on every front-desk request, including replay; second-factor protection applies and revocation is immediate. Staff can start the member sign-in step but cannot set availability. Preferences, scope revisions and source-linked offers remain portable. No health diagnosis, autonomous contract change, refund or outbound campaign is performed. STAFF-001 inherits these named booking scopes and denials for wider roles; SUCCESS-003 retains approved freeze and refund execution, and AUTO-001 and MSG clauses retain future automatic triggers and outreach obligations.

- **SUCCESS-003 — Book accepted help under human control.** After a member accepts a specific class offer the agent books through the ordinary capacity, waiver and entitlement rules and confirms the result. Refunds, debt waivers, plan/contract changes and freezes require the authorized human's approval of exact effects; agents cannot approve their own proposals. **Acceptance evidence:** Accept a suggested class, fill its last seat concurrently and verify a truthful conflict or single booking; request a freeze and refund and require explicit human approval with a recheck before execution. STAFF-006 obligation before this capability ships: every member action here must ship its table-mapped staff door and named right, the same preview, policy, notice and once-only identity, any member-owned authorization step, and one canonical staff-made actor/member/channel/before/after entry; assert the member/staff pair through HTTP and the 390-pixel staff view, including denied/revoked rights under STAFF-001.

- **SUCCESS-004 — Measure recovered visits and renewals.** The agent follows accepted and declined interventions through subsequent attendance, collected renewal revenue and member feedback, separating correlation from demonstrated experiments. Owners approve cohorts, incentives and spending; small or incomplete groups stay inconclusive and members can opt out. **Acceptance evidence:** Run an approved attendance-recovery campaign, record later visits and one failed renewal, compare observed and collected outcomes with source events and inspect an inconclusive small cohort without a fabricated success claim.

- **SUCCESS-005 — Recover billing without breaking access.** The agent compares invoice/payment events, ACH return state and entitlement policy, explains the actual failure and prepares a secure recovery action. Owner-set retries and grace may run deterministically; refunds, waived debt and contract changes require human approval. **Acceptance evidence:** Return an ACH debit after apparent success, ask for recovery help and inspect the provider-grounded explanation, correct debt/access and a secure update link; refuse an agent attempt to waive the balance.

- **SUCCESS-006 — Balance demand and instructor coverage.** The agent joins waitlists, occupancy, attendance, instructor availability and substitution history to propose additional classes, retiming or coverage. Managers approve the exact timetable/staffing change, recheck existing bookings and choose the member notification before publication. Semantics: the connected agent reads cited class/booking IDs and counts of usable seats, reservations, held offers, waiters, attendance and no-shows, together with retained substitution history and recorded availability, then supplies an additional-class, retiming or coverage proposal and its rationale. These are observed counts, not a demand forecast or a claim of recovered visits. Availability uses active instructors, published resource allocations and recorded unavailable intervals with the existing preparation/cleanup buffers and half-open UTC bounds (SCHED-003); absence of a block is not an instructor confirmation. Exception reasons stay owner-only. A frozen recommendation keeps those facts, the exact class, reservation/credit effects and member notice text; changed availability, bookings, qualifications or provider/origin facts require a fresh preview. The ordinary classes.publish door cannot publish a recommendation. Coverage requires the studio's current service qualification and retains substitution provenance. Until STAFF-001 the native human owner acts for the manager; agents only prepare, and STAFF-001 inherits the manager grant, denial and revocation cases before shipping. At approval the owner explicitly selects the shown notification: in-app plus configured email for each affected reservation, or no affected reservations for an addition/empty class. Notice suppression is not offered by this door; provider acceptance is not mailbox delivery, and unavailable or paused email is labelled honestly. Publication preserves current booking IDs, waitlist positions, reserved credits and charges; the same approval never repeats a class, audit or notice. **Acceptance evidence:** Create overfilled and underused classes through public doors, provide instructor availability and request a recommendation; review its cited demand, change availability before approval and require a fresh preview.

- **SUCCESS-007 — Make cutover reconcile.** The migration agent maps actual source members, bookings, plans, credits, signed-waiver evidence, schedules and processor-transfer exceptions, proposes ambiguous matches and explains discrepancies. The owner signs off balances and cutover; the agent cannot activate autopay or infer missing values. **Acceptance evidence:** Upload a real source package with duplicate names, a missing pack balance and an unsupported payment method; inspect cited proposed matches, resolve ambiguities and require owner sign-off before any collection.

- **SUCCESS-008 — Resolve routine member inquiries.** A scoped inbox agent answers from current studio policies, member entitlements, schedules and conversation history, cites its facts and proposes allowed bookings or self-service steps. It escalates uncertainty, sensitive intake, complaints, refund requests and contract changes to people and respects all channel preferences. **Acceptance evidence:** Ask about credits, a class time and a freeze by SMS and in-app, change the source schedule mid-conversation and verify grounded updated answers, approved booking actions and human escalation for the freeze and refund.

before1.text: # Strap Classes, class packs and member balances for a US yoga, Pilates or boutique fitness studio, priced in US dollars. You own the records and run the app in your Cloudflare account. Payments stay with your existing processor. MIT licensed. [First release](ACCEPTANCE.md); the [product contract](CONTRACT.md) is the full studio system it is growing into. The owner guides start at [Getting started](docs/getting-started.md); the run site serves them at `/docs`. ## Run Strap's run site is live at https://run-strap.com. To run it locally, install Git, then follow the same two steps as https://run-strap.com/run. Node is not required. 1. Install the launcher: ```sh curl -fsSL https://runeditrun.com/install.sh | sh ``` Before step 2, make the installed command available in this terminal: ```sh export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH" rer cli path ``` Run the shell startup line that `rer cli path` prints so `rer` is also available in new terminals. The installer does not change your shell startup file. 2. Clone and start Strap: ```sh rer dev just-every/run-strap ``` To start it again later, run `cd run-strap && rer dev`. For people who already have Node 22 or later, this is an alternative: ```sh npx -y @runeditrun/rer dev just-every/run-strap ``` RER installs the pinned dependencies and Node 22.20.0, builds the app, migrates local D1 and prepares an owner. First launch can take several minutes. Open the private `RER_OPEN` link printed in the terminal, confirm the owner and click **Finish setup**. Keep that link private. `RER_READY` is the ordinary app address. A repeated `rer dev` resumes or reuses the running app. On a busy Mac, RER may refuse when its 15-second process-ownership inspection times out; retry the same command. This is a launcher limitation, not a completed launch. For your own owner email, run `rer install just-every/run-strap`, then from the checkout `rer setup --owner-email you@example.com` and `rer dev`. Local development sends no external email. The server keeps running in the background after the command returns; stop it with `rer dev --stop`. If you explicitly launch with `--foreground`, Ctrl-C stops that foreground process. If a saved port is occupied, run `rer dev --port 8899` with an available port. Never expose local development publicly. ## Run your first week 1. Open **People**. Add an instructor with role `instructor` and members with role `member`; activate them, then **Invite to sign in**. Invites establish native sessions, and only the owner grants access. To use a second local browser profile, open the terminal's private `RER_OPEN` link there first, then sign out. In the second profile, open `/signin` and choose the invited person’s one-click sign-in. Local owner access uses the private launch link; local member access uses these invitations. Hosted email sign-in uses the configured mail sender. 2. Open **Studio** (the location under the logo) and save the studio's location and time zone. Open **Packs and payments**. Prepare a pack for a member with its credits, price in dollars and how long it is good for, review it, then approve. The approved amount becomes owed; no card is charged. Record payments only after receiving them through your processor, with a unique receipt reference. Credits and money balances are separate. 3. Open **Classes**. Prepare a Monday-starting week, one row per class: name, room, day, start time on the studio's clock, minutes, spots and instructor. Review the exact draft, then publish it. Times show in the studio's time zone, the US way ("Tue, Oct 20 · 6:00 am"). For a recurring timetable, open **Repeating timetable → Prepare repeating classes**, then choose its date range and repeat interval. Review and publish the exact occurrences before members can book; publication does not create an endless schedule. A published class cannot be silently edited. 4. Sign in as a member. Acknowledge the current waiver if the owner has published one, then book a class. A full class adds the member to its waitlist without spending a credit. Cancellation before start returns the booked credit once and promotes the first eligible waiting member with a valid credit. Members see their own balances and bookings. An assigned instructor opens **Today** and checks attendees in from the class roster. 5. An owner can prepare a balance reminder and review its exact wording and balance before approving the text export. Balance reminders remain reviewed text exports. Owners can configure class reminder email timing in **Studio**; member opt-out keeps in-app notices, and failed or unavailable email creates a private follow-up task. SMS and push reminders are not available. Strap does not collect payments. [Agent commands](docs/AGENT-COMMANDS.md) can prepare drafts, while native human owner sessions approve them. 6. **Import** accepts the [documented Mindbody member CSV shape](docs/MOVE-IN.md). Paste the [synthetic fixture](tests/fixtures/members.csv), preview, review and apply the unchanged CSV. Imports start inactive with no credits or charges. The journal retains original source and supports resume and conflict-preserving undo. Deactivate a person in **People** to revoke studio access immediately. Revoke preparation keys in **Agent access** and integration keys in **Integrations**. Waiver acknowledgement records receipt of the exact version; it is not a legal signature. The unused-identity erasure shortcut and verified owner privacy requests are documented in [People and access](docs/people.md). Supported used and imported member records can be redacted with explicit financial and document retention decisions. Unsupported related work is refused. Erasure blocks the same identity from being recreated or imported. ## Back up and restore Stop the app, and keep exports private: ```sh rer dev --stop rer export --output exports/strap.rer ``` Restore into a fresh clone of the same revision before setup or entering data: ```sh rer install just-every/run-strap cd run-strap rer import --input /private/path/strap.rer --yes rer setup --owner-email original-owner@example.com rer dev ``` The original owner/member identities, classes, packs, bookings, payments, approvals, waiver acknowledgements, import originals and journals travel. Sessions, sign-in links, agent keys, integration keys, provider credentials and the development outbox do not. Re-enter private configuration and sign in again. Setup uses the archived owner's email. Damaged archives and populated destinations are refused. After erasure, restore the current post-erasure archive. An older archive plus a later `--journal` may be refused with `erasure_epoch`; the journal is an erasure fence, not a guarantee that older data can be recovered. `--input` accepts an absolute archive path, but this launcher requires `--journal` to name a file inside the destination checkout, such as `exports/LATER.rer`. See [Backup and restore](docs/backup-and-restore.md) for that limited path. Offline older backups cannot discover later erasure; protect and retire old copies. `rer reset --yes` destroys local data and settings; export first if needed. ## Deploy No domain or provider account is needed locally. For hosting, use your own Cloudflare Workers and D1 account and verified mail sender. Resource identities in `wrangler.jsonc` and `deploy.json` stay stable. Provide `MAIL_FROM` as your verified sender address. Required private deployment inputs are `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`, `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`, `OWNER_EMAIL`, `SESSION_SECRET`, `SETUP_TOKEN`, `MFA_KEY` and `MAIL_API_KEY`; supply them through your secret manager. Assisted hosting can select Resend, SendGrid or Cloudflare Email Sending in rer-setup.json. Cloudflare also needs MAIL_ACCOUNT_ID. Managed hosting assigns MAIL_PROVIDER, MAIL_FROM and MAIL_RELAY_URL and provisions the private MAIL_API_KEY; the sender passes the assigned relay URL. Local development suppresses external delivery. Never put secrets in arguments or source. Commit intended configuration changes before deploying. ```sh rer dev --stop rer deploy --dry-run --owner-name "Your name" rer deploy --owner-name "Your name" ``` Stop local development before deploying: it owns the local state while it runs. Dry run validates and builds, then reads the target secret bindings from Cloudflare. It requires `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` and `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`; without them it exits with a credentials error after the local build. Nothing is deployed by a dry run. Real deployment provisions resources, applies migrations, uploads secrets and checks health. It claims the configured owner and retires the setup token. Open the returned workers.dev origin and sign in by email. A custom domain is optional. `rer signin` provides owner recovery when mail is not working yet; then correct the sender/email configuration. This round verifies local runtime and dry-run behavior; real provider delivery and hosted acceptance remain unverified. ## Develop Package mode pins `@runeditrun/rer@0.2.80`. The committed Base foundation was `c7cb0613120074c5ffca63f610533802afbda6bd`. [Source adaptation](docs/SOURCES.md), [operations](RUN-LOCALLY.md), [agent guide](AGENTS.md). ```sh pnpm run test:strap pnpm run test:archive pnpm run typecheck rer verify ``` Integration tests use real workerd/D1, native invitations/sessions and public HTTP commands, plus the public archive CLI. Build/deploy never run tests. One sharded Verify workflow runs per push commit; the separate lane runs the stranger journey. The mark is a sea-glass stability ball with a plum band (`public/brand/mark.svg`; `mark-dark.svg` for dark grounds; hand-tuned `favicon-16.svg` and `favicon-32.svg`). The run site's look (Playfair Display headings in plum, Figtree text, white and sea-glass grounds) has its tokens in `public/site/theme.css`. The app's tokens are in `public/rer-theme.css` (the faces and the theme tokens rer's reader takes) and `public/fonts/fonts.css` (the rest), Strap's shared app components in `public/brand/strap.css`, which also dresses Base's sign-in and setup frames, and the app layout in `src/strap/ui/style.ts`. ## Run site `rer build --site` writes the static run site to `dist/site`: the homepage (`src/site/landing`), whose **Run Strap** opens `/run`, Base's Run page with the commands in `src/site/run.json`, and the docs rendered from `docs/*.md` in the order `docs/site.json` gives. An installed Strap serves the Lobby at `/` instead. `rer dev` serves the run site too and prints its address as `RER_SITE`; open its `/run` page for the local install commands. `.github/workflows/run-site.yml` publishes it to the domain in `deploy-site.json` only when the repository variable `RUN_SITE_DEPLOY` is `true`. ## Stripe test plan payments Configure `STRIPE_BILLING_TEST_KEY` as an installation secret and `STRIPE_BILLING_WEBHOOK_SECRET` as the signing secret for the Stripe endpoint at `/api/strap/billing/webhook`. Credentials never appear in the app or portable archives. In Studio settings, an owner with second-factor verification reviews the merchant ID from their own Stripe dashboard and its readiness. A changed credential requires another review of the same merchant. Disconnect keeps all history; restoring an archive requires a fresh review and never reauthorizes historical stored methods. From Packs, the owner starts a one-time USD card payment for an approved, wholly unpaid plan. The payer enters their own card in Stripe-hosted checkout. Pending or uncertain outcomes are retained; another request never creates a second session. Reconcile with Stripe reads the canonical session, payment intent, captured charge and generated invoice before recording the actual receipt. Stripe can finish its invoice after returning from checkout; review the exception and reconcile again once Stripe has issued it. Existing plan access stays unchanged. Household billing, partial external receipts, recurring autopay and refunds remain their separate contract work. The exception queue retains unmatched events and failed comparisons. Configure the endpoint for checkout completion and expiry, payment-intent success and failure, and invoice payment events. Signatures and account identity are checked before processing; signed event payloads alone never settle money. The network-edge suite exercises replay, ordering, missing events and forged envelopes. `node tests/payments-sandbox.mjs` runs the held-key live TEST journey through the injector; it completes hosted card checkout and deliberately replays real Stripe events with a controlled local signing secret. It does not claim external endpoint delivery.

# Strap product contract

Target edition: 17 October 2026. Strap is the complete boutique fitness and yoga studio system a US owner buys to sell and auto-renew memberships, intro offers and class packs, collect payments, fill classes through a branded member app and follow people from first inquiry to sustained attendance. A yoga, Pilates or boutique fitness studio with 100–500 members can replace its incumbent without running billing, messaging, payroll preparation or retention in a second studio system.

This contract describes the destination, not a claim that it ships today. The status table records the distance from current code and tests; missing provider access, app distribution, payment migration or production evidence remains delivery work. USD, US buyers, US addresses/phone numbers, sales tax, ACH and W-2/1099 payroll handoff are the first-market defaults. Existing Australian copy and owner-approved homepage/UI remain untouched by this documentation change; STUDIO-001 is the required US product behavior.

## Product target

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Category | Boutique fitness and yoga studio management software |
| Incumbents a buyer switches from | Mindbody, WellnessLiving, Vagaro, Momence, Arketa, PushPress |
| First buyer | A US owner of a yoga, Pilates or boutique fitness studio with 100–500 members, front-desk staff and instructors, billing members in USD |

Strap owns scheduling, enrollment, memberships, payments through the studio's merchant account, POS, staff operations, member communication and retention. Its studio member pipeline is part of that category job. [Orbit](https://github.com/just-every/run-orbit) remains general CRM, [Nectar](https://github.com/just-every/run-nectar) remains general subscription billing, [Inkwell](https://github.com/just-every/run-inkwell) remains general signatures, [Pantry](https://github.com/just-every/run-pantry) remains the general ledger and [Crank](https://github.com/just-every/run-crank) remains cross-product automation. Shared infrastructure is welcome; these products keep their separate ownership.

## Reading and operating rules

Each named clause states buyer behavior and acceptance evidence through a screen, HTTP route, provider webhook, downloadable artifact or public command. ACCEPTANCE.md repeats every journey and its current status. Network/payment fakes belong only at the test edge; real provider delivery, store distribution and real-export compatibility need their own controlled evidence. Partial means a cited foundation exists while the named gap remains.

The previous contract had no clause IDs. Its positive guarantees receive published IDs below; no existing ID is renamed. Its receipt-only ceiling becomes one payment path alongside Stripe collection. Its disclaimer about unproved hosted delivery, legal signatures and real exports becomes an honest current-status gap rather than a limit on the target.

- Fresh installations start empty and owners enter or import real studio data.
- Monetary records use exact USD cents and explicit tax/rounding rules; entitlements and money remain separate ledgers.
- Every handler authorizes the current actor independently. Owners control staff rights, policy and automation; agents cannot self-approve refunds, debt waivers or contract changes.
- Approved recurring terms authorize scheduled renewal and routine notices under recorded policy. Changed facts invalidate stale previews and exceptional changes require a person's exact approval.
- Capacity, credit use, payment attempts, rewards and delivered events have stable identities so retries and restarts cannot create duplicate business effects. Pending and uncertain provider states remain visible.
- Import originals, financial corrections and audit histories remain attributable. Erasure and exports respect retention duties and do not pretend to erase external recipients or offline copies.

## Published guarantees

- **AUTH-001 — Native roles and private records.** Native human owners manage access and approve publication and money drafts. Members see their own balances, packs and bookings and book or cancel only their own classes; instructors see assigned rosters and check attendance only for assigned classes. Every page, JSON command and download checks its own authority. **Acceptance evidence:** Sign in through invitations as an owner, two members and two instructors; read state, submit commands and request reminder downloads across roles; unauthorized work is refused without writes.

- **AUTH-002 — Immediate revocation and origin protection.** Deactivating a member or instructor or revoking an agent credential rejects its next request. Browser mutations require the configured same origin; bearer credentials cannot impersonate human sessions. **Acceptance evidence:** Deactivate an invited member and revoke an agent key, then reuse their sessions or credentials; attempt cross-origin and malformed commands; require refusal and unchanged records.

- **AGENT-001 — Exact drafts and human approval.** Agents can read studio context and prepare immutable class weeks, finite packs and balance-reminder drafts. A native human owner approves the exact draft once; changed source facts invalidate approval. Approval keeps the human identity and time. Reminder approval exports reviewed text. **Acceptance evidence:** Use an agent key to prepare a pack and reminder, refuse agent approval and the human endpoint with that key, approve as owner, download the text and refuse duplicate approval.

- **DATA-001 — Authoritative transactional studio records.** D1 is authoritative for people, capacity, credits, recorded payments and approvals. State revision and transaction fences prevent concurrent requests from overspending a credit or seat; waiting consumes no credit. **Acceptance evidence:** Race public booking commands for one seat and one credit; inspect one confirmed booking, no negative credit balance and no duplicate committed effect.

- **BOOK-001 — Eligible credit bookings.** A published future class has an assigned instructor and explicit capacity. A member books only with the current waiver acknowledged and an unexpired eligible finite credit; duplicate booking is refused and the seat and credit commit together. **Acceptance evidence:** Publish a reviewed future class, grant packs, book through the member API, attempt a duplicate and missing-waiver booking and inspect capacity and credit state.

- **BOOK-002 — Cancellation and eligible FIFO promotion.** Before class start an owner or the booked member cancels once, returns one spent credit and promotes the first eligible waiting member in the same transaction. Ineligible waiters cannot spend another member's credits. Configurable late-cancel rules extend this under ATT-002, and front-desk staff and managers cancel, move and restore a member's booking on the member's behalf under SCHED-014. **Acceptance evidence:** Fill a one-seat class, add a waiter, refuse another member's cancellation, cancel the booked seat and inspect one refunded credit and the waiter's confirmed seat and single debit.

- **PACK-001 — Reviewed finite class packs.** The owner or an agent prepares a member-specific finite pack with credits, amount and expiry. Human approval creates the pack, owed charge and retained approval once. Class credits remain distinct from money owed. Target USD presentation and processor collection extend this foundation. **Acceptance evidence:** Prepare a ten-credit pack, inspect no credits before approval, approve once and inspect ten credits, the exact owed cents and approval; repeat approval is refused.

- **PAY-001 — Once-only external receipt recording.** Owners record externally received funds against a member with positive whole cents and a unique external reference. Reusing the reference cannot reduce the balance twice. Processor collection is also required by BILL clauses; receipts are one supported payment path. **Acceptance evidence:** Record a partial external receipt against an approved pack, repeat its reference and submit a negative amount; inspect one payment and the remaining balance.

- **WAIVER-001 — Exact current waiver acknowledgment.** The owner publishes immutable waiver text versions. Members acknowledge the exact current version; publishing a new version requires renewed acknowledgment before booking. An acknowledgment is a version receipt; signed waiver execution is MEM-005. **Acceptance evidence:** Publish two waiver versions, reject booking without acknowledgment and acknowledgment of the obsolete version, acknowledge the latest and book successfully.

- **IMPORT-001 — Reviewed member CSV and reversible journal.** The owner previews the documented four-column Mindbody-shaped UTF-8 CSV, reviews its fingerprint and applies those exact bytes. Imports create inactive members with no invented credits or charges, retain originals and a resumable journal, and undo untouched imports while preserving later edits. Real incumbent export coverage is MOVE-001 through MOVE-006. **Acceptance evidence:** Upload the documented CSV through import.preview, refuse altered bytes with the old fingerprint, apply and resume to completion, inspect originals, edit one member and undo; the edited member survives.

- **ARCHIVE-001 — Complete native archive and guarded restore.** The owner exports and restores studio people, classes, packs, bookings, payments, approvals, waivers, import originals and journals using rer export/import. Damaged archives and populated destinations are refused. Sessions, sign-in links, agent keys, provider secrets and development outboxes stay installation-local. A later erasure journal fences an older archive; offline copies cannot discover later erasure unaided. **Acceptance evidence:** Populate a studio through HTTP, export with the public CLI, restore into an empty destination and re-export equal product parts; refuse corruption, a populated destination and a pre-erasure archive with a later journal. MEM-005 obligation before complete signed-document recovery ships: retain exact attributed documents, declarations, stable relationships and historical authority provenance while excluding tablet credentials, personal-copy capabilities, mail-review authority and dispatch authority. Restoring history never restores former guardian access or permits new copy delivery; the native human owner must freshly review and reconnect the current installation. Prove these exclusions using initialized copy records through the public archive and restore doors.

- **ERASE-001 — Unused identity erasure fence.** The owner can erase an unused, uninvited, non-imported identity. Its identifying data is redacted and an identity fence prevents recreation, CSV reimport and resurrection through a restore supplied with the later journal. Used-member erasure is a further target under SEC-003. **Acceptance evidence:** Erase an unused person through person.erase, inspect absence of their email, refuse recreation and CSV reimport, and run the CLI older-backup/later-journal refusal.

- **AUDIT-001 — Retained draft approval records.** Class, pack and reminder approvals retain the approved draft, human approver and time. These records travel with native studio archives rather than being discarded on restore. Full staff and automation auditing is SEC-002. **Acceptance evidence:** Approve a pack through HTTP, inspect its draft-linked approval, archive the populated studio and compare the restored approval records.

- **PUBLIC-001 — Run site and installed studio doors.** The run-site homepage opens /run and serves owner guides at /docs. An installed studio has a separate Lobby at /, setup and sign-in doors and private /app routes. These existing owner-approved pages keep their design and behavior. **Acceptance evidence:** Build the run site, open its homepage, /run and /docs; open the installed Worker Lobby signed out and attempt /app before and after sign-in. Confirm the public and private routes remain separate.

Optional values clear explicitly; location/time-zone-only saves retain the profile. Weekly hours use Monday=1 through Sunday=7 and one opening-before-closing HH:MM interval on that location's clock per open day; absent days are closed, and hours do not modify booking-window or class-availability rules. Every class, repeating series, closure and class-week row is entered and shown on its own location's clock: a weekly class keeps its local start across daylight-saving changes (a nonexistent local time is refused) while the stored instant moves, and notices, reminders, check-in windows, reports and the member and staff screens read the class's location zone, naming the zone when it differs from the studio's.
